# Dream Book for iPad: everything in one file

**First version, 20 October 2026.** A polished version follows soon. It will have a cleaner Part 1 and Part 2, after a final strict review. The research, rules and code in this version are complete.

This one file is everything another AI chat needs to build **Dream Book**, an iPad app that reads books aloud and teaches English, made from my Mac app **Dream Read**. It holds all the instructions, the deep research (with fact-checks), the voices (best, cheap, free), what similar apps do, the 7 teaching characters, my own teaching style, my rules, how Dream Read works, and all the source code.

**How to use it:** open a new chat, attach this file, and paste the message in Part 1.

The same code is on GitHub: `948573034jackie-cpu/meh`, branch `claude/readalong-app`. When a part says "docs/RULES.md", "docs/MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md" or "docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md", it means Part 7, Part 6 or Part 8 of this file.

## Contents

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| 1 | The message to paste into the other chat |
| 2 | The plan at a glance: decisions, build order, costs, questions |
| 3 | Voices for Dream Book: best, cheap and free |
| 4 | What similar apps do, and what Dream Book should copy |
| 5 | The 7 teaching characters, with full prompts (Character 1 is my own style) |
| 6 | My own teaching style (RULE ONE, TWO, THREE) |
| 7 | My rules (they always win) |
| 8 | How Dream Read works (architecture and features) |
| 9 | All the source code of Dream Read |
| Appendix A | The full iPad research, R1 to R9, each with an independent fact-check |
| Appendix B | The full research on voices and similar apps |

# Part 1: The message to paste into the other chat

Copy everything between the two lines and send it with this file attached.

---

Hi. Please help me build an iPad app called **Dream Book**. I am a native Chinese speaker, about B2 in English. I have an **Intel MacBook Pro on macOS 13 Ventura** and an iPad. Please always answer in simple, clear English.

The attached file has everything you need. It has deep research on how to build this iPad app, with fact-checks. It also has the voices, similar apps, 7 teaching characters, my own teaching style, my rules, and all the code of my Mac app Dream Read. The code is also on GitHub: `948573034jackie-cpu/meh`, branch `claude/readalong-app`.

**What Dream Book is**
- An iPad app to **listen** to books and learn English, and learn anything else, with an AI teacher. Listening comes first. Reading pages come second.
- **Everything is automatic.**
  - When I add a book, the app reads and understands the whole book first and splits it into chapters and parts.
  - It finds every word, phrase, slang and short sentence above my level.
  - It prepares the explanations and the audio.
  - Then it plays by itself.
- **Sleep and listen.** I want to lie down, relax or fall asleep and just listen.
  - In Sleep mode there is no microphone and no waiting.
  - A sleep timer fades the sound out slowly.
  - The next day it starts again a little before where I fell asleep.
- **My level.** At the first start the app tests my level automatically. It keeps learning which words I know from what I do, so it knows my level all the time.
- **Explanations.** It explains hard words, phrases and sentences by itself. It uses my teaching style and the exact context of the book.
- **Saved everywhere.** My library, books, vocabulary, progress, settings and characters are saved on the iPad AND online in my account. Nothing is lost, even if I delete the app.
- **7 teaching characters.** Character 1 is my own style (Part 6). It is always first and is the default. I can change everything with very easy controls.
- **For everyone.** It is also for native speakers who want to learn anything: philosophy, poetry, science, history.

**Please read in this order**
1. **My rules and my teaching style, first.** Part 7 has my rules and Part 6 has my teaching style. These are final. If your plan or the research disagrees with them, follow them.
2. **The plan and the research.**
   - Part 2: the plan at a glance.
   - Appendix A: the iPad research, R1 to R9.
   - Part 3: voices.
   - Part 4: similar apps.
   - Part 5: the 7 characters.
3. **How Dream Read works and the code.** Part 8 explains how Dream Read works. Part 9 has all the code. Reuse `src/core` and `src/shared` instead of rewriting them: about 10,000 lines of plain TypeScript with about 650 tests.

**Decisions from the research** (change one only for a strong reason, and tell me why first)
- **How to build it.** Use **Expo (React Native, TypeScript) with EAS cloud builds**. My Mac cannot run the Xcode that Apple now requires, and the cloud builds do not need a Mac. Install it on my iPad with **TestFlight**. This needs the Apple Developer Program, $99 a year.
- **Sleep and listen.** Use a native background-audio player that plays audio files made ahead of time. The files hold the book, the word repeats, the explanations and the Chinese meanings. Add lock-screen and AirPods controls. A web page stops when the iPad locks, so audio must never depend on a web view.
- **Voices.** See Part 3.
  - Free: **Kokoro** on the iPad is the default, made ahead with word timings.
  - Backup: Apple's Premium voices. Apple's Chinese voice also says the Chinese meanings.
  - Paid: cloud voices as options, in three tiers: best, cheap, free.
- **AI.** Claude with my own API key.
  - Whole-book analysis: Haiku 5.5 through the Batch API.
  - Prepared explanations: Sonnet 5.5 through the Batch API.
  - When I say "I don't know": a live call.
  - Keep the AI provider replaceable.
- **Commands.** Apple's on-device speech recognition (SpeechAnalyzer) listens in the 5-second window. Its text goes to the existing command matcher with the accent fixes. Buttons and AirPods presses work too.
- **Data.** Everything is saved on the iPad first, so it works offline. It syncs to **Supabase** with Sign in with Apple, Google or email. My API key is kept in iCloud Keychain.

**How to work with me**
1. **Confirm first.** Repeat back in 5 to 10 short lines what you will build and in what order. Ask me the questions in Part 2. Wait for my OK.
2. **Week 1 is a test build on my iPad.** It must play 2 hours of book audio with the screen locked, with lock-screen controls, Kokoro speed and word timing. Build the rest only when this works.
3. **Small steps.** After every 2 or 3 features, give me a TestFlight build to test. Tell me how long each step will take before you start.
4. **Test and be honest.** Test everything before you give it to me. Tell me honestly what you could not test, for example sound on a real iPad.
5. **Explain my steps.** Explain every step I must do myself (Apple account, Expo account, API keys, Supabase) one click at a time, in simple words.

---

**Tips for working with the other chat**
- Send one topic per message when you can. Ask it to repeat back what it understood before it builds.
- When something is wrong, send a screenshot or the exact error text.
- If it can open GitHub, it can read the real code, which works better than descriptions.

# Part 2: The plan at a glance

This is a short summary of the research in Appendix A. The section numbers point to the details there. All prices are in US dollars, as of 20 October 2026.

## 2.1 The key decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| How to build | Expo (React Native) + EAS cloud builds, plus a small native "night player" module | It is the only route that keeps the app playing all night and still reuses the tested TypeScript. It needs no new Mac. | R1, R2, R9 |
| Runner-up | Capacitor 8 (wrap the existing web version) | It is faster to start, but the night player and Kokoro must still be native Swift plugins. | R1 |
| Not now | Native SwiftUI, PWA only, Tauri | SwiftUI means a full rewrite and an Apple-silicon Mac. A PWA stops when the screen locks. | R1 |
| Your Mac | Build in the cloud and install with TestFlight | Since 28 April 2026, Apple only accepts uploads built with Xcode 26, which does not run on macOS 13. Xcode 27 runs only on Apple-silicon Macs. | R2 |
| Book engine | "Plan once, render ahead, play offline" | When a book is added, the whole book is analysed once. Explanations and audio are prepared ahead, and playback works offline. | R3 |
| AI cost | Haiku 5.5 batch for the analysis (about $0.05–0.10 per novel). Sonnet 5.5 batch for about 700 prepared explanations (about $2.2 per book). Live calls for "I don't know" (about $0.008 each). | Batch is half price. A cheap model is enough for the analysis. | R3 |
| Modes | **Learn** (my rules exactly), **Relax** (hands-free, explains by itself), **Sleep** (no mic, short glosses or none, timer and fade, stops the story when I fall asleep, morning recap) | Sleep science: the brain does not learn new words consciously in deep sleep, but sleep helps keep words heard just before sleep. | R3, R4, R6, R7 |
| Knowing my level | The level test at first start. A per-word model from what I do (I know, I don't know, replays). FSRS review. A 5-word morning card. | Silence alone never marks a word as known. | R3 |
| Voices | Kokoro on the iPad (free, rendered ahead with word timings). Apple Premium voices as backup and for Chinese. Cloud voices as options. | Locked iPads cannot use the GPU, so audio is made before sleep while charging. | R5, Part 3 |
| Speech | SpeechAnalyzer + DictationTranscriber for the 5-second commands window. SpeechTranscriber with echo cancellation for talking with the tutor. Sherpa-onnx Moonshine as the fallback. | It is free, on the device, private, and works in China. | R6 |
| Screen | Home has one big Play button and the Learn · Relax · Sleep control. The Listen screen is karaoke with big buttons. The word card is a popover next to the word. Presets, about 8 simple settings, Advanced, and "Edit buttons". | It follows Apple's iPad design rules and copies Apple Books, Pocket Casts and BookPlayer. | R7, Part 4 |
| Data | Saved on the iPad first, synced to Supabase (Apple, Google or email sign-in). API key in iCloud Keychain. An append-only event log rebuilds everything after a reinstall. | Nothing is lost when the app is deleted. | R8 |
| Characters | 7 characters: **My Teacher** (my style, first, default), Clear Teacher, Storyteller, Painter, Friend, Memory Coach, Deep Reader. Six easy knobs each. | Each one comes from a well-tested teaching method. Together they cover the 10 styles Dream Read has now. | R4, Part 5 |

## 2.2 Build order

Each step ends with a TestFlight build to test on the iPad. The research suggests these weeks; they are estimates.

1. **Week 1, go / no-go test on the iPad.**
   - 2 hours of pre-rendered book audio with the screen locked.
   - Lock-screen controls, AirPods pause, phone-call interruption.
   - Apple voice word timing and Kokoro speed.
   - The sentence splitter working on Hermes.
2. **Weeks 2–3.** Move `src/core` and `src/shared` into a shared package, with all tests passing. Write the iPad adapters: voices, storage, AI client and PDF.
3. **Weeks 3–5.** Listening screen (karaoke), library, word card, the 7 characters in Settings.
4. **Weeks 5–7.** Whole-book analysis, prepared explanations, the pre-rendered audio queue, Relax and Sleep modes, and the sleep timer.
5. **Weeks 7–9.** Learn mode: the 5-second commands windows with speech recognition, and talking with the tutor.
6. **Then.**
   - Account and cloud restore.
   - Reading mode (pages).
   - FSRS review class.
   - App Store needs: privacy policy, consent before any book text goes to the AI, and in-app account deletion.

## 2.3 Costs for one learner

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Apple Developer Program, needed for TestFlight | $99 a year |
| Expo EAS cloud builds | 15 iOS builds a month free; Starter $19 a month |
| AI per book, about 10 hours | about $0.5 with Haiku only; about $2.2 with Sonnet explanations (recommended); live "I don't know" about $0.008 each |
| Voice | $0 with Kokoro or Apple voices. Paid voices are in Part 3. |
| Supabase | $0 on the free plan for one person. Pro is $25 a month before a public release. |

## 2.4 Questions the other chat should ask me first

1. My rules say to pause at *every* item above my level. That can be one pause every 30–50 words. May Learn mode use a limit on how often it pauses?
2. Sleep mode has two choices:
   - (a) no pauses: the story plays and the words are saved for the morning;
   - (b) short glosses only.
   My full rule takes a long time at night, because the word is said 10 times.
3. In Sleep mode, should a gloss give one Chinese meaning or two?
4. In Relax mode, is a 1.5-second pause before the automatic explanation right, or should there be no pause?
5. Where should the "I know" button be: at the edge, so it is harder to hit by mistake, or in the middle?

# Part 3: Voices for Dream Book: best, cheap and free

*Facts as of 20 October 2026. All prices are list prices in US dollars. "Checked" means the fact was confirmed on the company's own page on 20 Oct 2026. "Uncertain" means it could not be confirmed. Many other numbers come from third-party pages, so check the price again before you pay.*

**How the costs are worked out**
- One hour of listening is about **54,000 characters** of book text.
- A normal novel (about 90,000 words) is about 540,000 characters, or about **10 hours**.
- The app makes the audio for each book **once** and saves it. Listening again costs **$0**.
- Spoken explanations add about 10–20% more text. This is my estimate.

---

## 1. The short answer

| Tier | Main pick | Backup | Price per listening hour | Word timing (for the karaoke highlight) | Runs where |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BEST** | **ElevenLabs Eleven v4** | Cartesia Sonic 3.6 | v4: **$4.32** (checked: $0.08 per 1,000 characters). Sonic: about **$2.00–2.70** | v4: character timings from the `/with-timestamps` endpoint, joined into words. It is not confirmed that this endpoint accepts v4, so test it. Sonic: word timestamps built in | Cloud |
| **CHEAP** | **Speechify Simba 3.2** | Inworld TTS-2 Flash | Simba: **$0.32–0.54** (checked: $6–10 per 1M characters). Inworld Flash: **$0.81** (checked: $15 per 1M) | Both have word timings built in | Cloud |
| **FREE** | **Kokoro-82M on the iPad** | Apple Premium/Enhanced voices | **$0** | Kokoro: from the model's "duration" output, the way Dream Read does it now. Apple: the `willSpeakRange` word callback | **On the iPad, offline** |

**Why these picks**
- **Best: Eleven v4.**
  - It is **#2 of 97** on the Artificial Analysis (AA) Speech Arena, with an Elo score of 1,329. Its twin **Eleven v4 Turbo is #1 at 1,332** ([AA leaderboard](https://artificialanalysis.ai/text-to-speech/leaderboard), checked 20 Oct).
  - ElevenLabs launched both on 28 Sep 2026. It built v4 for audiobooks and voice-over ([ElevenLabs blog](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/eleven-v4)).
  - v4 is now also **#1 for Mandarin** on AA (about 1,301). So one company can read both the English book and the Chinese meanings.
  - **Tip:** v4 Turbo scores the same (a 3-point gap is noise) and costs half as much ($2.16/h). Listen to both on your own book before you choose.
- **Backup best: Sonic 3.6.** It is #4 (1,291). It gives clean word timestamps and connects quickly over a WebSocket.
- **Cheap: Simba 3.2.**
  - It is **#10 (1,245)**. Speechify says it is the lowest-priced model in the top ten ([Speechify blog](https://speechify.ai/blog/artificial-analysis-tts-leaderboard-elo-explained)), but that is the vendor's own claim.
  - An older claim that it was in the "top five" is **out of date**.
  - It costs about $40 a month even at 3 hours a day, and it gives word timings.
- **Backup cheap: Inworld TTS-2 Flash.**
  - It gives word timings in every language the model supports, so it covers Chinese too.
  - Its bigger model, Realtime TTS-2, is #7 (1,262).
- **Free: Kokoro.**
  - It scores about 1,065, so the best voices win about 4 of 5 blind tests against it.
  - But it costs nothing and needs no Wi-Fi, and Dream Read already knows how to get word timings from it.

**Honourable mention: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (#5, 1,280).**
- It scores higher than Simba in the arena.
- In Batch mode it costs about **$0.41/h until 31 Dec 2026**. From **1 Jan 2027** the price doubles to about **$0.81/h** (checked on [Google's pricing page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing)).
- But it gives **no word timings**. It only makes sense once the app has its own word-timing tool (the "shared aligner" in section 3.3).

**What the score gaps mean** (Elo maths)

| Comparison | Gap | How often listeners prefer the first voice |
|---|---|---|
| Eleven v4 vs Sonic 3.6 | 38 | about 55% (almost a tie) |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash vs Simba 3.2 | 35 | about 55% |
| Eleven v4 vs Simba 3.2 | 84 | about 62% |
| Simba 3.2 vs Kokoro | 180 | about 74% |
| Eleven v4 vs Kokoro | 264 | about 82% |

**Important:** these votes are on **short clips**, not on hours of narration. I found no independent test of long audiobook listening ([notevibes](https://notevibes.com/best-ai-voice-generator-for-audiobooks)). The real test is your own ears on 30 minutes of your own book.

## 3. How to build the voices into the iPad app

### 3.1 One "plug" for every voice
Make one interface, for example `VoiceProvider`, with one job:
`synthesize(text, voice) → (audio file, list of word timings)`.

ElevenLabs, Speechify, Inworld, Kokoro and Apple all plug in behind it. The rest of the app never needs to know which voice is in use, and one setting switches between the best, cheap and free tiers.

### 3.2 Make each book once and keep it (caching)
- **Name each saved piece** with a hash of: engine + model version + voice + text. If that name already exists, play the saved file. You never pay twice for the same text.
- **Size:** save AAC or Opus at 32–48 kbps. That is about **15–22 MB per hour**, or about **150–220 MB per novel**.
- **Where:** in **Application Support**, not in Caches, because iOS can delete Caches when space is low. Mark the folder "exclude from backup".
- **Speed:**
  - Make the audio at **1.0× speed only**.
  - Play it at 0.5–2.0× with `AVAudioUnitTimePitch`, and divide the word times by the speed.
  - A speed change then never costs a new render.
- **Cache these too:** spoken explanations (per word and context) and Chinese meanings (per word and meaning).

### 3.3 Word timings for the karaoke highlight

| Voice | How to get the word times |
|---|---|
| ElevenLabs | `/v1/text-to-speech/{voice}/with-timestamps` gives character times; join them into words ([Bifrost docs](https://docs.getbifrost.ai/providers/supported-providers/elevenlabs)). If v4 is not accepted there (unconfirmed), use the ElevenLabs Forced Alignment API ([Segmind](https://www.segmind.com/models/elevenlabs-forced-alignment)) or the shared aligner |
| Cartesia | `add_timestamps: true` gives word times. `add_phoneme_timestamps: true` gives sound-level times ([docs](https://docs.cartesia.ai/api-reference/tts/websocket)) |
| Inworld | WORD mode (with phonemes) or CHARACTER mode, in every language the model supports ([docs](https://docs.inworld.ai/tts/capabilities/timestamps)) |
| Speechify | The normal (batch) request `POST /v1/audio/speech` returns word marks on **any** model. The streaming request `/v1/audio/stream/with-timestamps` returns marks only on simba-3.0 and simba-3.2 ([changelog](https://docs.speechify.ai/build/changelog/2026/7/23)) |
| Azure Neural | `WordBoundary` events |
| Kokoro | The "duration" output, as in Dream Read (docs/KOKORO.md). **Check that the iOS port you choose exposes it.** KOKORO.md says only the kokoro-onnx export has it. The [mattmireles CoreML pipeline](https://huggingface.co/mattmireles/kokoro-coreml) is open source, so the output can be added. Fallback: run the same ONNX model with ONNX Runtime for iOS (untested) |
| Apple | `willSpeakRangeOfSpeechString` ([NSHipster](https://nshipster.com/avspeechsynthesizer)). `write(_:toBufferCallback:)` saves the audio to a file |
| Gemini, Chirp 3 HD, Qwen, MiniMax, Polly Generative | **None.** Use the shared aligner below |

**The shared aligner** is one tool that lets any voice drive the highlight. Because the app knows the exact text, matching words to times is easy.
- **On the iPad:**
  - Run Apple SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26).
  - Then fix its timings with **Align** by Desert Ant Labs, a Core ML model of about 560 KB.
  - Its model card says it cuts the average word-time error from 124.2 ms to 43.9 ms on clean audio, and from 106.4 ms to 20.2 ms on the LibriSpeech test-clean set ([model card v1.1.0](https://huggingface.co/desert-ant-labs/align)).
  - Licence: source-available. **A commercial licence is needed at scale.**
- **On a server:** aeneas ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/aeneas-ng/)) or the ElevenLabs aligner.
- **Last resort:** share the time between the words by their number of characters.

### 3.4 The Chinese voice (two short meanings per word)
There is very little Chinese text (tens of characters per word), and every meaning is cached. So even a premium voice costs only cents a month.

| Tier | Chinese voice | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Best | **ElevenLabs Eleven v4** (now #1 for Mandarin, about 1,301) | The same company as the English voice. Older notes said Inworld was #1; that was on 22 Sep, before v4 came out |
| Best (other choices) | Inworld TTS-2 (#3 for Mandarin, about 1,195), MiniMax Speech 2.8, Qwen-Audio | Strong Chinese |
| Cheap | Azure zh-CN Neural | 500,000 free characters a month; word boundaries |
| Free | Apple zh-CN Premium voice, or Kokoro v1.1-zh | Run on the iPad |

Simba 3.2 is **English only**: it rejects non-English voices. If you choose Simba, use simba-3.0 or another voice for Chinese.

### 3.5 Sleep-mode playback (all night, screen off)
1. **In sleep mode, play only files that are already saved.** Never depend on Wi-Fi at 3 a.m.
2. **Set up background audio:** use the `AVAudioSession` **`.playback`** category and the **"audio" background mode**. Add Now Playing information and lock-screen controls, and handle phone calls and alarms.
3. **Make audio ahead of time:**
   - Cloud voices: make the whole book when you import it, or chapter by chapter before you reach it. Gemini Batch is 50% cheaper and suits "make the book once".
   - Kokoro: make the next 1–3 hours while the app is open or while the iPad is charging (`BGProcessingTask`).
4. **Test with the screen locked.** iOS does not allow GPU work in the background, and Neural Engine work in the background is not guaranteed. Try it on a real iPad.
5. **Kokoro speed on Apple chips** (community numbers):
   - 16.9× real time on iPhone 16 Pro and 25× on an M4 Mac mini ([kokoro-coreml-ane](https://github.com/Jon-Schneider/kokoro-coreml-ane)).
   - 4–4.5× on the A17 Pro chip ([mattmireles](https://huggingface.co/mattmireles/kokoro-coreml)).
   - 3.3× with the MLX port on iPhone 13 Pro ([kokoro-ios](https://swiftpackageregistry.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios)).
   - Neural Engine speed needs an **A15 or M1 chip or newer**. Use CoreML on the Neural Engine.
   - Avoid int8 builds that run on the CPU through sherpa-onnx. On an old 2018 iPad Pro (A12X chip) they ran slower than real time, while the non-int8 Kokoro ran faster than real time ([VoicePing](https://voiceping.net/en/blog/research-offline-tts-eval/)).

### 3.6 Live explanations (active mode)
Each explanation is new text, and it must start quickly.
- Use the streaming version from the same company: v4 Turbo (about 150 ms), the Sonic WebSocket (40–90 ms), Inworld (about 90 ms) or Simba streaming. Or use Kokoro on the iPad.
- Cache the explanations too.

### 3.7 Limits to design around

| Service | Limit | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| ElevenLabs v4 | 10,000 characters per request (v3: 5,000) | Split the text by paragraph |
| Speechify | 2,000 characters per request (20,000 when streaming) | Split the text by paragraph |
| Gemini 3.8 TTS | 32k-token context; the free tier is small and its limits are not published | Split the text by chapter |
| MiniMax | 10,000 characters for a normal request; 1M for an async request | Use async for whole books |

## 4. Monthly cost examples

- **1 hour a day** = 30 hours ≈ 1.62M characters.
- **3 hours a day** = 90 hours ≈ 4.86M characters.
- These costs are for **new** book text only. Replays from the cache cost $0.
- Add 10–20% if the tutor's spoken explanations use the same voice (my estimate). Chinese meanings add only cents.

| Option | 1 h/day | 3 h/day | Per novel (~10 h) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ElevenLabs Eleven v4 | about $130 | **about $389** | about $43 |
| ElevenLabs Eleven v4 Turbo | about $65 | about $194 | about $22 |
| Cartesia Sonic 3.6 | about $60–81 | about $180–243 | about $20–27 |
| Inworld Realtime TTS-2 (pay as you go) | about $41 | about $122 | about $14 |
| Qwen-Audio TTS-Plus (3.0 price) | about $31–32 | about $92–97 | about $10 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, normal, until 31 Dec 2026 | about $24 | about $73 | about $8 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, normal, from 1 Jan 2027 | about $49 | about $146 | about $16 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, Batch, until 31 Dec 2026 | about $12 | about $36 | about $4 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, Batch, from 1 Jan 2027 | about $24 | about $73 | about $8 |
| Inworld TTS-2 Flash (pay as you go) | about $24 | about $73 | about $8 |
| Azure Neural (after the 500k free characters) | about $17–18 | about $65–70 | about $9 |
| **Speechify Simba 3.2** (Starter plan: $10 a month with 1.9M characters included, then $10 per 1M) | **$10** | **about $40** | about $3–5 |
| **Kokoro on the iPad / Apple voices** | **$0** | **$0** | **$0** |

Inworld's lower "Growth" prices need a **$1,500-a-month** plan. They are only for a company with many users, not for one learner.

**In plain words:** listening 3 hours every night costs about **$389 a month** with the best voice, about **$40** with the cheap voice, and **$0** with the free voice.

| **Kokoro-82M** | **Yes. Apache-2.0** ([model card](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M)) | Dream Read uses **espeak-ng** to turn words into sounds, and espeak-ng is **GPL-3.0**. That is a problem in a closed App Store app. Use the iOS port's own pronunciation step or another one with a permissive licence. The kokoro-ios Swift package is MIT |

## 6. Check these before you commit
1. Does the ElevenLabs `/with-timestamps` endpoint accept Eleven v4?
2. Do Simba 3.2's 8 voices include a British accent? Names like imogen, hugh and edmund *may* be British.
3. Does your chosen Kokoro CoreML port give the "duration" output?
4. Replace espeak-ng (GPL-3.0) with a pronunciation step that is safe for the App Store.
5. Does the Neural Engine keep working while the iPad is locked? If not, make audio ahead while the screen is on or the iPad is charging.
6. Does Azure HD support WordBoundary events? The docs disagree.
7. Check all prices again on the official pages. Gemini prices double on 1 Jan 2027.

## 7. What changed since docs/research/research-voice.md
- **New leaders:** Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo (28 Sep 2026) are #1 and #2 overall. They also lead 8 of the 9 language boards, including Mandarin. Sonic 3.6 now leads only Vietnamese (about 1,643).
- **Prices went down:**
  - ElevenLabs list prices are now $80 and $40 per 1M characters (they were $100 and $50).
  - Azure HD is $22 per 1M (it was $30 until March 2026).
- **A price goes up:** Gemini 3.8 TTS doubles on 1 Jan 2027.
- **Better timings:**
  - Inworld timestamps now work in all its languages.
  - Speechify's batch word marks now work on every model.
- **Gone or going:**
  - OpenAI's TTS models (removed on 6 Jan 2027).
  - PlayHT (bought by Meta; the shutdown dates are uncertain).
  - Edge TTS is unofficial, so it is not an option for the App Store.

# Part 4: What similar apps do, and what Dream Book should copy

*Facts as of 20 October 2026. I studied 16 apps using 54 web searches. "Checked" means it was confirmed on the official page or the App Store on 20 Oct 2026. "Unverified" means it was not confirmed. "(Secondary)" means it comes from a review site, not from the company.*

## The big picture in five points
1. **The top apps are native iOS apps.**
   - Speechify uses Swift (checked on its jobs page). So do Duolingo, Blinkist (it moved from Objective-C), Voice Dream and BookPlayer.
   - Kindle partly uses React Native (it is on the official React Native showcase).
   - I found no app that uses Flutter.
2. **Nobody does Dream Book's main idea.** No app reads a book aloud and *by itself* stops to explain hard words in context.
   - Speechify and Kindle answer only when you ask.
   - LingQ and Readlang explain only when you tap a word.
3. **Listening apps share the same basics:**
   - word-by-word highlighting
   - a sleep timer
   - playback with the screen locked
   - offline listening, often only for paying users
   - audio that is made once and then replayed for free (ElevenReader)
4. **Prices are close to each other:**
   - language readers: $48–120 a year
   - listening apps: $99–139 a year
   - sleep apps: $60–80 a year
5. **People hate:**
   - billing tricks (surprise yearly charges, Voice Dream's switch to a subscription)
   - robotic free voices
   - tiny free plans

## 2. How they are built, and what that means for Dream Book

**Dream Book must be a native app, not a web app in Safari.** The sleep features need things only native code can do.
- **Playback all night with the screen off:** `AVAudioSession` playback, Now Playing on the lock screen, and remote controls.
- **Listening to the microphone with the screen locked** (for voice commands):
  - This needs the "audio" background mode and a microphone-use message, and iOS shows a recording indicator ([Vivox docs](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/vivox-core/developer-guide/ios/ios-requirements)).
  - One developer found that speech stopped when the screen locked, even with background audio turned on ([Apple forum](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/849627)).
  - **Test this early on a real iPad.**
- **The free Kokoro voice on the iPad:**
  - A Swift CoreML package: about 80 MB (INT8), about 170 MB on first download, needs iOS 18+ ([soniqo](https://soniqo.audio/guides/kokoro)).
  - An MLX Swift port: about 3.3× faster than real time on iPhone 13 Pro, needs iOS 18+ ([kokoro-ios](https://swiftpackageregistry.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios)).
  - **Check whether these ports give the per-word "duration" output.** Dream Read needs it for the highlight.

**Three ways to build it (fastest first)**

| Way | What it means | Good | Not so good |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Capacitor shell** | Wrap the existing web app (`src/renderer` plus `src/web`) and add native Swift plugins for audio and sleep, the microphone and speech, and Kokoro | Fastest. Keeps almost all of the current screens and logic | Two worlds (web and Swift) to debug |
| **B. SwiftUI screens plus JavaScriptCore** | Native screens that run the existing TypeScript `src/core` inside JavaScriptCore | Keeps the ~650 tested core functions; feels native | More work |
| **C. Full Swift rewrite** | Everything in Swift | Best quality | The most work |

For a non-developer working with AI assistants, **A first, then B** is the realistic path. This is general advice, not a finding from the searches.

**Check your Mac first (UNVERIFIED).**
- The search limit stopped me before I could check this. From memory: the App Store now requires apps built with recent Xcode and SDK versions, and Xcode 26 needs macOS 15.6 or newer.
- If that is true, an Intel MacBook on macOS 13 cannot upload to the App Store. Then you would update macOS (if your MacBook model allows it) or use a cloud build service: Xcode Cloud, GitHub Actions macOS runners, Expo EAS or Codemagic.

**BookPlayer's code is GPL-3.0.** Read it to learn. Copying its code into your own app would bring the GPL-3.0 rules with it.

## 3. Voices: what the leaders use

**What each app uses**
- **Speechify and ElevenReader:** their **own** voice models, plus licensed celebrity voices.
- **Voice Dream and Readlang:** **Apple or browser voices** (free).
- **NaturalReader:** resells HD voices from other companies.
- **Apple Books:** its own AI voices.

**Current ranking** (AA Speech Arena, 20 Oct 2026, [leaderboard](https://artificialanalysis.ai/text-to-speech/leaderboard))
- **Top five:** Eleven v4 Turbo 1,332, Eleven v4 1,329, Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus 1,297, Sonic 3.6 1,291, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 1,280.
- **Further down:** Inworld Realtime TTS-2 is 7th (1,262) and Speechify Simba 3.2 is 10th (1,245).
- **Older notes:** a June 2026 list had Fun-Realtime-TTS, Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS and Realtime TTS-2 at the top. That list is **out of date**.

**For Dream Book** (full details are in the voices section):
- **Free default:** Kokoro on the iPad, with Apple Premium voices as backup.
- **Cheap HD cloud voice for Premium users:**
  - Speechify Simba 3.2 at about $0.32–0.54 per hour, with word timings.
  - Or Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS in Batch mode at about $0.41 per hour (about $0.81 from 1 Jan 2027). It needs an aligner.
  - An older note gave Inworld TTS-1.5 Mini at about $0.28 per hour, but that price **could not be confirmed**. Inworld's pricing page now shows TTS-2 Flash at $15 per 1M characters (about $0.81 per hour).
- **ElevenLabs only with the learner's own key:**
  - At $2.16–4.32 per hour (checked: $0.04–0.08 per 1,000 characters), 3 hours a day costs $194–389 a month.
  - That cannot fit inside a $15 subscription.
- **Save every sentence the app makes on the iPad**, so listening again costs nothing.

## 4. What to copy, avoid and do better

### Copy

| # | What | From | How in Dream Book |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pay for *making* audio; replays are free | ElevenReader | Save every sentence on the iPad. Keep the sleep timer free |
| 2 | A skip panel and a wide speed range; talking with the book | Speechify | Dream Read already has the skip panel and speeds |
| 3 | Spoiler-free AI; a "story so far" recap | Kindle (Ask this Book, Recaps) | Keep sending the ~200 words after the position for meaning, but tell the AI never to reveal what happens later. Add a morning "where was I" recap |
| 4 | One reading position everywhere | Whispersync | Share the position between reading and listening, and between Mac and iPad |
| 5 | A pronunciation dictionary; playback with the screen locked; word and line highlight | Voice Dream | Let the learner fix how character names are said |
| 6 | Word statuses, known-word milestones, spaced repetition | LingQ | Dream Read already has word statuses |
| 7 | A free plan with 10 AI explanations a day | Readlang | The AI explanation in context is the paid feature |
| 8 | Streak freezes and streak revival | Duolingo | A gentle streak, without guilt |
| 9 | A slow pace, a fade-out, no sudden sounds, no cliffhangers | Calm and sleep stories | In sleep mode: slower speed, longer pauses, quieter explanations. Test 120–140 words a minute (a weak source) |
| 10 | An "End of chapter" sleep-timer option | Audible | Add "after this explanation" as well |
| 11 | iOS 26 "Pause Media When Falling Asleep" on AirPods 4, AirPods Pro 2/3 and some Beats ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/2835295/ios-26-feature-that-turns-off-headphones-when-you-fall-asleep-isnt-limited-to-airpods.html), [iGeeksBlog](https://www.igeeksblog.com/airpods-auto-pause-when-you-fall-asleep/)). Sources disagree on whether it is on by default | Apple | Treat this pause as a "fell asleep here" signal |

### Avoid

| # | What | Who did it | Do this instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A surprise yearly charge after the trial, hard cancelling, charges after cancelling | Speechify | Remind the learner 2 days before the trial ends. Make cancelling one tap |
| 2 | Forcing a subscription on people who already paid | Voice Dream | If you ever change the pricing model, let old buyers keep what they paid for |
| 3 | Confusing plan names and many plan lengths | LingQ | Three plans; monthly or yearly only |
| 4 | A free plan that runs out in one lesson (20 saved words) | LingQ | A useful free plan that lasts |
| 5 | Robotic free voices | Free plans of Speechify and ElevenReader | Use Kokoro as the free voice |
| 6 | Playback that needs the cloud | – | Sleep mode plays only files already saved on the iPad |
| 7 | Guilt notifications ("Your streak is in danger!") | Duolingo, criticised by [WebdesignerDepot](https://webdesignerdepot.com/the-art-of-duolingo-notifications-the-subtle-manipulation-of-language-learners/) | Gentle reminders only |

### Do better (Dream Book's unique value)

1. **It explains words by itself while you listen.** Explanations match the learner's CEFR level and include phrases the AI finds. No competitor does this; the others only answer when you ask or tap.
2. **A tutor that knows you are asleep.**
   - Today, silence in the 5-second window means "explain". A sleeping learner would get about 20 explanations an hour that nobody hears.
   - Over 8 hours that is about 160 explanations a night: about $0.10 with Haiku 5.5, or about $1.90 with Sonnet 5.5.
   - Detect sleep by:
     - no reply in 2–3 windows in a row
     - the AirPods sleep pause
     - the timer ending
   - Then:
     - switch to "story only, slower, no pauses"
     - mark "fell asleep here"
     - stop the AI calls
3. **Chinese support for a Chinese speaker.** Two Chinese meanings spoken by a Chinese voice, and voice commands that understand a Chinese accent.
4. **A morning review.** For example: "Last night you heard 23 new words. Here are the 6 you asked about." Add a recap from where you fell asleep.
5. **Clear prices.** One free plan for ever, two paid plans, and no tricks.

## 5. iPad screen design to copy
- **Listening screen:**
  - Lines like song lyrics, with the current sentence large and the current word highlighted (as in ElevenReader, LingQ and Beelinguapp).
  - Landscape: the text on the left; the word card and the tutor's words on the right.
  - Portrait: the card slides up from the bottom.
  - Support Split View, Stage Manager and the existing keyboard shortcuts.
- **Night theme:** true black, a dimmer that goes very low, and no bright flash when the card appears.
- **A sleep timer behind a moon button** (as in Audible, Apple Books, ElevenReader and Voice Dream):
  - 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes
  - **End of chapter**
  - **After this explanation** (new)
  - a 30–60 second fade-out
  - an "Extend 15 min" button
- **Lock screen:**
  - Now Playing shows the book, chapter and cover.
  - While paused at a word, show the word and its Chinese meaning in the subtitle line.
  - Live Activities on iPad: UNVERIFIED (from memory).
- **Widgets:** "Continue last night" and "Words from last night".
- **CarPlay:** not needed on iPad. Add it later for iPhone.

### The plans

| Plan | Price | What is in it | Worst-case cost per user per month |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free (for ever)** | $0 | Unlimited listening with Kokoro and Apple voices; karaoke highlight; dictionary card with Chinese; sleep timer and basic sleep mode; voice commands on the iPad; **10 AI explanations a day** (Haiku 5.5). The learner's own API key unlocks unlimited AI and ElevenLabs voices | about $0.20 (300 explanations × $0.0006) |
| **Plus** | **$6.99 a month or $49.99 a year** | Unlimited AI tutor on Haiku 5.5 (fair use about 300 a day); deeper "I don't know" answers; morning review and recap; smart sleep detection; making audio ahead for offline use; Mac and iPad sync | about $1–2 for AI, plus Apple's 15% ($1.05) |
| **Premium** | **$14.99 a month or $119.99 a year** | Everything in Plus; **Sonnet 5.5 tutor** in active mode (fair use about 25 active hours a month, about $5–7); **HD cloud voice for about 10 hours of new audio a month** (Simba 3.2 at $0.32–0.54 an hour, about $3–5.40). Saved audio replays for free | about $8–12.40, plus Apple's 15% ($2.25) = about **$10.50–14.70** at the limits. Most users will use far less |

**Notes on the plans**
- **Why 10 HD hours, not 20:** the older plan used an Inworld price of $0.28 an hour that could not be confirmed. With confirmed prices, 20 hours plus a Sonnet tutor could cost more than $14.99.
- **Plus price:** $6.99 is a friendly launch price, but it is below the $8 monthly median, so $7.99 would also be normal.
- **Trial:** about 3 weeks, because 17–32-day trials convert best. Send a reminder 2 days before it ends, and make cancelling one tap.
- **ElevenLabs voices:** only with the learner's own key.
- **No lifetime plan that includes cloud AI,** because the AI costs never stop. A lifetime plan for the offline-only features is optional.

## 7. The 10 most important features for a learner who listens while falling asleep

| # | Feature | Why it matters | Learn from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Playback that never stops all night** with the screen locked; handles calls and alarms | If audio stops at 1 a.m., the night is lost | Voice Dream, Audible, BookPlayer code |
| 2 | **A calm, natural voice that works offline**: Kokoro on the iPad, slower in sleep mode, longer pauses between sentences | No Wi-Fi problems; costs $0 | Calm (pacing), ElevenReader (voices) |
| 3 | **A smart sleep timer**: minutes, end of chapter, or after this explanation; gentle fade-out; extend | Falling asleep gently | Audible, ElevenReader |
| 4 | **Sleep detection**: no reply in the 5-second windows, the AirPods sleep pause, or the timer. Then stop explanations and AI calls and play the story only, or stop | Avoids about 20 unheard explanations an hour and wasted AI cost | iOS 26 AirPods feature; new idea |
| 5 | **A "fell asleep here" bookmark and a morning recap** of the story, with a jump back | You find your place again easily | Kindle Recaps / Story So Far |
| 6 | **Hands-free voice commands with the screen off**: I know, I don't know, go on, again, slower, stop. They must understand a Chinese accent | No need to touch the iPad in bed | New (test microphone use with the screen locked early) |
| 7 | **Short spoken explanations in context, then two Chinese meanings in a Chinese voice**, quieter and shorter as you get sleepy | Dream Book's unique feature | Nobody does it automatically |
| 8 | **A karaoke "lyrics" view with word highlight and a true-black night theme**, for the minutes before sleep | Reading and listening together | ElevenReader, LingQ, Beelinguapp |
| 9 | **A morning review with spaced repetition and a gentle streak with freezes**: words from last night, no guilt | Turns night listening into learning | LingQ, Duolingo (freezes, not guilt) |
| 10 | **Easy import and preparation**: EPUB, PDF and text from Files or the Share sheet; a skip panel; next chapters made ahead on Wi-Fi; Mac and iPad position sync | Everything is ready before bedtime | Speechify, Whispersync |
