```ts
import type { Book, Position, CefrLevel } from '@core/model';
import type { Settings, VocabState, LibraryItem, WordStatus, MarkedRange, UsageRecord, TtsEngineId } from './settings';
import type { HintMap, PhraseMap } from '@core/ai/hints';

export type { HintMap, HintPair, PhraseHit, PhraseMap } from '@core/ai/hints';

/** Progress of the background chapter-hints job (src/main/hints.ts), broadcast as 'hints:progress'. */
export interface HintsProgress {
  bookId: string;
  chapter: number;
  state: 'queued' | 'running' | 'done' | 'error';
  /** learner-readable message when state is 'error' */
  error?: string;
  code?: AiErrorCode;
}

export interface DictData { w: Record<string, DictRaw>; f: Record<string, string> }
export interface DictRaw { i: string; t: string; g: string; f: number; b: number; c: number; o: number; l: string; s: string }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * My Vocabulary (src/main/vocabulary.ts): every word the learner had explained, with where it was met.
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

export type VocabEntryStatus = 'learning' | 'known';

export interface VocabEntry {
  /** dictionary lemma; the key of the entry and of VocabState.words */
  lemma: string;
  /** the word as it appeared in the text the first time */
  word: string;
  /** the sentence it was first met in (kept on later explanations) */
  sentence: string;
  /** the latest explanation */
  explanation: string;
  /** Chinese meaning (dictionary gloss or the explanation's Chinese line) */
  chinese: string;
  bookId: string;
  bookTitle: string;
  /** chapter title (or number) where the word was first met */
  chapter: string;
  position: Position | null;
  createdAt: string;
  lastSeenAt: string;
  timesExplained: number;
  status: VocabEntryStatus;
  level?: CefrLevel;
  /** how many times the learner said "I don't know" about this word */
  again: number;
}

/** What the reader sends when a word was explained; counters and dates are filled in by the store. */
export interface VocabEntryInput {
  lemma: string;
  word: string;
  sentence: string;
  explanation: string;
  chinese?: string;
  bookId: string;
  bookTitle: string;
  chapter: string;
  position?: Position | null;
  level?: CefrLevel;
  /** true when this explanation was an "I don't know" (explain again) */
  again?: boolean;
}

export interface LevelProgress {
  level: CefrLevel;
  /** words of this level (CEFR-tagged dictionary words) marked known */
  known: number;
  learning: number;
  /** CEFR-tagged dictionary words of this level that are neither known nor learning (ignored words are left out) */
  unknown: number;
  /** CEFR-tagged dictionary words at this level */
  total: number;
}

export interface VocabProgress {
  levels: LevelProgress[];
  totals: {
    /** all words marked known (any level, tagged or not) */
    known: number;
    learning: number;
    unknown: number;
    /** entries in My Vocabulary */
    entries: number;
  };
  /** entries added to My Vocabulary in the last 7 days */
  learnedThisWeek: number;
  /** days in a row (ending today or yesterday) with at least one word met or explained */
  streakDays: number;
  /** YYYY-MM-DD of the last day with activity, null when there is none */
  lastActiveDay: string | null;
}

/** A dictionary word the learner does not know yet, for the Progress page. */
export interface UnknownWord { word: string; zh: string; ipa: string; level: CefrLevel; frq: number }

export type ExplainKind = 'word' | 'phrase' | 'sentence' | 'passage' | 'question';

export interface ExplainRequest {
  kind: ExplainKind;
  /** the word, phrase, sentence or passage to explain */
  target: string;
  /** the sentence containing the target (for passage: the whole passage) */
  sentence: string;
  before: string;
  after: string;
  book: { title: string; chapter: string };
  dict?: { ipa?: string; zh?: string; level?: string } | null;
  question?: string;
  /** exact place being read, so the AI can follow the timeline */
  position?: Position;
  /** explanation style to use; undefined = the active style in settings */
  styleId?: string;
  /** the learner heard an explanation and said "I don't know": explain again, deeper */
  again?: boolean;
  /** previous exchanges in this chapter, oldest first */
  history: { role: 'user' | 'assistant'; text: string }[];
}

export interface KokoroStatus {
  state: 'missing' | 'downloading' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error';
  variant: string;
  modelDir: string;
  downloadBytes: number;
  progress: { file: string; received: number; total: number; percent: number } | null;
  error: string | null;
  queued: number;
  version: string;
}

/** Local speech-to-text engine status (mirrors src/main/stt/engine.ts EngineStatus), broadcast as 'stt:progress'. */
export interface SttStatus {
  state: 'missing' | 'downloading' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error';
  variant: 'moonshine-base' | 'moonshine-tiny' | 'parakeet-v3';
  modelDir: string;
  /** bytes still to download for the configured model (0 when installed) */
  downloadBytes: number;
  progress: { phase: 'download' | 'extract' | 'done'; file: string; received: number; total: number; overallReceived: number; overallTotal: number } | null;
  error: string | null;
  sessions: number;
  version: string;
  confidence: boolean;
}

/** One event of the speech-to-text engine ('stt:event'); same shape as SttEngineEvent in src/core/voice/session.ts. */
export type SttEvent =
  | { type: 'partial' | 'final'; text: string; confidence?: number; segmentId: string; sessionId: string }
  | { type: 'speechStart' | 'speechEnd'; sessionId: string; segmentId: string }
  | { type: 'error'; sessionId: string; message: string };

export type AiErrorCode = 'no_key' | 'auth' | 'rate_limit' | 'spend_limit' | 'model' | 'network' | 'timeout' | 'budget' | 'cancelled' | 'other';

export type AiEvent =
  | { type: 'delta'; streamId: string; text: string }
  | { type: 'done'; streamId: string; text: string; usage: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; cachedTokens: number; usd: number; dailyUsd: number; monthlyUsd: number; model: string } }
  | { type: 'error'; streamId: string; message: string; code?: AiErrorCode };

/**
 * API keys the app can store, one per service. Values are plain key strings, except:
 *  - azure: a JSON string {"key": "...", "region": "uksouth"}; a plain key is also accepted and then
 *    the region defaults to "uksouth" (see src/main/secrets.ts getAzureCredentials).
 *  - google: a Google Cloud API key (not a service-account JSON) with the Text-to-Speech API enabled.
 */
export type SecretName = 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'elevenlabs' | 'azure' | 'google';
export const SECRET_NAMES: readonly SecretName[] = ['anthropic', 'openai', 'elevenlabs', 'azure', 'google'];
export const SECRET_LABELS: Record<SecretName, string> = { anthropic: 'Anthropic', openai: 'OpenAI', elevenlabs: 'ElevenLabs', azure: 'Azure Speech', google: 'Google Cloud' };

export interface SecretStatus {
  /** a record for this key exists in secrets.json */
  saved: boolean;
  /** the record decrypts with the app's key file (false = saved but unreadable) */
  verified: boolean;
  /** the key could not be recovered at startup (old Keychain record after a re-sign); shown to the user once */
  lostAtStartup: boolean;
}
export type SecretStatusMap = Record<SecretName, SecretStatus>;

/** Result of the "Test" button for any provider key. */
export interface ProviderTestResult { ok: boolean; message: string; detail?: string }

export interface TtsVoiceInfo { id: string; name: string; lang: string; gender?: string; quality?: string; note?: string }

export interface WordTiming { start: number; end: number; charIndex: number; charLength: number }

export interface CloudTtsResult { audio: ArrayBuffer; mime: string; timings: WordTiming[] | null; durationSec: number | null }

export interface Diagnostics {
  platform: string; arch: string; electron: string; chrome: string; node: string; appVersion: string;
  userData: string; secretsFile: string; dictWords: number; secrets: SecretStatusMap;
}

/** Contract between renderer and main; implemented in src/preload/index.ts and src/main/ipc.ts. */
export interface ReadAlongApi {
  // library
  importBookDialog(): Promise<Book | null>;
  importFile(path: string): Promise<Book>;
  /** absolute path of a File dropped on the window (Electron's webUtils) */
  pathForFile(file: File): string;
  importText(title: string, text: string): Promise<Book>;
  listLibrary(): Promise<LibraryItem[]>;
  loadBook(id: string): Promise<Book | null>;
  removeBook(id: string): Promise<void>;
  saveProgress(id: string, position: Position, percent: number): Promise<void>;
  // dictionary
  loadDictionary(): Promise<DictData>;
  // vocabulary
  getVocab(): Promise<VocabState>;
  setWordStatus(lemma: string, status: WordStatus | null): Promise<void>;
  setMarkedRanges(bookId: string, ranges: MarkedRange[]): Promise<void>;
  // My Vocabulary (the explained-words list; keeps VocabState.words in sync)
  vocabEntries(): Promise<VocabEntry[]>;
  /** adds a word or merges into its entry: one more explanation, first sentence kept, latest explanation kept */
  vocabUpsertEntry(entry: VocabEntryInput): Promise<VocabEntry>;
  vocabSetEntryStatus(lemma: string, status: VocabEntryStatus): Promise<void>;
  vocabDeleteEntry(lemma: string): Promise<void>;
  /** writes ~/Documents/Dream Read/my-vocabulary.csv now, reveals it in Finder and resolves with the path */
  vocabExportCsv(): Promise<string>;
  /** where the CSV is written (it is also rewritten automatically after every change) */
  vocabCsvPath(): Promise<string>;
  vocabProgress(): Promise<VocabProgress>;
  /** dictionary words of that CEFR level the learner has not marked yet, most frequent first */
  vocabUnknownAtLevel(level: CefrLevel): Promise<UnknownWord[]>;
  // settings & secrets
  getSettings(): Promise<Settings>;
  setSettings(patch: Partial<Settings>): Promise<Settings>;
  /** Saves (or removes, when empty) a key; resolves with a warning when the key does not look right. Throws if the key cannot be read back. */
  setSecret(name: SecretName, value: string): Promise<{ warning: string | null }>;
  hasSecret(name: SecretName): Promise<boolean>;
  secretStatus(): Promise<SecretStatusMap>;
  /** clears the "could not be recovered" notices for this session */
  dismissLostKeys(): Promise<void>;
  // AI
  aiExplain(req: ExplainRequest): Promise<{ streamId: string }>;
  aiCancel(streamId: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Tests the saved key of any provider (AI or voice) with a tiny request; the message is meant for the user. */
  aiTest(provider: SecretName): Promise<ProviderTestResult>;
  onAiEvent(cb: (ev: AiEvent) => void): () => void;
  getUsage(): Promise<UsageRecord[]>;
  // chapter hints (Chinese meaning under hard words, chosen by the AI for the chapter; see src/main/hints.ts)
  /** cached hints of a chapter (lemma -> [meaning here, other meaning]) or null when the job has not run yet */
  hintsGet(bookId: string, chapter: number): Promise<HintMap | null>;
  /**
   * cached phrases of a chapter found by the same job: sentenceKey ("c.p.s") -> PhraseHit[] (token span with
   * INCLUSIVE end, lemma, the model's CEFR level, Chinese meaning), or null when the job has not run yet.
   * Refetch on the 'done' hints:progress event. Pass map[sentenceKey] to annotateSentence(…, hits).
   */
  hintsPhrases(bookId: string, chapter: number): Promise<PhraseMap | null>;
  /** queues the chapter (no-op when cached or already queued); progress arrives through onHintsProgress */
  hintsRequest(bookId: string, chapter: number): Promise<void>;
  /** forgets the cached hints of a book (next request recomputes them) */
  hintsClear(bookId: string): Promise<void>;
  onHintsProgress(cb: (ev: HintsProgress) => void): () => void;
  // cloud TTS (engines that synthesize in the main process)
  ttsListVoices(engine: TtsEngineId): Promise<TtsVoiceInfo[]>;
  ttsSynthesize(engine: TtsEngineId, text: string, voiceId: string, rate: number): Promise<CloudTtsResult>;
  // Kokoro (free local voice): model download and prefetch
  kokoroStatus(): Promise<KokoroStatus>;
  kokoroDownload(): Promise<KokoroStatus>;
  kokoroCancelDownload(): Promise<void>;
  kokoroPrepare(items: { text: string; voice?: string; speed?: number }[]): Promise<void>;
  onKokoroProgress(cb: (s: KokoroStatus) => void): () => void;
  // local speech-to-text (docs/VOICE.md); absent where there is no STT engine (the web build)
  sttStatus?(): Promise<SttStatus>;
  /** downloads the configured model; resolves when it is on disk (progress via onSttProgress) */
  sttDownload?(): Promise<SttStatus>;
  sttCancelDownload?(): Promise<void>;
  /** opens a mic session (loads the model first) */
  sttStart?(sessionId: string, opts?: { sampleRate?: number }): Promise<SttStatus>;
  /** Int16 mono PCM at the session rate (16 kHz), 20–40 ms per call */
  sttPush?(sessionId: string, pcm: ArrayBuffer): Promise<void>;
  /** closes the session; resolves after its last final transcript was sent */
  sttStop?(sessionId: string): Promise<void>;
  onSttEvent?(cb: (ev: SttEvent) => void): () => void;
  onSttProgress?(cb: (s: SttStatus) => void): () => void;
  // misc
  getDiagnostics(): Promise<Diagnostics>;
  openExternal(url: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Writes a text file into ~/Documents/Dream Read and reveals it in Finder; resolves with the full path. */
  exportText(fileName: string, contents: string): Promise<string>;
  onMenu(cb: (action: string) => void): () => void;
}

declare global {
  interface Window { readalong: ReadAlongApi }
}

import type { CefrLevel, Position } from '@core/model';

export type AiProviderId = 'anthropic' | 'openai';
export type TtsEngineId = 'webspeech' | 'edge' | 'openai' | 'elevenlabs' | 'kokoro' | 'azure' | 'google';
/** night (warm dark, default), sepia, light, grey; 'system' follows macOS (night or light). The old 'dark' is read as 'night'. */
export type ThemeId = 'night' | 'sepia' | 'light' | 'grey' | 'system';
/** Themes that render dark; the others use the light highlight palette. */

export type LayoutId = 'page' | 'scroll';

export interface HighlightColors {
  /** word above the learner's level (auto-explain candidate) */
  unknown: string;
  /** word the learner tapped / had explained */
  learning: string;
  /** sentence currently being read */
  sentence: string;
  /** word currently being spoken */
  word: string;
  /** phrase or sentence the learner marked for explanation */
  marked: string;
}

export interface Settings {
  version: 1;
  onboarded: boolean;
  learnerLevel: CefrLevel;
  nativeLanguage: 'zh';
  ai: {
    provider: AiProviderId;

     */

    speakChinese: boolean;

    activeStyle: StyleId;

    styles: Partial<Record<StyleId, StyleOverride>>;
    /** shared rules sent with every style (system prompt); editable, reset to DEFAULT_CONTEXT_RULES */
    contextRules: string;
    contextWordsBefore: number;
    contextWordsAfter: number;
    /** Picture style: also generate an image of the scene (OpenAI key, costs money) */
    /** @deprecated no images are made; the tutor paints the scene with words (kept so old settings files load) */
    generateScenePicture: boolean;
  };
  voice: {
    engine: TtsEngineId;

    voiceId: string;
    /** engine + voice for explanations; null = same as reading */
    explainEngine: TtsEngineId | null;

  listen: {

    /** a word explained once is not explained again within this many words of text (0 = every time) */

    sentenceRepeatsAfterWord: number; // read the sentence N times after a word explanation
    sentenceRepeatsForPhrase: number; // read the sentence N times (once before, once after by default = 2)
    lastSecondsWindow: 20 | 30 | 40 | 60;
    /** in listening mode, a single tap on a highlighted word cancels it instead of opening the popup */
    tapHighlightCancels: boolean;
    /** listening mode: silence after an explanation before the book continues */

    /**
     * Listening mode, at a hard word or phrase: how long the commands window stays open (mic listening for

     */
    commandWindowMs: number;

  appearance: {
    theme: ThemeId;

    /** book text size */

    /** whole-UI scale, 0.9 .. 1.3 */

    lineHeight: number;
    /** maximum line length of the reading column, in characters (ch) */
    maxLineChars: number;
    /** maximum line length of the listening screen (subtitles), in characters (ch); wider, with comfortable side margins */
    listenMaxLineChars: number;
    marginPx: number;
    /** "tap anything to see how it works" tooltips on the main buttons */
    showTips: boolean;
    bandEnabled: boolean;
    bandHeightPct: number; // 20..45
    highlightsDark: HighlightColors;
    highlightsLight: HighlightColors;
    underlineOnly: boolean;
    /** Word Wise-style hints: a small Chinese meaning under words above the learner's level */
    showHints: boolean;
    /** slide animation when a page turns in Reading mode */

  };
  shortcuts: Record<string, string>;
  /** the screen the learner used last (new books open in it) */

  /** bookId -> the screen the learner used last for that book */
  bookModes: Record<string, ReadMode>;
  /** vocabulary level test (src/core/level): the adaptive model, the last result and when it was taken */

  /** talking with the tutor by voice (src/renderer/voice) */

  /** Speechify-style skipping while reading aloud (src/core/import/skip.ts): what the voice leaves out */

}

export type SttModelId = 'moonshine-base' | 'moonshine-tiny' | 'parakeet-v3';

  /** the voice line opens by itself with the book (the mic listens all the time) */

    prevPage: 'PageUp', nextPage: 'PageDown', replaySentence: 'KeyR', explain: 'KeyE', explainLast: 'Shift+KeyE', markKnown: 'KeyK', markLearning: 'Shift+KeyL',
    ignore: 'KeyX', toggleListen: 'KeyQ', toggleBand: 'KeyB', sayWord: 'KeyS', speedUp: 'Equal', speedDown: 'Minus', speedReset: 'Digit0',
    nextHard: 'Tab', prevHard: 'Shift+Tab', closePopup: 'Escape', markPhrase: 'KeyH',
    switchMode: 'KeyL', dontKnow: 'KeyD', help: 'Shift+Slash', toggleHints: 'KeyW', goTo: 'KeyG',
  },
  lastMode: 'reading',
  bookModes: {},
  level: { model: null, lastResult: null, testedAt: null },
  voiceChat: { alwaysOn: false, model: 'moonshine-base', pushToTalkKey: 'KeyM', modelOffered: false },
  skip: { ...DEFAULT_SKIP },
};

/**
 * Brings a stored settings object up to date in place and returns it: the v1 theme 'dark' became 'night';
 * shared AI rules still equal to an earlier default get the current default (no filler, badly recognised
 * speech); the old 7 s pause after an explanation became the 5 s window.
 * Safe to call on partial objects (patches) and on the defaults.
 */
export function migrateSettings<T extends { appearance?: { theme?: string } }>(s: T): T {
  const theme = s?.appearance?.theme as string | undefined;
  if (theme === 'dark') s.appearance!.theme = 'night';
  const ai = (s as { ai?: { contextRules?: unknown } } | null)?.ai;
  if (ai && typeof ai.contextRules === 'string' && LEGACY_CONTEXT_RULES.some((old) => old.trim() === (ai.contextRules as string).trim())) ai.contextRules = DEFAULT_CONTEXT_RULES;
  const listen = (s as { listen?: { pauseAfterExplainMs?: unknown } } | null)?.listen;
  if (listen && listen.pauseAfterExplainMs === 7000) listen.pauseAfterExplainMs = 5000;
  return s;
}

export function isDarkTheme(theme: ThemeId): boolean { return DARK_THEMES.includes(theme); }

export type WordStatus = 'known' | 'learning' | 'ignored';

export interface VocabState {
  /** lemma -> status */
  words: Record<string, WordStatus>;
  /** bookId -> array of "chapter.paragraph.sentence:start-end" ranges the learner marked for explanation */
  marked: Record<string, MarkedRange[]>;
}

export interface MarkedRange { chapter: number; paragraph: number; sentence: number; start: number; end: number; text: string }

export interface LibraryItem {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  author?: string;
  kind: 'epub' | 'pdf' | 'text';
  addedAt: string;
  lastOpenedAt: string;
  position: Position | null;
  percent: number;
  words: number;
  /** the screen the learner used last for this book (filled in from settings.bookModes by the renderer) */
  mode?: ReadMode;
}

export interface UsageRecord { date: string; provider: AiProviderId; model: string; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; cachedTokens: number; usd: number }

import type { AiProviderId } from './settings';

/**
 * Explanation styles: how the AI teaches a word or a sentence. Every style is a pair of plain-text prompt
 * templates (word, sentence) plus the shape of the spoken script around the AI's answer. All text is
 * editable by the learner in Settings; DEFAULT_STYLES is the "reset to default" source.
 *
 * Template placeholders: {{word}} {{sentence}} {{before}} {{after}} {{title}} {{chapter}} {{level}} {{dict}}
 * {{native}} (the learner's first language, e.g. Chinese). Unknown placeholders are left as is.
 *
 * The reply must be plain prose for a voice. A quiz-style prompt may put the token [PAUSE] on its own line:
 * the app stops speaking there, waits for the learner (or the listening-mode pause), then speaks the rest.
 */
export type BuiltinStyleId = 'custom' | 'teacher' | 'picture' | 'chunks' | 'wordparts' | 'story' | 'quiz' | 'philosopher' | 'poetry' | 'lyrics';
/** built-in ids, or a learner-created style id ("my-<something>") */
export type StyleId = BuiltinStyleId | (string & {});

export type Personality = 'warm' | 'strict' | 'peer';
export type Length = 'short' | 'normal' | 'long';
export type AnswerType = 'explain' | 'quiz' | 'example';

/** The three knobs every style exposes; each value appends one sentence to the prompt (length, then personality, then answer type). */
export const KNOBS: { personality: Record<Personality, { label: string; text: string }>; length: Record<Length, { label: string; text: string }>; answerType: Record<AnswerType, { label: string; text: string }> } = {
  personality: {
    warm: { label: 'Warm teacher', text: 'Speak like a warm, encouraging teacher who is glad the learner asked, use "you" and "we", and praise one thing the learner already understands before you go on.' },
    strict: { label: 'Strict coach', text: 'Speak like a strict but fair coach who respects the learner\'s time: go straight to the point, no praise and no small talk, and end by telling the learner exactly one thing to remember.' },
    peer: { label: 'Friendly peer', text: 'Speak like a friendly classmate reading the same book, in a relaxed everyday voice, sharing what you noticed as if you were sitting next to the learner; it is fine to say "I think" or "to me".' },
  },
  length: {
    short: { label: 'Short (about 30 s)', text: 'Keep the whole answer to about fifty words, three or four short sentences, giving only the meaning in this context and one reason it matters here.' },
    normal: { label: 'Normal (about 1 min)', text: 'Keep the whole answer to about one hundred and thirty words, roughly a minute of speaking, covering the meaning, the role in this context and one example.' },
    long: { label: 'Long (up to 2 min)', text: 'You may use up to about two hundred and fifty words, up to two minutes of speaking, so take the learner through the meaning, the context, the sound or structure, one example and one nearby line that uses the same idea, but still stay only on what is in the text.' },
  },
  answerType: {
    explain: { label: 'Explain', text: 'Only explain; do not ask the learner any questions and do not add exercises.' },
    quiz: { label: 'Explain + quiz', text: 'After the explanation, ask the learner one short spoken question that checks the meaning in this exact context, then write the token [PAUSE] alone on its own line, and after it give the answer in one sentence.' },
    example: { label: 'Explain + example', text: 'After the explanation, give one new easy sentence of your own that uses the word or the same pattern in an everyday situation the learner could meet, say clearly that it is your example and not from the book, and if it is slang or a technical sense, show the safe everyday version too.' },
  },
};

export interface ScriptShape {
  /** say the word N times before the AI explanation */
  wordBefore: number;
  /** say the word N times after the AI explanation */
  wordAfter: number;
  /** read the sentence N times after a word explanation */
  sentenceAfterWord: number;
  /** read the sentence N times before / after a sentence explanation */
  sentenceBefore: number;
  sentenceAfter: number;
}

export interface ExplanationStyle {
  id: StyleId;
  name: string;
  /** the learner's own style (copied or new); built-ins are false */
  userMade?: boolean;
  /** deleted by the learner (built-ins are hidden, not removed) */
  hidden?: boolean;
  personality: Personality;
  length: Length;
  answerType: AnswerType;
  /** one line for the style picker */
  description: string;
  /** the research the style is built on, shown under the description */
  basis: string;
  wordPrompt: string;
  sentencePrompt: string;
  shape: ScriptShape;
  /** null = use the global provider/model */
  provider: AiProviderId | null;
  model: string | null;
  /** rough output budget: the AI is told how long to talk and max_tokens follows it */
  maxTokens: number;
}

/** The per-style fields a learner may override; merged over DEFAULT_STYLES by id. */
export type StyleOverride = Partial<Pick<ExplanationStyle, 'name' | 'description' | 'basis' | 'wordPrompt' | 'sentencePrompt' | 'shape' | 'provider' | 'model' | 'maxTokens' | 'personality' | 'length' | 'answerType' | 'hidden' | 'userMade'>>;

export const PLACEHOLDERS = ['word', 'sentence', 'before', 'after', 'title', 'chapter', 'level', 'dict', 'native'] as const;

/** The shared rules as they were before 19 Oct (no filler / speech rules); kept so settings still equal to it are upgraded. */
const CONTEXT_RULES_V1 = `You are a warm, patient English teacher inside a reading app. The learner's first language is {{native}} and their English is about CEFR level {{level}}.

Before you explain anything, read the whole passage you are given: the book title, the chapter, the text before, the sentence itself and the text after. Understand the story at this moment: who is there, what just happened, what each person wants and feels, and the meaning underneath the words. Explain the word or sentence as it is used in this exact moment of this story, never only a general dictionary meaning. If the word has other meanings, you may mention the most common one briefly, but the meaning in this story comes first and gets the most time.

When you describe the scene, paint it in the learner's mind with words so they can imagine being there: who is in the room, what they see, hear and feel. Never offer or mention pictures or images to look at; the picture is in their imagination. Use only what the book says or clearly implies. Never invent events, names, dialogue or details that are not in the book, and never quote text that is not in the passage you were given.

Your words will be spoken aloud by a voice, so write for the ear. Use easy, natural English with short sentences and common words. Plain text only: no headings, no labels, no numbers or bullet points, no markdown, no asterisks, no emojis, no phonetic symbols. Do not announce what you are about to do and do not name your steps; simply teach, in a smooth flow, as if talking to one person. No greeting and no closing line.

Do not translate the whole sentence into {{native}} unless the style asks for one easy translation. Use {{native}} only where the style asks for it.

First look at the title, the chapter and the text around the passage, and quietly decide what kind of text this is: a novel or story, a poem, a song, philosophy, history, science such as physics or maths, business or economics, a religious text, a public speech, sport or training, writing about art or music, or news. Let that decide how you explain. In a novel the hard words are often feelings, gestures, dialect and what a character really means, so explain the character's intention and the mood. In a poem or song the word matters for its sound and picture as much as its meaning, and the speaker is not the writer. In philosophy, science, maths, business, law or religion an ordinary word often has a special technical sense in this author's or this field's usage, and that special sense is the one that matters, so say it and name the everyday sense only to keep them apart. In history, news or a speech the hard part is usually who the people are, when and where this happens, and what the writer is trying to persuade the listener of, so explain the situation and the stance. In sport, training and practical texts the meaning is usually an action or an instruction, so explain what the reader is being told to do. Give at most one sentence of background, only when the passage cannot be understood without it and only when you are certain of it; never invent names, dates, numbers, events or quotations, and if you are not sure, say so. Match your tone to the text, lighter for stories and songs, calmer and more exact for philosophy, science and law, respectful for religious texts, but always easy spoken English about this exact passage, never a general lecture.`;

/** Added 19 Oct (docs/RULES.md): no filler, and the learner's spoken words may be badly recognised. */
const CONTEXT_RULES_NO_FILLER = `Never use filler. Never say things like "we already know this", "the Chinese translation is", "let me explain", "great question", "as I said" or "now". Start teaching at once with the first real point and go step by step.

Sometimes you are given what the learner just said aloud, written down by speech recognition. That transcript may be badly recognised, especially their pronunciation of English words. Never ask them to repeat it and never comment on their pronunciation; work out what they most probably meant from the book context and answer it inside your explanation.`;

/** Shared rules sent with every style (system prompt). Editable, with reset. */
export const DEFAULT_CONTEXT_RULES = `${CONTEXT_RULES_V1}\n\n${CONTEXT_RULES_NO_FILLER}`;

/** Earlier defaults of the shared rules: a stored copy equal to one of these is replaced by DEFAULT_CONTEXT_RULES. */
export const LEGACY_CONTEXT_RULES: readonly string[] = [CONTEXT_RULES_V1];

    wordPrompt: STORY_WORD, sentencePrompt: STORY_SENTENCE, shape: DEFAULT_SHAPE, provider: null, model: null, maxTokens: 900, personality: 'warm', length: 'normal', answerType: 'explain',
  },
  {
    id: 'quiz', name: 'Quiz Style', description: 'A short meaning, one quick question for you, then the answer.',
    basis: 'Retrieval practice and spaced repetition; the Involvement Load Hypothesis (Laufer and Hulstijn).',
    wordPrompt: QUIZ_WORD, sentencePrompt: QUIZ_SENTENCE, shape: DEFAULT_SHAPE, provider: null, model: null, maxTokens: 800, personality: 'warm', length: 'normal', answerType: 'explain',
  },
  {
    id: 'philosopher', name: 'Philosopher Style', description: 'Everyday sense vs the author\'s special sense, and the sentence\'s job in the argument.',
    basis: 'Adler, How to Read a Book (analytical reading: come to terms, find the propositions and arguments); the principle of charity; "How to Read a Philosophy Paper" guides.',
    wordPrompt: PHILOSOPHER_WORD, sentencePrompt: PHILOSOPHER_SENTENCE, shape: DEFAULT_SHAPE, provider: null, model: null, maxTokens: 1000, personality: 'warm', length: 'normal', answerType: 'explain',
  },
  {
    id: 'poetry', name: 'Poetry Style', description: 'Picture, sound and feeling: literal meaning first, then the figurative one.',
    basis: 'Edward Hirsch, How to Read a Poem; Poetry Foundation close-reading guides; TPCASTT (literal paraphrase before figurative, shifts, tone).',
    wordPrompt: POETRY_WORD, sentencePrompt: POETRY_SENTENCE, shape: DEFAULT_SHAPE, provider: null, model: null, maxTokens: 1000, personality: 'warm', length: 'normal', answerType: 'explain',
  },
  {
    id: 'lyrics', name: 'Lyrics Style', description: 'Slang and song grammar made safe, the singer\'s situation, wordplay, rhyme and hook.',
    basis: 'Genius-style annotation (explain and expand, add context); ESL research on songs: repetition, informal register, idioms.',
    wordPrompt: LYRICS_WORD, sentencePrompt: LYRICS_SENTENCE, shape: DEFAULT_SHAPE, provider: null, model: null, maxTokens: 1000, personality: 'peer', length: 'normal', answerType: 'explain',
  },
];

export const PAUSE_TOKEN = '[PAUSE]';

export function defaultStyle(id: StyleId): ExplanationStyle {
  return DEFAULT_STYLES.find((s) => s.id === id) ?? DEFAULT_STYLES[0];
}

/**
 * Merges learner overrides over the defaults (built-ins always exist, so new default styles appear for everyone);
 * learner-made styles (userMade, ids like "my-poetry-2") are appended, based on the custom style's defaults.
 * Hidden styles are kept in the list (the picker filters them) so "restore" is possible.
 */
export function resolveStyles(overrides: Partial<Record<StyleId, StyleOverride>> | undefined): ExplanationStyle[] {
  const merge = (d: ExplanationStyle, o: StyleOverride | undefined): ExplanationStyle => (o ? { ...d, ...o, shape: { ...d.shape, ...(o.shape ?? {}) } } : d);
  const builtins = DEFAULT_STYLES.map((d) => merge(d, overrides?.[d.id]));
  const made = Object.entries(overrides ?? {})
    .filter(([id, o]) => o && o.userMade && !DEFAULT_STYLES.some((d) => d.id === id))
    .map(([id, o]) => merge({ ...DEFAULT_STYLES[0], id, name: 'My style', description: '', basis: 'Your own style.', userMade: true }, o));
  return [...builtins, ...made];
}

export function resolveStyle(id: StyleId, overrides: Partial<Record<StyleId, StyleOverride>> | undefined): ExplanationStyle {
  const all = resolveStyles(overrides);
  return all.find((s) => s.id === id) ?? all.find((s) => !s.hidden) ?? all[0];
}

/** The sentences the style's knobs add to a prompt (length, then personality, then answer type). */
export function knobText(style: Pick<ExplanationStyle, 'personality' | 'length' | 'answerType'>): string {
  return [KNOBS.length[style.length]?.text, KNOBS.personality[style.personality]?.text, KNOBS.answerType[style.answerType]?.text].filter(Boolean).join(' ');
}

/** Fills {{placeholders}}; missing values become empty strings, unknown placeholders stay. */
export function fillTemplate(template: string, values: Partial<Record<(typeof PLACEHOLDERS)[number], string>>): string {
  return template.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (m, k: string) => (PLACEHOLDERS as readonly string[]).includes(k) ? (values[k as (typeof PLACEHOLDERS)[number]] ?? '') : m).replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n').trim();
}

/** Splits a reply at the [PAUSE] token: [spokenFirst, spokenAfterPause]. */
export function splitAtPause(text: string): [string, string | null] {
  const i = text.indexOf(PAUSE_TOKEN);
  if (i < 0) return [text.trim(), null];
  return [text.slice(0, i).trim(), text.slice(i + PAUSE_TOKEN.length).trim() || null];
}
```

## 9.5 Core logic, no Electron, reusable on iPad (src/core)

### `src/core/ai/client.ts` (36 lines)

```ts
import type { ExplainRequest, AiEvent } from '@shared/api';

export interface ExplainStream {
  done: Promise<{ text: string; usage: Extract<AiEvent, { type: 'done' }>['usage'] }>;
  cancel(): void;
}

/** Renderer-side client: starts an explanation in the main process and relays its streamed text. */
export function explain(req: ExplainRequest, onDelta?: (text: string, full: string) => void): ExplainStream {
  let streamId: string | null = null;
  let cancelled = false;
  let full = '';
  let resolve!: (v: { text: string; usage: Extract<AiEvent, { type: 'done' }>['usage'] }) => void;
  let reject!: (e: Error & { code?: string }) => void;
  const done = new Promise<{ text: string; usage: Extract<AiEvent, { type: 'done' }>['usage'] }>((res, rej) => { resolve = res; reject = rej; });
  const pending: AiEvent[] = [];
  const handle = (ev: AiEvent) => {
    if (ev.type === 'delta') { full += ev.text; onDelta?.(ev.text, full); }
    else if (ev.type === 'done') { off(); resolve({ text: ev.text, usage: ev.usage }); }
    else if (ev.type === 'error') { off(); const e = new Error(ev.message) as Error & { code?: string }; e.code = ev.code; reject(e); }
  };
  const off = window.readalong.onAiEvent((ev) => {
    if (!streamId) { pending.push(ev); return; }
    if (ev.streamId === streamId) handle(ev);
  });
  window.readalong.aiExplain(req).then(({ streamId: id }) => {
    streamId = id;
    for (const ev of pending.splice(0)) if (ev.streamId === id) handle(ev);
    if (cancelled) void window.readalong.aiCancel(id);
  }).catch((e) => { off(); reject(e as Error); });
  done.catch(() => undefined);
  return {
    done,
    cancel: () => { cancelled = true; if (streamId) void window.readalong.aiCancel(streamId); off(); const e = new Error('cancelled') as Error & { code?: string }; e.code = 'cancelled'; reject(e); },
  };
}
```

### `src/core/ai/hints.ts` (481 lines)

~~~~~ts
import type { Book, CefrLevel } from '@core/model';
import { sentenceText } from '@core/model';
import type { Dictionary } from '@core/dict/types';
import { annotateSentence } from '@core/vocab/analysis';
import type { PromptBundle } from './prompts';

/**
 * Word Wise in Chinese: for every word above the learner's level in a chapter, the AI picks the Chinese
 * meaning the word has *in that sentence* (and one other common meaning), so the reader can show it under
 * the word instead of the dictionary's first gloss. Pure helpers; the queue and cache live in src/main/hints.ts.
 *
 * Cost: a batch of 80 words is roughly 80 × ~15 tokens in (word + clipped sentence) and 80 × ~12 tokens out
 * (two short Chinese meanings in JSON) ≈ 2k tokens, about $0.0005 per chapter with Claude Haiku 5.5.
 */

/** [meaning as used in the chapter, another common meaning or ''] */
export type HintPair = [string, string];
/** lemma -> hint pair */
export type HintMap = Record<string, HintPair>;

export interface HardWord {
  /** vocabulary key (dictionary lemma) */
  lemma: string;
  /** the word as it first appears in the chapter */
  word: string;
  /** the sentence of that first appearance, clipped around the word */
  sentence: string;
}

/** Words per request: enough to amortise the system prompt, few enough that the JSON stays reliable. */
export const HINTS_BATCH_SIZE = 80;
/** Output budget per word: `"lemma": ["意思", "另一个意思"],` is about 20-30 tokens; 40 leaves room for longer lemmas. */
export const HINT_TOKENS_PER_WORD = 40;
/** Longest clipped sentence sent per word (characters). */
const SENTENCE_MAX_CHARS = 200;

/** Cuts a long sentence to a window around the word so each word costs a bounded number of tokens. */
export function clipSentence(sentence: string, word: string, max = SENTENCE_MAX_CHARS): string {
  const s = sentence.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  if (s.length <= max) return s;
  const at = word ? s.indexOf(word) : -1;
  const centre = at >= 0 ? at + word.length / 2 : max / 2;
  let start = Math.max(0, Math.round(centre - max / 2));
  let end = Math.min(s.length, start + max);
  if (end - start < max) start = Math.max(0, end - max);
  // cut at word boundaries where possible
  if (start > 0) { const sp = s.indexOf(' ', start); if (sp >= 0 && sp < start + 30) start = sp + 1; }
  if (end < s.length) { const sp = s.lastIndexOf(' ', end); if (sp > end - 30) end = sp; }
  return `${start > 0 ? '…' : ''}${s.slice(start, end).trim()}${end < s.length ? '…' : ''}`;
}

/**
 * Unique hard words of one chapter (above the learner's level, not names, not known/learning/ignored),
 * each with the sentence of its first appearance, in reading order.
 */
export function collectHardWords(
  book: Pick<Book, 'chapters'>,
  chapterIndex: number,
  dict: Dictionary,
  level: CefrLevel,
  names: ReadonlySet<string>,
  knownLemmas: ReadonlySet<string>,
): HardWord[] {
  const chapter = book.chapters[chapterIndex];
  if (!chapter) return [];
  const out: HardWord[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const para of chapter.paragraphs) {
    for (const s of para.sentences) {
      const { infos, hardTokens } = annotateSentence(para, s, dict, names as Set<string>, level);
      if (hardTokens.length === 0) continue;
      let text: string | null = null;
      for (const i of hardTokens) {
        const info = infos[i];
        if (!info || seen.has(info.lemma) || knownLemmas.has(info.lemma)) continue;
        seen.add(info.lemma);
        const word = s.tokens[i].text;
        text ??= sentenceText(para, s);
        out.push({ lemma: info.lemma, word, sentence: clipSentence(text, word) });
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Splits the words of a chapter into requests of at most `size` words. */
export function batchHardWords(words: HardWord[], size = HINTS_BATCH_SIZE): HardWord[][] {
  const out: HardWord[][] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i += size) out.push(words.slice(i, i + size));
  return out;
}

/**
 * System + user text for one batch. The reply must be a JSON object only; `parseHints` reads it back.
 * The sentence travels with each word so the first meaning is the one used in the book, not the headword's
 * most common sense ("spring" in "the spring of the trap" -> 弹簧, not 春天).
 */
export function buildHintsPrompt(batch: HardWord[], opts: { title: string; chapter: string; level: CefrLevel }): PromptBundle {
  const system = [
    `You write Word Wise hints for a native Chinese speaker reading an English book at CEFR level ${opts.level}.`,
    `For each English word you are given its dictionary form (the key), the form in the text and the sentence it appears in.`,
    `Give two short Chinese meanings per word: first the meaning the word has IN THAT SENTENCE, then one other common meaning of the word (or an empty string if it has no other common meaning).`,
    `Each meaning is 2 to 6 Chinese characters, like a dictionary gloss (房子, 不情愿的, 突然出现). No pinyin, no English, no part-of-speech labels, no explanations.`,
    `Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else: no code fences, no comments, no text before or after. The keys are exactly the dictionary forms given; every word must be present.`,
    `Format: {"<dictionary form>": ["<meaning here>", "<other meaning or empty>"], ...}`,
  ].join('\n');
  const where = `${opts.title}${opts.chapter ? ` — ${opts.chapter}` : ''}`;
  const lines = batch.map((w, i) => `${i + 1}. ${JSON.stringify(w.lemma)}${w.word.toLowerCase() !== w.lemma ? ` (in the text: ${w.word})` : ''} — ${w.sentence}`);
  const user = [
    `Book: ${where}`,
    `Words (${batch.length}):`,
    ...lines,
    '',
    `Return the JSON object with these ${batch.length} keys: ${batch.map((w) => JSON.stringify(w.lemma)).join(', ')}.`,
  ].join('\n');
  return { system, user, maxTokens: HINT_TOKENS_PER_WORD * batch.length + 100 };
}

const MEANING_MAX_CHARS = 20;

function cleanMeaning(v: unknown): string {
  if (typeof v !== 'string') return '';
  return v.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, MEANING_MAX_CHARS);
}

function toPair(v: unknown): HintPair | null {
  const arr = Array.isArray(v) ? v : typeof v === 'string' ? [v] : v && typeof v === 'object' ? Object.values(v as object) : null;
  if (!arr) return null;
  const first = cleanMeaning(arr[0]);
  if (!first) return null;
  return [first, cleanMeaning(arr[1])];
}

function fromObject(obj: unknown): HintMap {
  const out: HintMap = {};
  if (!obj || typeof obj !== 'object' || Array.isArray(obj)) return out;
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    const key = k.trim().toLowerCase();
    const pair = toPair(v);
    if (key && pair) out[key] = pair;
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Reads the model's reply back into a hint map. Tolerates code fences, prose around the object and a
 * truncated tail: when the object does not parse, each complete `"key": ["a", "b"]` entry is salvaged.
 */
export function parseHints(text: string): HintMap {
  if (!text) return {};
  let s = text.replace(/```[a-z]*\s*/gi, '').trim();
  const start = s.indexOf('{');
  const end = s.lastIndexOf('}');
  if (start >= 0 && end > start) s = s.slice(start, end + 1);
  else if (start >= 0) s = s.slice(start);
  try {
    return fromObject(JSON.parse(s));
  } catch { /* fall through to the per-entry salvage */ }
  const out: HintMap = {};
  const re = /"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*:\s*\[\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*(?:,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*)?\]/g;
  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
  while ((m = re.exec(s))) {
    try {
      const key = (JSON.parse(`"${m[1]}"`) as string).trim().toLowerCase();
      const pair = toPair([JSON.parse(`"${m[2]}"`), m[3] !== undefined ? JSON.parse(`"${m[3]}"`) : '']);
      if (key && pair) out[key] = pair;
    } catch { /* skip a broken entry */ }
  }
  return out;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Phrases: multi-word expressions of the chapter, each with a CEFR level decided by the model before
 * anything is shown (docs/RULES.md "Phrases").
 *
 * Cost: a chunk of at most PHRASE_CHUNK_CHARS (~4.5k tokens of text + ~350 of instructions) and at most
 * 40 phrases out (~35 tokens each, ≈ 1.4k tokens) ≈ $0.0012 with Claude Haiku 5.5. Most chapters are one chunk.
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/** A multi-word expression the model found in a chapter (validated: it literally appears there). */
export interface PhraseItem {
  /** exact text as it appears in the book ("took it for granted") */
  text: string;
  /** base form, lower case ("take for granted") */
  lemma: string;
  /** the model's CEFR level of the expression itself */
  level: CefrLevel;
  /** short Chinese meaning as used in the chapter ('' when the model gave none) */
  zh: string;
}

/**
 * One occurrence of a chapter phrase in a sentence. `start`/`end` are token indices of `sentence.tokens`,
 * both INCLUSIVE (unlike PhraseSpan in analysis.ts): the phrase covers tokens[start]..tokens[end].
 */
export interface PhraseHit {
  /** sentenceKey(): "chapter.paragraph.sentence" */
  sentenceKey: string;
  start: number;
  end: number;
  /** the covered text of this sentence (para.text from tokens[start].start to tokens[end].end) */
  text: string;
  lemma: string;
  level: CefrLevel;
  zh: string;
}

/** sentenceKey -> phrase hits of that sentence, ordered by start; sentences without hits are absent. */
export type PhraseMap = Record<string, PhraseHit[]>;

/** Characters of chapter text per phrase request (~4.5k tokens; the request stays under ~6k with the instructions). */
export const PHRASE_CHUNK_CHARS = 18_000;
/** Phrases asked for per chapter (split across chunks in proportion to their length). */
export const PHRASES_PER_CHAPTER = 40;
/** Output budget per phrase: `{"text":"…","lemma":"…","level":"B2","zh":"…"},` ≈ 30-40 tokens. */
export const PHRASE_TOKENS_PER_ITEM = 45;
/** Longest text accepted: a 5-word expression plus one inserted object ("kept him at arm's length"). */
export const MAX_PHRASE_TEXT_WORDS = 6;

const WORD_RE = /[\p{L}\p{N}]+(?:['’\-‐‑][\p{L}\p{N}]+)*/gu;

/** Folds case, curly quotes, dashes and whitespace so the model's copy compares equal to the book's text. */
export function normalizePhraseText(s: string): string {
  return s
    .normalize('NFKC')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[‘’ʼ`´′]/g, "'")
    .replace(/[“”„″]/g, '"')
    .replace(/[‐‑‒–—―]/g, '-')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim();
}

/** The words of a phrase, normalised, punctuation dropped ("Took it for granted," -> ["took","it","for","granted"]). */
export function phraseWords(s: string): string[] {
  return normalizePhraseText(s).match(WORD_RE) ?? [];
}

/** The plain text of a chapter, one paragraph per line. */
export function chapterText(book: Pick<Book, 'chapters'>, chapterIndex: number): string {
  const ch = book.chapters[chapterIndex];
  return ch ? ch.paragraphs.map((p) => p.text).join('\n') : '';
}

/**
 * Splits a chapter into request-sized chunks at sentence boundaries (paragraphs keep their line breaks).
 * A single sentence longer than `max` becomes its own chunk.
 */
export function chunkChapter(book: Pick<Book, 'chapters'>, chapterIndex: number, max = PHRASE_CHUNK_CHARS): string[] {
  const ch = book.chapters[chapterIndex];
  if (!ch) return [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  let cur = '';
  for (const para of ch.paragraphs) {
    let first = true;
    for (const s of para.sentences) {
      const t = sentenceText(para, s).trim();
      if (!t) continue;
      const sep = cur ? (first ? '\n' : ' ') : '';
      if (cur && cur.length + sep.length + t.length > max) { out.push(cur); cur = t; }
      else cur += sep + t;
      first = false;
    }
  }
  if (cur.trim()) out.push(cur);
  return out;
}

/** How many phrases to ask for in each chunk: PHRASES_PER_CHAPTER shared by length, at least 10 each. */
export function phraseQuota(chunks: string[]): number[] {
  const total = chunks.reduce((n, c) => n + c.length, 0) || 1;
  return chunks.map((c) => Math.max(10, Math.ceil((PHRASES_PER_CHAPTER * c.length) / total)));
}

/** System + user text asking for the multi-word expressions of one chunk; `parsePhrases` reads the reply. */
export function buildPhrasesPrompt(
  chunk: string,
  opts: { title: string; chapter: string; level: CefrLevel; max?: number; part?: [number, number] },
): PromptBundle {
  const max = opts.max ?? PHRASES_PER_CHAPTER;
  const system = [
    `You find multi-word expressions in an English book for a native Chinese speaker reading at CEFR level ${opts.level}.`,
    `List the expressions of 2 to 5 words — idioms, phrasal verbs, fixed expressions, collocations whose meaning is not obvious, slang — that a learner at level ${opts.level} would not understand from the single words.`,
    `Rules:`,
    `- Only expressions that literally appear in the text. "text" is copied exactly as it appears in the text (same words, same forms, same order), nothing added or left out.`,
    `- "lemma" is the dictionary form in lower case (take for granted, look forward to, give up).`,
    `- "level" is the CEFR level of the expression itself: A2, B1, B2, C1 or C2.`,
    `- "zh" is its Chinese meaning as used here, 2 to 6 characters, like a dictionary gloss. No pinyin, no English.`,
    `- No single words, no names, no free combinations whose meaning is just the sum of the words (old man, big house, went home, a cup of tea).`,
    `- At most ${max} expressions, each once, the hardest and most useful first.`,
    `Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else: no code fences, no comments, no text before or after.`,
    `Format: {"phrases":[{"text":"<as in the text>","lemma":"<base form>","level":"<A2|B1|B2|C1|C2>","zh":"<中文>"}]}`,
    `If there are none: {"phrases":[]}`,
  ].join('\n');
  const where = `${opts.title}${opts.chapter ? ` — ${opts.chapter}` : ''}`;
  const part = opts.part && opts.part[1] > 1 ? ` (part ${opts.part[0]} of ${opts.part[1]})` : '';
  const user = [
    `Phrases. Book: ${where}${part}`,
    `Text:`,
    '<<<',
    chunk,
    '>>>',
    '',
    `Return the JSON object with at most ${max} expressions.`,
  ].join('\n');
  return { system, user, maxTokens: PHRASE_TOKENS_PER_ITEM * max + 100 };
}

/** A phrase as the model wrote it, before validation. */
export interface RawPhrase { text: string; lemma: string; level: string; zh: string }

function str(v: unknown): string { return typeof v === 'string' ? v.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() : ''; }

function toRawPhrase(v: unknown): RawPhrase | null {
  if (!v || typeof v !== 'object' || Array.isArray(v)) return null;
  const o = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  const text = str(o.text ?? o.phrase ?? o.expression);
  if (!text) return null;
  return { text, lemma: str(o.lemma ?? o.base), level: str(o.level ?? o.cefr), zh: str(o.zh ?? o.chinese ?? o.meaning) };
}

/**
 * Reads the model's reply back into raw phrases. Accepts {"phrases":[…]}, a bare array, code fences and prose
 * around the JSON; when the whole does not parse (a truncated tail), each complete `{…}` item is salvaged.
 */
export function parsePhrases(text: string): RawPhrase[] {
  if (!text) return [];
  const s = text.replace(/```[a-z]*\s*/gi, '').trim();
  const objAt = s.indexOf('{');
  const arrAt = s.indexOf('[');
  const candidates: string[] = [];
  if (objAt >= 0) { const e = s.lastIndexOf('}'); if (e > objAt) candidates.push(s.slice(objAt, e + 1)); }
  if (arrAt >= 0) { const e = s.lastIndexOf(']'); if (e > arrAt) candidates.push(s.slice(arrAt, e + 1)); }
  for (const c of candidates) {
    try {
      const v: unknown = JSON.parse(c);
      const list = Array.isArray(v) ? v : v && typeof v === 'object' ? (v as Record<string, unknown>).phrases : null;
      if (Array.isArray(list)) return list.map(toRawPhrase).filter((x): x is RawPhrase => x !== null);
    } catch { /* try the next shape, then salvage */ }
  }
  const out: RawPhrase[] = [];
  for (const m of s.matchAll(/\{[^{}]*\}/g)) {
    try {
      const p = toRawPhrase(JSON.parse(m[0]));
      if (p) out.push(p);
    } catch { /* skip a broken item */ }
  }
  return out;
}

const CEFR_RE = /^(A1|A2|B1|B2|C1|C2)$/;
const PLACEHOLDERS = new Set(['sb', 'sth', 'somebody', 'someone', 'something', "one's", "someone's", "somebody's", 'oneself', 'do', 'doing']);

function escapeRe(s: string): string { return s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'); }

/**
 * Keeps the phrases worth showing: a valid CEFR level, 2 to MAX_PHRASE_TEXT_WORDS words, the text literally in the
 * chapter (case, quotes, dashes and spaces folded; whole words only), not a free combination (when `isFree` is
 * given, e.g. looksLikeFreeCombination over the dictionary), each text once, at most `max`.
 */
export function validatePhrases(
  items: RawPhrase[],
  chapter: string,
  opts: { max?: number; isFree?: (words: string[], zh: string) => boolean } = {},
): PhraseItem[] {
  const hay = normalizePhraseText(chapter);
  const out: PhraseItem[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const max = opts.max ?? Infinity;
  for (const it of items) {
    if (out.length >= max) break;
    const level = it.level.toUpperCase().trim();
    if (!CEFR_RE.test(level)) continue;
    const words = phraseWords(it.text);
    if (words.length < 2 || words.length > MAX_PHRASE_TEXT_WORDS) continue;
    const norm = normalizePhraseText(it.text).replace(/^[^\p{L}\p{N}]+|[^\p{L}\p{N}]+$/gu, '');
    if (!norm || seen.has(norm)) continue;
    const re = new RegExp(`(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])${escapeRe(norm)}(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])`, 'u');
    if (!re.test(hay)) continue;
    const zh = cleanMeaning(it.zh);
    if (opts.isFree?.(words, zh)) continue;
    seen.add(norm);
    const lemma = normalizePhraseText(it.lemma) || words.join(' ');
    out.push({ text: it.text, lemma, level: level as CefrLevel, zh });
  }
  return out;
}

/** True for words that may stand between the first word and the rest of a phrasal verb ("took it for granted"). */
const GAP_WORDS = new Set(['it', 'him', 'her', 'them', 'me', 'us', 'you', 'this', 'that', 'one', 'something', 'someone', 'everything', 'nothing']);

interface Pattern { words: string[]; item: PhraseItem; /** lemma pattern: allow one object pronoun after the first word */ gap: boolean }

/**
 * Finds every occurrence of the chapter's phrases in its sentences. A match starts and ends on word tokens and
 * runs over consecutive word tokens (only space tokens between them). Each phrase is matched by its text and by
 * its lemma; the first and last word may be inflected (compared through `lemmaOf`, e.g. the dictionary's), and
 * a lemma match may carry one object pronoun after its first word ("took it for granted" for "take for
 * granted"). Longer matches win; matches never overlap.
 */
export function mapPhraseHits(
  book: Pick<Book, 'chapters'>,
  chapterIndex: number,
  items: PhraseItem[],
  lemmaOf?: (word: string) => string,
): PhraseMap {
  const ch = book.chapters[chapterIndex];
  const out: PhraseMap = {};
  if (!ch || items.length === 0) return out;
  const lemmaCache = new Map<string, string>();
  const lem = (w: string): string => {
    if (!lemmaOf) return w;
    let l = lemmaCache.get(w);
    if (l === undefined) { l = normalizePhraseText(lemmaOf(w)); lemmaCache.set(w, l); }
    return l;
  };
  const patterns: Pattern[] = [];
  const seenPat = new Set<string>();
  for (const item of items) {
    const tw = phraseWords(item.text);
    const lw = phraseWords(item.lemma);
    for (const [words, gap] of [[tw, false], [lw, true]] as const) {
      if (words.length < 2 || words.length > MAX_PHRASE_TEXT_WORDS || words.some((w) => PLACEHOLDERS.has(w))) continue;
      const k = `${words.join(' ')}|${gap}`;
      if (seenPat.has(k)) continue;
      seenPat.add(k);
      patterns.push({ words: [...words], item, gap });
    }
  }
  const same = (tok: string, pw: string, edge: boolean): boolean => tok === pw || (edge && lemmaOf !== undefined && lem(tok) === lem(pw));

  for (const para of ch.paragraphs) {
    for (const s of para.sentences) {
      const toks = s.tokens;
      const wi: number[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < toks.length; i++) if (toks[i].kind === 'word') wi.push(i);
      if (wi.length < 2) continue;
      const norm = wi.map((i) => phraseWords(toks[i].text).join('-'));
      // joined[k]: word k and word k+1 are separated by spaces only
      const joined = wi.map((i, k) => {
        if (k + 1 >= wi.length) return false;
        for (let j = i + 1; j < wi[k + 1]; j++) if (toks[j].kind !== 'space') return false;
        return true;
      });
      const found: { k0: number; k1: number; item: PhraseItem; n: number }[] = [];
      for (const p of patterns) {
        const n = p.words.length;
        for (let k = 0; k + n <= wi.length; k++) {
          if (!same(norm[k], p.words[0], true)) continue;
          for (const g of p.gap && n >= 2 ? [0, 1] : [0]) {
            const kEnd = k + n - 1 + g;
            if (kEnd >= wi.length) continue;
            if (g === 1 && !GAP_WORDS.has(norm[k + 1])) continue;
            let ok = true;
            for (let q = k; q < kEnd; q++) if (!joined[q]) { ok = false; break; }
            for (let j = 1; ok && j < n; j++) {
              if (!same(norm[k + j + g], p.words[j], j === n - 1)) ok = false;
            }
            if (ok) { found.push({ k0: k, k1: kEnd, item: p.item, n: kEnd - k + 1 }); break; }
          }
        }
      }
      if (found.length === 0) continue;
      found.sort((a, b) => b.n - a.n || a.k0 - b.k0);
      const taken = new Array<boolean>(wi.length).fill(false);
      const hits: PhraseHit[] = [];
      const key = `${chapterIndex}.${para.index}.${s.index}`;
      for (const f of found) {
        let free = true;
        for (let k = f.k0; k <= f.k1; k++) if (taken[k]) { free = false; break; }
        if (!free) continue;
        for (let k = f.k0; k <= f.k1; k++) taken[k] = true;
        const start = wi[f.k0], end = wi[f.k1];
        hits.push({ sentenceKey: key, start, end, text: para.text.slice(toks[start].start, toks[end].end), lemma: f.item.lemma, level: f.item.level, zh: f.item.zh });
      }
      hits.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start);
      out[key] = hits;
    }
  }
  return out;
}

```ts
import type { ExplainRequest, ExplainKind } from '@shared/api';
import type { CefrLevel } from '@core/model';

export interface PromptBundle { system: string; user: string; maxTokens: number }

/**
 * Builds the system prompt (stable across a session, cacheable) and the per-request user message.
 * The reply is spoken aloud, so the prompts insist on plain spoken English and a fixed line format
 * that parseExplanation() turns into script parts.
 */
export function buildPrompt(req: ExplainRequest, opts: { level: CefrLevel; instructions: string; length: 'short' | 'normal' | 'long' }): PromptBundle {
  const system = [
    `You are a patient English tutor inside a reading app. The learner is a native Chinese speaker at CEFR level ${opts.level}.`,
    `Your reply will be SPOKEN ALOUD by a text-to-speech voice. Write for the ear: short sentences, plain common words, no markdown, no bullet points, no headings, no asterisks, no emojis, no phonetic symbols, and do not put quotation marks around words.`,
    `Never translate a whole sentence into Chinese. Use Chinese only for the meaning of single words or short phrases, where the format asks for it.`,
    `Keep to the exact line labels requested. Do not add greetings or closing remarks.`,
    opts.instructions.trim() ? `The learner's own instructions: ${opts.instructions.trim()}` : '',
  ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');

  const len = opts.length;
  const ctx = [
    `Book: ${req.book.title}${req.book.chapter ? ` — ${req.book.chapter}` : ''}`,
    req.before ? `Text before: ${req.before}` : '',
    `Sentence: ${req.sentence}`,
    req.after ? `Text after: ${req.after}` : '',
  ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');

  let task = '';
  let maxTokens = 600;
  const t = req.target;
  const dict = req.dict ? ` (dictionary hint: ${[req.dict.ipa, req.dict.zh, req.dict.level ? `level ${req.dict.level}` : ''].filter(Boolean).join('; ')})` : '';
  switch (req.kind) {
    case 'word':
    case 'phrase': {
      const what = req.kind === 'word' ? 'word' : 'phrase';
      const n = len === 'short' ? 'one short sentence' : len === 'long' ? 'two or three sentences' : 'one or two sentences';
      task = [
        `${what[0].toUpperCase()}${what.slice(1)} to explain: ${t}${dict}`,
        `Answer with exactly these lines, each starting with the label:`,
        `DEFINITION: ${n} saying what ${t} means in general, in simple English.`,
        `IN THIS SENTENCE: ${n} explaining what ${t} means here, in this story, and why the author uses it.`,
        len === 'short' ? '' : `EXAMPLE: one short new example sentence using ${t} with the same meaning.`,
        `CHINESE: the Chinese meaning of ${t} as used here, two to eight characters, nothing else.`,
      ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');
      maxTokens = len === 'long' ? 700 : 450;
      break;
    }
    case 'sentence': {
      task = [
        `Explain this sentence: ${t}`,
        `Answer with exactly these lines, each starting with the label:`,
        `MEANING: ${len === 'short' ? 'one or two' : len === 'long' ? 'three to five' : 'two to four'} short, simple English sentences explaining what this sentence means in the story. Break it into parts if it is long.`,
        `HARD WORDS: up to three difficult words or phrases from the sentence, each as: word, then its simple English meaning, then its Chinese meaning, separated by commas; separate items with semicolons. If there are none, write: none.`,
      ].join('\n');
      maxTokens = len === 'long' ? 800 : 500;
      break;
    }
    case 'passage': {
      task = [
        `Explain this passage the learner just listened to: ${t}`,
        `Answer with exactly these lines, each starting with the label:`,
        `SUMMARY: ${len === 'short' ? 'two' : len === 'long' ? 'four to six' : 'three or four'} short, simple English sentences explaining what happens and what it means.`,
        `HARD WORDS: up to five difficult words or phrases from the passage, each as: word, then its simple English meaning, then its Chinese meaning, separated by commas; separate items with semicolons. If there are none, write: none.`,
      ].join('\n');
      maxTokens = 900;
      break;
    }
    case 'question': {
      task = [`The learner asks: ${req.question ?? ''}`, `Answer in plain spoken English in at most ${len === 'short' ? 60 : len === 'long' ? 180 : 110} words. Give the Chinese meaning of any single word you define.`].join('\n');
      maxTokens = 700;
      break;
    }
  }
  const history = req.history.length ? `Earlier in this chapter you were asked:\n${req.history.slice(-6).map((h) => `${h.role === 'user' ? 'Learner' : 'You'}: ${h.text.slice(0, 400)}`).join('\n')}\n\n` : '';
  return { system, user: `${history}${ctx}\n\n${task}`, maxTokens };
}

export interface ExplanationParts {
  definition?: string;
  inSentence?: string;
  example?: string;
  chinese?: string;
  meaning?: string;
  summary?: string;
  hardWords?: { word: string; meaning: string; zh: string }[];
  /** everything, when no labels were found */
  free?: string;
}

const LABELS: Record<string, keyof ExplanationParts> = {
  'DEFINITION': 'definition', 'IN THIS SENTENCE': 'inSentence', 'EXAMPLE': 'example', 'CHINESE': 'chinese', 'MEANING': 'meaning', 'SUMMARY': 'summary', 'HARD WORDS': 'hardWords',
};

/**
 * Parses the labelled reply into parts. Tolerant of what models actually produce: markdown bold, bullets or
 * numbering before a label, a Chinese colon or a dash after it, several labels on one line (upper-case only,
 * so "for example:" inside a definition is not a label), extra lines, and pinyin after the Chinese meaning.
 */
export function parseExplanation(text: string, kind: ExplainKind): ExplanationParts {
  const clean = text.replace(/\*\*|__/g, '').replace(/^#+[ \t]*/gm, '').replace(/\r/g, '').trim();
  const parts: ExplanationParts = {};
  const re = /(^|\n[ \t]*|[ \t]+)(?:(?:[-*•]|\d+[.)])[ \t]*)?(DEFINITION|IN THIS SENTENCE|EXAMPLE|CHINESE|MEANING|SUMMARY|HARD WORDS)[ \t]*(?:[:：]|[-–—](?=\s))[ \t]*/gi;
  const hits: { key: keyof ExplanationParts; start: number; end: number }[] = [];
  for (const m of clean.matchAll(re)) {
    const atLineStart = m.index === 0 || m[1].startsWith('\n');
    if (!atLineStart && m[2] !== m[2].toUpperCase()) continue;
    hits.push({ key: LABELS[m[2].toUpperCase()], start: m.index!, end: m.index! + m[0].length });
  }
  if (!hits.length) {
    parts.free = clean;
    return parts;
  }
  const buf: Partial<Record<keyof ExplanationParts, string[]>> = {};
  hits.forEach((h, i) => {
    const body = clean.slice(h.end, i + 1 < hits.length ? hits[i + 1].start : undefined).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    (buf[h.key] ??= []).push(body);
  });
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(buf) as [keyof ExplanationParts, string[]][]) {
    const joined = v.join(' ').trim();
    if (k === 'hardWords') parts.hardWords = parseHardWords(joined);
    else if (k === 'chinese') parts.chinese = chineseOnly(joined);
    else (parts as Record<string, unknown>)[k] = joined;
  }
  void kind;
  return parts;
}

const CJK = /[\u3400-\u4DBF\u4E00-\u9FFF\uF900-\uFAFF]/;

/** Keeps the Chinese meaning itself: no pinyin, no bracketed notes, no trailing full stop (it is read by a Chinese voice). */
function chineseOnly(s: string): string {
  let t = s.replace(/[(（][^)）]*[)）]/g, ' ').trim();
  if (!CJK.test(t)) return t;
  t = t.replace(/[^\u3400-\u4DBF\u4E00-\u9FFF\uF900-\uFAFF、，,；;/ ]+/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  return t.replace(/^[、，,；;/ ]+|[、，,；;/ .。]+$/g, '');
}

function parseHardWords(s: string): { word: string; meaning: string; zh: string }[] {
  const t = s.trim();
  if (!t || /^(?:there (?:are|is) )?none\b/i.test(t) || /^no (?:hard|difficult) words/i.test(t)) return [];
  return t.split(/;|；|\n/).map((item) => item.trim()).filter(Boolean).map((item) => {
    const bits = item.split(/,|，|=|—|–/).map((b) => b.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    const zhIdx = bits.findIndex((b) => CJK.test(b));
    const zh = zhIdx >= 0 ? bits[zhIdx] : '';
    const rest = bits.filter((_, i) => i !== zhIdx);
    return { word: rest[0] ?? item, meaning: rest.slice(1).join(', '), zh };
  }).filter((h) => h.meaning || h.zh);
}

/** The English text to speak for a parsed explanation, in the order the learner asked for. */
export function spokenEnglish(parts: ExplanationParts): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  if (parts.free) return [parts.free];
  if (parts.definition) out.push(parts.definition);
  if (parts.inSentence) out.push(`In this sentence: ${parts.inSentence}`);
  if (parts.example) out.push(`For example: ${parts.example}`);
  if (parts.meaning) out.push(parts.meaning);
  if (parts.summary) out.push(parts.summary);
  if (parts.hardWords?.length) out.push(...parts.hardWords.map((h) => (h.meaning ? `${h.word}: ${h.meaning}` : h.word)));
  return out;
}

/** Chinese fragments to speak with a Chinese voice (the word meaning only, never whole sentences). */
export function spokenChinese(parts: ExplanationParts): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  if (parts.chinese) out.push(parts.chinese);
  if (parts.hardWords?.length) out.push(...parts.hardWords.filter((h) => h.zh).map((h) => `${h.word}, ${h.zh}`));
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Style-based prompts (Dream Read): plain prose replies, long context, learner-editable templates.

import { fillTemplate, knobText, type ExplanationStyle } from '@shared/styles';

export interface StyledPromptOpts {
  style: ExplanationStyle;
  /** shared rules (DEFAULT_CONTEXT_RULES or the learner's edited version) */
  contextRules: string;
  level: CefrLevel;
  /** learner's first language, as a word for the AI: 'Chinese' */
  native: string;
}

/**
 * Builds the system + user messages for a word/phrase/sentence explanation in a given style.
 * The system part (rules + learner facts) is stable within a session and cacheable; the user part carries
 * the book context (title, chapter, ~500 words before, the sentence, ~200 words after) and the filled template.
 */
export function buildStyledPrompt(req: ExplainRequest, opts: StyledPromptOpts): PromptBundle {
  const values = {
    word: req.target,
    sentence: req.sentence,
    before: req.before,
    after: req.after,
    title: req.book.title,
    chapter: req.book.chapter,
    level: opts.level,
    native: opts.native,
    dict: req.dict ? `Dictionary hint for the word: ${[req.dict.ipa ? `pronunciation ${req.dict.ipa}` : '', req.dict.zh ? `${opts.native} meaning ${req.dict.zh}` : '', req.dict.level ? `CEFR level ${req.dict.level}` : ''].filter(Boolean).join(', ')}.` : '',
  };
  const system = fillTemplate(opts.contextRules, values);
  const ctx = [
    `Book: ${req.book.title || 'Untitled'}`,
    req.book.chapter ? `Chapter: ${req.book.chapter}` : '',
    req.position ? `Place in the book: chapter ${req.position.chapter + 1}, paragraph ${req.position.paragraph + 1}, sentence ${req.position.sentence + 1}.` : '',
    req.before ? `Text before the sentence:\n${req.before}` : '',
    `The sentence being read now:\n${req.sentence}`,
    req.after ? `Text after the sentence:\n${req.after}` : '',
  ].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
  const template = req.kind === 'sentence' ? opts.style.sentencePrompt : opts.style.wordPrompt;
  let task = fillTemplate(template, values);
  if (req.question && req.question.trim()) task += `\n\nThe learner just said this out loud (speech recognition may have got some words wrong; work out what they most likely meant from the book, and never ask them to repeat): "${req.question.trim()}". Answer it as part of your explanation.`;
  const knobs = knobText(opts.style);
  if (knobs) task += `\n\n${knobs}`;
  if (req.again) task += `\n\nThe learner has just heard a first explanation of this and said they still do not understand. Explain it again from a different angle, more slowly and in more detail than before: start from what they surely know, use the story around this moment, compare it with a simpler word or situation, give one more everyday example, and check the meaning in this exact sentence once more at the end. Take the time it needs.`;
  const history = req.history.length ? `Earlier in this chapter:\n${req.history.slice(-4).map((h) => `${h.role === 'user' ? 'Learner' : 'You'}: ${h.text.slice(0, 300)}`).join('\n')}\n\n` : '';
  return { system, user: `${history}${ctx}\n\n${task}`, maxTokens: req.again ? Math.round(opts.style.maxTokens * 1.6) : opts.style.maxTokens };
}

/** Opening filler the learner asked never to hear (docs/RULES.md, "No filler"); removed from the start of a reply. */
const OPENING_FILLER = [
  /^(?:what a |that's a |that is a )?(?:great|good|nice|excellent|lovely) question[.!,]*\s*/i,
  /^let me explain(?: (?:it|this|that|again))?(?: to you)?[.!:,]*\s*/i,
  /^as I (?:said|mentioned)(?: (?:before|earlier))?[.!:,]*\s*/i,
  /^we already know (?:this|that)(?: word)?[.!:,]*\s*/i,
  /^now,\s*/i,
];

/** Strips anything a model might still add that a voice should not read: markdown, labels, list markers, opening filler. */
export function cleanSpokenProse(text: string): string {
  let out = text
    .replace(/\*\*|__|`/g, '')
    .replace(/^#+[ \t]*/gm, '')
    .replace(/^[ \t]*(?:[-*•]|\d+[.)])[ \t]+/gm, '')
    .replace(/^(?:DEFINITION|IN THIS SENTENCE|EXAMPLE|MEANING|SUMMARY|SCENE|CONTEXT|STEP \d+)[ \t]*[:：][ \t]*/gim, '')
    .replace(/[ \t]+\n/g, '\n')
    .replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n')
    .trim();
  for (let changed = true; changed;) {
    changed = false;
    for (const re of OPENING_FILLER) {
      const next = out.replace(re, '');
      if (next !== out && next.trim()) { out = next.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + next.slice(1); changed = true; }
    }
  }
  return out;
}
