### `src/core/dict/dictionary.ts` (398 lines)

```ts
import type { CefrLevel } from '@core/model';
import { CEFR_LEVELS } from '@core/model';
import type { DictData, DictRaw } from '@shared/api';
import type { Dictionary, DictEntry, LookupResult } from './types';

/**
 * Offline dictionary over the ECDICT-derived data in resources/dict/dict.json.gz.
 *
 * Lookup strategy (see `createDictionary`): the token is normalised, then tried as an exact headword,
 * with a possessive stripped, through the inflection map, through English suffix-stripping rules, and
 * finally with accents folded (and hyphens removed) — the first hit wins and `via` records which step
 * produced it. Everything is O(1) hash lookups per candidate; no per-headword variants are precomputed.
 */

/** Longest phrase in the data is 4 words; the API accepts up to 5. */
export const MAX_PHRASE_WORDS = 5;

const LEVEL_SOURCES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['cefrj', 'oct', 'est']);

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Text normalisation helpers (exported for reuse by names/analysis and for unit tests)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

const isAlnum = (ch: string): boolean => /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(ch);

/**
 * Normalises a token as it appears in text: trims, straightens curly apostrophes, lower-cases, collapses
 * internal whitespace and strips surrounding punctuation/quotes. A trailing apostrophe is kept only when
 * it directly follows a letter ("parents'", "goin'") so possessive handling can see it.
 */
export function normalizeToken(token: string): string {
  let t = token.replace(/[‘’ʼ′`]/g, "'").trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
  let start = 0;
  while (start < t.length && !isAlnum(t[start])) start++;
  let end = t.length;
  while (end > start) {
    const ch = t[end - 1];
    if (isAlnum(ch)) break;
    if (ch === "'" && end - 2 >= start && isAlnum(t[end - 2])) break;
    end--;
  }
  t = t.slice(start, end);
  return t;
}

/** Removes diacritics and maps the few Latin ligatures/special letters ECDICT spells with plain ASCII. */
export function foldAccents(s: string): string {
  if (!/[^\x00-\x7f]/.test(s)) return s;
  return s
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, '')
    .replace(/ß/g, 'ss').replace(/æ/g, 'ae').replace(/œ/g, 'oe').replace(/ø/g, 'o')
    .replace(/ð/g, 'd').replace(/þ/g, 'th').replace(/ł/g, 'l').replace(/đ/g, 'd');
}

/** "darcy's" -> "darcy", "parents'" -> "parents", "goin'" -> "goin"; null when there is nothing to strip. */
export function stripPossessive(t: string): string | null {
  if (t.length > 2 && t.endsWith("'s")) return t.slice(0, -2);
  if (t.length > 1 && t.endsWith("'")) return t.slice(0, -1);
  return null;
}

/**
 * Candidate stems for a token that is neither a headword nor a listed inflection, most specific first.
 * Candidates are only *proposed* here; the caller accepts the first one that is a headword, which is what
 * makes "-ly only if the stem exists" (and every other rule) safe. Deliberately not stripped: -ness, -ment,
 * -tion, -ful, -less — those are separate words and ECDICT lists them on their own.
 */
export function suffixCandidates(t: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const n = t.length;
  if (n < 3 || !/^[a-z][a-z'-]*$/.test(t)) return out;
  const push = (c: string): void => { if (c.length >= 2 && !out.includes(c)) out.push(c); };
  const end = (s: string): boolean => t.endsWith(s);
  // 'runn' -> 'run', 'stopp' -> 'stop', 'controll' -> 'control'. Not for ss/ff/zz, which end real words (kiss,
  // stuff, buzz) and are never doubled; 'll' words ('fill', 'smell') are found at the plain-stem step first.
  const undouble = (stem: string): string | null => {
    const a = stem[stem.length - 1];
    return stem.length >= 3 && a === stem[stem.length - 2] && /[bdgklmnprtv]/.test(a) ? stem.slice(0, -1) : null;
  };
  const stemVariants = (stem: string): void => {
    push(stem);            // walk-ed, fast-er, quick-ly
    push(stem + 'e');      // hop(e)-ed, nic(e)-er, mak(e)-ing, gentl(e)-y
    const u = undouble(stem);
    if (u) push(u);        // stopp-ed -> stop, bigg-er -> big, runn-ing -> run
  };

  // plurals / third person: -ies -> -ie|-y, -es after sibilants and -o, else -s
  if (end('ies') && n > 4) { push(t.slice(0, -1)); push(t.slice(0, -3) + 'y'); }            // movies -> movie, cities -> city
  else if (end('es') && n > 3) {
    if (/(?:[sxz]|ch|sh|o)es$/.test(t)) { push(t.slice(0, -2)); push(t.slice(0, -1)); }      // boxes -> box, goes -> go, shoes -> shoe
    else { push(t.slice(0, -1)); push(t.slice(0, -2)); }                                      // makes -> make
  } else if (end('s') && !end('ss') && n > 2) push(t.slice(0, -1));                           // cats -> cat

  // past tense / participle
  if (end('ied') && n > 4) { push(t.slice(0, -1)); push(t.slice(0, -3) + 'y'); }             // tried -> try (died -> die via -ed below)
  else if (end('ed') && n > 3) stemVariants(t.slice(0, -2));                                 // walked, hoped, stopped

  // progressive / gerund
  if (end('ing') && n > 4) {
    if (end('ying')) push(t.slice(0, -4) + 'ie');                                             // lying -> lie, dying -> die
    stemVariants(t.slice(0, -3));                                                             // walking, making, running
  }

  // comparative / superlative (also agent nouns such as 'worker' -> 'work')
  if (end('iest') && n > 5) push(t.slice(0, -4) + 'y');                                       // happiest -> happy
  else if (end('est') && n > 4) stemVariants(t.slice(0, -3));                                 // fastest, nicest, biggest
  if (end('ier') && n > 4) push(t.slice(0, -3) + 'y');                                        // happier -> happy
  else if (end('er') && n > 3) stemVariants(t.slice(0, -2));                                  // faster, nicer, bigger

  // adverbs: accepted only when the stem is itself a headword
  if (end('ly') && n > 4) {
    if (end('ily')) push(t.slice(0, -3) + 'y');                                               // happily -> happy
    if (end('ically')) push(t.slice(0, -4));                                                  // basically -> basic
    const stem = t.slice(0, -2);
    push(stem); push(stem + 'e'); push(stem + 'l');                                           // quickly, truly (true), fully (full)
    push(t.slice(0, -1) + 'e');                                                               // gently -> gentle, despicably -> despicable
  }
  return out;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Gloss helpers
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/** Leading part-of-speech tags: "n.", "vt.", "vt.& vi.", "a. & n.", "[医]", "[网络]", "<法>" ... */
const POS_RE = /^((?:[a-z]+\.)(?:\s*&?\s*[a-z]+\.)*|\[[^\]]*\]|<[^>]{1,12}>)\s*/;

/** Splits an ECDICT Chinese gloss into lines of {pos, zh}; lines without a tag get pos ''. */
export function parseGloss(t: string): { pos: string; zh: string }[] {
  const out: { pos: string; zh: string }[] = [];
  for (const raw of t.split(/\r?\n|\r/)) {
    const line = raw.trim();
    if (!line) continue;
    const m = POS_RE.exec(line);
    if (m) out.push({ pos: m[1].replace(/\s+/g, ''), zh: line.slice(m[0].length).trim() });
    else out.push({ pos: '', zh: line });
  }
  return out;
}

/** First gloss line ("n. 房子, 住宅…") cut to at most `maxChars` characters at a sense boundary where possible. */
export function firstGloss(entry: Pick<DictEntry, 'zh'> | null | undefined, maxChars = 40): string {
  if (!entry) return '';
  const g = parseGloss(entry.zh).find((x) => x.zh.length > 0);
  if (!g) return '';
  const s = g.pos ? `${g.pos} ${g.zh}` : g.zh;
  if (maxChars <= 0 || s.length <= maxChars) return s;
  const cut = s.slice(0, Math.max(1, maxChars - 1));
  let sep = -1;
  for (const d of [', ', ',', '，', '; ', ';', '；', '、']) sep = Math.max(sep, cut.lastIndexOf(d));
  const head = sep >= Math.floor(maxChars / 3) ? cut.slice(0, sep) : cut;
  return `${head.trimEnd()}…`;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Dictionary
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

function toLevel(l: string): CefrLevel {
  return (CEFR_LEVELS as string[]).includes(l) ? (l as CefrLevel) : 'C2';
}

function toIpa(i: string): string {
  const s = i.trim().replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, '');
  return s ? `/${s}/` : '';
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Phrase list hygiene
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/** Placeholder slots in a headword ("pick sth up", "tell sb off"): never literal text, so never matchable. */
const PLACEHOLDER_RE = /(?:^| )(?:sth|sb)(?: |$)/;

/** Gloss markers that make a two-word entry an idiom rather than a free combination ("high ground": phr.). */
const IDIOM_MARKER_RE = /phr\.|习语|成语|俗语|谚|喻/;

/**
 * Comparatives/superlatives whose lemma is a different word ("better" -> "good"). Lemmatising them inside a
 * phrase would turn "better for" into the entry "good for", so they only ever match as written.
 */
const SUPPLETIVE = new Set(['better', 'best', 'worse', 'worst', 'more', 'most', 'less', 'least', 'further', 'furthest', 'farther', 'farthest']);

const EASY: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['A1', 'A2']);

/** CJK characters too common in glosses to show that a translation is built from a word's own gloss. */
const GLOSS_STOP = new Set('的地得之一个人者性化物有于为在了是等或与和及其用'.split(''));

function glossChars(t: string | undefined): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const g of parseGloss(t ?? '')) for (const ch of g.zh) if (/\p{Script=Han}/u.test(ch) && !GLOSS_STOP.has(ch)) out.add(ch);
  return out;
}

const shares = (a: Set<string>, b: Set<string>): boolean => { for (const x of a) if (b.has(x)) return true; return false; };

function posTags(t: string | undefined): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const g of parseGloss(t ?? '')) for (const p of g.pos.split('&')) if (p) out.add(p);
  return out;
}

export type PhraseClass = 'ok' | 'placeholder' | 'free-combination';

/**
 * Whether a multi-word headword is a learnable phrase. ECDICT lists many transparent compounds ("old man",
 * "old lady", "big city") whose level is only *estimated* (C1 by default for a phrase with no Collins rating),
 * which made the reader flag them as advanced phrases. Rule — a free combination, not offered as a phrase, is:
 *   - a phrase whose level does not come from a CEFR list (source 'est'),
 *   - of exactly two words, adjective (not also a preposition: "in case", "on board") + noun,
 *   - both words themselves A1-A2,
 *   - with no idiom marker in its gloss, and
 *   - whose Chinese gloss is built from the two words' own glosses ("old man" 老头儿/丈夫 from old 老的 and
 *     man 丈夫; "big city" 大城市): the meaning is the sum of the parts. Idioms whose translation shares
 *     nothing with a part ("red tape" 官样文章, "big deal", "small print") are kept.
 * Entries with a placeholder slot ("pick sth up") can never match running text and are skipped too.
 * Single-word lookups are unaffected.
 */
export function classifyPhrase(key: string, w: ReadonlyMap<string, DictRaw>): PhraseClass {
  if (PLACEHOLDER_RE.test(key)) return 'placeholder';
  const raw = w.get(key);
  if (!raw || raw.s === 'cefrj' || raw.s === 'oct') return 'ok';
  if (IDIOM_MARKER_RE.test(raw.t ?? '')) return 'ok';
  const parts = key.split(' ');
  if (parts.length !== 2) return 'ok';
  const a = w.get(parts[0]);
  const n = w.get(parts[1]);
  if (!a || !n || !EASY.has(a.l) || !EASY.has(n.l)) return 'ok';
  const aPos = posTags(a.t);
  if (!aPos.has('a.') && !aPos.has('adj.') || aPos.has('prep.')) return 'ok';
  if (!posTags(n.t).has('n.')) return 'ok';
  const own = glossChars(raw.t);
  return shares(own, glossChars(a.t)) && shares(own, glossChars(n.t)) ? 'free-combination' : 'ok';
}

/** Only the grammatical particles; a model's short gloss ("老人") must be allowed to share 人 with "man". */
const LIGHT_STOP = new Set('的地得之了是'.split(''));

/**
 * Whether a phrase the AI proposed looks like a free combination (the same rule as classifyPhrase, applied to
 * the AI's own Chinese meaning): two words, an A1-A2 adjective (not also a preposition) + an A1-A2 noun, and a
 * meaning built from both words' glosses ("old man" 老人 from 老的 + 男人). "red tape" 官僚作风 is kept.
 */
export function looksLikeFreeCombination(dict: Dictionary, words: string[], zh: string): boolean {
  if (words.length !== 2) return false;
  const a = dict.lookup(words[0]);
  const n = dict.lookup(words[1]);
  if (!a || !n || !EASY.has(a.entry.level) || !EASY.has(n.entry.level)) return false;
  const aPos = posTags(a.entry.zh);
  if ((!aPos.has('a.') && !aPos.has('adj.')) || aPos.has('prep.')) return false;
  if (!posTags(n.entry.zh).has('n.')) return false;
  const chars = (t: string): Set<string> => {
    const out = new Set<string>();
    for (const g of parseGloss(t)) for (const ch of g.zh) if (/\p{Script=Han}/u.test(ch) && !LIGHT_STOP.has(ch)) out.add(ch);
    return out;
  };
  const own = chars(zh);
  return own.size > 0 && shares(own, chars(a.entry.zh)) && shares(own, chars(n.entry.zh));
}

/** The multi-word headwords dropped from phrase matching, with the reason (for reporting and tests). */
export function droppedPhrases(data: DictData): { key: string; reason: Exclude<PhraseClass, 'ok'> }[] {
  const w = new Map<string, DictRaw>(Object.entries(data.w));
  const out: { key: string; reason: Exclude<PhraseClass, 'ok'> }[] = [];
  for (const k of w.keys()) {
    if (!k.includes(' ')) continue;
    const c = classifyPhrase(k, w);
    if (c !== 'ok') out.push({ key: k, reason: c });
  }
  return out;
}

export function createDictionary(data: DictData): Dictionary {
  // Maps rather than the raw objects: no prototype keys ("constructor" is a real headword, "__proto__" must not be)
  // and predictable hash performance for 50k keys.
  const words = new Map<string, DictRaw>(Object.entries(data.w));
  const forms = new Map<string, string>(Object.entries(data.f));
  const entries = new Map<string, DictEntry>();
  // Learnable multi-word headwords (see classifyPhrase), and their first words so phrase scans over
  // ordinary prose can fail fast.
  const phrases = new Set<string>();
  const phraseStarts = new Set<string>();
  for (const key of words.keys()) {
    const sp = key.indexOf(' ');
    if (sp <= 0 || classifyPhrase(key, words) !== 'ok') continue;
    phrases.add(key);
    phraseStarts.add(key.slice(0, sp));
  }

  const entry = (headword: string): DictEntry => {
    let e = entries.get(headword);
    if (!e) {
      const raw = words.get(headword)!;
      e = {
        word: headword,
        ipa: toIpa(raw.i ?? ''),
        zh: (raw.t ?? '').replace(/\r/g, '').trim(),
        tags: raw.g ? raw.g.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean) : [],
        frq: raw.f | 0,
        bnc: raw.b | 0,
        collins: raw.c | 0,
        oxford: raw.o === 1,
        level: toLevel(raw.l),
        levelSource: LEVEL_SOURCES.has(raw.s) ? (raw.s as DictEntry['levelSource']) : 'est',
      };
      entries.set(headword, e);
    }
    return e;
  };

  /**
   * Builds the result for a matched headword `h`. When `h` is itself a listed inflection of another headword
   * ('running' -> 'run', 'children' -> 'child', 'better' -> 'good') the vocabulary lemma is always that base
   * form, so that knowing "run" covers "running". The entry shown is h's own when it comes from a real CEFR
   * list (it is then a vocabulary item in its own right: 'boring' A1 vs 'bore' B1); when h's level is only
   * estimated the base entry is far more reliable ('children' est B2 vs 'child' A1, 'stopped' est C2).
   */
  const resolve = (h: string, via: LookupResult['via']): LookupResult => {
    const base = forms.get(h);
    if (base !== undefined && base !== h && words.has(base)) {
      if (words.get(h)!.s === 'est') return { entry: entry(base), lemma: base, via: via === 'exact' ? 'form' : via };
      return { entry: entry(h), lemma: base, via };
    }
    return { entry: entry(h), lemma: h, via };
  };

  /** The exact -> possessive -> forms -> suffix chain on an already normalised token. */
  const lookupCore = (t: string): LookupResult | null => {
    if (!t) return null;
    if (words.has(t)) return resolve(t, 'exact');
    const poss = stripPossessive(t);
    if (poss !== null) {
      const r = lookupCore(poss);
      if (r) return r.via === 'exact' ? { ...r, via: 'possessive' } : r;
    }
    const base = forms.get(t);
    if (base !== undefined && words.has(base)) return { entry: entry(base), lemma: base, via: 'form' };
    for (const c of suffixCandidates(t)) if (words.has(c)) return resolve(c, 'suffix');
    return null;
  };

  const lookup = (token: string): LookupResult | null => {
    const t = normalizeToken(token);
    if (!t) return null;
    const r = lookupCore(t);
    if (r) return r;
    const folded = foldAccents(t);
    if (folded !== t) {
      const r2 = lookupCore(folded);
      if (r2) return { ...r2, via: 'fold' };
    }
    // Old-fashioned hyphenation ("to-morrow", "co-operate") — the joined spelling is the modern headword.
    if (folded.includes('-')) {
      const r3 = lookupCore(folded.replace(/-/g, ''));
      if (r3) return { ...r3, via: 'fold' };
    }
    return null;
  };

  const lemmaOf = (token: string): string => {
    const r = lookup(token);
    if (r) return r.lemma;
    const t = foldAccents(normalizeToken(token));
    return stripPossessive(t) ?? t;
  };

  /**
   * Phrase lookup is token-for-token: the n words given must spell an n-word headword, so a phrase is never
   * matched with extra words around it. Lemmatisation is allowed only where an inflected entry form is
   * plausible: the first word (the verb of "gave up", "looking forward to") and the last word (the plural of
   * "human beings"), never a middle word and never a suppletive comparative ("better for" is not "good for").
   */
  const lookupPhrase = (ws: string[]): LookupResult | null => {
    if (ws.length < 2 || ws.length > MAX_PHRASE_WORDS) return null;
    const norm = ws.map(normalizeToken);
    if (norm.some((x) => !x || x.includes(' '))) return null;
    const first = norm[0];
    const lemFirst = SUPPLETIVE.has(first) ? first : lemmaOf(first);
    if (!phraseStarts.has(first) && !phraseStarts.has(foldAccents(first)) && !phraseStarts.has(lemFirst)) return null;
    const exact = norm.join(' ');
    if (phrases.has(exact)) return { entry: entry(exact), lemma: exact, via: 'exact' };
    const foldedWs = norm.map(foldAccents);
    const folded = foldedWs.join(' ');
    if (folded !== exact && phrases.has(folded)) return { entry: entry(folded), lemma: folded, via: 'fold' };
    const lastIdx = foldedWs.length - 1;
    const last = foldedWs[lastIdx];
    const lemLast = SUPPLETIVE.has(last) ? last : lemmaOf(last);
    const middle = foldedWs.slice(1, lastIdx);
    for (const [a, b] of [[lemFirst, last], [foldedWs[0], lemLast], [lemFirst, lemLast]]) {
      const cand = [a, ...middle, b].join(' ');
      if (cand !== folded && phrases.has(cand)) return { entry: entry(cand), lemma: cand, via: 'form' };
    }
    return null;
  };

  return { size: words.size, lookup, lookupPhrase, lemmaOf };
}
```

```ts
import type { Book, Paragraph, Token } from '@core/model';
import type { Dictionary } from './types';

/**
 * Proper-noun detection for a whole book.
 *
 * Names are never auto-explained in listening mode, so the goal is to catch the people and places of a
 * novel ("Darcy", "Elizabeth", "Netherfield") without ever swallowing ordinary words that merely start a
 * sentence ("The", "He", "Yes"). Heuristics, in order of strength:
 *
 *  1. A Title-case word directly after a title ("Mr. Darcy", "Lady Catherine", "St. James") is a name.
 *  2. A Title-case word seen at least twice where capitalisation is *not* conventional — i.e. not at the
 *     start of a sentence, nor after an opening quote, colon or sentence-final punctuation the segmenter
 *     left inside a sentence, nor inside a heading (headings are often Title Case throughout) — is a name.
 *  3. A Title-case word seen once in such a position is a name when the dictionary does not know it at all,
 *     or only knows it as an obscure term with no corpus frequency, no BNC rank and no exam tags (ECDICT
 *     glosses 'darcy' as a permeability unit and 'bennet' as a plant).
 *
 * Guards: ALL-CAPS tokens ("CHAPTER", "LONDON") are not counted — they only become names through Title-case
 * occurrences elsewhere; a word used in lower case more often than in Title-case mid-sentence is a common
 * word, not a name ("will"/"Will", "the"); 'I' and its contractions, single letters and a short stop list of
 * function words are excluded outright. Returns lower-cased, possessive-stripped, unique, sorted names.
 */

/** Titles that may be abbreviated with a period, which the segmenter usually emits as its own token. */
const ABBREV_TITLES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'mr', 'mrs', 'ms', 'dr', 'prof', 'rev', 'st', 'capt', 'col', 'gen', 'lt', 'sgt', 'mme', 'mlle', 'hon', 'messrs',
]);
/** Full-word titles; these must be directly adjacent to the name (no period in between). */
const WORD_TITLES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'miss', 'mister', 'master', 'madam', 'madame', 'mademoiselle', 'monsieur', 'sir', 'dame', 'lady', 'lord',
  'king', 'queen', 'prince', 'princess', 'duke', 'duchess', 'count', 'countess', 'earl', 'baron', 'baroness',
  'captain', 'colonel', 'general', 'lieutenant', 'sergeant', 'major', 'admiral', 'bishop', 'saint',
  'uncle', 'aunt', 'cousin', 'brother', 'sister', 'father', 'mother',
]);

/** Function words that are capitalised for structural reasons often enough to slip past the counters. */
const STOP_WORDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'the', 'a', 'an', 'and', 'but', 'or', 'nor', 'so', 'yet', 'for', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'they', 'we', 'you', 'me',
  'him', 'her', 'us', 'them', 'my', 'your', 'his', 'its', 'our', 'their', 'this', 'that', 'these', 'those',
  'there', 'here', 'then', 'than', 'when', 'where', 'why', 'how', 'what', 'who', 'whom', 'which', 'if', 'as',
  'at', 'by', 'in', 'on', 'of', 'to', 'up', 'out', 'off', 'no', 'not', 'yes', 'oh', 'ah', 'well', 'now', 'one',
  'all', 'any', 'some', 'each', 'every', 'both', 'few', 'more', 'most', 'other', 'such', 'only', 'own', 'same',
  'too', 'very', 'can', 'will', 'just', 'let', 'also', 'after', 'before', 'while', 'because', 'though',
  'although', 'until', 'since', 'with', 'from', 'into', 'about', 'again', 'once', 'never', 'always', 'perhaps',
]);

/** Punctuation after which a capital letter is conventional even mid-sentence (quotes, colon, sentence-final). */
const OPENER_RE = /["“”‘’'„‚«»‹›:.!?…]/;

const HEADING_KINDS: ReadonlySet<Paragraph['kind']> = new Set(['h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'caption']);

interface Stat { cap: number; lower: number; titled: boolean }

/** Canonical key for a word token: lower-cased, curly apostrophes straightened, possessive/period stripped. */
export function nameKey(text: string): string | null {
  let t = text.replace(/[‘’ʼ]/g, "'").toLowerCase().replace(/\.$/, '');
  if (t.endsWith("'s")) t = t.slice(0, -2);
  else if (t.endsWith("'")) t = t.slice(0, -1);
  if (t.length < 2 || t === 'i' || t.startsWith("i'")) return null;
  if (!/^\p{L}[\p{L}'-]*$/u.test(t)) return null;
  return t;
}

const startsUpper = (s: string): boolean => /^\p{Lu}/u.test(s);
const startsLower = (s: string): boolean => /^\p{Ll}/u.test(s);
/** "CHAPTER", "LONDON" — but not "I", "McDonald" or "I'm". */
const isAllCaps = (s: string): boolean => s.length >= 2 && s === s.toUpperCase() && /\p{Lu}/u.test(s);

/** True when a capital at tokens[i] is conventional: nothing but spaces/openers before it in the sentence. */
function conventionalCapital(tokens: Token[], i: number): boolean {
  for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
    const t = tokens[j];
    if (t.kind === 'space') continue;
    if (t.kind === 'punct') {
      if (OPENER_RE.test(t.text)) return true;
      continue; // commas, dashes, closing brackets: keep looking for a word
    }
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

function hasWordBefore(tokens: Token[], i: number): boolean {
  for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--) if (tokens[j].kind === 'word' || tokens[j].kind === 'number') return true;
  return false;
}

/** True when the word token before position i (scanning back from i - 1) is a title such as "Mr." or "Lady". */
function titleBefore(tokens: Token[], i: number): boolean {
  let sawPeriod = false;
  for (let j = i - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
    const t = tokens[j];
    if (t.kind === 'space') continue;
    if (t.kind === 'punct') {
      if (t.text === '.' && !sawPeriod) { sawPeriod = true; continue; }
      return false;
    }
    if (t.kind !== 'word') return false;
    const w = t.text.toLowerCase().replace(/\.$/, '');
    if (ABBREV_TITLES.has(w)) return true;
    return WORD_TITLES.has(w) && !sawPeriod;
  }
  return false;
}

const CALENDAR_WORDS = new Set(['monday', 'tuesday', 'wednesday', 'thursday', 'friday', 'saturday', 'sunday', 'january', 'february', 'march', 'april', 'may', 'june', 'july', 'august', 'september', 'october', 'november', 'december', 'christmas', 'easter']);

export function detectNames(book: Pick<Book, 'chapters'>, dict: Dictionary): string[] {
  const stats = new Map<string, Stat>();
  const stat = (key: string): Stat => {
    let s = stats.get(key);
    if (!s) { s = { cap: 0, lower: 0, titled: false }; stats.set(key, s); }
    return s;
  };

  for (const chapter of book.chapters) {
    for (const para of chapter.paragraphs) {
      const heading = HEADING_KINDS.has(para.kind);
      let prevTokens: Token[] | null = null;
      for (const sentence of para.sentences) {
        const tokens = sentence.tokens;
        for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) {
          const tok = tokens[i];
          if (tok.kind !== 'word') continue;
          const key = nameKey(tok.text);
          if (!key) continue;
          if (startsLower(tok.text)) { stat(key).lower++; continue; }
          if (!startsUpper(tok.text) || isAllCaps(tok.text)) continue;
          const st = stat(key);
          // "Mr." at the end of the previous sentence: the segmenter should repair this, but be tolerant.
          const titled = titleBefore(tokens, i) || (!hasWordBefore(tokens, i) && prevTokens !== null && titleBefore(prevTokens, prevTokens.length));
          if (titled) st.titled = true;
          if (!heading && !conventionalCapital(tokens, i)) st.cap++;
        }
        prevTokens = tokens;
      }
    }
  }

  const names: string[] = [];
  for (const [key, st] of stats) {
    // honorifics are ordinary dictionary words, not names, however often they precede one
    if (STOP_WORDS.has(key) || ABBREV_TITLES.has(key) || WORD_TITLES.has(key)) continue;
    if (!st.titled && st.cap === 0) continue;      // only ever capitalised where capitals are conventional
    if (st.lower > st.cap) continue;                // a common word that is sometimes capitalised
    if (CALENDAR_WORDS.has(key)) continue;          // days and months are always capitalised but are vocabulary
    const r = dict.lookup(key);
    // a word from a CEFR list (countries, languages, nationalities) is vocabulary unless it carries a title ("Mr Long")
    if (r && r.entry.levelSource !== 'est' && !st.titled) continue;
    if (st.titled || st.cap >= 2) { names.push(key); continue; }
    if (!r) { names.push(key); continue; }
    const e = r.entry;
    if (e.frq === 0 && e.bnc === 0 && e.tags.length === 0) names.push(key);
  }
  return names.sort();
}
```

```ts
import type { CefrLevel } from '@core/model';

export interface DictEntry {
  word: string;
  ipa: string;
  zh: string;
  tags: string[];
  frq: number;
  bnc: number;
  collins: number;
  oxford: boolean;
  level: CefrLevel;
  levelSource: 'cefrj' | 'oct' | 'est';
}

export interface LookupResult {
  entry: DictEntry;
  /** the dictionary headword that matched */
  lemma: string;
  /** how the match was found */
  via: 'exact' | 'possessive' | 'form' | 'suffix' | 'fold';
}

/**
 * Offline dictionary (ECDICT + ipa-dict + CEFR-J/Octanove), loaded from resources/dict/dict.json.gz.
 * Implemented in src/core/dict/dictionary.ts; see test/unit/dictionary.test.ts.
 */
export interface Dictionary {
  size: number;
  /** Looks up a single token as it appears in text (any case, curly or straight apostrophes). */
  lookup(token: string): LookupResult | null;
  /** Looks up a multi-word phrase (2-5 words, as they appear in the text). */
  lookupPhrase(words: string[]): LookupResult | null;
  /** The lemma used as the key for vocabulary status (lookup lemma, else the folded lower-cased token). */
  lemmaOf(token: string): string;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * EPUB importer (EPUB 2 and EPUB 3). Runs in the Electron main process.
 *
 * Pipeline: unzip (JSZip) -> META-INF/container.xml -> package document (OPF: metadata, manifest, spine)
 * -> DRM check (META-INF/encryption.xml) -> TOC labels (EPUB 3 nav document and/or EPUB 2 NCX)
 * -> every linear spine content document is parsed with the tolerant XML/XHTML parser below and its
 * <body> is flattened into plain-text paragraphs -> paragraphs are segmented and the Book assembled.
 *
 * The parser is hand-written because htmlparser2 is not a dependency of the app. It never throws on
 * malformed input: unmatched end tags are ignored, unclosed elements close implicitly, a stray '<' is
 * text, and in html mode HTML's implied end tags for <p>, <li>, <dt>/<dd>, <tr>, <td>/<th> apply.
 */
import JSZip from 'jszip';
import type { Book, Chapter, ParagraphKind } from '@core/model';
import type { ImportContext, Importer } from './types';
import { assembleParagraphs, computeStats, decodeTextBytes, normalizeWhitespace, type RawParagraph } from './text';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tolerant XML / XHTML parser
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface XmlElement {
  type: 'element';
  /** lower-cased qualified name as written, e.g. 'p', 'dc:title', 'epub:switch' */
  name: string;
  /** lower-cased attribute name -> entity-decoded value; the first occurrence of a duplicate wins */
  attrs: Map<string, string>;
  children: XmlNode[];
}
export interface XmlText { type: 'text'; text: string }
export type XmlNode = XmlElement | XmlText;

/** HTML void elements never have content, so no end tag is expected (html mode only). */
const VOID_ELEMENTS = new Set(['area', 'base', 'br', 'col', 'embed', 'hr', 'img', 'input', 'link', 'meta', 'param', 'source', 'track', 'wbr']);
/** Content is raw text up to the matching end tag, so '<' inside is not markup (html mode only). */
const RAW_TEXT_ELEMENTS = new Set(['script', 'style']);
/** Block-level elements: they start a new paragraph and their start tag implicitly closes an open <p>. */
const BLOCK_ELEMENTS = new Set([
  'address', 'article', 'aside', 'blockquote', 'body', 'caption', 'center', 'colgroup', 'dd', 'details', 'dialog', 'div', 'dl', 'dt',
  'fieldset', 'figcaption', 'figure', 'footer', 'form', 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6', 'header', 'hgroup', 'hr', 'html', 'li',
  'main', 'nav', 'ol', 'p', 'pre', 'section', 'summary', 'table', 'tbody', 'td', 'tfoot', 'th', 'thead', 'tr', 'ul',
]);
/** Deeper nesting than this is flattened (a malformed document with thousands of unclosed tags must not blow the stack). */
const MAX_DEPTH = 512;

/** An implied end tag: a start tag of `closes` while one is open (without passing a `stopAt` ancestor) closes it. */
interface ImpliedEnd { closes: Set<string>; stopAt: Set<string> }
const LIST_ITEM_END: ImpliedEnd = { closes: new Set(['li']), stopAt: new Set(['ul', 'ol', 'menu']) };
const DEFINITION_END: ImpliedEnd = { closes: new Set(['dt', 'dd']), stopAt: new Set(['dl']) };
const ROW_END: ImpliedEnd = { closes: new Set(['tr', 'td', 'th']), stopAt: new Set(['table', 'tbody', 'thead', 'tfoot']) };
const CELL_END: ImpliedEnd = { closes: new Set(['td', 'th']), stopAt: new Set(['tr', 'table']) };
const PARAGRAPH_END: ImpliedEnd = { closes: new Set(['p']), stopAt: BLOCK_ELEMENTS };
const IMPLIED_ENDS = new Map<string, ImpliedEnd>([
  ['li', LIST_ITEM_END], ['dt', DEFINITION_END], ['dd', DEFINITION_END], ['tr', ROW_END], ['td', CELL_END], ['th', CELL_END],
]);

const CH_BANG = 0x21, CH_SLASH = 0x2f, CH_QUESTION = 0x3f, CH_GT = 0x3e, CH_EQ = 0x3d, CH_DQUOTE = 0x22, CH_SQUOTE = 0x27;

function isWhitespace(c: number): boolean { return c === 0x20 || c === 0x0a || c === 0x0d || c === 0x09 || c === 0x0c; }
function isNameStart(c: number): boolean { return (c >= 0x41 && c <= 0x5a) || (c >= 0x61 && c <= 0x7a) || c === 0x5f || c === 0x3a || c >= 0x80; }
function isNameEnd(c: number): boolean { return isWhitespace(c) || c === CH_SLASH || c === CH_GT; }
function isAttrNameEnd(c: number): boolean { return isNameEnd(c) || c === CH_EQ; }

/** Pops the stack down to (and including) the innermost element the rule closes, if any. */
function applyImpliedEnd(stack: XmlElement[], rule: ImpliedEnd): void {
  let cut = -1;
  for (let k = stack.length - 1; k > 0; k--) {
    const name = stack[k].name;
    if (rule.closes.has(name)) cut = k;
    else if (rule.stopAt.has(name)) break;
  }
  if (cut !== -1) stack.length = cut;
}

/** End tag: pops to the nearest open element with that name; an unmatched end tag is ignored. */
function closeElement(stack: XmlElement[], name: string): void {
  for (let k = stack.length - 1; k > 0; k--) {
    if (stack[k].name === name) { stack.length = k; return; }
  }
}

/** Skips '<!DOCTYPE ...>' including an internal subset in [ ]. Returns the index after '>'. */
function skipDeclaration(src: string, start: number): number {
  let depth = 0;
  for (let k = start + 2; k < src.length; k++) {
    const c = src.charCodeAt(k);
    if (c === 0x5b) depth++; // [
    else if (c === 0x5d) depth--; // ]
    else if (c === CH_GT && depth <= 0) return k + 1;
  }
  return src.length;
}

/** Index of '</name' (case-insensitive, followed by a delimiter) at or after `from`, or -1. */
function findEndTag(src: string, from: number, name: string): number {
  let k = from;
  for (;;) {
    k = src.indexOf('</', k);
    if (k === -1) return -1;
    const after = k + 2 + name.length;
    if (src.slice(k + 2, after).toLowerCase() === name && (after >= src.length || isNameEnd(src.charCodeAt(after)))) return k;
    k += 2;
  }
}

interface StartTag { name: string; attrs: Map<string, string>; selfClosing: boolean; end: number }

/** Reads a start tag beginning at `start` ('<'). Tolerates unquoted/valueless attributes, '>' inside quotes, EOF. */
function readStartTag(src: string, start: number): StartTag {
  const n = src.length;
  let i = start + 1;
  const nameStart = i;
  while (i < n && !isNameEnd(src.charCodeAt(i))) i++;
  const name = src.slice(nameStart, i).toLowerCase();
  const attrs = new Map<string, string>();
  let selfClosing = false;
  for (;;) {
    while (i < n && isWhitespace(src.charCodeAt(i))) i++;
    if (i >= n) return { name, attrs, selfClosing, end: n };
    const c = src.charCodeAt(i);
    if (c === CH_GT) return { name, attrs, selfClosing, end: i + 1 };
    if (c === CH_SLASH) { selfClosing = true; i++; continue; }
    const attrStart = i;
    while (i < n && !isAttrNameEnd(src.charCodeAt(i))) i++;
    if (i === attrStart) { i++; continue; } // stray character such as a lone quote
    const attrName = src.slice(attrStart, i).toLowerCase();
    selfClosing = false;
    while (i < n && isWhitespace(src.charCodeAt(i))) i++;
    let value = '';
    if (i < n && src.charCodeAt(i) === CH_EQ) {
      i++;
      while (i < n && isWhitespace(src.charCodeAt(i))) i++;
      const q = src.charCodeAt(i);
      if (q === CH_DQUOTE || q === CH_SQUOTE) {
        let close = src.indexOf(String.fromCharCode(q), i + 1);
        // A raw '<' cannot occur inside an attribute value, so the quote was never closed: the "value"
        // would swallow the following markup. Recover at the end of the tag instead.
        if (close !== -1 && src.slice(i + 1, close).indexOf('<') !== -1) close = -1;
        if (close === -1) {
          const gt = src.indexOf('>', i + 1);
          value = src.slice(i + 1, gt === -1 ? n : gt);
          i = gt === -1 ? n : gt;
        } else {
          value = src.slice(i + 1, close);
          i = close + 1;
        }
      } else {
        const valueStart = i;
        while (i < n && !isWhitespace(src.charCodeAt(i)) && src.charCodeAt(i) !== CH_GT) i++;
        value = src.slice(valueStart, i);
      }
    }
    if (!attrs.has(attrName)) attrs.set(attrName, decodeEntities(value));
  }
}

/**
 * Parses XML or XHTML into a tree rooted at a synthetic '#document' element. Never throws.
 * `html` enables HTML rules: void elements, raw-text <script>/<style>, implied end tags.
 */
export function parseXml(src: string, html = false): XmlElement {
  const root: XmlElement = { type: 'element', name: '#document', attrs: new Map(), children: [] };
  const stack: XmlElement[] = [root];
  const n = src.length;
  let i = 0;

  const addText = (text: string, raw: boolean): void => {
    if (text.length === 0) return;
    stack[stack.length - 1].children.push({ type: 'text', text: raw ? text : decodeEntities(text) });
  };

  while (i < n) {
    const lt = src.indexOf('<', i);
    if (lt === -1) { addText(src.slice(i), false); break; }
    if (lt > i) addText(src.slice(i, lt), false);
    i = lt;
    const next = src.charCodeAt(i + 1);
    if (next === CH_BANG) {
      if (src.startsWith('<!--', i)) {
        const e = src.indexOf('-->', i + 4);
        i = e === -1 ? n : e + 3;
      } else if (src.startsWith('<![CDATA[', i)) {
        const e = src.indexOf(']]>', i + 9);
        addText(src.slice(i + 9, e === -1 ? n : e), true);
        i = e === -1 ? n : e + 3;
      } else {
        i = skipDeclaration(src, i);
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (next === CH_QUESTION) { // <?xml ...?> and other processing instructions
      const e = src.indexOf('?>', i + 2);
      i = e === -1 ? n : e + 2;
      continue;
    }
    if (next === CH_SLASH) {
      const e = src.indexOf('>', i + 2);
      if (e === -1) { addText(src.slice(i), false); break; }
      const name = src.slice(i + 2, e).trim().toLowerCase().split(/\s/, 1)[0];
      closeElement(stack, name);
      i = e + 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (!isNameStart(next)) { addText('<', false); i++; continue; } // "a < b" in text

    const tag = readStartTag(src, i);
    i = tag.end;
    if (html) {
      if (BLOCK_ELEMENTS.has(tag.name)) applyImpliedEnd(stack, PARAGRAPH_END);
      const rule = IMPLIED_ENDS.get(tag.name);
      if (rule) applyImpliedEnd(stack, rule);
    }
    const el: XmlElement = { type: 'element', name: tag.name, attrs: tag.attrs, children: [] };
    stack[stack.length - 1].children.push(el);
    if (tag.selfClosing || (html && VOID_ELEMENTS.has(tag.name))) continue;
    if (html && RAW_TEXT_ELEMENTS.has(tag.name)) {
      const close = findEndTag(src, i, tag.name);
      el.children.push({ type: 'text', text: src.slice(i, close === -1 ? n : close) });
      if (close === -1) i = n;
      else { const e = src.indexOf('>', close); i = e === -1 ? n : e + 1; }
      continue;
    }
    if (stack.length < MAX_DEPTH) stack.push(el);
  }
  return root;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Character references
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const NAMED_ENTITIES = new Map<string, string>(Object.entries({

}));

/** Browsers map numeric references in the C1 range to Windows-1252 glyphs ("&#146;" is a right single quote). */
const CP1252_C1: Record<number, number> = {
  0x80: 0x20ac, 0x82: 0x201a, 0x83: 0x0192, 0x84: 0x201e, 0x85: 0x2026, 0x86: 0x2020, 0x87: 0x2021, 0x88: 0x02c6, 0x89: 0x2030, 0x8a: 0x0160,
  0x8b: 0x2039, 0x8c: 0x0152, 0x8e: 0x017d, 0x91: 0x2018, 0x92: 0x2019, 0x93: 0x201c, 0x94: 0x201d, 0x95: 0x2022, 0x96: 0x2013, 0x97: 0x2014,
  0x98: 0x02dc, 0x99: 0x2122, 0x9a: 0x0161, 0x9b: 0x203a, 0x9c: 0x0153, 0x9e: 0x017e, 0x9f: 0x0178,
};

const ENTITY = /&(#[xX][0-9a-fA-F]{1,6}|#[0-9]{1,7}|[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,31});/g;

/** Decodes numeric and the common named character references; unknown references stay as written. */
export function decodeEntities(s: string): string {
  if (s.indexOf('&') === -1) return s;
  return s.replace(ENTITY, (match: string, body: string): string => {
    if (body.charCodeAt(0) === 0x23) {
      const hex = body.charCodeAt(1) === 0x78 || body.charCodeAt(1) === 0x58;
      let cp = hex ? parseInt(body.slice(2), 16) : parseInt(body.slice(1), 10);
      if (cp >= 0x80 && cp <= 0x9f && CP1252_C1[cp] !== undefined) cp = CP1252_C1[cp];
      if (!Number.isFinite(cp) || cp === 0 || cp > 0x10ffff || (cp >= 0xd800 && cp <= 0xdfff)) return '�';
      return String.fromCodePoint(cp);
    }
    const named = NAMED_ENTITIES.get(body);
    return named !== undefined ? named : match;
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tree helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** 'dc:title' -> 'title' */
export function localName(name: string): string {
  const i = name.lastIndexOf(':');
  return i === -1 ? name : name.slice(i + 1);
}

function findFirst(root: XmlElement, local: string): XmlElement | null {
  const stack: XmlElement[] = [root];
  while (stack.length) {
    const el = stack.pop()!;
    if (el !== root && localName(el.name) === local) return el;
    for (let k = el.children.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) {
      const c = el.children[k];
      if (c.type === 'element') stack.push(c);
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/** All descendants with that local name, in document order. */
function findAll(root: XmlElement, local: string): XmlElement[] {
  const out: XmlElement[] = [];
  const stack: XmlElement[] = [root];
  while (stack.length) {
    const el = stack.pop()!;
    if (el !== root && localName(el.name) === local) out.push(el);
    for (let k = el.children.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) {
      const c = el.children[k];
      if (c.type === 'element') stack.push(c);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function childElements(el: XmlElement, local: string): XmlElement[] {
  const out: XmlElement[] = [];
  for (const c of el.children) if (c.type === 'element' && localName(c.name) === local) out.push(c);
  return out;
}

function textContent(el: XmlElement): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  const stack: XmlNode[] = [el];
  while (stack.length) {
    const node = stack.pop()!;
    if (node.type === 'text') { parts.push(node.text); continue; }
    for (let k = node.children.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) stack.push(node.children[k]);
  }
  return parts.join('');
}

function hasDescendant(el: XmlElement, local: string): boolean { return findFirst(el, local) !== null; }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// XHTML -> paragraphs
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Elements whose content is never read: metadata, code, media, ruby annotations, EPUB switch cases. */
const SKIP_ELEMENTS = new Set([
  'script', 'style', 'head', 'title', 'template', 'svg', 'math', 'rt', 'rp', 'img', 'audio', 'video', 'object', 'iframe',
  'noscript', 'canvas', 'map', 'input', 'select', 'textarea', 'button', 'epub:case',
]);
/** epub:type tokens that mark navigation lists and notes (whole element skipped). */
const SKIP_EPUB_TYPES = new Set(['toc', 'landmarks', 'page-list', 'lot', 'loi', 'loa', 'lov', 'pagebreak', 'noteref']);
const SKIP_EPUB_TYPE_PREFIXES = ['footnote', 'endnote', 'rearnote'];
const SKIP_ROLES = new Set(['doc-pagebreak', 'doc-footnote', 'doc-endnote', 'doc-noteref', 'doc-toc', 'doc-pagelist']);
const HEADING_KIND: Record<string, ParagraphKind> = { h1: 'h1', h2: 'h2', h3: 'h3', h4: 'h3', h5: 'h3', h6: 'h3' };
const FOOTNOTE_MARKER = /^[\d*†‡§¶]{1,4}$/;

function skipEpubType(value: string): boolean {
  for (const token of value.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/)) {
    if (SKIP_EPUB_TYPES.has(token)) return true;
    for (const prefix of SKIP_EPUB_TYPE_PREFIXES) if (token.startsWith(prefix)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

function shouldSkip(el: XmlElement): boolean {
  if (SKIP_ELEMENTS.has(el.name) || SKIP_ELEMENTS.has(localName(el.name))) return true;
  if (el.attrs.has('hidden')) return true;
  const role = el.attrs.get('role');
  if (role && role.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).some((r) => SKIP_ROLES.has(r))) return true;
  for (const [name, value] of el.attrs) {
    if (name === 'epub:type' || (name.endsWith(':type') && name !== 'xlink:type')) {
      if (skipEpubType(value)) return true;
    }
  }
  // "<sup><a href="#fn1">1</a></sup>": an EPUB 2 style footnote marker; "mc<sup>2</sup>" is kept.
  if (localName(el.name) === 'sup' && hasDescendant(el, 'a') && FOOTNOTE_MARKER.test(normalizeWhitespace(textContent(el)))) return true;
  return false;
}

/** The kind for inline text directly inside a block element; `inherited` comes from an enclosing li/blockquote. */
function looseKindFor(name: string, inherited: ParagraphKind): ParagraphKind {
  const heading = HEADING_KIND[name];
  if (heading) return heading;
  if (name === 'pre') return 'pre';
  if (name === 'figcaption' || name === 'caption') return 'caption';
  if (name === 'li') return 'li';
  if (name === 'blockquote') return 'blockquote';
  return inherited;
}

/** The kind that p/div descendants of this block inherit: li and blockquote (innermost wins) and the strong kinds. */
function inheritedKindFor(name: string, own: ParagraphKind, inherited: ParagraphKind): ParagraphKind {
  if (name === 'li' || name === 'blockquote' || name === 'pre' || name === 'figcaption' || name === 'caption' || HEADING_KIND[name]) return own;
  return inherited;
}

/**
 * Flattens an XHTML document's <body> into paragraphs. Blocks never merge; inline elements concatenate
 * without added spaces ('word<i>italic</i>word' -> 'worditalicword'); <br> is a space; whitespace is
 * collapsed. Loose text directly inside a container (div, section, body) becomes its own paragraph.
 */
export function xhtmlToParagraphs(html: string): RawParagraph[] {
  const doc = parseXml(html, true);
  const out: RawParagraph[] = [];
  let pieces: string[] = [];
  let runKind: ParagraphKind = 'p';

  const flush = (): void => {
    if (pieces.length === 0) return;
    const text = normalizeWhitespace(pieces.join(''));
    pieces = [];
    if (text.length > 0) out.push({ kind: runKind, text });
  };

  const walkBlock = (el: XmlElement, loose: ParagraphKind, inherited: ParagraphKind): void => {
    flush();
    runKind = loose;
    for (const child of el.children) {
      if (child.type === 'text') { pieces.push(child.text); continue; }
      if (shouldSkip(child)) continue;
      const name = localName(child.name);
      if (BLOCK_ELEMENTS.has(name)) {
        const kind = looseKindFor(name, inherited);
        walkBlock(child, kind, inheritedKindFor(name, kind, inherited));
        runKind = loose;
      } else {
        walkInline(child, loose, inherited);
      }
    }
    flush();
  };

  const walkInline = (el: XmlElement, loose: ParagraphKind, inherited: ParagraphKind): void => {
    const name = localName(el.name);
    if (name === 'br') { pieces.push(' '); return; }
    if (name === 'q') pieces.push('“');
    for (const child of el.children) {
      if (child.type === 'text') { pieces.push(child.text); continue; }
      if (shouldSkip(child)) continue;
      const childName = localName(child.name);
      if (BLOCK_ELEMENTS.has(childName)) { // a block inside an inline (valid for <a>, common in sloppy markup)
        const kind = looseKindFor(childName, inherited);
        walkBlock(child, kind, inheritedKindFor(childName, kind, inherited));
        runKind = loose;
      } else {
        walkInline(child, loose, inherited);
      }
    }
    if (name === 'q') pieces.push('”');
  };

  walkBlock(findFirst(doc, 'body') ?? doc, 'p', 'p');
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Paths and zip access
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function dirOf(path: string): string {
  const i = path.lastIndexOf('/');
  return i === -1 ? '' : path.slice(0, i + 1);
}

/** Resolves an href against a directory inside the zip: strips fragment/query, %-decodes, normalises '.' and '..'. */
export function resolvePath(baseDir: string, href: string): string {
  let h = href.trim();
  const hash = h.indexOf('#');
  if (hash !== -1) h = h.slice(0, hash);
  const query = h.indexOf('?');
  if (query !== -1) h = h.slice(0, query);
  try { h = decodeURIComponent(h); } catch { /* malformed %-sequence: keep as written */ }
  h = h.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  const joined = h.startsWith('/') ? h.slice(1) : baseDir + h;
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const seg of joined.split('/')) {
    if (seg === '' || seg === '.') continue;
    if (seg === '..') out.pop(); else out.push(seg);
  }
  return out.join('/');
}

/** Decodes an XML/XHTML entry: BOM-aware UTF-8/UTF-16, honouring a legacy encoding named in the XML declaration. */
function decodeXmlBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  if (bytes.length >= 2 && ((bytes[0] === 0xff && bytes[1] === 0xfe) || (bytes[0] === 0xfe && bytes[1] === 0xff))) return decodeTextBytes(bytes);
  const head = String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(0, Math.min(bytes.length, 160)));
  const m = /^\s*<\?xml[^>]*encoding=["']([\w.:-]+)["']/i.exec(head);
  if (m && !/^utf-?8$/i.test(m[1])) {
    try { return new TextDecoder(m[1]).decode(bytes); } catch { /* unknown label: fall through to UTF-8 */ }
  }
  return decodeTextBytes(bytes);
}

/** Zip entries by path, with a case-insensitive fallback for packages whose hrefs disagree with the entry names. */
class ZipFiles {
  private lower: Map<string, string> | null = null;
  constructor(private readonly zip: JSZip) {}

  entry(path: string): JSZip.JSZipObject | null {
    const direct = this.zip.file(path);
    if (direct) return direct;
    if (!this.lower) {
      this.lower = new Map();
      for (const name of Object.keys(this.zip.files)) if (!this.zip.files[name].dir) this.lower.set(name.toLowerCase(), name);
    }
    const alt = this.lower.get(path.toLowerCase());
    return alt ? this.zip.file(alt) : null;
  }

  async readText(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
    const e = this.entry(path);
    if (!e) return null;
    return decodeXmlBytes(await e.async('uint8array'));
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Package document (OPF)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface ManifestItem { id: string; path: string; mediaType: string; properties: string[] }

interface EpubPackage {
  title?: string;
  author?: string;
  language?: string;
  manifest: ManifestItem[];
  byId: Map<string, ManifestItem>;
  byPath: Map<string, ManifestItem>;
  /** linear spine items, in reading order */
  spine: ManifestItem[];
  /** spine@toc: the NCX item id (EPUB 2) */
  tocId?: string;
}

const CONTENT_MEDIA_TYPES = new Set(['application/xhtml+xml', 'text/html', 'application/xml', 'text/xml']);
const CONTENT_EXTENSION = /\.(xhtml|html|htm|xml)$/i;

function isContentDocument(item: ManifestItem): boolean {
  if (item.mediaType === 'application/xhtml+xml' || item.mediaType === 'text/html') return true;
  return (item.mediaType === '' || CONTENT_MEDIA_TYPES.has(item.mediaType)) && CONTENT_EXTENSION.test(item.path);
}

function findRootfile(container: XmlElement): string | null {
  const rootfiles = findAll(container, 'rootfile');
  const opf = rootfiles.find((r) => (r.attrs.get('media-type') ?? '').toLowerCase() === 'application/oebps-package+xml') ?? rootfiles[0];
  const fullPath = opf?.attrs.get('full-path');
  return fullPath ? resolvePath('', fullPath) : null;
}

function parsePackage(doc: XmlElement, opfDir: string): EpubPackage {
  const pkg: EpubPackage = { manifest: [], byId: new Map(), byPath: new Map(), spine: [] };

  const metadata = findFirst(doc, 'metadata');
  if (metadata) {
    const text = (local: string): string[] => findAll(metadata, local).map((el) => normalizeWhitespace(textContent(el))).filter((t) => t.length > 0);
    pkg.title = text('title')[0];
    const creators = [...new Set(text('creator'))];
    if (creators.length) pkg.author = creators.join(', ');
    pkg.language = text('language')[0];
  }

  const manifest = findFirst(doc, 'manifest');
  if (manifest) {
    for (const item of childElements(manifest, 'item')) {
      const id = item.attrs.get('id');
      const href = item.attrs.get('href');
      if (!id || !href) continue;
      const entry: ManifestItem = {
        id,
        path: resolvePath(opfDir, href),
        mediaType: (item.attrs.get('media-type') ?? '').trim().toLowerCase(),
        properties: (item.attrs.get('properties') ?? '').toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean),
      };
      pkg.manifest.push(entry);
      if (!pkg.byId.has(id)) pkg.byId.set(id, entry);
      if (!pkg.byPath.has(entry.path)) pkg.byPath.set(entry.path, entry);
    }
  }

  const spine = findFirst(doc, 'spine');
  if (spine) {
    pkg.tocId = spine.attrs.get('toc');
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const ref of childElements(spine, 'itemref')) {
      if ((ref.attrs.get('linear') ?? 'yes').trim().toLowerCase() === 'no') continue;
      const idref = ref.attrs.get('idref');
      const item = idref ? pkg.byId.get(idref) : undefined;
      if (!item || seen.has(item.path)) continue;
      seen.add(item.path);
      pkg.spine.push(item);
    }
  }
  return pkg;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// DRM detection
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Font obfuscation is not DRM: the text stays readable. */
const FONT_OBFUSCATION_ALGORITHMS = new Set(['http://www.idpf.org/2008/embedding', 'http://ns.adobe.com/pdf/enc#RC']);

export const DRM_ERROR_MESSAGE = 'This EPUB is protected by DRM and cannot be opened';

/** Throws when META-INF/encryption.xml encrypts any content document (Adobe ADEPT, Apple FairPlay, LCP, ...). */
async function assertNotDrm(files: ZipFiles, pkg: EpubPackage): Promise<void> {
  const xml = await files.readText('META-INF/encryption.xml');
  if (xml === null) return;
  const spinePaths = new Set(pkg.spine.map((it) => it.path));
  for (const data of findAll(parseXml(xml), 'encrypteddata')) {
    const method = findFirst(data, 'encryptionmethod');
    const algorithm = method?.attrs.get('algorithm') ?? '';
    if (FONT_OBFUSCATION_ALGORITHMS.has(algorithm)) continue;
    const uri = findFirst(data, 'cipherreference')?.attrs.get('uri');
    if (!uri) continue;
    const path = resolvePath('', uri);
    const item = pkg.byPath.get(path);
    const isContent = item ? isContentDocument(item) : CONTENT_EXTENSION.test(path);
    if (isContent || spinePaths.has(path)) throw new Error(DRM_ERROR_MESSAGE);
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Table of contents labels
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** EPUB 3 navigation document: <nav epub:type="toc"> links, resolved against the nav document's directory. */
function collectNavLabels(doc: XmlElement, navDir: string, labels: Map<string, string>): void {
  const navs = findAll(doc, 'nav');
  let tocs = navs.filter((nav) => [...nav.attrs].some(([k, v]) => k.endsWith('type') && v.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).includes('toc')));
  if (tocs.length === 0) tocs = navs.slice(0, 1);
  for (const nav of tocs) {
    for (const a of findAll(nav, 'a')) {
      const href = a.attrs.get('href');
      if (!href) continue;
      const path = resolvePath(navDir, href);
      const label = normalizeWhitespace(textContent(a));
      if (label && !labels.has(path)) labels.set(path, label); // the first (outermost) entry for a document wins
    }
  }
}

/** EPUB 2 NCX: navPoint/navLabel/text + content@src, in document order (parents before children). */
function collectNcxLabels(doc: XmlElement, ncxDir: string, labels: Map<string, string>): void {
  for (const point of findAll(doc, 'navpoint')) {
    const label = childElements(point, 'navlabel')[0];
    const src = childElements(point, 'content')[0]?.attrs.get('src');
    if (!label || !src) continue;
    const text = normalizeWhitespace(textContent(label));
    const path = resolvePath(ncxDir, src);
    if (text && !labels.has(path)) labels.set(path, text);
  }
}

async function readTocLabels(files: ZipFiles, pkg: EpubPackage): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
  const labels = new Map<string, string>();
  const nav = pkg.manifest.find((it) => it.properties.includes('nav'));
  if (nav) {
    const html = await files.readText(nav.path);
    if (html !== null) collectNavLabels(parseXml(html, true), dirOf(nav.path), labels);
  }
  const ncx = (pkg.tocId ? pkg.byId.get(pkg.tocId) : undefined) ?? pkg.manifest.find((it) => it.mediaType === 'application/x-dtbncx+xml');
  if (ncx) {
    const xml = await files.readText(ncx.path);
    if (xml !== null) collectNcxLabels(parseXml(xml), dirOf(ncx.path), labels);
  }
  return labels;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Importer
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function isHeading(kind: ParagraphKind): boolean { return kind === 'h1' || kind === 'h2' || kind === 'h3'; }

export const epubImporter: Importer = {
  kind: 'epub',
  async importBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, ctx: ImportContext): Promise<Book> {
    let zip: JSZip;
    try {
      zip = await JSZip.loadAsync(bytes);
    } catch {
      throw new Error('Not a valid EPUB: the file is not a readable zip archive');
    }
    const files = new ZipFiles(zip);

    const containerXml = await files.readText('META-INF/container.xml');
    if (containerXml === null) throw new Error('Not a valid EPUB: META-INF/container.xml is missing');
    const opfPath = findRootfile(parseXml(containerXml));
    if (!opfPath) throw new Error('Not a valid EPUB: container.xml names no package document');
    const opfXml = await files.readText(opfPath);
    if (opfXml === null) throw new Error(`Not a valid EPUB: package document "${opfPath}" is missing`);
    const pkg = parsePackage(parseXml(opfXml), dirOf(opfPath));

    await assertNotDrm(files, pkg);
    const tocLabels = await readTocLabels(files, pkg);

    const chapters: Chapter[] = [];
    for (const item of pkg.spine) {
      if (!isContentDocument(item)) continue;
      const html = await files.readText(item.path);
      if (html === null) continue;
      const paragraphs = assembleParagraphs(xhtmlToParagraphs(html), ctx.segmenter);
      if (paragraphs.length === 0) continue; // nothing to read: the item contributes no chapter
      const index = chapters.length;
      const heading = paragraphs.find((p) => isHeading(p.kind));
      const title = heading?.text ?? tocLabels.get(item.path) ?? `Chapter ${index + 1}`;
      chapters.push({ index, title, paragraphs });
    }
    if (chapters.length === 0) throw new Error('This EPUB contains no readable text');

    const book: Book = {
      id: ctx.id,
      title: pkg.title ?? chapters[0].title,
      source: { kind: 'epub', importedAt: new Date().toISOString() },
      chapters,
      names: [],
      stats: computeStats(chapters),
    };
    if (pkg.author) book.author = pkg.author;
    if (pkg.language) book.language = pkg.language;
    if (ctx.sourcePath) book.source.path = ctx.sourcePath;
    return book;
  },
};
```

### `src/core/import/pdf.ts` (988 lines)

```ts
import path from 'node:path';
import type { Book, Chapter, Paragraph, ParagraphKind } from '@core/model';
import type { ImportContext, Importer } from './types';

/**
 * PDF importer (Electron main process, Node; pdf.js legacy build, no worker).
 *
 * pdf.js hands us positioned text runs per page, optionally with marked-content tags. Turning those
 * into paragraphs is a heuristic pipeline. Every stage is a pure function over plain data, so the unit
 * tests feed hand-built pages as well as real files (`buildBook` is the pure entry point, `readPdf`
 * the pdf.js glue, `pdfImporter` the combination).
 *
 *  1. Runs -> lines. Within a page, runs are grouped by baseline (transform[5]) within half a font
 *     size and ordered by x. Between two runs the horizontal gap (next x minus the previous run's
 *     x + width, in units of the line's font size) decides the spacing: below 0.15 em the runs are one
 *     word (kerning, a font change inside a word, a ligature drawn as its own glyph run), from 0.25 em
 *     on they are separated by a space, and in between a space is assumed unless a ligature glyph is
 *     involved. Ligature glyphs (U+FB00-FB06) are what pdf.js hands us when a font draws "fi" as one
 *     glyph; their advance is often misreported, so pdf.js itself splits "fi ght" with a space and a
 *     following run looks far away. A run ending in fi/fl/ffi/ffl/ft/st (no English word ends with
 *     these) is therefore joined to a following lowercase run across gaps up to 0.75 em, and a run
 *     starting with ff/ffi/ffl/ft/st (no English word starts with these) to a preceding letter; the
 *     same two rules remove spaces pdf.js put inside one run. A run that pdf.js marks `hasEOL` ends
 *     a line, so a run after it on the same baseline always gets a space. Afterwards the ligatures are
 *     NFKC-normalised to plain letters and soft hyphens (U+00AD) inside a line are removed.
 *     Two-column pages are detected from a clear vertical gap in the x coverage of the runs: the page
 *     is then read left column top-to-bottom, then right column; a full-width line (a title spanning
 *     both columns) splits the columns into bands that are read one after the other.
 *     On tagged pages (a structure tree, or P/H marked content in the content stream) the structure
 *     element decides which runs belong to one paragraph, and /Artifact content (running headers,
 *     page numbers) is dropped outright.
 *  2. Running headers/footers. A line whose text repeats at the same height on >= 3 pages (>= 60% of
 *     the pages of a short document) is dropped. In the top/bottom 10% of the page the comparison
 *     also ignores digits ("Page 3 of 10"), and lines that are nothing but a page number (digits,
 *     roman numerals, "Page 3", "- 3 -") are dropped too. Headings outside that band are never
 *     treated as running lines, so "Chapter 1/2/3" at the top of chapter pages survives.
 *  3. Body statistics: the character-weighted median font size is the body size; the median
 *     baseline-to-baseline distance (ignoring big gaps) is the leading; the mean advance per
 *     character of body-sized lines is the character width.
 *  4. Headings: lines whose font size is >= 1.25 x the body size, or short ALL-CAPS lines. Adjacent
 *     heading lines of the same size merge into one heading. The largest size used by at least two
 *     headings is the chapter level (h1), anything larger (a title page) is h1 too, the next size
 *     down is h2, everything else h3.
 *  5. Lines -> paragraphs (untagged content). A new paragraph starts at a heading, at a bullet, when
 *     the gap to the previous line is clearly bigger than the leading (> 1.4 x body size and > 1.15 x
 *     leading), when the line is indented by more than 1.5 character widths after a line ending in
 *     terminal punctuation, or after a short line (< 65% of the column width) ending in terminal
 *     punctuation. Across column and page boundaries only the last two rules apply, so paragraphs
 *     continue across pages. Tagged paragraphs continue across a page boundary only when the previous
 *     line has no terminal punctuation or the next line starts with a lowercase letter.
 *  6. Lines are joined with a space. A line ending in a hyphen is joined to a following line that
 *     starts with a lowercase letter without a space; the hyphen is KEPT when the compound occurs
 *     hyphenated elsewhere in the document ("well-known") or when the part before it is a single
 *     letter or ALL CAPS ("T-shirt"), REMOVED when the closed form occurs elsewhere, and otherwise
 *     REMOVED ("hyphen-" + "ated" -> "hyphenated"). Soft hyphens (U+00AD) at a line end are always
 *     removed. A hyphen before a capital or a digit is kept with no space ("Jean-" + "Paul").
 *  7. Chapters start at h1 headings. With fewer than two h1 headings the document is cut into
 *     15-page chunks titled "Pages 1-15" etc., or is a single chapter when it is shorter than that.
 *  8. Title: PDF metadata title (ignoring producer placeholders such as "untitled" and stripping
 *     "Microsoft Word - x.docx"), else the first heading, else the file name.
 *
 * Rejected documents: image-only PDFs (fewer than 40 text characters per page on average) and text
 * layers that do not decode to English (fonts without a usable ToUnicode map give private-use or
 * shifted characters; non-Latin documents are refused for the same reason).
 *
 * Not handled in v1: rotated text (skipped), OCR, footnotes, tables, page numbers in the Book model.
 */

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Input model: structurally what pdf.js returns, declared here so the pipeline is testable without it.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface RawTextItem {
  str: string;
  /** [a, b, c, d, e, f]; e/f are the baseline origin in PDF points (y grows upwards). */
  transform: number[];
  width: number;
  height: number;
  hasEOL?: boolean;
  fontName?: string;
  dir?: string;
}
export interface RawMarkedContent {
  type: string; // 'beginMarkedContent' | 'beginMarkedContentProps' | 'endMarkedContent'
  id?: string | null;
  tag?: string;
}
export type RawItem = RawTextItem | RawMarkedContent;

/** pdf.js `page.getStructTree()` node shapes. */
export interface StructContent { type: string; id: string }
export interface StructNode { role: string; children: Array<StructNode | StructContent> }

export interface RawPage {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  /** `getTextContent({ includeMarkedContent: true }).items` */
  items: RawItem[];
  structTree?: StructNode | null;
}

export interface PdfInput {
  pages: RawPage[];
  /** metadata title/author as pdf.js reports them (may be placeholders; cleaned here) */
  title?: string | null;
  author?: string | null;
}

export const SCANNED_ERROR = 'This PDF has no text layer (scanned images). OCR is not supported yet.';
export const GARBAGE_ERROR =
  'The text layer of this PDF cannot be read: its fonts have no usable character mapping, or the text is not English. ' +
  'Try re-exporting the PDF or using an EPUB.';

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tuning constants (see the module comment for what each one does)
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE = 40;
const FOREIGN_TOKEN_RATIO = 0.4;
const MIN_COMMON_WORD_RATIO = 0.08;
const BASELINE_TOLERANCE = 0.5; // x font size
const TIGHT_GAP_EM = 0.15; // below: runs are one word
const WORD_GAP_EM = 0.25; // from here on: a space between the runs
const LIGATURE_GAP_EM = 0.75; // a ligature glyph with a misreported advance leaves a gap up to this
const HEADING_SIZE_RATIO = 1.25;
const PARAGRAPH_GAP_RATIO = 1.4; // x body size
const LEADING_GAP_RATIO = 1.15; // x typical leading
const INDENT_CHAR_WIDTHS = 1.5;
const SHORT_LINE_RATIO = 0.65;

const PAGES_PER_CHUNK = 15;

/** Structure roles that start a paragraph, with the paragraph kind they imply. */
const BLOCK_ROLES: Record<string, ParagraphKind> = {
  P: 'p', H: 'h2', H1: 'h1', H2: 'h2', H3: 'h3', H4: 'h3', H5: 'h3', H6: 'h3', Title: 'h1',

/**

const COMMON_WORDS = new Set((
  'the of and a to in is you that it he was for on are as with his they i at be this have from or one had by ' +

  'number no way could people my than first water been call who oil its now find long down day did get come ' +
  'made may part over new sound take only little work know place year live me back give most very after thing ' +
  'our just name good sentence man think say great where help through much before line right too mean old any ' +
  'same tell boy follow came want show also around form three small set put end does another well large must ' +
  'big even such because turn here why ask went men read need land different home us move try kind hand ' +
  'picture again change off play spell air away animal house point page letter mother answer found study still ' +
  'learn should world high every near add food between own below country plant last school father keep tree ' +
  'never start city earth eye light thought head under story saw left don\'t few while along might close ' +
  'something seem next hard open example begin life always those both paper together got group often run'

/** A token looks Latin when every character is in the ranges a normal English text layer uses. */
const LATIN_TOKEN = /^[ -~ -ÿĀ-ɏḀ-ỿ‐-‧‰-⁞ﬀ-ﬆ]+$/;
const HAS_LETTER = /\p{L}/u;
const STARTS_LOWER = /^\p{Ll}/u;
const TERMINAL_END = /[.!?…:]["”’'»)\]]*$/u;
const BULLET_START = /^(?:[•·▪◦‣⁃■□●○*]|[-–—](?=\s))/u;
const LABEL_ONLY = /^(?:[•·▪◦‣⁃■□●○*\-–—]|\(?\d{1,3}[.)]?|\(?[a-z][.)]|\(?[ivx]{1,5}[.)])$/i;

/** Ligature glyphs as pdf.js reports them: ff fi fl ffi ffl ft st (U+FB00-FB06). */

/** Ligatures no English word ends with (fi fl ffi ffl ft st): a space after one is a split word. */
const WORD_END_LIGATURE = /[\uFB01-\uFB06]/u;
/** Ligatures no English word starts with (ff ffi ffl ft st): a space before one is a split word. */
const WORD_START_LIGATURE = /[\uFB00\uFB03-\uFB06]/u;
```
