// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Internal data model
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** One pdf.js text item, unrotated, in page coordinates. */
interface Run {
  text: string;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  blank: boolean;
  /** pdf.js saw a line break after this run */
  hasEOL: boolean;
  /** structure element ordinal (document-wide) or null for untagged content */
  elem: number | null;
  /** content-stream order, used as a tie breaker */
  order: number;
}

/** A line of text: runs on one baseline, in one reading-order block. */
interface Line {
  page: number;
  block: number;
  x0: number;
  x1: number;
  y: number;
  size: number;
  text: string;
  elem: number | null;
  role: ParagraphKind | null;
  /** font size class when the line is a heading, 0 otherwise */
  headingSize: number;
  running: boolean;
}

/** A reading-order region of a page: a whole single-column page, one column band, or a tagged element. */
interface Block {
  id: number;
  page: number;
  left: number;
  width: number;
}

interface Region { runs: Run[]; left: number; width: number }

interface DocState { nextBlock: number; nextElem: number; roleOf: Map<number, ParagraphKind> }

interface PageResult { lines: Line[]; blocks: Block[]; chars: number }

interface BodyStats { size: number; leading: number; charWidth: number }

interface Para {
  lines: Line[];
  role: ParagraphKind | null;
  headingSize: number;
  page: number;
  text: string;
}

const isTextItem = (it: RawItem): it is RawTextItem => typeof (it as RawTextItem).str === 'string';

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 1: runs -> lines (per page)
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Maps every content id of a page's structure tree to the ordinal of its innermost block-level
 * element (P, H1, LI, ...). Ordinals are assigned in tree (= logical reading) order.
 */
function mapStructTree(tree: StructNode, state: DocState): Map<string, number> {
  const map = new Map<string, number>();
  const visit = (node: StructNode, block: number | null): void => {
    for (const child of node.children ?? []) {
      if ('type' in child) {
        if (child.type === 'content' && block !== null && typeof child.id === 'string') map.set(child.id, block);
        continue;
      }
      const role = BLOCK_ROLES[child.role];
      if (role !== undefined) {
        const elem = state.nextElem++;
        state.roleOf.set(elem, role);
        visit(child, elem);
      } else {
        visit(child, block);
      }
    }
  };
  visit(tree, null);
  return map;
}

/**
 * Converts a page's items into runs. Handles the marked-content stack: /Artifact content is dropped
 * (page furniture), and every run learns which structure element it belongs to, either through the
 * structure tree or, without one, through the block-level BDC tags in the content stream.
 */
function collectRuns(raw: RawPage, state: DocState): { runs: Run[]; chars: number } {
  const treeMap = raw.structTree ? mapStructTree(raw.structTree, state) : null;
  const runs: Run[] = [];
  let chars = 0;
  // One entry per open marked-content sequence: its content id, and the element it opened (BDC path).
  const stack: { id: string | null; artifact: boolean; elem: number | null }[] = [];
  let artifactDepth = 0;
  let lastRun: Run | null = null;

  const innermostElem = (): number | null => {
    for (let i = stack.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (stack[i].elem !== null) return stack[i].elem;
    return null;
  };

  for (const it of raw.items) {
    if (!isTextItem(it)) {
      if (it.type === 'endMarkedContent') {
        const top = stack.pop();
        if (top?.artifact) artifactDepth--;
        continue;
      }
      const artifact = it.tag === 'Artifact';
      if (artifact) artifactDepth++;
      let elem: number | null = null;
      if (!treeMap && it.tag !== undefined && BLOCK_ROLES[it.tag] !== undefined) {
        elem = state.nextElem++;
        state.roleOf.set(elem, BLOCK_ROLES[it.tag]);
      }
      stack.push({ id: typeof it.id === 'string' ? it.id : null, artifact, elem });
      continue;
    }

    const t = it.transform;
    const text = it.str;
    const blank = text.trim().length === 0;
    if (!blank) chars += text.replace(/\s+/g, '').length;
    // Rotated or vertical text (watermarks, margin notes) is not prose; skip it.
    if (Math.abs(t[1]) > 1e-3 || Math.abs(t[2]) > 1e-3 || it.dir === 'ttb') continue;
    if (artifactDepth > 0) continue;

    let elem: number | null = null;
    if (treeMap) {
      for (let i = stack.length - 1; i >= 0 && elem === null; i--) {
        const id = stack[i].id;
        if (id !== null && treeMap.has(id)) elem = treeMap.get(id)!;
      }
    } else {
      elem = innermostElem();
      // BDC path: a new block that starts on the same baseline as the previous text continues the same
      // paragraph ("/P ... /Link ... /P ..." is how some producers tag a paragraph with a link in it),
      // and so does an inline sequence without a block tag of its own (the /Link in the middle).
      const prevOnLine = lastRun !== null && lastRun.elem !== null && !blank &&
        Math.abs(lastRun.y - t[5]) <= BASELINE_TOLERANCE * Math.max(it.height, lastRun.height) ? lastRun : null;
      if (prevOnLine && elem === null && stack.length > 0) {
        stack[stack.length - 1].elem = prevOnLine.elem;
        elem = prevOnLine.elem;
      } else if (prevOnLine && elem !== null && prevOnLine.elem !== elem) {
        for (let i = stack.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (stack[i].elem === elem) { stack[i].elem = prevOnLine.elem; break; }
        elem = prevOnLine.elem;
      }
    }
    const run: Run = {
      text, x: t[4], y: t[5], width: it.width, height: blank ? 0 : it.height, blank, hasEOL: it.hasEOL === true, elem, order: runs.length,
    };
    runs.push(run);
    if (!blank) lastRun = run;
  }
  return { runs, chars };
}

function extentsOf(runs: Run[]): { left: number; right: number } {
  let left = Infinity;
  let right = -Infinity;
  for (const r of runs) {
    if (r.blank) continue;
    if (r.x < left) left = r.x;
    if (r.x + r.width > right) right = r.x + r.width;
  }
  return { left, right };
}

interface BaselineCluster { y: number; size: number; runs: Run[] }

/** Groups runs by baseline, top of the page first. Blank runs attach to the line they sit on. */
function clusterBaselines(runs: Run[]): BaselineCluster[] {
  const words = runs.filter((r) => !r.blank).sort((a, b) => b.y - a.y || a.x - b.x || a.order - b.order);
  const lines: BaselineCluster[] = [];
  for (const w of words) {
    const cur = lines[lines.length - 1];
    if (cur && Math.abs(w.y - cur.y) <= BASELINE_TOLERANCE * Math.max(cur.size, w.height)) {
      cur.runs.push(w);
      if (w.height > cur.size) { cur.size = w.height; cur.y = w.y; } // the biggest run defines the baseline
    } else {
      lines.push({ y: w.y, size: w.height, runs: [w] });
    }
  }
  for (const b of runs) {
    if (!b.blank) continue;
    const line = lines.find((l) => Math.abs(b.y - l.y) <= BASELINE_TOLERANCE * l.size);
    if (line) line.runs.push(b);
  }
  return lines;
}

/** Removes the spaces pdf.js puts inside a run when a ligature glyph's advance is misreported ("fi ght", "o ffer"). */
export function joinSplitLigatures(text: string): string {
  if (!LIGATURE.test(text)) return text;
  return text.replace(SPLIT_AFTER_LIGATURE, '$1').replace(SPLIT_BEFORE_LIGATURE, '$1');
}

/**
 * Does a space belong between the text so far (ending in `before`) and a run starting with `after`,
 * `gap` points apart on a line of font size `em`? See the module comment, stage 1.
 */
export function needsSpace(before: string, after: string, gap: number, em: number, prevEOL = false): boolean {
  if (prevEOL) return true;
  const a = before[before.length - 1] ?? '';
  const b = after[0] ?? '';
  if (/\p{L}/u.test(a) && /\p{L}/u.test(b) && gap < LIGATURE_GAP_EM * em) {
    if (WORD_END_LIGATURE.test(a) && /\p{Ll}/u.test(b)) return false;
    if (WORD_START_LIGATURE.test(b)) return false;
  }
  if (gap < TIGHT_GAP_EM * em) return false;
  if (gap >= WORD_GAP_EM * em) return true;
  // Ambiguous zone: a squeezed space in justified text, unless a ligature glyph sits on the boundary.
  return !(LIGATURE.test(a) || LIGATURE.test(b));
}

/** Ligature glyphs become plain letters; soft hyphens inside a line vanish (a trailing one is for the line join). */
function normaliseLineText(text: string): string {
  const t = text.replace(/[\uFB00-\uFB06]/g, (c) => c.normalize('NFKC')).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  return t.replace(/\u00AD+(?!$)/g, '');
}

/** Joins the runs of one baseline into text, inserting spaces where the geometry shows a word gap. */
function joinRuns(cluster: BaselineCluster): string {
  const runs = cluster.runs.slice().sort((a, b) => a.x - b.x || a.order - b.order);
  const em = cluster.size || 1;
  let text = '';
  let end = -Infinity;
  let prev: Run | null = null; // the last run that contributed text
  for (const r of runs) {
    const str = joinSplitLigatures(r.text);
    if (prev && str.length > 0 && !/\s$/.test(text) && !/^\s/.test(str) && needsSpace(text, str, r.x - end, em, prev.hasEOL)) text += ' ';
    text += str;
    if (r.x + r.width > end) end = r.x + r.width;
    if (!r.blank) prev = r;
  }
  return normaliseLineText(text);
}

function formLines(runs: Run[], page: number, block: number, state: DocState): Line[] {
  const out: Line[] = [];
  for (const cluster of clusterBaselines(runs)) {
    const text = joinRuns(cluster);
    if (!text) continue;
    const ext = extentsOf(cluster.runs);
    const elem = cluster.runs[0].elem;
    out.push({
      page, block, x0: ext.left, x1: ext.right, y: cluster.y, size: cluster.size, text, elem,
      role: elem === null ? null : state.roleOf.get(elem) ?? null, headingSize: 0, running: false,
    });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Finds a vertical gap that splits the runs into two columns: a band of x positions that (almost) no
 * run crosses, at least 1.5 characters wide, somewhere in the middle half of the text width.
 */
function findColumnGap(words: Run[], left: number, right: number): { start: number; end: number; charWidth: number } | null {
  const width = right - left;
  if (width < 100) return null;
  let totalWidth = 0;
  let totalChars = 0;
  for (const w of words) { totalWidth += w.width; totalChars += w.text.trim().length; }
  const charWidth = totalWidth / Math.max(1, totalChars);
  const BINS = 256;
  const cover = new Uint16Array(BINS);
  for (const w of words) {
    const b0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor(((w.x - left) / width) * BINS));
    const b1 = Math.min(BINS - 1, Math.ceil(((w.x + w.width - left) / width) * BINS) - 1);
    for (let b = b0; b <= b1; b++) cover[b]++;
  }
  const limit = Math.max(1, Math.floor(words.length * COLUMN_SPAN_SHARE));
  let best: { start: number; end: number; charWidth: number } | null = null;
  let bestWidth = 0;
  for (let b = 0; b < BINS;) {
    if (cover[b] > limit) { b++; continue; }
    let e = b;
    while (e < BINS && cover[e] <= limit) e++;
    const gapWidth = ((e - b) / BINS) * width;
    const center = (b + e) / 2 / BINS;
    if (gapWidth >= Math.max(6, 1.5 * charWidth) && center >= 0.25 && center <= 0.75 && gapWidth > bestWidth) {
      best = { start: left + (b / BINS) * width, end: left + (e / BINS) * width, charWidth };
      bestWidth = gapWidth;
    }
    b = e;
  }
  return best;
}

/**
 * Splits untagged runs of a page into reading-order regions. A single-column page is one region. On
 * a two-column page, runs crossing the gutter (a spanning title) cut the columns into bands; each band
 * is read left column then right column.
 */
function layoutRegions(runs: Run[]): Region[] {
  const words = runs.filter((r) => !r.blank);
  if (words.length === 0) return [];
  const ext = extentsOf(words);
  const whole: Region = { runs, left: ext.left, width: ext.right - ext.left };
  if (words.length < MIN_RUNS_FOR_COLUMNS) return [whole];
  const gap = findColumnGap(words, ext.left, ext.right);
  if (!gap) return [whole];

  const eps = 0.5 * gap.charWidth;
  const left: Run[] = [];
  const right: Run[] = [];
  const span: Run[] = [];
  for (const r of runs) {
    if (r.x + r.width <= gap.start + eps) left.push(r);
    else if (r.x >= gap.end - eps) right.push(r);
    else span.push(r);
  }
  const count = (a: Run[]): number => a.filter((r) => !r.blank).length;
  if (count(left) < 3 || count(right) < 3 || count(span) > 0.2 * words.length) return [whole];

  const leftExt = extentsOf(left);
  const rightExt = extentsOf(right);
  const spanLines = clusterBaselines(span); // top to bottom
  const bandOf = (r: Run): number => {
    let band = 0;
    for (const s of spanLines) if (s.y > r.y + BASELINE_TOLERANCE * s.size) band++;
    return band;
  };
  const leftBands: Run[][] = [];
  const rightBands: Run[][] = [];
  for (const r of left) (leftBands[bandOf(r)] ??= []).push(r);
  for (const r of right) (rightBands[bandOf(r)] ??= []).push(r);

  const regions: Region[] = [];
  for (let band = 0; band <= spanLines.length; band++) {
    if (band > 0) {
      const s = spanLines[band - 1];
      const e = extentsOf(s.runs);
      regions.push({ runs: s.runs, left: e.left, width: e.right - e.left });
    }
    if (leftBands[band]?.length) regions.push({ runs: leftBands[band], left: leftExt.left, width: leftExt.right - leftExt.left });
    if (rightBands[band]?.length) regions.push({ runs: rightBands[band], left: rightExt.left, width: rightExt.right - rightExt.left });
  }
  return regions;
}

function extractPage(raw: RawPage, page: number, state: DocState): PageResult {
  const { runs, chars } = collectRuns(raw, state);
  const lines: Line[] = [];
  const blocks: Block[] = [];
  const addBlock = (region: Region): void => {
    const block: Block = { id: state.nextBlock++, page, left: region.left, width: Math.max(1, region.width) };
    const got = formLines(region.runs, page, block.id, state);
    if (got.length === 0) return;
    blocks.push(block);
    lines.push(...got);
  };

  // Tagged content first, element by element (tree order / stream order), then untagged content.
  const tagged = new Map<number, Run[]>();
  const untagged: Run[] = [];
  for (const r of runs) {
    if (r.elem === null) untagged.push(r);
    else { let a = tagged.get(r.elem); if (!a) tagged.set(r.elem, (a = [])); a.push(r); }
  }
  if (tagged.size > 0) {
    const pageExt = extentsOf(runs);
    for (const elem of [...tagged.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b)) {
      addBlock({ runs: tagged.get(elem)!, left: pageExt.left, width: pageExt.right - pageExt.left });
    }
  }
  for (const region of layoutRegions(untagged)) addBlock(region);
  return { lines, blocks, chars };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 2: document-level checks and running headers/footers
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Throws when the text layer is not usable English (see the module comment). */
export function checkTextLayer(text: string): void {
  let alphabetic = 0;
  let foreign = 0;
  let common = 0;
  for (const tok of text.split(/\s+/)) {
    if (!HAS_LETTER.test(tok) && !PRIVATE_USE.test(tok)) continue;
    alphabetic++;
    if (!LATIN_TOKEN.test(tok)) foreign++;
    const word = tok.toLowerCase().replace(/^[^\p{L}]+|[^\p{L}']+$/gu, '').replace(/[’]/g, "'");
    if (COMMON_WORDS.has(word)) common++;
  }
  if (alphabetic >= 20 && foreign / alphabetic > FOREIGN_TOKEN_RATIO) throw new Error(GARBAGE_ERROR);
  if (alphabetic >= 60 && common / alphabetic < MIN_COMMON_WORD_RATIO) throw new Error(GARBAGE_ERROR);
}

/** "3", "iv", "Page 3 of 10", "- 3 -", "p. 12", "3 / 10". */
export function isPageNumberLine(text: string): boolean {
  return PAGE_NUMBER.test(text.trim());
}

const normaliseKey = (s: string): string => s.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();

/**
 * Marks running headers/footers and page numbers. `candidates` are grouped by a text key; within a
 * group, lines at (almost) the same relative height on at least `need` different pages are running.
 */
function markRepeated(candidates: { line: Line; key: string; yRel: number }[], need: number): void {
  const groups = new Map<string, { line: Line; yRel: number }[]>();
  for (const c of candidates) {
    if (!c.key) continue;
    let g = groups.get(c.key);
    if (!g) groups.set(c.key, (g = []));
    g.push(c);
  }
  for (const g of groups.values()) {
    if (g.length < need) continue;
    g.sort((a, b) => a.yRel - b.yRel);
    let start = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i <= g.length; i++) {
      if (i < g.length && g[i].yRel - g[i - 1].yRel <= RUNNING_Y_TOLERANCE) continue;
      const cluster = g.slice(start, i);
      if (new Set(cluster.map((c) => c.line.page)).size >= need) for (const c of cluster) c.line.running = true;
      start = i;
    }
  }
}

function markRunningLines(lines: Line[], pageHeights: number[], bodySize: number): void {
  const numPages = pageHeights.length;
  const need = numPages >= 5 ? 3 : Math.max(2, Math.ceil(0.6 * numPages));
  const exact: { line: Line; key: string; yRel: number }[] = [];
  const digits: { line: Line; key: string; yRel: number }[] = [];
  for (const line of lines) {
    const h = pageHeights[line.page] || 1;
    const yRel = line.y / h;
    const inMargin = yRel <= MARGIN_BAND || yRel >= 1 - MARGIN_BAND;
    const heading = line.size >= HEADING_SIZE_RATIO * bodySize;
    if (inMargin && isPageNumberLine(line.text)) { line.running = true; continue; }
    const key = normaliseKey(line.text);
    if (inMargin || !heading) exact.push({ line, key, yRel });
    if (inMargin) digits.push({ line, key: key.replace(/\d+/g, '#'), yRel });
  }
  markRepeated(exact, need);
  markRepeated(digits, need);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 3: body statistics and headings
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function round2(n: number): number { return Math.round(n * 2) / 2; }

function bodySizeOf(lines: Line[]): number {
  const byChars = new Map<number, number>();
  let total = 0;
  for (const l of lines) {
    const s = round2(l.size);
    byChars.set(s, (byChars.get(s) ?? 0) + l.text.length);
    total += l.text.length;
  }
  let acc = 0;
  for (const s of [...byChars.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b)) {
    acc += byChars.get(s)!;
    if (acc * 2 >= total) return s;
  }
  return 10;
}

function median(values: number[]): number {
  if (values.length === 0) return 0;
  const s = values.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const m = s.length >> 1;
  return s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m - 1] + s[m]) / 2;
}

function bodyStats(lines: Line[]): BodyStats {
  const size = bodySizeOf(lines);
  const gaps: number[] = [];
  let width = 0;
  let chars = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const l = lines[i];
    if (Math.abs(l.size - size) <= 0.1 * size) { width += l.x1 - l.x0; chars += l.text.length; }
    const p = lines[i - 1];
    if (p && p.block === l.block) {
      const gap = p.y - l.y;
      if (gap > 0 && gap <= 3 * size) gaps.push(gap);
    }
  }
  const leading = gaps.length > 0 ? median(gaps) : 1.2 * size;
  const charWidth = chars > 0 ? width / chars : size * 0.5;
  return { size, leading, charWidth };
}

const isAllCaps = (s: string): boolean => /\p{Lu}/u.test(s) && !/\p{Ll}/u.test(s) && s.replace(/[^\p{L}]/gu, '').length >= 2;

function markHeadings(lines: Line[], blocks: Map<number, Block>, stats: BodyStats): void {
  for (const l of lines) {
    if (l.size >= HEADING_SIZE_RATIO * stats.size) { l.headingSize = round2(l.size); continue; }
    const block = blocks.get(l.block)!;
    const words = l.text.split(' ').length;
    if (isAllCaps(l.text) && words <= MAX_CAPS_HEADING_WORDS && l.x1 - l.x0 < SHORT_LINE_RATIO * block.width && !/[!?,;]$/.test(l.text)) {
      l.headingSize = round2(l.size);
    }
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 4: lines -> paragraphs
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface HyphenEvidence { hyphenated: Set<string>; closed: Set<string> }

function collectHyphenEvidence(lines: Line[]): HyphenEvidence {
  const hyphenated = new Set<string>();
  const closed = new Set<string>();
  for (const l of lines) {
    for (const m of l.text.matchAll(/\p{L}+(?:-\p{L}+)+/gu)) hyphenated.add(m[0].toLowerCase());
    for (const m of l.text.matchAll(/\p{L}{3,}/gu)) closed.add(m[0].toLowerCase());
  }
  return { hyphenated, closed };
}

/** Decides whether the hyphen between `before` (end of a line) and `after` (start of the next) stays. */
export function keepHyphen(before: string, after: string, ev: HyphenEvidence): boolean {
  const a = before.toLowerCase();
  const b = after.toLowerCase();
  if (ev.hyphenated.has(`${a}-${b}`)) return true;
  if (ev.closed.has(a + b)) return false;
  // One-letter or ALL-CAPS prefixes are compounds ("T-shirt", "UN-backed"); everything else is a word
  // broken by the typesetter.
  return before.length < 2 || before === before.toUpperCase();
}

/** Joins consecutive lines of a paragraph, de-hyphenating line ends (see the module comment, rule 6). */
export function joinLineTexts(texts: string[], ev: HyphenEvidence): string {
  let text = texts[0] ?? '';
  for (let i = 1; i < texts.length; i++) {
    const next = texts[i];
    const m = /(\p{L}+)([-‐­])$/u.exec(text);
    if (m) {
      const soft = m[2] === '­';
      const letters = /^\p{L}+/u.exec(next);
      if (letters && STARTS_LOWER.test(next)) {
        text = soft || !keepHyphen(m[1], letters[0], ev) ? text.slice(0, -1) + next : text + next;
        continue;
      }
      if (soft) { text = text.slice(0, -1) + next; continue; }
      if (/^[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(next)) { text += next; continue; } // "Jean-" + "Paul", "COVID-" + "19"
    }
    text += ' ' + next;
  }
  return text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
}

const endsTerminal = (s: string): boolean => TERMINAL_END.test(s);

/** Does `cur` start a new paragraph after `prev`? */
function startsParagraph(prev: Line, cur: Line, blocks: Map<number, Block>, stats: BodyStats): boolean {
  if (prev.headingSize > 0 || cur.headingSize > 0) {
    // Adjacent heading lines of the same size are one multi-line heading.
    const bothHeadings = prev.headingSize > 0 && cur.headingSize > 0 && Math.abs(prev.headingSize - cur.headingSize) < 0.5;
    const adjacent = prev.block === cur.block && prev.y - cur.y <= 1.8 * cur.size;
    return !(bothHeadings && adjacent);
  }
  if (cur.elem !== null || prev.elem !== null) {
    if (cur.elem === prev.elem) return false;
    if (cur.page === prev.page) return true;
    // A tagged paragraph split by a page break: pdf.js reports one element per page.
    return endsTerminal(prev.text) && !STARTS_LOWER.test(cur.text);
  }
  if (BULLET_START.test(cur.text)) return true;
  if (prev.block === cur.block) {
    const gap = prev.y - cur.y;
    if (gap > PARAGRAPH_GAP_RATIO * stats.size && gap > LEADING_GAP_RATIO * stats.leading) return true;
  }
  if (!endsTerminal(prev.text)) return false;
  const curBlock = blocks.get(cur.block)!;
  const prevBlock = blocks.get(prev.block)!;
  if (cur.x0 - curBlock.left > INDENT_CHAR_WIDTHS * stats.charWidth) return true;
  return prev.x1 - prev.x0 < SHORT_LINE_RATIO * prevBlock.width;
}

function assembleParagraphs(lines: Line[], blocks: Map<number, Block>, stats: BodyStats): Para[] {
  const ev = collectHyphenEvidence(lines);
  const paras: Para[] = [];
  let cur: Line[] = [];
  const flush = (): void => {
    if (cur.length === 0) return;
    const first = cur[0];
    paras.push({
      lines: cur,
      role: first.role,
      headingSize: cur.every((l) => l.headingSize > 0) ? first.headingSize : 0,
      page: first.page,
      text: joinLineTexts(cur.map((l) => l.text), ev),
    });
    cur = [];
  };
  for (const line of lines) {
    if (cur.length > 0 && startsParagraph(cur[cur.length - 1], line, blocks, stats)) flush();
    cur.push(line);
  }
  flush();

  // A paragraph that is only a list label ("1.", "•") belongs to the paragraph that follows it.
  const merged: Para[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < paras.length; i++) {
    const p = paras[i];
    const next = paras[i + 1];
    if (next && next.page === p.page && LABEL_ONLY.test(p.text) && next.headingSize === 0) {
      merged.push({ ...next, lines: [...p.lines, ...next.lines], text: `${p.text} ${next.text}`, role: next.role === null || next.role === 'p' ? 'li' : next.role, page: p.page });
      i++;
    } else {
      merged.push(p);
    }
  }
  return merged;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 5: paragraph kinds, chapters, metadata
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function paragraphKinds(paras: Para[]): ParagraphKind[] {
  const counts = new Map<number, number>();
  for (const p of paras) if (p.headingSize > 0) counts.set(p.headingSize, (counts.get(p.headingSize) ?? 0) + 1);
  const sizes = [...counts.keys()].sort((a, b) => b - a);
  const chapterSize = sizes.find((s) => counts.get(s)! >= 2) ?? sizes[0] ?? Infinity;
  const secondSize = sizes.find((s) => s < chapterSize) ?? Infinity;
  return paras.map((p) => {
    if (p.role === 'h1' || p.role === 'h2' || p.role === 'h3') return p.role;
    if (p.headingSize > 0) return p.headingSize >= chapterSize ? 'h1' : p.headingSize >= secondSize ? 'h2' : 'h3';
    return p.role ?? 'p';
  });
}

/** Cleans a metadata title: producer placeholders and "Microsoft Word - name.docx" wrappers are not titles. */
export function cleanMetaTitle(raw: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null;
  let t = raw.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  t = t.replace(/^microsoft (?:word|powerpoint|excel) - /i, '').replace(/\.(?:docx?|pdf|txt|rtf|odt|tex|indd|pptx?|md|html?)$/i, '').trim();
  if (!t || /^[(\[]?(?:untitled|anonymous|unspecified|unknown|none|null|document|title|microsoft word)[)\]]?$/i.test(t)) return null;
  return t;
}

export function cleanMetaAuthor(raw: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null;
  const t = raw.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  if (!t || /^[(\[]?(?:anonymous|unspecified|unknown|none|null|author|user)[)\]]?$/i.test(t)) return null;
  return t;
}

function buildChapters(paras: Para[], kinds: ParagraphKind[], numPages: number, title: string): { title: string; paras: number[] }[] {
  const h1 = paras.map((_, i) => i).filter((i) => kinds[i] === 'h1');
  const chapters: { title: string; paras: number[] }[] = [];
  if (h1.length >= 2) {
    let cur: { title: string; paras: number[] } | null = null;
    for (let i = 0; i < paras.length; i++) {
      if (kinds[i] === 'h1') { cur = { title: paras[i].text, paras: [] }; chapters.push(cur); }
      else if (!cur) { cur = { title: 'Front matter', paras: [] }; chapters.push(cur); }
      cur.paras.push(i);
    }
    return chapters;
  }
  if (numPages < PAGES_PER_CHUNK) return [{ title, paras: paras.map((_, i) => i) }];
  for (let i = 0; i < paras.length; i++) {
    const chunk = Math.floor(paras[i].page / PAGES_PER_CHUNK);
    const last = chapters[chapters.length - 1] as ({ title: string; paras: number[]; chunk?: number } | undefined);
    if (!last || last.chunk !== chunk) {
      const from = chunk * PAGES_PER_CHUNK + 1;
      const to = Math.min(numPages, from + PAGES_PER_CHUNK - 1);
      chapters.push(Object.assign({ title: `Pages ${from}-${to}`, paras: [] as number[] }, { chunk }));
    }
    chapters[chapters.length - 1].paras.push(i);
  }
  return chapters;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Pure entry point
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Builds a Book from extracted pages. Throws SCANNED_ERROR / GARBAGE_ERROR for unusable text layers. */
export function buildBook(input: PdfInput, ctx: ImportContext): Book {
  const numPages = input.pages.length;
  if (numPages === 0) throw new Error('This PDF has no pages.');
  const state: DocState = { nextBlock: 0, nextElem: 0, roleOf: new Map() };
  const allLines: Line[] = [];
  const blocks = new Map<number, Block>();
  let chars = 0;
  input.pages.forEach((raw, i) => {
    const res = extractPage(raw, i, state);
    chars += res.chars;
    allLines.push(...res.lines);
    for (const b of res.blocks) blocks.set(b.id, b);
  });
  if (chars / numPages < MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE) throw new Error(SCANNED_ERROR);
  checkTextLayer(allLines.map((l) => l.text).join('\n'));

  markRunningLines(allLines, input.pages.map((p) => p.height), bodySizeOf(allLines));
  const lines = allLines.filter((l) => !l.running);
  if (lines.length === 0) throw new Error(SCANNED_ERROR);
  const stats = bodyStats(lines);
  markHeadings(lines, blocks, stats);
  const paras = assembleParagraphs(lines, blocks, stats);
  const kinds = paragraphKinds(paras);

  const fileName = ctx.sourcePath ? path.basename(ctx.sourcePath, path.extname(ctx.sourcePath)) : '';
  const firstHeading = paras.find((_, i) => kinds[i] === 'h1' || kinds[i] === 'h2' || kinds[i] === 'h3');
  const title = cleanMetaTitle(input.title) ?? firstHeading?.text ?? (fileName.trim() || 'Untitled PDF');
  const author = cleanMetaAuthor(input.author) ?? undefined;

  let words = 0;
  let sentenceCount = 0;
  let paragraphCount = 0;
  const chapters: Chapter[] = buildChapters(paras, kinds, numPages, title).map((c, ci) => {
    const paragraphs: Paragraph[] = [];
    for (const pi of c.paras) {
      const text = paras[pi].text;
      const sentences = ctx.segmenter.segmentParagraph(text);
      if (sentences.length === 0) continue;
      for (const s of sentences) for (const t of s.tokens) if (t.kind === 'word') words++;
      sentenceCount += sentences.length;
      paragraphs.push({ index: paragraphs.length, kind: kinds[pi], text, sentences });
    }
    paragraphCount += paragraphs.length;
    return { index: ci, title: c.title, paragraphs };
  }).filter((c) => c.paragraphs.length > 0).map((c, ci) => ({ ...c, index: ci }));

  return {
    id: ctx.id,
    title,
    author,
    language: 'en',
    source: { kind: 'pdf', path: ctx.sourcePath, importedAt: new Date().toISOString() },
    chapters,
    names: [],
    stats: { words, paragraphs: paragraphCount, sentences: sentenceCount },
  };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// pdf.js glue
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Loads the file with pdf.js and extracts text items, marked content, structure trees and metadata. */
export async function readPdf(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<PdfInput> {
  const pdfjs = await import('pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs');
  // pdf.js refuses Node Buffers and may transfer the buffer, so always hand it a private copy.
  // (pdf.js 6 dropped the `isEvalSupported` option: fonts are never compiled with `new Function` now.)
  const data = new Uint8Array(bytes);
  const task = pdfjs.getDocument({ data, useSystemFonts: true, verbosity: 0 });
  try {
    const doc = await task.promise;
    const pages: RawPage[] = [];
    for (let i = 1; i <= doc.numPages; i++) {
      const page = await doc.getPage(i);
      const viewport = page.getViewport({ scale: 1 });
      const content = await page.getTextContent({ includeMarkedContent: true });
      const items = content.items as unknown as RawItem[];
      let structTree: StructNode | null = null;
      if (items.some((it) => !isTextItem(it) && typeof it.tag === 'string')) {
        structTree = (await page.getStructTree().catch(() => null)) as StructNode | null;
      }
      pages.push({ width: viewport.width, height: viewport.height, items, structTree });
      page.cleanup();
    }
    let title: string | null = null;
    let author: string | null = null;
    try {
      const meta = await doc.getMetadata();
      const info = (meta.info ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
      title = typeof info.Title === 'string' ? info.Title : null;
      author = typeof info.Author === 'string' ? info.Author : null;
      if (!cleanMetaTitle(title) && meta.metadata) {
        const dc = (meta.metadata as { get(name: string): unknown }).get('dc:title');
        if (typeof dc === 'string') title = dc;
        else if (Array.isArray(dc) && typeof dc[0] === 'string') title = dc[0];
      }
    } catch {
      // metadata is optional
    }
    return { pages, title, author };
  } finally {
    await task.destroy().catch(() => undefined);
  }
}

export const pdfImporter: Importer = {
  kind: 'pdf',
  async importBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, ctx: ImportContext): Promise<Book> {
    let input: PdfInput;
    try {
      input = await readPdf(bytes);
    } catch (e) {
      const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
      if (/password|encrypted/i.test(msg)) throw new Error('This PDF is password-protected. Remove the password and try again.');
      throw new Error(`Could not open this PDF: ${msg}`);
    }
    return buildBook(input, ctx);
  },
};
```

### `src/core/import/skip.ts` (250 lines)

```ts
import type { Book, Paragraph } from '@core/model';

/**
 * Speechify-style "Enhanced Skipping": parts of a book the voice leaves out. Whole paragraphs (running
 * headers and footers, page numbers, footnotes, table-of-contents lines, figure captions) are found by
 * classifySkippable(); inline spans ((…), […], {…}, citations, URLs) are removed from the SPOKEN text by
 * stripInline(), which also returns an offset map so word timings of the stripped text can be mapped
 * back to the original sentence for highlighting. The displayed text is never changed.
 */

export type SkipCategory =
  | 'headers' | 'footers' | 'footnotes' | 'braces' | 'citations' | 'parentheses' | 'brackets' | 'urls'
  | 'pageNumbers' | 'toc' | 'captions';

export type SkipSettings = Record<SkipCategory, boolean>;

/** Settings → Skip rows, in Speechify's order (then the extra ones). */
export const SKIP_OPTIONS: { id: SkipCategory; label: string; hint: string }[] = [
  { id: 'headers', label: 'Headers', hint: 'Running headers repeated at the top of pages (book or chapter title).' },
  { id: 'footers', label: 'Footers', hint: 'Running footers repeated at the bottom of pages (copyright lines, web addresses).' },
  { id: 'footnotes', label: 'Footnotes', hint: 'Notes that start with a number, [1] or ^1, and small raised note numbers¹.' },
  { id: 'braces', label: 'Braces', hint: 'Anything inside { curly braces }.' },
  { id: 'citations', label: 'Citations', hint: 'References like (Smith, 2020), (Smith et al. 2019; Lee 2021) or [12].' },
  { id: 'parentheses', label: 'Parentheses', hint: 'Anything inside ( round brackets ).' },
  { id: 'brackets', label: 'Brackets', hint: 'Anything inside [ square brackets ].' },
  { id: 'urls', label: 'URLs', hint: 'Web addresses such as https://example.com or www.example.com.' },
  { id: 'pageNumbers', label: 'Page numbers', hint: 'Lines that are only a page number, like "12" or "Page 12".' },
  { id: 'toc', label: 'Table of contents', hint: 'Contents lines ending in dots and a page number ("Chapter 1 ....... 7").' },
  { id: 'captions', label: 'Captions', hint: 'Figure and table captions ("Figure 1: …", "Table 2. …").' },
];

export const SKIP_CATEGORIES: SkipCategory[] = SKIP_OPTIONS.map((o) => o.id);

export const DEFAULT_SKIP: SkipSettings = {
  headers: false, footers: false, footnotes: false, braces: false, citations: false, parentheses: false, brackets: false, urls: false,
  pageNumbers: true, toc: false, captions: false,
};

/** Every category on (or off). */
export function skipAll(on = true): SkipSettings {
  return Object.fromEntries(SKIP_CATEGORIES.map((c) => [c, on])) as SkipSettings;
}

export function allSkipped(s: SkipSettings): boolean { return SKIP_CATEGORIES.every((c) => s[c]); }

// ---- paragraph classification ------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface SkipContext {
  /** normalised short lines (see runningKey) -> how often they occur in the book */
  repeated: Map<string, number>;
  /** the paragraph is the last one of its chapter (a repeated line there is more likely a footer) */
  lastInChapter?: boolean;
}

const MAX_RUNNING_CHARS = 80;
const MAX_RUNNING_WORDS = 12;
/** a short line repeated this often in the book is a running header or footer */
const MIN_REPEATS = 3;

function isHeading(p: Paragraph): boolean { return p.kind === 'h1' || p.kind === 'h2' || p.kind === 'h3'; }

/** Key for running header/footer detection: lower case, digits and page-number words removed, punctuation collapsed. */
export function runningKey(text: string): string | null {
  const t = text.trim();
  if (!t || t.length > MAX_RUNNING_CHARS || t.split(/\s+/).length > MAX_RUNNING_WORDS) return null;
  const key = t.toLowerCase().replace(/\bpage\b|\bof\b(?=\s*\d)/g, ' ').replace(/\d+/g, ' ').replace(/[^\p{L}]+/gu, ' ').trim();
  return key.length >= 2 ? key : null;
}

/** Counts repeated short lines across the whole book (headings excluded: chapter titles are never skipped). */
export function buildSkipContext(book: Book): Map<string, number> {
  const counts = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const ch of book.chapters) for (const p of ch.paragraphs) {
    if (isHeading(p)) continue;
    const k = runningKey(p.text);
    if (k) counts.set(k, (counts.get(k) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  for (const [k, n] of counts) if (n < MIN_REPEATS) counts.delete(k);
  return counts;
}

/** "12", "- 12 -", "Page 12", "page 3 of 10", "xii" (lower-case roman numerals only: "I" or "MIX" alone are words) */
const PAGE_NUMBER = /^[\s\-–—|]*(?:(?:[Pp]age|PAGE|[Pp]\.|[Pp]g\.?)\s*)?(?:\d{1,4}|[ivxlc]{1,7})(?:\s*(?:of|OF|\/)\s*\d{1,4})?[\s\-–—|]*$/;
const TOC_LINE = /(?:\.\s*){3,}\s*(?:\d{1,4}|[ivxlc]{1,7})\s*$|(?:…\s*)+(?:\d{1,4}|[ivxlc]{1,7})\s*$/i;
const CAPTION = /^(?:figure|fig\.|table|chart|plate|illustration|image|photo|map|diagram|exhibit|listing|graph)\s*\d+(?:\.\d+)*[a-z]?\s*[:.—–-](?:\s|$)/i;
const FOOTNOTE = /^(?:\[\d{1,3}\]|\^\d{1,3}|\d{1,3}\s+(?=[\p{Lu}“"‘'(])|[*†‡§¶]+\s*(?=\S)|[¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹⁰]+\s*(?=\S))/u;
const FOOTER_HINT = /©|\bcopyright\b|all rights reserved|https?:\/\/|www\.|\bpage\b|\.(?:com|org|net)\b/i;
const CITATION_ONLY = /^\s*(?:\[\d{1,4}(?:\s*[,–-]\s*\d{1,4})*\]\s*)+$/;

/**
 * The skip category of a whole paragraph, or null when it is ordinary text. The caller decides whether
 * that category is switched on. `ctx.repeated` comes from buildSkipContext(book); without it running
 * headers/footers are not detected.
 */
export function classifySkippable(paragraph: Paragraph, ctx?: SkipContext): SkipCategory | null {
  const text = paragraph.text.trim();
  if (!text) return null;
  if (PAGE_NUMBER.test(text)) return 'pageNumbers';
  if (TOC_LINE.test(text)) return 'toc';
  if (paragraph.kind === 'caption' || CAPTION.test(text)) return 'captions';
  if (CITATION_ONLY.test(text)) return 'citations';
  if (isHeading(paragraph)) return null;
  if (paragraph.kind !== 'li' && paragraph.kind !== 'pre' && FOOTNOTE.test(text)) return 'footnotes';
  const key = ctx ? runningKey(text) : null;
  if (key && ctx!.repeated.has(key)) return FOOTER_HINT.test(text) || ctx!.lastInChapter ? 'footers' : 'headers';
  return null;
}

/** Category of a paragraph if it is switched on in `settings`, else null. */
export function paragraphSkip(paragraph: Paragraph, settings: SkipSettings, ctx?: SkipContext): SkipCategory | null {
  const c = classifySkippable(paragraph, ctx);
  return c && settings[c] ? c : null;
}

function anyOn(s: SkipSettings): boolean { return SKIP_CATEGORIES.some((c) => s[c]); }
const INLINE: SkipCategory[] = ['parentheses', 'brackets', 'braces', 'citations', 'urls', 'footnotes'];

/**
 * Keys ("chapter.paragraph.sentence", as sentenceKey()) of every sentence the voice should skip: all
 * sentences of skipped paragraphs, plus sentences left with nothing to say once inline spans are stripped.
 */
export function skippedSentences(book: Book, settings: SkipSettings): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  if (!anyOn(settings)) return out;
  const repeated = buildSkipContext(book);
  const inline = INLINE.some((c) => settings[c]);
  for (const ch of book.chapters) {
    ch.paragraphs.forEach((p, i) => {
      const whole = paragraphSkip(p, settings, { repeated, lastInChapter: i === ch.paragraphs.length - 1 });
      for (const s of p.sentences) {
        const key = `${ch.index}.${p.index}.${s.index}`;
        if (whole) { out.add(key); continue; }
        if (inline && !/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(stripInline(p.text.slice(s.start, s.end), settings).text)) out.add(key);
      }
    });
  }
  return out;
}

// ---- inline stripping ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface StrippedText {
  /** the text to speak */
  text: string;
  /** map[i] = offset in the original text of text[i]; map[text.length] = original length */
  map: number[];
  /** removed [start, end) ranges of the original text */
  removed: [number, number][];
}

const PAIRS: Record<string, { close: string; cat: 'parentheses' | 'brackets' | 'braces' }> = {
  '(': { close: ')', cat: 'parentheses' }, '[': { close: ']', cat: 'brackets' }, '{': { close: '}', cat: 'braces' },
};
const CITE_PART = /^(?:(?:see(?:\s+also)?|cf\.|e\.g\.,?|i\.e\.,?)\s+)?(?:\p{Lu}[\p{L}'’\-]+(?:\s+(?:et\s+al\.?|and|&)(?:\s+\p{Lu}[\p{L}'’\-]+)?)?,?\s+)?(?:\d{4}[a-z]?|n\.d\.|in\s+press|forthcoming)(?:\s*,\s*(?:pp?\.\s*)?\d+(?:\s*[–-]\s*\d+)?)?$/u;
const NUMERIC_CITE = /^\d{1,4}(?:\s*[,–-]\s*\d{1,4})*$/;
const URL = /\b(?:https?:\/\/|www\.)[^\s<>"'”’]+/gi;
const SUPERSCRIPT_NOTE = /(?<=[\p{L}\p{N}.,;:!?”"')\]])[¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹⁰]+/gu;

/** True when the content of (…) or […] is a reference: "Smith, 2020", "Smith et al. 2019; Lee 2021, p. 4", "12", "3–5". */
export function isCitation(inner: string, open: string): boolean {
  const t = inner.trim();
  if (!t) return false;
  if (open === '[') return NUMERIC_CITE.test(t) || t.split(/\s*;\s*/).every((p) => CITE_PART.test(p));
  if (open === '(') return t.split(/\s*;\s*/).every((p) => CITE_PART.test(p));
  return false;
}

/** Balanced (…)/[…]/{…} spans of `text`, nested ones included, sorted by start. */
function bracketSpans(text: string): { start: number; end: number; open: string }[] {
  const out: { start: number; end: number; open: string }[] = [];
  const stack: { ch: string; at: number }[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    const c = text[i];
    if (PAIRS[c]) stack.push({ ch: c, at: i });
    else if (c === ')' || c === ']' || c === '}') {
      // pop to the matching opener; an unmatched closer is ignored
      let j = stack.length - 1;
      while (j >= 0 && PAIRS[stack[j].ch].close !== c) j--;
      if (j < 0) continue;
      const open = stack[j];
      stack.length = j;
      // nested spans are kept too, so an inner citation can go when only citations are skipped
      out.push({ start: open.at, end: i + 1, open: open.ch });
    }
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start);
}

/**
 * Removes the switched-on inline spans from text to be spoken and returns the remaining text with an
 * offset map back to the original. Whitespace left doubled by a removal is collapsed, and a space before
 * following punctuation is dropped ("word (x)." -> "word.").
 */
export function stripInline(text: string, settings: SkipSettings): StrippedText {
  const spans: [number, number][] = [];
  if (settings.parentheses || settings.brackets || settings.braces || settings.citations) {
    for (const s of bracketSpans(text)) {
      const cat = PAIRS[s.open].cat;
      if (settings[cat] || (settings.citations && isCitation(text.slice(s.start + 1, s.end - 1), s.open))) spans.push([s.start, s.end]);
    }
  }
  if (settings.urls) {
    for (const m of text.matchAll(URL)) {
      let end = m.index! + m[0].length;
      while (end > m.index! && /[.,;:!?)\]]/.test(text[end - 1])) end--;
      spans.push([m.index!, end]);
    }
  }
  if (settings.footnotes) for (const m of text.matchAll(SUPERSCRIPT_NOTE)) spans.push([m.index!, m.index! + m[0].length]);
  if (!spans.length) return { text, map: identity(text.length), removed: [] };

  // merge overlapping spans, then widen each over one side of its surrounding whitespace
  spans.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0] || b[1] - a[1]);
  const merged: [number, number][] = [];
  for (const s of spans) {
    const last = merged[merged.length - 1];
    if (last && s[0] <= last[1]) last[1] = Math.max(last[1], s[1]);
    else merged.push([s[0], s[1]]);
  }
  for (const r of merged) {
    let [a, b] = r;
    const before = a > 0 && /\s/.test(text[a - 1]);
    const after = b < text.length && /\s/.test(text[b]);
    if (before && (after || b === text.length || /[.,;:!?…)\]}”"’]/.test(text[b]))) { while (a > 0 && /\s/.test(text[a - 1])) a--; }
    else if (!before && after && a === 0) { while (b < text.length && /\s/.test(text[b])) b++; }
    r[0] = a; r[1] = b;
  }
  let out = '';
  const map: number[] = [];
  let k = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    while (k < merged.length && i >= merged[k][1]) k++;
    if (k < merged.length && i >= merged[k][0] && i < merged[k][1]) continue;
    out += text[i];
    map.push(i);
  }
  map.push(text.length);
  return { text: out, map, removed: merged };
}

function identity(n: number): number[] { return Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, (_, i) => i); }

/** Maps a (charIndex, charLength) in the stripped text back to the original text. */
export function toOriginalRange(s: StrippedText, charIndex: number, charLength: number): { charIndex: number; charLength: number } {
  const i = Math.max(0, Math.min(charIndex, s.map.length - 1));
  const j = Math.max(i, Math.min(charIndex + Math.max(1, charLength) - 1, s.map.length - 2));
  const start = s.map[i];
  const end = j >= 0 && j < s.map.length - 1 ? s.map[j] + 1 : start + charLength;
  return { charIndex: start, charLength: Math.max(0, end - start) };
}

### `src/core/import/text.ts` (357 lines)

~~~~~ts
/**
 * Plain-text / Markdown importer, plus the paragraph and statistics helpers shared by every importer.
 *
 * Text rules (see parseBlock): paragraphs are separated by blank lines; single newlines inside a
 * paragraph are hard wraps and join with a space (a trailing hyphen followed by a lower-case line joins
 * the word back together); Markdown headings ('# ', setext underlines) become h1/h2/h3; a lone short
 * line without terminal punctuation between blank lines is a heading (h2); '- ' / '* ' / '1. ' lines are
 * list items; '> ' lines are block quotes; fenced code blocks are 'pre'. The book title comes from the
 * YAML front matter, else the first heading, else the first line. There is one chapter per '# ' heading
 * when there are at least two of them (or per "Chapter N" style heading), otherwise a single chapter.
 */
import type { Book, Chapter, Paragraph, ParagraphKind } from '@core/model';
import type { Segmenter } from '@core/segment';
import type { ImportContext, Importer } from './types';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Shared helpers (used by the EPUB importer too)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A paragraph before segmentation: plain text with a kind. */
export interface RawParagraph { kind: ParagraphKind; text: string }

/** Zero-width space, word joiner and BOM: typesetting noise that only confuses segmentation and TTS. */
const STRIP_INVISIBLES = /[​⁠﻿]/g;
const WHITESPACE_RUN = /\s+/g;

/** Collapses every whitespace run (including no-break spaces) to one space and trims. */
export function normalizeWhitespace(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(STRIP_INVISIBLES, '').replace(WHITESPACE_RUN, ' ').trim();
}

/** Normalises, segments and numbers paragraphs, dropping those with no text or no sentences. */
export function assembleParagraphs(raw: readonly RawParagraph[], segmenter: Segmenter): Paragraph[] {
  const out: Paragraph[] = [];
  for (const r of raw) {
    const text = normalizeWhitespace(r.text);
    if (text.length === 0) continue;
    const sentences = segmenter.segmentParagraph(text);
    if (sentences.length === 0) continue; // nothing speakable (only invisible characters)
    out.push({ index: out.length, kind: r.kind, text, sentences });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Book.stats: words count 'word' and 'number' tokens (as a word processor would). */
export function computeStats(chapters: readonly Chapter[]): Book['stats'] {
  let words = 0;
  let paragraphs = 0;
  let sentences = 0;
  for (const ch of chapters) {
    for (const p of ch.paragraphs) {
      paragraphs++;
      sentences += p.sentences.length;
      for (const s of p.sentences) {
        for (const t of s.tokens) if (t.kind === 'word' || t.kind === 'number') words++;
      }
    }
  }
  return { words, paragraphs, sentences };
}

/** Decodes a text file: UTF-16 with a BOM, else UTF-8 (a UTF-8 BOM is consumed by the decoder). */
export function decodeTextBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  if (bytes.length >= 2) {
    if (bytes[0] === 0xff && bytes[1] === 0xfe) return new TextDecoder('utf-16le').decode(bytes.subarray(2));
    if (bytes[0] === 0xfe && bytes[1] === 0xff) return decodeUtf16be(bytes.subarray(2));
  }
  return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes);
}

/** UTF-16BE without relying on ICU (small-icu Node builds lack the 'utf-16be' label): swap to LE. */
function decodeUtf16be(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  const even = bytes.length & ~1;
  const swapped = new Uint8Array(even);
  for (let i = 0; i < even; i += 2) {
    swapped[i] = bytes[i + 1];
    swapped[i + 1] = bytes[i];
  }
  return new TextDecoder('utf-16le').decode(swapped);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Line classification
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

type LineType = 'blank' | 'fence' | 'atx' | 'hr' | 'underline' | 'list' | 'quote' | 'text';

const RE = {
  blank: /^\s*$/,
  fence: /^\s{0,3}(?:```|~~~)/,
  /** '# Title', '## Title ##' (closing hashes stripped later). A bare '#' line matches atxBare instead. */
  atx: /^\s{0,3}(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.+?)[ \t]*$/,
  atxBare: /^\s{0,3}#{1,6}[ \t]*$/,
  trailingHashes: /[ \t]+#+$/,
  /** setext underlines: '===' under a line is h1, '---' (three or more) is h2 */
  underlineH1: /^\s{0,3}=+[ \t]*$/,
  underlineH2: /^\s{0,3}-{3,}[ \t]*$/,
  /** horizontal rule / scene break: '---', '* * *', '___' */
  hr: /^\s{0,3}([-*_])(?:[ \t]*\1){2,}[ \t]*$/,
  /** '- item', '* item', '+ item', '• item', '1. item', '2) item' */
  list: /^\s{0,8}(?:[-*+•]|\d{1,3}[.)])[ \t]+(\S.*)$/,
  quote: /^\s{0,3}>[ \t]?(.*)$/,
};

function lineType(line: string): LineType {
  if (RE.blank.test(line)) return 'blank';
  if (RE.fence.test(line)) return 'fence';
  if (RE.atx.test(line) || RE.atxBare.test(line)) return 'atx';
  if (RE.hr.test(line)) return 'hr'; // before list: '- - -' is a rule, not an item
  if (RE.underlineH1.test(line)) return 'underline';
  if (RE.list.test(line)) return 'list';
  if (RE.quote.test(line)) return 'quote';
  return 'text';
}

function isUnderline(line: string): boolean {
  return RE.underlineH1.test(line) || RE.underlineH2.test(line);
}

/**
 * Heading heuristic for plain text: short, starts with a capital or digit, no terminal punctuation,
 * at most a dozen words. Callers also require it to be a block of its own with text after it.
 */
export function looksLikeHeading(line: string): boolean {
  const t = line.trim();
  if (t.length === 0 || t.length > 80) return false;
  if (!/^[\p{Lu}\p{N}]/u.test(t)) return false;
  if (/[.!?,;…]$/.test(t)) return false;
  if (/[”"’')\]]$/.test(t)) return false;
  return t.split(/\s+/).length <= 12;
}

/** "Chapter 3", "CHAPTER XII", "Part Two", "Book 1: The Beginning" — used to split plain text into chapters. */
const CHAPTER_HEADING = /^(?:chapter|part|book|act|canto|letter|section)\s+(?:\d+|[ivxlc]+|one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve|thirteen|fourteen|fifteen|sixteen|seventeen|eighteen|nineteen|twenty|thirty|forty|fifty|first|second|third|last)\b/i;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Block parsing
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface TextBlock extends RawParagraph {
  /** A level-1 Markdown heading ('# ' or a '===' underline): candidate chapter start. */
  top?: boolean;
}

/** Joins hard-wrapped lines with spaces, re-joining a word hyphenated across the break ("some-\nthing"). */
export function joinWrappedLines(lines: readonly string[]): string {
  let out = '';
  for (const raw of lines) {
    const l = raw.trim();
    if (l.length === 0) continue;
    if (out.length === 0) out = l;
    else if (/\p{L}-$/u.test(out) && /^\p{Ll}/u.test(l)) out = out.slice(0, -1) + l;
    else out += ' ' + l;
  }
  return out;
}

/** Removes light Markdown inline syntax so the reader sees prose: links, images, code spans, emphasis. */
export function cleanInline(s: string): string {
  return s
    .replace(/!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)/g, '') // images
    .replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)/g, '$1') // [text](url)
    .replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\[[^\]]*\]/g, '$1') // [text][ref]
    .replace(/<br\s*\/?>/gi, ' ')
    .replace(/`([^`]*)`/g, '$1')
    .replace(/(\*\*|__)(?=\S)([\s\S]+?)(?<=\S)\1/g, '$2')
    .replace(/(?<![\p{L}\p{N}])([*_])(?=\S)([^*_]+?)(?<=\S)\1(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/gu, '$2');
}

function headingKind(level: number): ParagraphKind {
  return level === 1 ? 'h1' : level === 2 ? 'h2' : 'h3';
}

/** Turns one blank-line-delimited block into paragraphs. `hasFollowing`: more blocks come after it. */
function parseBlock(lines: readonly string[], hasFollowing: boolean): TextBlock[] {
  const out: TextBlock[] = [];
  if (lines.length === 1 && hasFollowing && lineType(lines[0]) === 'text' && looksLikeHeading(lines[0])) {
    out.push({ kind: 'h2', text: cleanInline(lines[0].trim()) });
    return out;
  }
  let i = 0;
  while (i < lines.length) {
    const line = lines[i];
    const type = lineType(line);

    if (type === 'text' && i + 1 < lines.length && isUnderline(lines[i + 1])) {
      const h1 = RE.underlineH1.test(lines[i + 1]);
      out.push({ kind: h1 ? 'h1' : 'h2', text: cleanInline(line.trim()), top: h1 });
      i += 2;
      continue;
    }
    if (type === 'atx') {
      const m = RE.atx.exec(line);
      if (m) {
        const text = cleanInline(m[2].replace(RE.trailingHashes, '').trim());
        if (text) out.push({ kind: headingKind(m[1].length), text, top: m[1].length === 1 });
      }
      i++;
      continue;
    }
    if (type === 'hr' || type === 'underline' || type === 'blank' || type === 'fence') { i++; continue; }
    if (type === 'list') {
      const item = [RE.list.exec(line)![1]];
      i++;
      while (i < lines.length && lineType(lines[i]) === 'text') item.push(lines[i++]); // wrapped item
      out.push({ kind: 'li', text: cleanInline(joinWrappedLines(item)) });
      continue;
    }
    if (type === 'quote') {
      let para: string[] = [];
      const flush = (): void => {
        if (para.length) out.push({ kind: 'blockquote', text: cleanInline(joinWrappedLines(para)) });
        para = [];
      };
      while (i < lines.length) {
        const t = lineType(lines[i]);
        if (t === 'quote') {
          const inner = RE.quote.exec(lines[i])![1];
          if (RE.blank.test(inner)) flush(); else para.push(inner); // a bare '>' separates quote paragraphs
          i++;
        } else if (t === 'text' && para.length) {
          para.push(lines[i++]); // lazy continuation line
        } else break;
      }
      flush();
      continue;
    }
    // plain text: consecutive text lines are one hard-wrapped paragraph
    const para: string[] = [];
    while (i < lines.length && lineType(lines[i]) === 'text') {
      if (para.length && i + 1 < lines.length && isUnderline(lines[i + 1])) break; // leave "line + underline" to the heading branch
      para.push(lines[i++]);
    }
    if (para.length) out.push({ kind: 'p', text: cleanInline(joinWrappedLines(para)) });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Splits the body into blank-line-delimited blocks (fenced code is its own block) and parses each. */
export function parseTextBlocks(body: string): TextBlock[] {
  const lines = body.split('\n');
  const blocks: { lines: string[]; pre: boolean }[] = [];
  let cur: string[] = [];
  const flush = (): void => { if (cur.length) { blocks.push({ lines: cur, pre: false }); cur = []; } };
  let i = 0;
  while (i < lines.length) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (RE.fence.test(line)) {
      flush();
      const code: string[] = [];
      i++;
      while (i < lines.length && !RE.fence.test(lines[i])) code.push(lines[i++]);
      i++; // closing fence (or end of text)
      if (code.some((l) => !RE.blank.test(l))) blocks.push({ lines: code, pre: true });
      continue;
    }
    if (RE.blank.test(line)) flush(); else cur.push(line);
    i++;
  }
  flush();
  const out: TextBlock[] = [];
  blocks.forEach((b, idx) => {
    if (b.pre) out.push({ kind: 'pre', text: b.lines.map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean).join(' ') });
    else out.push(...parseBlock(b.lines, idx < blocks.length - 1));
  });
  return out;
}

interface FrontMatter { title?: string; author?: string; body: string }

/** Pandoc/Jekyll style YAML front matter: only `title:` and `author:` scalars are read; the block is removed. */
function stripFrontMatter(text: string): FrontMatter {
  const m = /^---[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)\n(?:---|\.\.\.)[ \t]*(?:\n|$)/.exec(text);
  if (!m || m[1].split('\n').length > 50) return { body: text };
  const fm: FrontMatter = { body: text.slice(m[0].length) };
  for (const line of m[1].split('\n')) {
    const kv = /^(title|author)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$/i.exec(line);
    if (!kv || kv[2].startsWith('[')) continue;
    const value = kv[2].replace(/^(["'])(.*)\1$/, '$2');
    if (kv[1].toLowerCase() === 'title') fm.title ??= value; else fm.author ??= value;
  }
  return fm;
}

interface ChapterGroup { title: string; paragraphs: RawParagraph[] }

/** One chapter per level-1 heading (or "Chapter N" heading) when there are at least two; else one chapter 'Text'. */
function groupChapters(blocks: readonly TextBlock[]): ChapterGroup[] {
  let starts: number[] = [];
  blocks.forEach((b, i) => { if (b.top) starts.push(i); });
  if (starts.length < 2) {
    starts = [];
    blocks.forEach((b, i) => { if ((b.kind === 'h1' || b.kind === 'h2' || b.kind === 'h3') && CHAPTER_HEADING.test(b.text)) starts.push(i); });
  }
  if (starts.length < 2) return [{ title: 'Text', paragraphs: [...blocks] }];
  const out: ChapterGroup[] = [];
  if (starts[0] > 0) out.push({ title: 'Introduction', paragraphs: blocks.slice(0, starts[0]) });
  starts.forEach((start, k) => {
    const end = k + 1 < starts.length ? starts[k + 1] : blocks.length;
    out.push({ title: normalizeWhitespace(blocks[start].text), paragraphs: blocks.slice(start, end) });
  });
  return out;
}

const MAX_DERIVED_TITLE = 80;

/** The first heading, else the first line cut at a word boundary. */
function deriveTitle(blocks: readonly TextBlock[]): string {
  const heading = blocks.find((b) => b.kind === 'h1' || b.kind === 'h2' || b.kind === 'h3');
  if (heading) return normalizeWhitespace(heading.text);
  const first = blocks.find((b) => normalizeWhitespace(b.text).length > 0);
  if (!first) return 'Untitled';
  const text = normalizeWhitespace(first.text);
  if (text.length <= MAX_DERIVED_TITLE) return text;
  const cut = text.lastIndexOf(' ', MAX_DERIVED_TITLE);
  return text.slice(0, cut > 20 ? cut : MAX_DERIVED_TITLE).replace(/[\s,;:]+$/, '') + '…';
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public API
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Builds a Book from plain text or Markdown. `title` wins when non-empty (the paste flow); otherwise the
 * title is derived from the text. Throws when the text contains no readable paragraphs.
 */
export async function textToBook(title: string, text: string, ctx: ImportContext): Promise<Book> {
  const source = text.replace(/^﻿/, '').replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').replace(/\f/g, '\n\n');
  const fm = stripFrontMatter(source);
  const blocks = parseTextBlocks(fm.body);
  const chapters: Chapter[] = [];
  for (const group of groupChapters(blocks)) {
    const paragraphs = assembleParagraphs(group.paragraphs, ctx.segmenter);
    if (paragraphs.length === 0) continue;
    chapters.push({ index: chapters.length, title: group.title, paragraphs });
  }
  if (chapters.length === 0) throw new Error('No readable text found');
  const bookTitle = normalizeWhitespace(title) || (fm.title ? normalizeWhitespace(fm.title) : '') || deriveTitle(blocks);
  const book: Book = {
    id: ctx.id,
    title: bookTitle,
    source: { kind: 'text', importedAt: new Date().toISOString() },
    chapters,
    names: [],
    stats: computeStats(chapters),
  };
  if (fm.author) book.author = normalizeWhitespace(fm.author);
  if (ctx.sourcePath) book.source.path = ctx.sourcePath;
  return book;
}

export const textImporter: Importer = {
  kind: 'text',
  importBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, ctx: ImportContext): Promise<Book> {
    return textToBook('', decodeTextBytes(bytes), ctx);
  },
};

import type { Book } from '@core/model';
import type { Segmenter } from '@core/segment';

/**
 * Importers turn a file (or pasted text) into a Book. They run in the Electron main process (Node),
 * so they may use Node APIs and npm packages that work without a DOM (jszip, htmlparser2, pdfjs-dist legacy build).
 * Every importer must: produce plain-text paragraphs (no HTML), keep headings as their own paragraphs,
 * join hyphenated line breaks, drop running headers/footers/page numbers where detectable,
 * segment every paragraph with the given Segmenter, and compute Book.stats and Book.names (see names.ts).
 */
export interface ImportContext {
  segmenter: Segmenter;
  /** sha256 hex of the source bytes/text; the importer must copy it to Book.id */
  id: string;
  sourcePath?: string;
}

export interface Importer {
  kind: 'epub' | 'pdf' | 'text';
  importBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, ctx: ImportContext): Promise<Book>;
}

### `src/core/level/adapt.ts` (150 lines)

```ts
import type { Dictionary } from '@core/dict/types';
import { levelIndex } from '@core/model';
import { BANDS, bandOfRank, rankOf } from './items';
import { randBeta, seededRng } from './rng';
import type { BandCounts, LevelResult } from './score';
import { bandKnowledge, buildResult, percentile, sizeFromKnowledge } from './score';

/**
 * Daily adaptation of the level estimate from "I know / I don't know" taps (spec section 5).
 *
 * One Beta(alpha_b, beta_b) posterior per frequency band, initialised from a test result
 * (alpha = 1 + k_b n_b, beta = 1 + (1 - k_b) n_b). A tap on a word of band b is one observation of weight 0.5:
 * "know" adds to alpha_b, "don't know" (or a lookup) adds to beta_b; a lemma counts once. Both parameters decay
 * toward the Beta(1,1) prior by 0.98 per week so recent evidence dominates. `estimate()` recomputes V and the
 * CEFR level with the section-3 formula (taps carry no pseudowords, so the counts are used uncorrected).
 */

export const TAP_WEIGHT = 0.5;
export const WEEKLY_DECAY = 0.98;
export const ESTIMATE_DRAWS = 1000;

export interface LevelModelJSON {
  version: 1;
  alpha: number[];
  beta: number[];
  /** false-alarm rate of the test the model was initialised from (0 when none) */
  falseAlarmRate: number;
  /** lemmas already counted */
  seen: string[];
  /** ISO time of the last observation or decay, for the caller's own bookkeeping */
  updatedAt: string | null;
  /** ISO time of the test the model was reset from */
  testedAt: string | null;
}

export class LevelModel {
  private alpha: number[];
  private beta: number[];
  private falseAlarm: number;
  private seen: Set<string>;
  updatedAt: string | null;
  testedAt: string | null;

  private constructor(j: LevelModelJSON) {
    this.alpha = BANDS.map((b) => (Number.isFinite(j.alpha[b.index]) ? Math.max(1, j.alpha[b.index]) : 1));
    this.beta = BANDS.map((b) => (Number.isFinite(j.beta[b.index]) ? Math.max(1, j.beta[b.index]) : 1));
    this.falseAlarm = Number.isFinite(j.falseAlarmRate) ? j.falseAlarmRate : 0;
    this.seen = new Set(j.seen ?? []);
    this.updatedAt = j.updatedAt ?? null;
    this.testedAt = j.testedAt ?? null;
  }

  /** A flat Beta(1,1) in every band: no information yet. */
  static initial(): LevelModel {
    return new LevelModel({ version: 1, alpha: BANDS.map(() => 1), beta: BANDS.map(() => 1), falseAlarmRate: 0, seen: [], updatedAt: null, testedAt: null });
  }

  /** Resets the posteriors from a test result: alpha = 1 + k n, beta = 1 + (1 - k) n per band. */
  static fromTest(result: LevelResult, testedAt: string | null = null): LevelModel {
    const alpha = BANDS.map(() => 1); const beta = BANDS.map(() => 1);
    for (const pb of result.perBand) {
      if (pb.band < 0 || pb.band >= BANDS.length) continue;
      alpha[pb.band] = 1 + pb.k * pb.n;
      beta[pb.band] = 1 + (1 - pb.k) * pb.n;
    }
    return new LevelModel({ version: 1, alpha, beta, falseAlarmRate: result.falseAlarmRate, seen: [], updatedAt: testedAt, testedAt });
  }

  static fromJSON(j: LevelModelJSON | string): LevelModel {
    const o = typeof j === 'string' ? (JSON.parse(j) as LevelModelJSON) : j;
    if (!o || o.version !== 1 || !Array.isArray(o.alpha) || !Array.isArray(o.beta)) throw new Error('not a LevelModel');
    return new LevelModel(o);
  }

  toJSON(): LevelModelJSON {
    return {
      version: 1, alpha: [...this.alpha], beta: [...this.beta], falseAlarmRate: this.falseAlarm,
      seen: [...this.seen].sort(), updatedAt: this.updatedAt, testedAt: this.testedAt,
    };
  }

  /** Posterior parameters per band (for display: "2-3k: 14 of 18 known"). */
  bands(): { band: number; alpha: number; beta: number; mean: number }[] {
    return BANDS.map((b) => ({ band: b.index, alpha: this.alpha[b.index], beta: this.beta[b.index], mean: this.alpha[b.index] / (this.alpha[b.index] + this.beta[b.index]) }));
  }

  /**
   * One tap on a word as it appears in text. Returns false (and changes nothing) when the word is unknown to
   * the dictionary, has no corpus rank in the test's range, or its lemma was already counted.
   */
  observe(word: string, knows: boolean, dict: Dictionary, at: string | null = null): boolean {
    const r = dict.lookup(word);
    if (!r) return false;
    const band = bandOfRank(rankOf({ f: r.entry.frq, b: r.entry.bnc }));
    if (band < 0) return false;
    if (this.seen.has(r.lemma)) return false;
    this.seen.add(r.lemma);
    if (knows) this.alpha[band] += TAP_WEIGHT; else this.beta[band] += TAP_WEIGHT;
    if (at) this.updatedAt = at;
    return true;
  }

  /** Decays the evidence (the part above the Beta(1,1) prior) by 0.98 per week. */
  decay(weeks: number, at: string | null = null): void {
    if (!(weeks > 0)) return;
    const d = Math.pow(WEEKLY_DECAY, weeks);
    for (let b = 0; b < BANDS.length; b++) {
      this.alpha[b] = 1 + (this.alpha[b] - 1) * d;
      this.beta[b] = 1 + (this.beta[b] - 1) * d;
    }
    if (at) this.updatedAt = at;
  }

  /** Evidence counted so far (alpha + beta - 2 summed over bands). */
  observations(): number {
    return this.alpha.reduce((s, a, b) => s + a + this.beta[b] - 2, 0);
  }

  /**
   * Current estimate in the test's result shape. The point estimate uses the posterior counts (n = alpha + beta - 2,
   * yes = alpha - 1) through the section-3 shrinkage; the 80% interval is a parametric bootstrap from the
   * posteriors (deterministic for a given seed). There are no CEFR-tagged items here, so `cefr` is the size level.
   */
  estimate(seed: number | string = 'level-model'): LevelResult {
    const counts: BandCounts[] = BANDS.map((b) => ({ n: this.alpha[b.index] + this.beta[b.index] - 2, yes: this.alpha[b.index] - 1 }));
    const k = bandKnowledge(counts, 0);
    const rng = seededRng(seed);
    const sizes: number[] = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < ESTIMATE_DRAWS; r++) {
      const draw: BandCounts[] = BANDS.map((b) => {
        const p = randBeta(rng, this.alpha[b.index], this.beta[b.index]);
        return { n: counts[b.index].n, yes: p * counts[b.index].n };
      });
      sizes.push(sizeFromKnowledge(bandKnowledge(draw, 0)));
    }
    sizes.sort((x, y) => x - y);
    return buildResult({ k, counts, f: this.falseAlarm, interval: [percentile(sizes, 0.1), percentile(sizes, 0.9)] });
  }
}

/**
 * Whether a nightly re-estimate should be surfaced to the learner: only when the 80% interval has moved a whole
 * CEFR level in the same direction (both ends up, or both ends down), or the point level changed by two.
 */
export function significantChange(prev: LevelResult, next: LevelResult): boolean {
  const dLo = levelIndex(next.cefrRange[0]) - levelIndex(prev.cefrRange[0]);
  const dHi = levelIndex(next.cefrRange[1]) - levelIndex(prev.cefrRange[1]);
  if ((dLo > 0 && dHi > 0) || (dLo < 0 && dHi < 0)) return true;
  return Math.abs(levelIndex(next.cefr) - levelIndex(prev.cefr)) >= 2;
}
```

import type { CefrLevel } from '@core/model';
import type { DictData, DictRaw } from '@shared/api';
import { parseGloss, suffixCandidates } from '@core/dict/dictionary';
import type { Rng } from './rng';
import { shuffle } from './rng';

/**
 * Item pools for the vocabulary level test (docs/research/research-level-test.md, sections 3-4).
 *
 * Every headword of the dictionary is assigned to one of eight frequency bands by its COCA rank (`frq`,
 * falling back to the BNC rank), and the ones that make good yes/no items are kept: single lower-case
 * alphabetic tokens of 3-12 letters, base forms, content words, not names, abbreviations, swear words,
 * transparent derivations of a more frequent word or loans a Chinese speaker knows anyway. CEFR-tagged
 * words are preferred at selection time so the CEFR cross-check has data in every band.
 */

export interface Band {
  /** 0-based position in BANDS */
  index: number;
  /** inclusive rank range */
  lo: number;
  hi: number;
  /** number of lemmas the band stands for (hi - lo + 1) */
  width: number;
  /** "1-2k", "5-7k" ... */
  label: string;
}

const BAND_EDGES: readonly [number, number][] = [
  [1, 2000], [2001, 3000], [3001, 4000], [4001, 5000], [5001, 7000], [7001, 10000], [10001, 14000], [14001, 20000],
];

export const BANDS: readonly Band[] = BAND_EDGES.map(([lo, hi], index) => ({
  index, lo, hi, width: hi - lo + 1, label: `${lo <= 1 ? 1 : Math.round((lo - 1) / 1000)}-${hi / 1000}k`,
}));

/** Lemmas covered by all bands together (the largest size the test can report). */
export const MAX_RANK = BAND_EDGES[BAND_EDGES.length - 1][1];

/** The corpus rank used for banding: COCA `frq`, else BNC `bnc`, else 0 (unranked). */
export function rankOf(raw: Pick<DictRaw, 'f' | 'b'>): number {
  if (raw.f > 0) return raw.f;
  if (raw.b > 0) return raw.b;
  return 0;
}

/** Band index for a rank, or -1 when the rank is 0 or beyond the last band. */
export function bandOfRank(rank: number): number {
  if (!(rank > 0) || rank > MAX_RANK) return -1;
  for (const b of BANDS) if (rank <= b.hi) return b.index;
  return -1;
}

/** The band in which a vocabulary size (lemmas) falls: 0 for sizes up to 2,000, 7 for anything over 14,000. */
export function bandOfSize(lemmas: number): number {
  const v = Math.max(1, Math.min(MAX_RANK, Math.round(lemmas)));
  return bandOfRank(v);
}

export type ItemPos = 'n' | 'v' | 'adj' | 'adv';

export interface PoolItem {
  word: string;
  rank: number;
  band: number;
  pos: ItemPos;
  /** CEFR-J / Octanove level; null when the dictionary only estimated one */
  level: CefrLevel | null;
  /** Oxford 3000 or Collins 3+ stars: a "textbook" word */
  textbook: boolean;
}

export interface ItemPools {
  /** one array per band, in BANDS order, sorted by word (shuffle at selection time) */
  bands: PoolItem[][];
  /** candidates rejected per rule, for diagnostics */
  rejected: Record<string, number>;
}

export interface PoolOptions {
  /** lemmas to leave out, e.g. words the learner met in the last 30 days of reading */
  exclude?: Iterable<string>;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Word lists
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/** Whole-word swear/taboo list: never shown as a test item. */
export const SWEAR_WORDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'fuck', 'fucker', 'fucking', 'shit', 'shitty', 'bullshit', 'cunt', 'bitch', 'bastard', 'asshole', 'arsehole',
  'arse', 'ass', 'dick', 'cock', 'prick', 'pussy', 'whore', 'slut', 'fag', 'faggot', 'nigger', 'negro', 'piss',
  'crap', 'damn', 'bugger', 'wank', 'wanker', 'twat', 'bollocks', 'tits', 'boobs', 'penis', 'vagina', 'retard',

/** Substrings that disqualify a generated pseudoword. */
export const SWEAR_SUBSTRINGS: readonly string[] = [
  'fuck', 'shit', 'cunt', 'nigg', 'fag', 'dick', 'piss', 'slut', 'whore', 'wank', 'twat', 'jizz', 'cock', 'tits',

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Classification helpers (exported for tests)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

const WORD_RE = /^[a-z]{3,12}$/;
/** ECDICT marks inflections in the gloss ("give的过去分词", "child的复数") */
const INFLECTION_GLOSS_RE = /的?(过去式|过去分词|复数|现在分词|比较级|最高级|第三人称|单数)/;
/** Abbreviations: "abbr." tag, or a gloss that says so, or an "=expansion" gloss. */
const ABBREV_GLOSS_RE = /缩写|缩略|略语|简称|^=|\(=|（=/;
/** Proper nouns ECDICT lower-cased: explicit markers in the first gloss line. */
const PROPER_GLOSS_RE = /人名|地名|姓氏|\[姓\]|（姓）|\(姓\)|国名|州名|城市名|河名|山名|湖名|海名|首都|的首府|希腊字母|字母表的第/;
/** Common names, nationalities, languages, religions and calendar words ECDICT lists as plain lower-case headwords. */
export const PROPER_WORDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'english', 'england', 'britain', 'british', 'briton', 'london', 'scotland', 'scottish', 'scot', 'wales', 'welsh',
