```ts
import type { Sentence, Token, TokenKind } from './model';

/**
 * Sentence and word segmentation for English prose.
 *
 * Built on Intl.Segmenter (ICU) with a merge pass that repairs the known ICU failures on literary
 * text: title abbreviations ("Mr. Darcy"), initials ("J. K. Rowling"), common Latin abbreviations
 * ("e.g.", "etc."), closing quotes/brackets after sentence punctuation, and ellipses.
 * Word tokens keep internal apostrophes ("don't", "Darcy's") and single hyphens ("well-known").
 *
 * Conventions (consumers rely on these):
 * - All offsets index the ORIGINAL string passed in (UTF-16 code units, end exclusive), and
 *   `token.text === text.slice(token.start, token.end)` always holds.
 * - Whitespace is never emitted as a token. Tokens are sorted and non-overlapping; the gaps between
 *   them (spaces, soft hyphens, invisible format characters) are rendered as plain text by the reader.
 *   The 'space' TokenKind therefore never occurs in the output of this module.
 * - Sentences are trimmed (no leading/trailing whitespace or invisible format characters) and never
 *   empty; a paragraph with no terminal punctuation is a single sentence; a whitespace-only paragraph
 *   yields no sentences. Every sentence of a paragraph that contains any letter or digit contains at
 *   least one letter or digit: stray punctuation between sentences ("Hello. “") is absorbed.
 * - Invisible format characters (Unicode category Cf: soft hyphen U+00AD, zero-width joiners, bidi
 *   marks and isolates, BOM/word joiner, ...) are removed before segmentation so ICU and the
 *   abbreviation heuristics see the intact word. Offsets are mapped back, so a token that contains
 *   such a character in the middle keeps it in its text ("ab­solutely"); a token never starts
 *   or ends with one. Dictionary lookups should fold them (at least U+00AD). The zero-width SPACE
 *   (U+200B) is a word separator, not glue, and is left for ICU to break on.
 * - Runs of adjacent punctuation collapse into one 'punct' token ("?!", "...", ".”").
 * - word + single hyphen (- U+2010 U+2011) + word, with no spaces, joins into one token
 *   ("well-known", "state-of-the-art"); a double hyphen or dash never joins. A joined token is a
 *   'number' only when every part is a number ("10-12"), otherwise a 'word' ("5-year").
 *
 * Known limitations of the heuristics (documented so the reader can explain surprising splits):
 * - A single capital letter before a period is always treated as an initial, so "Plan A. Then we
 *   left." becomes one sentence. "I." is only an initial when it follows another initial or a title.
 * - Title abbreviations always merge, so "Main St. The house..." is one sentence (spec requirement).
 * - A conditional abbreviation followed by an ALL CAPS word splits ("THE U.S. ECONOMY" is two
 *   sentences): in capitals, the uppercase signal that ends "the U.S. Then he left." is lost.
 * - A hard line break followed by an uppercase letter is a sentence boundary (ICU behaviour);
 *   importers normalise whitespace so this does not arise for imported books.
 * - A straight single quote before a lowercase elision ("'tis") counts as an opening quote.
 */
export interface Segmenter {
  /** Splits one paragraph of plain text into sentences with word/number/punct tokens. Offsets index into `text`. */
  segmentParagraph(text: string): Sentence[];
  /** Tokenises arbitrary text (used for popups and phrase selection). */
  tokenize(text: string): Token[];
}

export type { Sentence, Token, TokenKind };

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Abbreviation tables
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Title-like abbreviations: a sentence practically never ends with one, so a split after them is
 * always repaired. Matched with the exact capitalisation shown, or in ALL CAPS (headings).
 */
const TITLE_ABBREVIATIONS = new Set([
  'Mr', 'Mrs', 'Ms', 'Dr', 'Prof', 'St', 'Mt', 'Capt', 'Col', 'Gen', 'Lt', 'Sgt', 'Sr', 'Jr', 'Rev', 'Hon',
  'Messrs', 'Mme', 'Mlle',
  // a few more that behave exactly like the ones above
  'Fr', 'Sen', 'Gov', 'Pres', 'Maj', 'Adm', 'Cmdr', 'Cpl', 'Pvt', 'Supt', 'Insp', 'Brig',
]);

/**
 * Abbreviations that introduce something and therefore never end a sentence ("Brown vs. Board",
 * "e.g. Apples"). Always merged, whatever follows. Lower-cased, internal dots kept.
 */
const ALWAYS_MERGE_ABBREVIATIONS = new Set(['vs', 'v', 'e.g', 'i.e', 'cf', 'viz']);

/**
 * Abbreviations that usually continue the sentence but can also end one ("at 5 p.m. He left.").
 * Merged unless the next segment starts with an uppercase letter. Lower-cased, internal dots kept.
 */
const CONDITIONAL_ABBREVIATIONS = new Set([
  'etc', 'no', 'fig', 'figs', 'p', 'pp', 'ch', 'vol', 'vols', 'ed', 'eds', 'approx', 'inc', 'ltd', 'co', 'corp',
  'jan', 'feb', 'mar', 'apr', 'jun', 'jul', 'aug', 'sep', 'sept', 'oct', 'nov', 'dec',
  'a.m', 'p.m', 'u.s', 'u.k', 'u.s.a', 'b.c', 'a.d',
  // common in non-fiction
  'al', 'sec', 'dept', 'univ', 'ave', 'blvd', 'rd', 'est', 'op', 'cit', 'ibid', 'eq', 'ff', 'cont', 'misc', 'bros',
]);

/** Closing quotes/brackets that ICU sometimes leaves at the start of the following segment. */
const UNAMBIGUOUS_CLOSERS = new Set(['”', '»', ')', ']']); // ” » ) ]
const AMBIGUOUS_CLOSERS = new Set(['"', "'", '’']); // " ' ’  (also used as openers / apostrophes)
/** Opening quotes/brackets that ICU sometimes glues to the END of the previous segment ("end.”“Start"). */
const UNAMBIGUOUS_OPENERS = new Set(['“', '‘', '«', '(', '[']); // “ ‘ « ( [
/** Everything that may precede the first letter of a sentence ("“Then", '("Then'). */
const LEADING_OPENERS = new Set(['“', '‘', '«', '‹', '(', '[', '{', '"', "'"]);

/** Hyphens that join two words into one token (ASCII hyphen-minus, U+2010 hyphen, U+2011 non-breaking hyphen). */
const JOINING_HYPHENS = new Set(['-', '‐', '‑']);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Character classes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Invisible format characters (category Cf) that glue to the surrounding text in ICU's word rules:
 * soft hyphen, ZWJ/ZWNJ, bidi marks/embeddings/isolates, BOM, word joiner, invisible operators,
 * tag characters. The zero-width space U+200B is excluded: it separates words.
 */
const FORMAT_CHAR = /(?!​)\p{Cf}/u;
const FORMAT_CHAR_G = /(?!​)\p{Cf}/gu;
/** Whitespace plus invisible control/format characters (never part of a token, trimmed from sentences). */
const INVISIBLE_CHAR = /[\s\p{Cf}\p{Cc}]/u;
const ONLY_INVISIBLE = /^[\s\p{Cf}\p{Cc}]*$/u;
const WORD_CHAR = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const STARTS_LOWER = /^\p{Ll}/u;
const STARTS_UPPER = /^\p{Lu}/u;
const STARTS_ALNUM = /^[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const SINGLE_UPPER = /^\p{Lu}$/u;
/** "3", "3.50", "1,000", "3,000.5" — digits with number punctuation between digit groups. */
const NUMBER_TOKEN = /^\p{Nd}+(?:[.,]\p{Nd}+)*$/u;
/**
 * The abbreviation candidate ending a segment: a run of letters (with optional internal dots, as in
 * "e.g" or "U.S") followed by exactly one period at the very end. Must not be preceded by a letter,
 * digit or dot, so "first." yields "first" (not "st") and "etc..." yields nothing (ellipsis).
 */
const TRAILING_ABBREVIATION = /(?:^|[^\p{L}\p{N}.])(\p{L}+(?:\.\p{L}+)*)\.$/u;
/** How much of a segment's tail the abbreviation check looks at; keeps the merge pass O(n). */
const TAIL_WINDOW = 64;
/** A straight quote after one of these opens a quotation (start of text, whitespace, brackets, dashes, quotes). */
const BEFORE_OPENING_QUOTE = /[\s\p{Ps}\p{Pi}\p{Pd}"']/u;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Format-character stripping with an offset map back to the original string
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Stripped {
  /** text without format characters */
  text: string;
  /** orig[i] = index in the original string of the i-th code unit of `text`; null when nothing was stripped */
  orig: Int32Array | null;
}

function stripFormatChars(text: string): Stripped {
  if (!FORMAT_CHAR.test(text)) return { text, orig: null };
  const orig = new Int32Array(text.length);
  let out = '';
  let n = 0;
  // Build the kept text in chunks between format characters (some are astral, hence m[0].length).
  let chunkStart = 0;
  for (const m of text.matchAll(FORMAT_CHAR_G)) {
    const i = m.index;
    for (let k = chunkStart; k < i; k++) orig[n++] = k;
    out += text.slice(chunkStart, i);
    chunkStart = i + m[0].length;
  }
  for (let k = chunkStart; k < text.length; k++) orig[n++] = k;
  out += text.slice(chunkStart);
  return { text: out, orig: orig.subarray(0, n) };
}

/** Maps a half-open range in the stripped text to the original text. Requires start < end. */
function mapRange(st: Stripped, start: number, end: number): [number, number] {
  if (!st.orig) return [start, end];
  // End maps to just after the last KEPT character, so a token never ends with a stripped character.
  return [st.orig[start], st.orig[end - 1] + 1];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sentence segmentation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Range { start: number; end: number }

function trimRange(s: string, start: number, end: number): Range {
  while (start < end && INVISIBLE_CHAR.test(s[start])) start++;
  while (end > start && INVISIBLE_CHAR.test(s[end - 1])) end--;
  return { start, end };
}

function hasWordChar(s: string, r: Range): boolean {
  return WORD_CHAR.test(s.slice(r.start, r.end));
}

/** Returns the abbreviation candidate (without its period) that ends the trimmed text, or null. */
function trailingAbbreviation(trimmedText: string): string | null {
  const tail = trimmedText.length > TAIL_WINDOW ? trimmedText.slice(-TAIL_WINDOW) : trimmedText;
  const m = TRAILING_ABBREVIATION.exec(tail);
  return m ? m[1] : null;
}

function isTitleAbbreviation(abbr: string): boolean {
  if (TITLE_ABBREVIATIONS.has(abbr)) return true;
  // ALL CAPS headings: "MR. DARCY" -> "Mr"
  if (abbr.length > 1 && abbr === abbr.toUpperCase()) {
    return TITLE_ABBREVIATIONS.has(abbr[0] + abbr.slice(1).toLowerCase());
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * Is a trailing single capital letter an initial ("J. K. Rowling")? Every capital letter is, except
 * the pronoun "I", which only counts when it follows another initial or a title ("J. I. Packer").
 */
function isInitial(abbr: string, trimmedText: string): boolean {
  if (!SINGLE_UPPER.test(abbr)) return false;
  if (abbr !== 'I') return true;
  const before = trimmedText.slice(0, -2).trimEnd(); // drop "I."
  const prev = trailingAbbreviation(before);
  return prev !== null && (isTitleAbbreviation(prev) || (SINGLE_UPPER.test(prev) && prev !== 'I'));
}

/**
 * Running count of the straight quotes (" and ') still open in the sentence being assembled by the
 * merge pass. The scan resumes where it stopped as the sentence grows, which keeps the pass linear
 * even in a paragraph that never closes its quotes.
 */
interface QuoteScan { start: number; pos: number; double: number; single: number }

function newQuoteScan(start: number): QuoteScan {
  return { start, pos: start, double: 0, single: 0 };
}

/**
 * Advances the scan to `end`. A quote opens when it follows the start of the sentence, whitespace, a
 * bracket, a dash or another quote and is followed by a visible character; any other quote closes
 * (never below zero, so a plural possessive like "boys' hats" is not an unmatched quote). An
 * apostrophe between two letters ("don't") is not a quote.
 */
function scanQuotes(s: string, q: QuoteScan, end: number): void {
  for (let k = q.pos; k < end; k++) {
    const c = s[k];
    if (c !== '"' && c !== "'") continue;
    const prev = k > q.start ? s[k - 1] : '';
    const next = k + 1 < end ? s[k + 1] : '';
    const opens = (prev === '' || BEFORE_OPENING_QUOTE.test(prev)) && next !== '' && !INVISIBLE_CHAR.test(next);
    if (c === '"') {
      if (opens) q.double++;
      else if (q.double > 0) q.double--;
    } else {
      if (prev !== '' && WORD_CHAR.test(prev) && next !== '' && WORD_CHAR.test(next)) continue;
      if (opens) q.single++;
      else if (q.single > 0) q.single--;
    }
  }
  q.pos = end;
}

/**
 * Decides whether a closing quote at the start of the next segment belongs to the sentence before it
 * (merge) or opens a new quotation (keep the split). `i` is the index of the quote character; `cur`
 * is the trimmed sentence so far and `quotes` its running quote scan.
 */
function closerBelongsToPrevious(s: string, i: number, cur: Range, quotes: QuoteScan): boolean {
  const c = s[i];
  if (UNAMBIGUOUS_CLOSERS.has(c)) return true;
  if (!AMBIGUOUS_CLOSERS.has(c)) return false;
  const after = s.slice(i + 1, i + 3);
  // A standalone quote (followed by space, punctuation or end of text) is a closer.
  if (!STARTS_ALNUM.test(after)) return true;
  // ’ directly before a letter is an apostrophe ("’tis") or an opening single quote, never a closer.
  if (c === '’') return false;
  // " or ' directly before a letter closes the previous sentence only if that sentence still has an
  // open quote of the same kind ('He said "stop. "Then he left.' is a misplaced space, not a quote).
  scanQuotes(s, quotes, cur.end);
  return (c === '"' ? quotes.double : quotes.single) > 0;
}

/** Index of the first character of `r` that is not an opening quote/bracket (so '"Then' reads as 'Then'). */
function skipLeadingOpeners(s: string, r: Range): number {
  let k = r.start;
  while (k < r.end && LEADING_OPENERS.has(s[k])) k++;
  return k;
}

/**
 * True when the ICU boundary between `cur` and `next` is spurious and the two should be one sentence.
 * Both ranges are non-empty after trimming and contain at least one letter or digit (the caller
 * absorbs word-less segments before asking).
 */
function shouldMerge(s: string, cur: Range, next: Range, quotes: QuoteScan): boolean {
  const curTrim = trimRange(s, cur.start, cur.end);
  const nextTrim = trimRange(s, next.start, next.end);

  const nextHead = s.slice(nextTrim.start, nextTrim.start + 2); // 2 code units so astral letters match
  // 1. A sentence does not start with a lowercase letter: "...!" | "he said."  "whispered..." | "and"
  if (STARTS_LOWER.test(nextHead)) return true;
  // 2. Closing quote/bracket left at the start of the next segment: 'He said. ' | '” Then.'
  if (closerBelongsToPrevious(s, nextTrim.start, curTrim, quotes)) return true;

  // 3. Abbreviations and initials before the boundary.
  const curText = s.slice(Math.max(curTrim.start, curTrim.end - TAIL_WINDOW), curTrim.end);
  const abbr = trailingAbbreviation(curText);
  if (abbr === null) return false;
  if (isTitleAbbreviation(abbr)) return true;
  if (isInitial(abbr, curText)) return true;
  const lower = abbr.toLowerCase();
  if (ALWAYS_MERGE_ABBREVIATIONS.has(lower)) return true;
  if (!CONDITIONAL_ABBREVIATIONS.has(lower)) return false;
  // "5 p.m. on Tuesday" merges; "5 p.m. He left.", "the U.S. Then he left." and 'etc. "Fine," she
  // said.' stay split: an uppercase letter (possibly behind an opening quote) starts a new sentence.
  const w = skipLeadingOpeners(s, nextTrim);
  return !STARTS_UPPER.test(s.slice(w, w + 2));
}

/**
 * ICU occasionally glues an opening quote/bracket to the end of the previous sentence when there is
 * no space between them ("end.”“Start" -> 'end.”“' | 'Start'). Move such openers to the next segment.
 */
function moveTrailingOpeners(s: string, raw: Range[]): void {
  for (let i = 0; i + 1 < raw.length; i++) {
    const cur = raw[i];
    const t = trimRange(s, cur.start, cur.end);
    let end = t.end;
    while (end > t.start && UNAMBIGUOUS_OPENERS.has(s[end - 1])) end--;
    // Move only when something visible remains before the openers; a segment that is nothing but
    // openers is absorbed into its neighbour by the word-less rule of the merge pass instead.
    if (end < t.end && end > t.start) {
      cur.end = end;
      raw[i + 1].start = end;
    }
  }
}

function segmentSentenceRanges(sentenceSegmenter: Intl.Segmenter, s: string): Range[] {
  if (s.length === 0) return [];
  const raw: Range[] = [];
  for (const seg of sentenceSegmenter.segment(s)) {
    raw.push({ start: seg.index, end: seg.index + seg.segment.length });
  }
  if (raw.length === 0) return [];
  moveTrailingOpeners(s, raw);

  const merged: Range[] = [];
  let cur: Range = { start: raw[0].start, end: raw[0].end };
  let curHasWord = hasWordChar(s, cur);
  let quotes = newQuoteScan(cur.start);
  for (let i = 1; i < raw.length; i++) {
    const next = raw[i];
    const nextHasWord = hasWordChar(s, next);
    // A segment without any letter or digit (whitespace, stray punctuation, an opening quote at the
    // end of the paragraph) is never a sentence of its own: absorb it into its neighbour.
    if (!curHasWord || !nextHasWord || shouldMerge(s, cur, next, quotes)) {
      cur.end = next.end;
      curHasWord = curHasWord || nextHasWord;
    } else {
      merged.push(cur);
      cur = { start: next.start, end: next.end };
      curHasWord = nextHasWord;
      quotes = newQuoteScan(cur.start);
    }
  }
  merged.push(cur);

  const out: Range[] = [];
  for (const r of merged) {
    const t = trimRange(s, r.start, r.end);
    if (t.end > t.start) out.push(t);
  }
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tokenisation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Token in stripped-text coordinates, before mapping back to the original string. */
interface RawToken { start: number; end: number; kind: TokenKind }

/**
 * Tokenises the whole of `s` in one ICU pass (one call per paragraph is ~2x faster than one per
 * sentence). Whitespace and invisible characters are skipped, punctuation runs collapse, and
 * hyphenated compounds are joined.
 */
function tokenizeText(wordSegmenter: Intl.Segmenter, s: string): RawToken[] {
  const out: RawToken[] = [];
  for (const seg of wordSegmenter.segment(s)) {
    const text = seg.segment;
    const start = seg.index;
    const end = start + text.length;
    if (seg.isWordLike) {
      out.push({ start, end, kind: NUMBER_TOKEN.test(text) ? 'number' : 'word' });
      continue;
    }
    if (ONLY_INVISIBLE.test(text)) continue; // spaces are not tokens (see module doc)
    const prev = out.length > 0 ? out[out.length - 1] : null;
    if (prev && prev.kind === 'punct' && prev.end === start) prev.end = end; // collapse "?!", "..."
    else out.push({ start, end, kind: 'punct' });
  }
  joinHyphenatedWords(s, out);
  return out;
}

/** In place: word + single hyphen + word (no spaces) -> one token. Chains ("state-of-the-art") join too. */
function joinHyphenatedWords(s: string, tokens: RawToken[]): void {
  let w = 0; // write index
  for (let r = 0; r < tokens.length; r++) {
    const t = tokens[r];
    if (
      w >= 2 &&
      t.kind !== 'punct' &&
      tokens[w - 1].kind === 'punct' &&
      tokens[w - 1].end - tokens[w - 1].start === 1 &&
      JOINING_HYPHENS.has(s[tokens[w - 1].start]) &&
      tokens[w - 2].kind !== 'punct' &&
      tokens[w - 2].end === tokens[w - 1].start &&
      tokens[w - 1].end === t.start
    ) {
      const head = tokens[w - 2];
      head.end = t.end;
      if (head.kind === 'number' && t.kind !== 'number') head.kind = 'word';
      w -= 1; // drop the hyphen token; `head` stays at w-1
      continue;
    }
    tokens[w++] = t;
  }
  tokens.length = w;
}

function toTokens(st: Stripped, original: string, raw: RawToken[]): Token[] {
  const out: Token[] = new Array(raw.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) {
    const [start, end] = mapRange(st, raw[i].start, raw[i].end);
    out[i] = { start, end, text: original.slice(start, end), kind: raw[i].kind };
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Hands the paragraph's tokens out to its sentences by offset. `raw` and `ranges` are both sorted.
 * Sentence boundaries and ICU word boundaries agree in practice; the one exception is a collapsed
 * punctuation run spanning a boundary we moved ("end.”“Start" -> '.”' | '“'),
 * which is clipped at the boundary so every token lies inside its sentence.
 */
function distributeTokens(s: string, raw: RawToken[], ranges: Range[]): RawToken[][] {
  const out: RawToken[][] = new Array(ranges.length);
  let j = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < ranges.length; i++) {
    const r = ranges[i];
    const toks: RawToken[] = [];
    while (j < raw.length && raw[j].start < r.end) {
      const t = raw[j];
      if (t.end <= r.start) { j++; continue; } // entirely in the gap before this sentence
      if (t.start >= r.start && t.end <= r.end) {
        toks.push(t);
        j++;
        continue;
      }
      const start = Math.max(t.start, r.start);
      const end = Math.min(t.end, r.end);
      if (end > start) {
        const kind: TokenKind = t.kind === 'punct' ? 'punct' : NUMBER_TOKEN.test(s.slice(start, end)) ? 'number' : 'word';
        toks.push({ start, end, kind });
      }
      if (t.end <= r.end) j++; else break; // the rest of a straddling token belongs to the next sentence
    }
    out[i] = toks;
  }
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public factory
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function requireString(text: unknown, fn: string): asserts text is string {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TypeError(`Segmenter.${fn}: expected a string, got ${text === null ? 'null' : typeof text}`);
}

export function createSegmenter(): Segmenter {
  const sentenceSegmenter = new Intl.Segmenter('en', { granularity: 'sentence' });
  const wordSegmenter = new Intl.Segmenter('en', { granularity: 'word' });

  return {
    segmentParagraph(text: string): Sentence[] {
      requireString(text, 'segmentParagraph');
      if (text.length === 0) return [];
      const st = stripFormatChars(text);
      const ranges = segmentSentenceRanges(sentenceSegmenter, st.text);
      if (ranges.length === 0) return [];
      const perSentence = distributeTokens(st.text, tokenizeText(wordSegmenter, st.text), ranges);
      const sentences: Sentence[] = new Array(ranges.length);
      for (let i = 0; i < ranges.length; i++) {
        const r = ranges[i];
        const [start, end] = mapRange(st, r.start, r.end);
        sentences[i] = { index: i, start, end, tokens: toTokens(st, text, perSentence[i]) };
      }
      return sentences;
    },

    tokenize(text: string): Token[] {
      requireString(text, 'tokenize');
      if (text.length === 0) return [];
      const st = stripFormatChars(text);
      return toTokens(st, text, tokenizeText(wordSegmenter, st.text));
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import type { TtsEngineId } from '@shared/settings';
import type { CloudTtsResult, WordTiming } from '@shared/api';
import type { TtsEngine, TtsVoice, SpeakOptions, SpeakHandle, SpeakOutcome } from './engine';
import { ENGINE_LABELS } from './engine';
import { estimateWordTimes } from './timing';
import { synthesisSegments, PRIORITY, type SynthesisSegment } from './segments';

type Synthesize = (engine: TtsEngineId, text: string, voiceId: string, rate: number) => Promise<CloudTtsResult>;
type ListVoices = (engine: TtsEngineId) => Promise<{ id: string; name: string; lang: string; gender?: string; quality?: string; note?: string }[]>;

/** an item of the main process's kokoro:prepare channel (src/main/kokoro/ipc.ts) */
export interface PrepareItem { text: string; voice?: string; speed?: number; priority?: number; wait?: boolean; replace?: boolean; release?: boolean }
/** kokoro:prepare; with `wait` items it resolves true when they are ready, false when they were dropped */
export type Prepare = (items: PrepareItem[]) => Promise<unknown>;

export interface AudioEngineOptions {
  /**
   * Local synthesis queue (Kokoro): read-ahead goes to the main process's priority queue instead of being
   * fetched here, and the next sentence is fetched once the main process reports it ready.
   */
  prepare?: Prepare;
  /** speak long texts as clause segments played back to back (synthesisSegments), so the first one starts sooner */
  segment?: boolean;
}

/** cloud voices cost money per character: never fetch further ahead than this */
const CLOUD_PREFETCH = 2;
/** decoded audio elements kept for upcoming segments */
const PRELOAD_MAX = 8;

/**
 * Engine for voices synthesized elsewhere (cloud providers or the local neural model), which return an
 * audio file plus optional word timings. Audio plays through an HTMLAudioElement so the speed slider can
 * change playbackRate live (pitch preserved; Web Audio buffers would change the pitch). Word highlights come
 * from the provider's timings when present, otherwise from a character-based estimate over the real audio
 * duration.
 *
 * Gaps between sentences: synthesized audio is cached (LRU) and the next sentence is fetched and pre-decoded (an
 * audio element loaded ahead of time) while the current one plays, so starting it is just play(). With `segment`,
 * a long sentence is requested as clause segments that play back to back; word timings are shifted to the
 * sentence's offsets, so the highlighter sees one sentence.
 */
export class AudioTtsEngine implements TtsEngine {
  readonly kind = 'cloud' as const;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly costNote: string;
  readonly wordBoundaries: boolean;
  private cache = new Map<string, Promise<CloudTtsResult>>();
  /** requests not answered yet (their cache entries are forgotten when the speech that wanted them is cancelled) */
  private unresolved = new Set<string>();
  /** audio elements already loaded for upcoming segments, by cache key */
  private preloaded = new Map<string, { audio: HTMLAudioElement; url: string; durationSec: number | null }>();
  private current: { audio: HTMLAudioElement; cancel: () => void } | null = null;
  /** every unfinished speak(), including those still waiting for synthesis */
  private pending = new Set<SpeakHandle>();
  private _paused = false;
  private resumeWaiters: (() => void)[] = [];
  private liveRate = 1;
  /** bumped by stopReadAhead()/readAhead(): a read-ahead chain from before stops */
  private aheadGen = 0;
  /** ms from speak() to the audio playing, for the last speak() (diagnostics and tests) */
  lastStartDelayMs: number | null = null;
  private opts: AudioEngineOptions;

  constructor(readonly id: TtsEngineId, private synthesize: Synthesize, private voices: ListVoices, wordBoundaries: boolean, opts: AudioEngineOptions = {}) {
    this.label = ENGINE_LABELS[id].label;
    this.costNote = ENGINE_LABELS[id].cost;
    this.wordBoundaries = wordBoundaries;
    this.opts = opts;
  }
  get paused(): boolean { return this._paused; }

  async listVoices(): Promise<TtsVoice[]> {
    return (await this.voices(this.id)).map((v) => ({ ...v, engine: this.id }));
  }

  private key(text: string, voiceId: string): string { return `${voiceId}\u0000${text}`; }

  private segmentsOf(text: string): SynthesisSegment[] { return this.opts.segment ? synthesisSegments(text) : [{ text, start: 0 }]; }

  private fetch(text: string, voiceId: string): Promise<CloudTtsResult> {
    const k = this.key(text, voiceId);
    let p = this.cache.get(k);
    if (!p) {
      // audio is synthesized at rate 1 and sped up on playback so cached audio is reusable at any speed
      const req: Promise<CloudTtsResult> = this.synthesize(this.id, text, voiceId, 1).then(
        (r) => { this.unresolved.delete(k); return r; },
        (e) => { this.unresolved.delete(k); if (this.cache.get(k) === req) this.cache.delete(k); throw e; },
      );
      p = req;
      this.cache.set(k, p);
      this.unresolved.add(k);
      while (this.cache.size > 32) this.cache.delete(this.cache.keys().next().value as string);
    } else { this.cache.delete(k); this.cache.set(k, p); }
    return p;
  }

  prefetch(text: string, voiceId: string, _rate: number): void {
    for (const s of this.segmentsOf(text)) void this.fetch(s.text, voiceId).catch(() => undefined);
  }

  /**
   * The sentences after the one being spoken, nearest first. The next one is fetched and pre-decoded as soon as
   * possible. Local synthesis (prepare): all of them go to the main process's read-ahead queue (replacing the
   * previous list), the next one at 'next' priority. Cloud voices: only the next two are fetched (they cost money).
   */
  readAhead(texts: string[], voiceId: string, _rate: number): void {
    const gen = ++this.aheadGen;
    const next = texts[0];
    const prepare = this.opts.prepare;
    if (!prepare) {
      texts.slice(0, CLOUD_PREFETCH).forEach((t) => this.prefetch(t, voiceId, 1));
      if (next) this.predecode(next, voiceId, gen);
      return;
    }
    const items: PrepareItem[] = [{ text: '', replace: true }];
    texts.forEach((text, i) => { if (text.trim()) items.push({ text, voice: voiceId, speed: 1, priority: PRIORITY.ahead - (i + 1) }); });
    void prepare(items).catch(() => undefined);
    if (!next?.trim()) return;
    // ask to be told when the next sentence is ready rather than requesting it as 'now': an explanation the
    // learner is waiting for must not queue behind it
    prepare([{ text: next, voice: voiceId, speed: 1, priority: PRIORITY.next, wait: true }]).then((ok) => {
      if (ok !== false && gen === this.aheadGen) this.predecode(next, voiceId, gen);
    }).catch(() => undefined);
  }

  /** Playback paused or stopped: drop the read-ahead (local synthesis stops working for nothing). */
  stopReadAhead(): void {
    this.aheadGen++;
    void this.opts.prepare?.([{ text: '', replace: true }])?.catch(() => undefined);
  }

  /** Fetches every segment of `text` and loads an audio element for each, so speak() only has to call play(). */
  private predecode(text: string, voiceId: string, gen: number): void {
    for (const s of this.segmentsOf(text)) {
      const k = this.key(s.text, voiceId);
      if (this.preloaded.has(k)) continue;
      this.fetch(s.text, voiceId).then((res) => {
        if (gen !== this.aheadGen || this.preloaded.has(k)) return;
        this.preloaded.set(k, this.load(res));
        while (this.preloaded.size > PRELOAD_MAX) {
          const oldest = this.preloaded.keys().next().value as string;
          const p = this.preloaded.get(oldest)!;
          this.preloaded.delete(oldest);
          URL.revokeObjectURL(p.url);
        }
      }).catch(() => undefined);
    }
  }

  private load(res: CloudTtsResult): { audio: HTMLAudioElement; url: string; durationSec: number | null } {
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([res.audio], { type: res.mime }));
    const audio = new Audio(url);
    audio.preload = 'auto';
    audio.preservesPitch = true;
    audio.load?.();
    return { audio, url, durationSec: res.durationSec };
  }

  speak(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions): SpeakHandle {
    let resolve!: (o: SpeakOutcome) => void;
    const done = new Promise<SpeakOutcome>((r) => { resolve = r; });
    let finished = false;
    let cleanup: (() => void) | null = null;
    const handle: SpeakHandle = { done, cancel: () => finish('cancelled') };
    const finish = (o: SpeakOutcome) => {
      if (finished) return;
      finished = true;
      this.pending.delete(handle);
      cleanup?.(); cleanup = null;
      if (this.current?.cancel === handle.cancel) this.current = null;
      resolve(o);
    };
    this.pending.add(handle);
    this.liveRate = opts.rate;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    const segs = this.segmentsOf(text);
    // every segment is requested now, in order: the main process synthesizes them one after the other
    const results = segs.map((s) => { const p = this.fetch(s.text, opts.voiceId); p.catch(() => undefined); return p; });
    let started = false;
    const playSegment = (seg: SynthesisSegment, res: CloudTtsResult): Promise<SpeakOutcome> => new Promise<SpeakOutcome>((segDone) => {
      const k = this.key(seg.text, opts.voiceId);
      const ready = this.preloaded.get(k);
      if (ready) this.preloaded.delete(k);
      const { audio, url } = ready ?? this.load(res);
      audio.playbackRate = clampRate(this.liveRate);
      // provider timings index the text it synthesized (trimmed by the main process); shift them to this text
      const offset = seg.start + (seg.text.length - seg.text.trimStart().length);
      let timings: WordTiming[] | null = res.timings?.length ? res.timings.map((w) => ({ ...w, charIndex: w.charIndex + offset })) : null;
      let nextWord = 0;
      let raf = 0;
      let over = false;
      const tick = () => {
        if (over) return;
        const t = audio.currentTime;
        if (!timings && Number.isFinite(audio.duration) && audio.duration > 0) {
          timings = estimateWordTimes(seg.text, audio.duration).map((w) => ({ start: w.at, end: w.at, charIndex: w.charIndex + seg.start, charLength: w.charLength }));
        }
        while (timings && nextWord < timings.length && timings[nextWord].start <= t) {
          opts.onWord?.(timings[nextWord].charIndex, timings[nextWord].charLength);
          nextWord++;
        }
        raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      };
      const end = (o: SpeakOutcome) => {
        if (over) return;
        over = true;
        cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
        audio.onplaying = audio.onended = audio.onerror = null;
        audio.pause(); audio.src = ''; URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
        segDone(o);
      };
      cleanup = () => end('cancelled');
      audio.onplaying = () => {
        if (!started) { started = true; this.lastStartDelayMs = performance.now() - t0; opts.onStart?.(); }
        cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
        raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      };
      audio.onended = () => {
        // words whose start the last frame did not reach are still announced, in order
        while (timings && nextWord < timings.length) { opts.onWord?.(timings[nextWord].charIndex, timings[nextWord].charLength); nextWord++; }
        end('ended');
      };
      audio.onerror = () => { handle.error = new Error('audio playback failed'); end('error'); };
      this.current = { audio, cancel: handle.cancel };
      audio.play().catch((e: Error) => { if (!over) { handle.error = e; end('error'); } });
    });

    (async () => {
      for (let i = 0; i < segs.length; i++) {
        let res: CloudTtsResult;
        try { res = await results[i]; } catch (e) { handle.error = e as Error; finish('error'); return; }
        if (finished) return;
        if (this._paused) await new Promise<void>((r) => this.resumeWaiters.push(r));
        if (finished) return;
        // load the following segment while this one plays
        if (i + 1 < segs.length) {
          const nk = this.key(segs[i + 1].text, opts.voiceId);
          results[i + 1].then((r) => { if (!finished && !this.preloaded.has(nk)) this.preloaded.set(nk, this.load(r)); }).catch(() => undefined);
        }
        const o = await playSegment(segs[i], res);
        if (o !== 'ended') { finish(o); return; }
      }
      finish('ended');
    })();
    return handle;
  }

  pause(): void { if (this.current) { this.current.audio.pause(); } this._paused = true; }
  resume(): void {
    if (this.current) this.current.audio.play().catch(() => undefined);
    this._paused = false;
    const w = this.resumeWaiters; this.resumeWaiters = [];
    w.forEach((r) => r());
  }
  cancelAll(): void {
    this._paused = false;
    const w = this.resumeWaiters; this.resumeWaiters = [];
    w.forEach((r) => r());
    for (const h of [...this.pending]) h.cancel();
    this.current = null;
    // requests nobody waits for any more: forget them here and tell the local queue they are no longer urgent
    for (const k of this.unresolved) this.cache.delete(k);
    this.unresolved.clear();
    void this.opts.prepare?.([{ text: '', release: true }])?.catch(() => undefined);
  }
  setRate(rate: number): void { this.liveRate = rate; if (this.current) this.current.audio.playbackRate = clampRate(rate); }
}

function clampRate(rate: number): number { return Math.min(4, Math.max(0.25, rate)); }
```

### `src/core/tts/engine.ts` (98 lines)

```ts
import type { TtsEngineId } from '@shared/settings';

/** A voice offered by an engine. `id` is engine-specific (voiceURI for Web Speech, provider voice id otherwise). */
export interface TtsVoice {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  lang: string;
  engine: TtsEngineId;
  gender?: string;
  quality?: string;
  note?: string;
}

export interface SpeakOptions {
  voiceId: string;
  /** 0.5 .. 2.5, 1 = normal */
  rate: number;
  onStart?: () => void;
  /** charIndex/charLength index into the spoken text (UTF-16 units) */
  onWord?: (charIndex: number, charLength: number) => void;
}

export type SpeakOutcome = 'ended' | 'cancelled' | 'error';

export interface SpeakHandle {
  /** resolves when speech finishes, is cancelled, or fails (never rejects) */
  done: Promise<SpeakOutcome>;
  error?: Error;
  cancel(): void;
}

/**
 * Text-to-speech engine. One sentence (or short text) per speak() call. Engines must support
 * cancel() at any time and must never leave a dangling promise. Renderer-side only.
 */
export interface TtsEngine {
  readonly id: TtsEngineId;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly kind: 'local' | 'cloud';
  readonly costNote: string;
  /** true when the engine delivers real per-word timing; false means word highlight is estimated */
  readonly wordBoundaries: boolean;
  listVoices(): Promise<TtsVoice[]>;
  speak(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions): SpeakHandle;
  /** optional: synthesize ahead of time so the next sentence starts without delay */
  prefetch?(text: string, voiceId: string, rate: number): void;
  /**
   * optional, preferred over prefetch: the sentences after the one being spoken, nearest first (up to about a
   * minute of speech). Each call replaces the previous list; the engine decides how far to go (cloud voices cost
   * money, the local voice reads ahead as far as the CPU allows) and pre-decodes the next one.
   */
  readAhead?(texts: string[], voiceId: string, rate: number): void;
  /** optional: playback paused or stopped, drop the read-ahead */
  stopReadAhead?(): void;
  pause(): void;
  resume(): void;
  cancelAll(): void;
  /** true when a paused utterance exists */
  readonly paused: boolean;
  /** optional: checks that the engine can actually start speaking (a "Test voice" button); `reason` explains a failure */
  probe?(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; reason?: string }>;
}

/** Engines offered in the UI, free ones first. */
export const AVAILABLE_ENGINES: TtsEngineId[] = ['kokoro', 'webspeech', 'edge', 'azure', 'google', 'openai', 'elevenlabs'];

/**
 * Characters of book text read aloud in one hour: about 150 words a minute x 6 characters (word + space)
 * x 60 minutes. The per-hour prices below are per-character list prices times this figure.
 */
export const CHARS_PER_HOUR = 54_000;

/** "$0.81/h" for a list price in US dollars per million characters. */
export function pricePerHour(usdPerMillionChars: number): string {
  return `$${((usdPerMillionChars * CHARS_PER_HOUR) / 1e6).toFixed(2)}/h`;
}

export interface EngineInfo {
  label: string;
  kind: 'local' | 'cloud';
  /** one-line cost note shown under the engine; starts with "Free" for free engines */
  cost: string;
  quality: string;
  /** short price per hour of listening ("free" or "$0.81/h") */
  perHour: string;
  /** the API key the engine needs, if any (Settings shows its status) */
  key?: 'openai' | 'elevenlabs' | 'azure' | 'google';
}

export const ENGINE_LABELS: Record<TtsEngineId, EngineInfo> = {
  webspeech: { label: 'Mac voices (built in)', kind: 'local', cost: 'Free', perHour: 'free', quality: 'Good with the Enhanced or Premium British voices (free download in System Settings)' },
  edge: { label: 'Microsoft neural voices', kind: 'cloud', cost: 'Free (unofficial, needs internet)', perHour: 'free', quality: 'Very good British voices (Sonia, Ryan, Libby, Thomas)' },
  azure: { label: 'Azure neural voices', kind: 'cloud', key: 'azure', perHour: `≈ ${pricePerHour(15)}`, cost: `Paid, about ${pricePerHour(15)} of listening ($15 per million characters); the first 500,000 characters a month are free (about 9 hours)`, quality: 'The same British voices as Microsoft Edge (Sonia, Ryan, Libby, Thomas), official and reliable. Word highlight is estimated.' },
  google: { label: 'Google Cloud voices', kind: 'cloud', key: 'google', perHour: `≈ $${((16 * CHARS_PER_HOUR) / 1e6).toFixed(2)}–${((30 * CHARS_PER_HOUR) / 1e6).toFixed(2)}/h`, cost: `Paid: Neural2 about ${pricePerHour(16)}, Chirp 3 HD about ${pricePerHour(30)} of listening; the first 1 million characters a month of each are free (about 18 hours)`, quality: 'Natural British voices; Neural2 voices give exact word highlight, Chirp 3 HD sound most human' },
  openai: { label: 'OpenAI voice', kind: 'cloud', key: 'openai', perHour: '≈ $0.90/h', cost: 'Paid, about $0.90/h of listening (1.5 cents per minute)', quality: 'Very natural, British accent on request' },
  elevenlabs: { label: 'ElevenLabs voice', kind: 'cloud', key: 'elevenlabs', perHour: `≈ ${pricePerHour(50)}`, cost: `Paid subscription, Flash voices about ${pricePerHour(50)} of listening; 10,000 free characters a month`, quality: 'Best, true British voices' },
  kokoro: { label: 'Dream voice (Kokoro, offline)', kind: 'local', cost: 'Free, one-time 192 MB download', perHour: 'free', quality: 'Natural British voices (Emma, George), runs on your Mac, no internet needed' },
};
```

### `src/core/tts/fake.ts` (43 lines)

```ts
import type { TtsEngine, TtsVoice, SpeakOptions, SpeakHandle, SpeakOutcome } from './engine';
import { estimateWordTimes } from './timing';

/**
 * Deterministic engine for tests and for CI machines without voices: "speaks" by emitting word
 * boundaries on a timer. `msPerChar` controls speed (0 makes everything finish on the next tick).
 */
export class FakeTtsEngine implements TtsEngine {
  readonly id = 'webspeech' as const;
  readonly label = 'Fake voice (testing)';
  readonly kind = 'local' as const;
  readonly costNote = 'Free';
  readonly wordBoundaries = true;
  spoken: { text: string; rate: number; voiceId: string }[] = [];
  private timers = new Set<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();
  private active: SpeakHandle[] = [];
  private _paused = false;
  constructor(public msPerChar = 4) {}
  get paused(): boolean { return this._paused; }
  async listVoices(): Promise<TtsVoice[]> {
    return [{ id: 'fake-gb', name: 'Fake Daniel', lang: 'en-GB', engine: 'webspeech' }, { id: 'fake-zh', name: 'Fake Tingting', lang: 'zh-CN', engine: 'webspeech' }];
  }
  speak(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions): SpeakHandle {
    this.spoken.push({ text, rate: opts.rate, voiceId: opts.voiceId });
    let resolve!: (o: SpeakOutcome) => void;
    const done = new Promise<SpeakOutcome>((r) => { resolve = r; });
    const timers: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>[] = [];
    let finished = false;
    const finish = (o: SpeakOutcome) => { if (finished) return; finished = true; timers.forEach((t) => { clearTimeout(t); this.timers.delete(t); }); this.active = this.active.filter((h) => h !== handle); resolve(o); };
    const handle: SpeakHandle = { done, cancel: () => finish('cancelled') };
    const durationMs = Math.max(1, text.length * this.msPerChar / Math.max(0.1, opts.rate));
    const words = estimateWordTimes(text, durationMs / 1000);
    const at = (ms: number, fn: () => void) => { const t = setTimeout(() => { this.timers.delete(t); if (!finished) fn(); }, ms); timers.push(t); this.timers.add(t); };
    at(0, () => opts.onStart?.());
    for (const w of words) at(w.at * 1000, () => opts.onWord?.(w.charIndex, w.charLength));
    at(durationMs, () => finish('ended'));
    this.active.push(handle);
    return handle;
  }
  pause(): void { this._paused = true; }
  resume(): void { this._paused = false; }
  cancelAll(): void { this._paused = false; for (const h of [...this.active]) h.cancel(); }
}
```

```ts
import type { TtsEngine, TtsVoice, SpeakOptions, SpeakHandle } from './engine';
import { ENGINE_LABELS } from './engine';
import { AudioTtsEngine, type Prepare } from './audio';

/**
 * Kokoro-82M, synthesized in the main process (src/main/kokoro) and played here through the same
 * HTMLAudioElement path as the cloud voices. The main process returns a WAV plus word timings taken from the
 * model's duration predictor, so `onWord` fires on real word boundaries. Long sentences are spoken as clause
 * segments back to back, and Playback's read-ahead keeps the main process synthesizing up to ~60 s ahead. The first use downloads the model
 * (about 190 MB); the main process reports progress on the 'kokoro:progress' channel.
 */
export class KokoroTtsEngine implements TtsEngine {
  readonly id = 'kokoro' as const;
  readonly kind = 'local' as const;
  readonly label = ENGINE_LABELS.kokoro.label;
  readonly costNote = ENGINE_LABELS.kokoro.cost;
  readonly wordBoundaries = true;
  private inner: AudioTtsEngine;

  constructor() {
    const api = window.readalong;
    // read-ahead and the "tell me when the next sentence is ready" requests go to the main process's priority queue
    // (kokoro:prepare); a speak() is a tts:synthesize request, which always goes first
    const prepare: Prepare | undefined = typeof api.kokoroPrepare === 'function' ? (items) => api.kokoroPrepare(items as Parameters<typeof api.kokoroPrepare>[0]) : undefined;
    this.inner = new AudioTtsEngine('kokoro', (engine, text, voiceId, rate) => api.ttsSynthesize(engine, text, voiceId, rate), (engine) => api.ttsListVoices(engine), true, { prepare, segment: true });
  }
  get paused(): boolean { return this.inner.paused; }
  listVoices(): Promise<TtsVoice[]> { return this.inner.listVoices(); }
  speak(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions): SpeakHandle { return this.inner.speak(text, opts); }
  prefetch(text: string, voiceId: string, rate: number): void { this.inner.prefetch(text, voiceId, rate); }
  readAhead(texts: string[], voiceId: string, rate: number): void { this.inner.readAhead(texts, voiceId, rate); }
  stopReadAhead(): void { this.inner.stopReadAhead(); }
  pause(): void { this.inner.pause(); }
  resume(): void { this.inner.resume(); }
  cancelAll(): void { this.inner.cancelAll(); }
  setRate(rate: number): void { this.inner.setRate(rate); }
  /** Synthesizes a short phrase (downloading the model on first use); the reason is the main process error. */
  async probe(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; reason?: string }> {
    try {
      const r = await window.readalong.ttsSynthesize('kokoro', 'Hello.', 'bf_emma', 1);
      return r.audio.byteLength > 0 ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, reason: 'The Kokoro voice returned no audio.' };
    } catch (e) { return { ok: false, reason: (e as Error).message }; }
  }
}
```

```ts
import type { TtsEngineId } from '@shared/settings';
import type { TtsEngine } from './engine';
import { WebSpeechEngine } from './webspeech';
import { AudioTtsEngine } from './audio';
import { FakeTtsEngine } from './fake';
import { KokoroTtsEngine } from './kokoro';

const engines = new Map<TtsEngineId, TtsEngine>();
let fake: FakeTtsEngine | null = null;

/** In tests (READALONG_E2E) or on machines without system voices the fake engine stands in for Web Speech. */
export function useFakeEngine(msPerChar = 2): FakeTtsEngine {
  fake = new FakeTtsEngine(msPerChar);
  engines.set('webspeech', fake);
  return fake;
}

export function getEngine(id: TtsEngineId): TtsEngine {
  let e = engines.get(id);
  if (e) return e;
  if (id === 'webspeech') e = fake ?? new WebSpeechEngine();
  else if (id === 'kokoro') e = new KokoroTtsEngine();
  else e = new AudioTtsEngine(id, (engine, text, voiceId, rate) => window.readalong.ttsSynthesize(engine, text, voiceId, rate), (engine) => window.readalong.ttsListVoices(engine), id === 'edge' || id === 'elevenlabs' || id === 'google');
  engines.set(id, e);
  return e;
}

export function cancelAllEngines(): void { for (const e of engines.values()) e.cancelAll(); }

/** Sensible default voice per engine when the learner has not picked one. */
export async function defaultVoiceFor(id: TtsEngineId): Promise<string> {
  if (id === 'webspeech') return fake ? 'fake-gb' : WebSpeechEngine.defaultVoiceId();
  const fallback: Record<TtsEngineId, string> = { webspeech: '', edge: 'en-GB-SoniaNeural', openai: 'ballad', elevenlabs: 'JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb', kokoro: 'bf_emma', azure: 'en-GB-SoniaNeural', google: 'en-GB-Neural2-A' };
  try {
    const voices = await getEngine(id).listVoices();
    const gb = voices.find((v) => v.lang.toLowerCase() === 'en-gb');
    return gb?.id ?? voices[0]?.id ?? fallback[id];
  } catch { return fallback[id]; }
}

/** A Chinese system voice for speaking word meanings, if the Mac has one. */
export async function chineseVoiceId(): Promise<string | null> {
  const voices = await getEngine('webspeech').listVoices();
  const zh = voices.filter((v) => /^zh[-_]?(cn|hans)?$/i.test(v.lang) || v.lang.toLowerCase() === 'zh-cn');
  const preferred = zh.find((v) => /tingting|ting-ting|meijia|lili/i.test(v.name)) ?? zh[0];
  return preferred?.id ?? null;
}
```

### `src/core/tts/segments.ts` (98 lines)

```ts
/**
 * Synthesis segments for the local neural voice (Kokoro). Synthesis time grows with the text, so a long sentence
 * (or a multi-sentence explanation) is synthesized in clause-sized pieces: the first piece is ready after a
 * fraction of the time and the rest is synthesized while it plays. The renderer plays the pieces back to back
 * (src/core/tts/audio.ts) and the main process uses the same split for prepare()/synthesize() of whole texts
 * (src/main/kokoro/engine.ts), so both ask for exactly the same pieces and share one cache entry per piece.
 *
 * The split is deterministic and ignores leading/trailing whitespace (the main process trims what it is given).
 * Cut points, best first: the end of a sentence, then ; : — , then a comma; never after a title such as "Mr.".
 * A text with no punctuation at all is cut at a space.
 */

export interface SynthesisSegment {
  /** the piece to synthesize (trimmed) */
  text: string;
  /** offset of `text` in the text given to synthesisSegments() (UTF-16 units) */
  start: number;
}

/** texts up to this many characters (about 10 s of speech) are synthesized whole */
export const SEGMENT_SPLIT_ABOVE = 180;
/** a piece is at most this long (about 8 s of speech, 2–4 s to synthesize on a 4-core Intel Mac) */
export const SEGMENT_MAX = 150;
/** and at least this long (shorter pieces sound choppy and gain nothing) */
export const SEGMENT_MIN = 40;

const TITLE_BEFORE_DOT = /(?:^|[\s“"‘'(])(?:Mr|Mrs|Ms|Dr|St|Prof|Jr|Sr|vs|etc|e\.g|i\.e|[A-Z])$/;
const CLOSERS = /["”’'»)\]]/;

/** Strength of a cut right after index `i` of `s` (0 = not a cut point). */
function cutStrength(s: string, i: number): number {
  const ch = s[i];
  let end = i;
  while (end + 1 < s.length && CLOSERS.test(s[end + 1])) end++; // keep closing quotes with the clause they close
  const after = s[end + 1];
  if (ch === '—' || ch === '–') return after === undefined ? 0 : 2;
  if (after !== undefined && !/\s/.test(after)) return 0;
  if (ch === '.' || ch === '!' || ch === '?' || ch === '…') {
    if (ch === '.' && TITLE_BEFORE_DOT.test(s.slice(Math.max(0, i - 6), i))) return 0;
    return 3;
  }
  if (ch === ';' || ch === ':') return 2;
  if (ch === ',') return 1;
  return 0;
}

/** Index just after the cut at `i` (closing quotes included). */
function cutEnd(s: string, i: number): number {
  let end = i;
  while (end + 1 < s.length && CLOSERS.test(s[end + 1])) end++;
  return end + 1;
}

export function synthesisSegments(text: string, splitAbove = SEGMENT_SPLIT_ABOVE, max = SEGMENT_MAX, min = SEGMENT_MIN): SynthesisSegment[] {
  const lead = text.length - text.trimStart().length;
  const s = text.trim();
  if (s.length <= splitAbove) return [{ text: s, start: lead }];
  const out: SynthesisSegment[] = [];
  let pos = 0;
  while (pos < s.length) {
    if (s.length - pos <= max) { out.push(piece(s, pos, s.length, lead)); break; }
    let best = -1; let bestStrength = 0;
    for (let i = pos + min; i < Math.min(s.length, pos + max); i++) {
      const st = cutStrength(s, i);
      if (!st) continue;
      const end = cutEnd(s, i);
      if (end - pos > max || s.length - end < min / 2) continue;
      // strongest cut wins; between equals the later one (fewer, longer pieces)
      if (st >= bestStrength) { best = end; bestStrength = st; }
    }
    if (best < 0) {
      const space = s.lastIndexOf(' ', pos + max);
      best = space > pos + min ? space : Math.min(s.length, pos + max);
    }
    out.push(piece(s, pos, best, lead));
    pos = best;
    while (pos < s.length && /\s/.test(s[pos])) pos++;
  }
  return out.filter((p) => p.text.length > 0);
}

function piece(s: string, from: number, to: number, lead: number): SynthesisSegment {
  const raw = s.slice(from, to);
  const l = raw.length - raw.trimStart().length;
  return { text: raw.trim(), start: lead + from + l };
}

/** Request priorities of the Kokoro queue in the main process (higher first). */
export const PRIORITY = {
  /** a speak() waiting for its audio right now (reading or an explanation) */
  now: 100,
  /** the sentence after the one playing: synthesized as soon as nothing is waiting */
  next: 90,
  /** read-ahead: `ahead - distance` (distance 1 = the next sentence) */
  ahead: 80,
  /** a plain prepare() without priority (ReaderView) */
  background: 0,
} as const;
```

### `src/core/tts/timing.ts` (45 lines)

```ts
import type { Sentence } from '@core/model';

/** Maps a char index inside a sentence's text to the index of the token containing it (or the next token). */
export function tokenIndexAtChar(sentence: Sentence, charIndexInSentence: number): number {
  const abs = sentence.start + charIndexInSentence;
  const toks = sentence.tokens;
  let lo = 0, hi = toks.length - 1, ans = -1;
  while (lo <= hi) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
    if (toks[mid].start <= abs) { ans = mid; lo = mid + 1; } else hi = mid - 1;
  }
  if (ans >= 0 && abs < toks[ans].end) return ans;
  // inside a gap between tokens: return the next word-ish token
  return Math.min(ans + 1, toks.length - 1);
}

export interface EstimatedWord { charIndex: number; charLength: number; at: number }

/**
 * Estimates when each word of `text` is spoken, spreading `durationSec` over the characters.
 * Punctuation gets a small extra pause weight. Used when an engine gives no word boundaries.
 */
export function estimateWordTimes(text: string, durationSec: number): EstimatedWord[] {
  const words: { start: number; end: number; weight: number }[] = [];
  const re = /[\p{L}\p{N}][\p{L}\p{N}'’\-]*/gu;
  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
  while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
    const after = text.slice(m.index + m[0].length, m.index + m[0].length + 2);
    const pause = /[.!?;:,—…]/.test(after) ? 2.5 : 0;
    words.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, weight: m[0].length + 1 + pause });
  }
  const total = words.reduce((s, w) => s + w.weight, 0) || 1;
  let acc = 0;
  return words.map((w) => {
    const at = (acc / total) * durationSec;
    acc += w.weight;
    return { charIndex: w.start, charLength: w.end - w.start, at };
  });
}

/** Rough spoken duration in seconds for text at a given rate (about 2.7 words per second at rate 1). */
export function estimateDurationSec(text: string, rate: number): number {
  const words = (text.match(/[\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu) ?? []).length;
  return Math.max(0.3, (words / 2.7 + 0.25) / Math.max(0.3, rate));
}
```

```ts
import type { TtsEngine, TtsVoice, SpeakOptions, SpeakHandle, SpeakOutcome } from './engine';

/** onstart must arrive within this long, else the engine is assumed stuck and the utterance is retried */
export const START_TIMEOUT_MS = 4000;
/** the first utterance after a voice change: Enhanced/Premium voices warm up slowly */
export const START_TIMEOUT_NEW_VOICE_MS = 8000;
/** margin added to twice the expected duration before an utterance without onend/onerror is given up */
export const END_TIMEOUT_EXTRA_MS = 5000;
/** Chromium pauses long utterances on some versions; a resume() tick while speaking is the usual workaround */
export const RESUME_TICK_MS = 10_000;
/**
 * the synthesizer reports nothing speaking or queued and no word boundary came for this long (and at least half
 * of the expected duration has passed): the utterance is over even though onend never arrived. Without this a
 * lost onend left the learner in silence until the end watchdog (twice the expected duration + 5 s).
 */
export const IDLE_END_MS = 1500;
/** how often the idle check runs while speaking */
const IDLE_POLL_MS = 500;
/** a "Test voice" probe must start within this long */
export const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
/** words per minute at rate 1, used to estimate how long an utterance should take */
const WORDS_PER_MINUTE = 150;

export const VOICE_DID_NOT_START = 'The Mac voice did not start';

/** an utterance handed to the engine or waiting for it */
interface Job {
  started: boolean;
  finished: boolean;
  finish: (o: SpeakOutcome) => void;
}

/**
 * Web Speech API engine (window.speechSynthesis). On macOS, Chromium backs this with Apple's
 * AVSpeechSynthesizer: every local system voice delivers word boundary events (charIndex/charLength),
 * including downloaded Enhanced/Premium voices. Rate 0.1-4 is honoured (we use 0.5-2.5).
 *
 * Known engine quirks handled here:
 * - getVoices() may be empty until 'voiceschanged'; a chosen voice may disappear (renamed/removed).
 * - utterances must be kept referenced until they end.
 * - cancel() followed immediately by speak() can drop the new utterance, so a new speak waits for the
 *   previous utterance's end/error event (or a short timeout).
 * - the synthesizer can stay `paused` after a cancel, or report `speaking` forever with nothing playing:
 *   speak() resumes a paused synthesizer, a start watchdog cancels and retries an utterance whose onstart
 *   never arrives, and an end watchdog finishes one whose onend/onerror never arrives.
 * - every step is reject-proof: a throwing speak() fails that one utterance instead of silencing all later ones.
 */
export class WebSpeechEngine implements TtsEngine {
  readonly id = 'webspeech' as const;
  readonly label = 'Mac voices (built in)';
  readonly kind = 'local' as const;
  readonly costNote = 'Free';
  readonly wordBoundaries = true;
  private inflight = new Set<Job>();
  /** serializes speak() calls behind any cancellation still settling; never left rejected */
  private settling: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
  private _paused = false;
  /** voiceURI of the last utterance (null before the first): a change means the voice has to warm up */
  private lastVoiceURI: string | null = null;
  /** true once we waited for 'voiceschanged' and none came: do not wait 2 s for every sentence on a voiceless machine */
  private voicesChecked = false;
  get paused(): boolean { return this._paused; }

  static available(): boolean { return typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'speechSynthesis' in window; }

  async listVoices(): Promise<TtsVoice[]> {
    const voices = await waitForVoices();
    return voices
      .map((v) => ({ id: v.voiceURI, name: v.name, lang: v.lang.replace('_', '-'), engine: 'webspeech' as const, note: v.localService ? undefined : 'online voice (no word highlight)' }))
      .sort((a, b) => rank(b) - rank(a) || a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  }

  /** Picks the best British voice when the user has not chosen one. */
  static async defaultVoiceId(lang = 'en-gb'): Promise<string> {
    const voices = await waitForVoices();
    const enGb = voices.filter((v) => v.lang.replace('_', '-').toLowerCase() === lang && v.localService);
    const preferred = ['Serena', 'Jamie', 'Daniel', 'Stephanie', 'Kate', 'Oliver'];
    for (const name of preferred) {
      const hit = enGb.find((v) => v.name.includes(name) && /premium|enhanced/i.test(v.name)) ?? enGb.find((v) => v.name.includes(name));
      if (hit) return hit.voiceURI;
    }
    return (enGb[0] ?? voices.find((v) => v.default) ?? voices[0])?.voiceURI ?? '';
  }

  speak(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions): SpeakHandle { return this.start(text, opts, 1); }

  /**
   * Speaks a short text silently and reports whether the synthesizer actually started it.
   * Used by a "Test voice" button; `reason` is a message the learner can act on.
   */
  async probe(voiceId?: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean; reason?: string }> {
    if (!WebSpeechEngine.available()) return { ok: false, reason: 'Speech synthesis is not available in this window' };
    const voices = await waitForVoices();
    if (!voices.length) return { ok: false, reason: 'No system voices found. Download a voice in System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content.' };
    const id = voiceId || (await WebSpeechEngine.defaultVoiceId());
    this.cancelAll();
    let started = false;
    const handle = this.start('Testing the voice.', { voiceId: id, rate: 1, onStart: () => { started = true; } }, 0.01); // not 0: some AVSpeech builds skip events for silent utterances
    const outcome = await Promise.race([handle.done, settle(PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS).then(() => 'timeout' as const)]);
    handle.cancel();
    if (outcome === 'error') return { ok: false, reason: handle.error?.message ?? VOICE_DID_NOT_START };
    if (started) return { ok: true };
    if (outcome === 'cancelled') return { ok: false, reason: 'The voice test was interrupted' };
    return { ok: false, reason: `${VOICE_DID_NOT_START} within ${PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000} seconds` };
  }

  private start(text: string, opts: SpeakOptions, volume: number): SpeakHandle {
    let resolve!: (o: SpeakOutcome) => void;
    const done = new Promise<SpeakOutcome>((r) => { resolve = r; });
    const job: Job = { started: false, finished: false, finish: () => undefined };
    let utterance: SpeechSynthesisUtterance | null = null;
    let timers: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>[] = [];
    let resumeTick: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
    let idlePoll: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
    const clearTimers = () => {
      for (const t of timers) clearTimeout(t);
      timers = [];
      if (resumeTick) { clearInterval(resumeTick); resumeTick = null; }
      if (idlePoll) { clearInterval(idlePoll); idlePoll = null; }
    };
    const words = Math.max(1, text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length);
    const expectedMs = (words / (WORDS_PER_MINUTE * clampRate(opts.rate))) * 60_000;
    let startedAt = 0;
    let lastActivity = 0;
    /** stops routing engine events of the current utterance (a cancelled/abandoned one still emits 'canceled') */
    const detach = () => { if (utterance) utterance.onstart = utterance.onend = utterance.onerror = utterance.onboundary = null; };
    job.finish = (o) => {
      if (job.finished) return;
      job.finished = true;
      clearTimers();
      detach();
      this.inflight.delete(job);
      resolve(o);
    };
    const handle: SpeakHandle = {
      done,
      cancel: () => {
        if (job.finished) return;
        job.finish('cancelled');
        cancelSynth();
        // cancel() immediately followed by speak() can drop the new utterance (Chromium): let the engine settle first
        this.settling = settle();
      },
    };
    const fail = (message: string) => { handle.error = new Error(message); job.finish('error'); };
    this.inflight.add(job);

    const armEndWatchdog = () => {
      const ms = expectedMs * 2 + END_TIMEOUT_EXTRA_MS;
      const arm = () => timers.push(setTimeout(() => {
        if (job.finished) return;
        if (this._paused) { arm(); return; } // paused by the user: wait the same again
        // neither onend nor onerror arrived: the engine lost the utterance, do not hang the reading loop
        job.finish('ended');
        cancelSynth();
        this.settling = settle();
      }, ms));
      arm();
    };

    const armStartWatchdog = (ms: number, attempt: number) => {
      timers.push(setTimeout(() => {
        if (job.finished || job.started) return;
        // another utterance is legitimately still talking: this one is queued behind it
        if ([...this.inflight].some((j) => j !== job && j.started && !j.finished)) { armStartWatchdog(ms, attempt); return; }
        detach();
        cancelSynth();
        if (attempt === 0) {
          // the synthesizer was stuck (paused after a cancel, or speaking nothing): clear it and try once more
          this.settling = settle(250).then(() => launch(1)).catch((e) => fail(`speech error: ${describe(e)}`));
        } else {
          this.settling = settle();
          fail(VOICE_DID_NOT_START);
        }
      }, ms));
    };

    const launch = async (attempt: number): Promise<void> => {
      if (job.finished) return;
      const voice = await this.resolveVoice(opts.voiceId);
      if (job.finished) return;
      const voiceURI = voice?.voiceURI ?? '';
      const newVoice = voiceURI !== this.lastVoiceURI;
      this.lastVoiceURI = voiceURI;
      const u = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(text);
      utterance = u;
      u.rate = clampRate(opts.rate);
      u.volume = volume;
      u.lang = voice?.lang ?? 'en-GB';
      if (voice) u.voice = voice;
      let lastIndex = -1;
      u.onstart = () => {
        if (job.finished || job.started) return;
        job.started = true;
        clearTimers();
        armEndWatchdog();
        resumeTick = setInterval(() => { if (speechSynthesis.speaking && !this._paused) safe(() => speechSynthesis.resume()); }, RESUME_TICK_MS);
        startedAt = lastActivity = Date.now();
        idlePoll = setInterval(() => {
          if (job.finished || this._paused) { lastActivity = Date.now(); return; }
          // still talking (or queued): the idle time counts from when it stops
          if (speechSynthesis.speaking || speechSynthesis.pending) { lastActivity = Date.now(); return; }
          const now = Date.now();
          if (now - lastActivity >= IDLE_END_MS && now - startedAt >= expectedMs / 2) job.finish('ended');
        }, IDLE_POLL_MS);
        opts.onStart?.();
      };
      u.onboundary = (e) => {
        if (e.name !== 'word') return;
        lastActivity = Date.now();
        if (e.charIndex < lastIndex) return; // guard against engines that shuffle ranges
        lastIndex = e.charIndex;
        opts.onWord?.(e.charIndex, e.charLength ?? wordLengthAt(text, e.charIndex));
      };
      u.onend = () => job.finish('ended');
      u.onerror = (e) => {
        if (e.error === 'interrupted' || e.error === 'canceled') job.finish('cancelled');
        else fail(`speech error: ${e.error}`);
      };
      // a synthesizer left paused (e.g. after a cancel) queues new utterances silently forever
      if (speechSynthesis.paused) speechSynthesis.resume();
      this._paused = false;
      armStartWatchdog(newVoice ? START_TIMEOUT_NEW_VOICE_MS : START_TIMEOUT_MS, attempt);
      speechSynthesis.speak(u);
      // Safari/Chromium occasionally never fire onstart for empty/whitespace text
      if (!text.trim()) job.finish('ended');
    };

    // serialize behind any cancellation still settling, then speak; a failure settles this handle only
    this.settling = this.settling
      .then(() => launch(0), () => launch(0))
      .catch((e) => fail(`speech error: ${describe(e)}`));
    return handle;
  }

  /** The voice the learner chose, or the default British voice when it no longer exists; null when there are no voices at all. */
  private async resolveVoice(voiceId: string): Promise<SpeechSynthesisVoice | null> {
    let voices = speechSynthesis.getVoices();
    if (!voices.length && !this.voicesChecked) {
      voices = await waitForVoices();
      this.voicesChecked = true;
    }
    const chosen = voiceId ? voices.find((v) => v.voiceURI === voiceId || v.name === voiceId) : undefined;
    if (chosen) return chosen;
    if (!voices.length) return null;
    const fallback = await WebSpeechEngine.defaultVoiceId();
    return voices.find((v) => v.voiceURI === fallback) ?? null;
  }

  pause(): void { if (speechSynthesis.speaking && !speechSynthesis.paused) { speechSynthesis.pause(); this._paused = true; } }
  resume(): void { if (speechSynthesis.paused) { speechSynthesis.resume(); } this._paused = false; }
  cancelAll(): void {
    this._paused = false;
    // utterances still waiting behind a settle window never reach the engine: settle them here
    for (const job of [...this.inflight]) job.finish('cancelled');
    cancelSynth();
    // give the engine a moment to emit end/error events before the next speak()
    this.settling = settle();
  }
}

function settle(ms = 60): Promise<void> { return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); }
function clampRate(rate: number): number { return Math.min(4, Math.max(0.1, Number.isFinite(rate) ? rate : 1)); }
function safe(fn: () => void): void { try { fn(); } catch { /* a broken synthesizer must not break the caller */ } }
function cancelSynth(): void { safe(() => speechSynthesis.cancel()); }
function describe(e: unknown): string { return e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e); }

function rank(v: TtsVoice): number {
  let r = 0;
  if (v.lang.toLowerCase() === 'en-gb') r += 100;
  else if (v.lang.toLowerCase().startsWith('en')) r += 50;
  if (/premium/i.test(v.name)) r += 20; else if (/enhanced/i.test(v.name)) r += 10;
  if (v.note) r -= 30;
  return r;
}

function wordLengthAt(text: string, i: number): number {
  const m = /^[\p{L}\p{N}'’\-]+/u.exec(text.slice(i));
  return m ? m[0].length : 1;
}

let voicesPromise: Promise<SpeechSynthesisVoice[]> | null = null;
export function waitForVoices(timeoutMs = 2000): Promise<SpeechSynthesisVoice[]> {
  if (!WebSpeechEngine.available()) return Promise.resolve([]);
  const now = speechSynthesis.getVoices();
  if (now.length) return Promise.resolve(now);
  if (voicesPromise) return voicesPromise;
  voicesPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {
    const finish = () => { speechSynthesis.removeEventListener('voiceschanged', finish); resolve(speechSynthesis.getVoices()); voicesPromise = null; };
    speechSynthesis.addEventListener('voiceschanged', finish);
    setTimeout(finish, timeoutMs);
  });
  return voicesPromise;
}
```

```ts
import type { CefrLevel, Paragraph, Sentence, Token } from '@core/model';
import { levelIndex, CEFR_LEVELS } from '@core/model';
import type { Dictionary, DictEntry, LookupResult } from '@core/dict/types';
import type { PhraseHit } from '@core/ai/hints';
import { MAX_PHRASE_WORDS } from '@core/dict/dictionary';
import { nameKey } from '@core/dict/names';

/**
 * Vocabulary analysis of segmented text: which words are above the learner's level, which spans are
 * dictionary phrases, and which capitalised tokens are names (never explained).
 */

export interface WordInfo {
  /** vocabulary key: the dictionary lemma, else the folded lower-cased token */
  lemma: string;
  level: CefrLevel | null;
  levelSource: 'cefrj' | 'oct' | 'est' | null;
  isName: boolean;
  inDict: boolean;
  entry: DictEntry | null;
}

/**
 * A dictionary phrase found in a token list. `start`/`end` are token indices with `end` EXCLUSIVE (like
 * Token.start/end): the phrase's last word is `tokens[end - 1]`. The segmenter emits no whitespace tokens, so
 * `tokens[end]` is the word or punctuation AFTER the phrase ("who" in "old man who") and must not be included.
 */
export interface PhraseSpan { start: number; end: number; words: number; result: LookupResult }

export interface SentenceAnnotation {
  /** one entry per token; null for space/punct/number tokens */
  infos: (WordInfo | null)[];
  /**
   * dictionary phrases, with `level` = the level used (see phraseLevel; the chapter job's level when it
   * confirmed the phrase), `confirmed` = the chapter job found the same phrase here, `above` = that level is
   * above the learner's
   */
  phrases: (PhraseSpan & { above: boolean; level: CefrLevel; confirmed: boolean })[];
  /**
   * the chapter job's phrases in this sentence (PhraseHit, `end` INCLUSIVE) that are not already a dictionary
   * phrase over the same tokens, with `above` = the model's level is above the learner's
   */
  aiPhrases: (PhraseHit & { above: boolean })[];
  /** token indices above the learner's level (names excluded; words inside an above-level phrase are left to the phrase) */
  hardTokens: number[];
}

export function analyzeToken(token: Token, sentenceFirst: boolean, dict: Dictionary, names: Set<string>): WordInfo {
  const text = token.text;
  const r = token.kind === 'word' ? dict.lookup(text) : null;
  const lemma = r ? r.lemma : dict.lemmaOf(text);
  // A name must be capitalised in the text ("Grace" the person, not "grace"). Besides the book's name list,
  // a capitalised word mid-sentence that the dictionary has never heard of is treated as a name on the spot.
  let isName = false;
  if (token.kind === 'word' && /^\p{Lu}/u.test(text)) {
    const key = nameKey(text);
    isName = (key !== null && names.has(key)) || (!sentenceFirst && r === null);
  }
  return {
    lemma,
    level: r ? r.entry.level : null,
    levelSource: r ? r.entry.levelSource : null,
    isName,
    inDict: r !== null,
    entry: r ? r.entry : null,
  };
}

/**
 * Strictly above the learner's level. Unknown level and names are never "above". An estimated C2 with no
 * corpus frequency means ECDICT has the word but nothing else does — a rare word worth explaining only if the
 * dictionary actually has a gloss for it, otherwise it is most likely junk (an abbreviation, a misspelling).
 */
export function isAboveLevel(info: WordInfo, learner: CefrLevel): boolean {
  if (info.isName || info.level === null) return false;
  if (levelIndex(info.level) <= levelIndex(learner)) return false;
  if (info.levelSource === 'est' && info.level === 'C2' && info.entry !== null && info.entry.frq === 0) {
    return info.inDict && info.entry.zh.trim().length > 0;
  }
  return true;
}

/**
 * Longest-match, non-overlapping scan for dictionary phrases ("look forward to", "in spite of") over runs of
 * word tokens separated only by spaces. Windows of MAX_PHRASE_WORDS down to 2 are tried at each word; a window
 * matches only when its n words spell an n-word phrase headword (see Dictionary.lookupPhrase), so a span never
 * carries a word beyond the phrase.
 */
export function findPhrases(tokens: Token[], dict: Dictionary): PhraseSpan[] {
  const out: PhraseSpan[] = [];
  const wordIdx: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) if (tokens[i].kind === 'word') wordIdx.push(i);
  if (wordIdx.length < 2) return out;

  // run[k] = how many consecutive word tokens starting at wordIdx[k] are joined by spaces only
  const run = new Array<number>(wordIdx.length).fill(1);
  for (let k = wordIdx.length - 2; k >= 0; k--) {
    let onlySpaces = true;
    for (let i = wordIdx[k] + 1; i < wordIdx[k + 1]; i++) if (tokens[i].kind !== 'space') { onlySpaces = false; break; }
    run[k] = onlySpaces ? run[k + 1] + 1 : 1;
  }

  let k = 0;
  while (k < wordIdx.length) {
    let matched = 0;
    for (let n = Math.min(MAX_PHRASE_WORDS, run[k]); n >= 2; n--) {
      const words = wordIdx.slice(k, k + n).map((i) => tokens[i].text);
      const result = dict.lookupPhrase(words);
      if (result) {
        out.push({ start: wordIdx[k], end: wordIdx[k + n - 1] + 1, words: n, result });
        matched = n;
        break;
      }
    }
    k += matched || 1;
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The level a dictionary phrase is judged at. A level from a CEFR list (cefrj/oct) is used as is. An estimated
 * one ('est': C1 by default for any phrase without a Collins rating) is not trusted: it is replaced by the
 * level of the phrase's hardest word, at least B1 (a listed multi-word headword is an idiom or a fixed
 * expression, and an idiom-marked gloss says so outright), and never above the estimate ("look forward to"
 * stays B1, "lip service" becomes B1, "in spite of" B2 from "spite").
 */
export function phraseLevel(result: LookupResult, dict: Dictionary): CefrLevel {
  const e = result.entry;
  if (e.levelSource !== 'est') return e.level;
  let lvl = levelIndex('B1');
  for (const w of result.lemma.split(' ')) {
    const r = dict.lookup(w);
    if (r) lvl = Math.max(lvl, levelIndex(r.entry.level));
  }
  return CEFR_LEVELS[Math.min(lvl, levelIndex(e.level))];
}

/**
 * Per-token analysis of one sentence. `para` is part of the addressing contract (sentence offsets index into
 * `para.text`); the tokens themselves carry the text the analysis needs.
 */
export function annotateSentence(
  para: Paragraph,
  s: Sentence,
  dict: Dictionary,
  names: Set<string>,
  learner: CefrLevel,
  /** the chapter job's phrases of THIS sentence (hintsPhrases(bookId, chapter)[sentenceKey]), when available */
  hits: readonly PhraseHit[] = [],
): SentenceAnnotation {
  void para;
  const tokens = s.tokens;
  const firstWord = tokens.findIndex((t) => t.kind === 'word');
  const infos = tokens.map((t, i) => (t.kind === 'word' ? analyzeToken(t, i === firstWord, dict, names) : null));
  const above = (l: CefrLevel): boolean => levelIndex(l) > levelIndex(learner);
  const overlaps = (h: PhraseHit, start: number, endExcl: number): boolean => h.start < endExcl && h.end >= start;
  const phrases = findPhrases(tokens, dict).map((p) => {
    // confirmed: the chapter job found this phrase here (same tokens, or the same lemma over overlapping tokens)
    const hit = hits.find((h) => (h.start === p.start && h.end === p.end - 1) || (h.lemma === p.result.lemma && overlaps(h, p.start, p.end)));
    const level = hit ? hit.level : phraseLevel(p.result, dict);
    return { ...p, level, confirmed: hit !== undefined, above: above(level) };
  });
  const aiPhrases = hits
    .filter((h) => !phrases.some((p) => h.start === p.start && h.end === p.end - 1))
    .map((h) => ({ ...h, above: above(h.level) }));

  const coveredByHardPhrase = new Set<number>();
  for (const p of phrases) if (p.above) for (let i = p.start; i < p.end; i++) coveredByHardPhrase.add(i);
  for (const h of aiPhrases) if (h.above) for (let i = h.start; i <= h.end; i++) coveredByHardPhrase.add(i);

  const hardTokens: number[] = [];
  infos.forEach((info, i) => {
    if (info && !coveredByHardPhrase.has(i) && isAboveLevel(info, learner)) hardTokens.push(i);
  });
  return { infos, phrases, aiPhrases, hardTokens };
}
```
