### `test/unit/voice-turns.test.ts` (226 lines)

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { CommandListener, ConversationTurn, type CommandEvent, type QuestionEvent, type TurnState } from '@core/voice/turns';

function collect(listener: CommandListener) {
  const commands: CommandEvent[] = [];
  const questions: QuestionEvent[] = [];
  const suppressed: CommandEvent[] = [];
  listener.on('command', (e) => commands.push(e));
  listener.on('question', (e) => questions.push(e));
  listener.on('suppressed', (e) => suppressed.push(e));
  return { commands, questions, suppressed };
}

describe('CommandListener', () => {
  beforeEach(() => { vi.useFakeTimers(); vi.setSystemTime(10_000); });
  afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); });

  it('fires immediately on a final transcript', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    const r = l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    expect(r).toMatchObject({ intent: 'know', via: 'final', segmentId: 1, matched: 'i know' });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('needs two agreeing partials before firing', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    expect(l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'bye', segmentId: 's1' })).toBeNull();
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    const r = l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 's1' });
    expect(r).toMatchObject({ intent: 'bye', via: 'partials' });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('does not fire on partials that disagree, and a non-command partial resets agreement', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: "I don't know", segmentId: 1 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I', segmentId: 1 }); // not a command: resets agreement
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: "I don't know", segmentId: 1 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: "I don't know", segmentId: 1 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(commands[0].intent).toBe('dont_know');
  });

  it('emits at most one command per segment', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 7 });
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 7 });
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(2000);
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 7 })).toBeNull();
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('debounces: a second command within 1 s is suppressed, after 1 s it fires', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands, suppressed } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(500);
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 2 })).toBeNull();
    expect(suppressed).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(600); // 1100 ms after the first command
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 3 })).toMatchObject({ intent: 'bye' });
    expect(commands.map((c) => c.intent)).toEqual(['know', 'bye']);
  });

  it('a suppressed segment stays consumed', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener({ debounceMs: 1000 });
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(200);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 2 });
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 2 }); // suppressed
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(2000);
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'bye bye', segmentId: 2 })).toBeNull();
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('honours a custom debounce and clock', () => {
    let t = 0;
    const l = new CommandListener({ debounceMs: 250, now: () => t });
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    t = 200;
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 2 });
    t = 260;
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 3 });
    expect(commands.map((c) => c.segmentId)).toEqual([1, 3]);
  });

  it('emits question for a non-command final and nothing for an empty final', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands, questions } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'what does', segmentId: 1 });
    expect(questions).toHaveLength(0);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'what does this word mean', segmentId: 1, confidence: 0.9 });
    expect(questions).toEqual([{ text: 'what does this word mean', segmentId: 1, confidence: 0.9 }]);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: '', segmentId: 2 });
    expect(questions).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    // the segment is consumed: a late command final for it is ignored
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('passes confidence through to the classifier', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands, questions } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'i kno', segmentId: 1, confidence: 0.3 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(questions).toHaveLength(1);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'i kno', segmentId: 2, confidence: 0.9 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('reset forgets pending partials and consumed segments', () => {
    const l = new CommandListener();
    const { commands } = collect(l);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    l.reset();
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(0);
    l.push({ type: 'partial', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 });
    expect(commands).toHaveLength(1);
    l.reset();
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1500);
    expect(l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'I know', segmentId: 1 })).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it('supports an injected classifier and unsubscribing', () => {
    const detect = vi.fn(() => ({ intent: 'bye' as const, score: 1, matched: 'stub' }));
    const l = new CommandListener({ detect });
    const seen: string[] = [];
    const off = l.on('command', (e) => seen.push(e.matched ?? ''));
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'anything', segmentId: 'a' });
    off();
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1500);
    l.push({ type: 'final', text: 'anything', segmentId: 'b' });
    expect(seen).toEqual(['stub']);
    expect(detect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('anything', { confidence: undefined, minRatio: undefined });
  });
});

describe('ConversationTurn', () => {
  it('walks idle → listening → thinking → speaking → listening', () => {
    const t = new ConversationTurn();
    const log: string[] = [];
    t.on('state', (to, from) => log.push(`${from}>${to}`));
    expect(t.state).toBe('idle');
    expect(t.listen()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.think()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.speak()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.done()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.state).toBe('listening');
    expect(log).toEqual(['idle>listening', 'listening>thinking', 'thinking>speaking', 'speaking>listening']);
  });

  it('ignores invalid transitions', () => {
    const t = new ConversationTurn();
    const states: TurnState[] = [];
    t.on('state', (to) => states.push(to));
    expect(t.speak()).toBe(false);
    expect(t.think()).toBe(false);
    expect(t.done()).toBe(false);
    expect(t.listen()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.listen()).toBe(false);
    expect(t.speak()).toBe(false); // listening → speaking is not allowed
    expect(t.state).toBe('listening');
    expect(states).toEqual(['listening']);
  });

  it('interrupt() on VAD speech start while speaking returns to listening and emits interrupt', () => {
    const t = new ConversationTurn();
    const interrupted: TurnState[] = [];
    t.on('interrupt', (from) => interrupted.push(from));
    t.listen(); t.think(); t.speak();
    expect(t.onSpeechStart()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.state).toBe('listening');
    expect(interrupted).toEqual(['speaking']);
    expect(t.done()).toBe(false); // nothing left to finish
  });

  it('interrupt() is a no-op while listening or idle, but cancels thinking', () => {
    const t = new ConversationTurn();
    const interrupted: TurnState[] = [];
    t.on('interrupt', (from) => interrupted.push(from));
    expect(t.interrupt()).toBe(false);
    t.listen();
    expect(t.interrupt()).toBe(false);
    t.think();
    expect(t.interrupt()).toBe(true);
    expect(t.state).toBe('listening');
    expect(interrupted).toEqual(['thinking']);
  });

  it('bye() ends the conversation from any active state and emits bye', () => {
    for (const setup of [(t: ConversationTurn) => t.listen(), (t: ConversationTurn) => { t.listen(); t.think(); }, (t: ConversationTurn) => { t.listen(); t.think(); t.speak(); }]) {
      const t = new ConversationTurn();
      const byes: TurnState[] = [];
      t.on('bye', (from) => byes.push(from));
      setup(t);
      const from = t.state;
      expect(t.bye()).toBe(true);
      expect(t.state).toBe('idle');
      expect(byes).toEqual([from]);
      expect(t.bye()).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  it('once() fires a single time and off() removes a listener', () => {
    const t = new ConversationTurn();
    const seen: TurnState[] = [];
    t.once('state', (to) => seen.push(to));
    const fn = (to: TurnState) => seen.push(to);
    t.on('state', fn);
    t.listen();
    t.off('state', fn);
    t.think();
    expect(seen).toEqual(['listening', 'listening']);
  });
});
```

### `test/unit/webspeech.test.ts` (234 lines)

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';

/** Minimal stand-in for window.speechSynthesis: records spoken utterances, cancel() fires 'canceled' on them. */
class FakeUtterance {
  rate = 1; lang = ''; voice: FakeVoice | null = null; volume = 1;
  onstart: (() => void) | null = null; onend: (() => void) | null = null; onboundary: ((e: unknown) => void) | null = null; onerror: ((e: { error: string }) => void) | null = null;
  constructor(public text: string) {}
}
interface FakeVoice { voiceURI: string; name: string; lang: string; localService: boolean; default: boolean }
const DANIEL: FakeVoice = { voiceURI: 'com.apple.voice.premium.en-GB.Daniel', name: 'Daniel (Premium)', lang: 'en-GB', localService: true, default: false };
const SAMANTHA: FakeVoice = { voiceURI: 'com.apple.voice.en-US.Samantha', name: 'Samantha', lang: 'en-US', localService: true, default: true };
const TINGTING: FakeVoice = { voiceURI: 'com.apple.voice.zh-CN.Tingting', name: 'Tingting', lang: 'zh-CN', localService: true, default: false };

const synth = {
  spoken: [] as FakeUtterance[], speaking: false, paused: false, resumes: 0, throwOnSpeak: false,
  voices: [DANIEL, SAMANTHA, TINGTING] as FakeVoice[],
  listeners: new Set<() => void>(),
  getVoices() { return this.voices; },
  speak(u: FakeUtterance) { if (this.throwOnSpeak) throw new Error('synthesizer exploded'); this.spoken.push(u); this.speaking = true; },
  cancel() { this.speaking = false; this.paused = false; for (const u of this.spoken.splice(0)) u.onerror?.({ error: 'canceled' }); },
  pause() { this.paused = true; }, resume() { this.paused = false; this.resumes++; },
  addEventListener(_ev: string, fn: () => void) { this.listeners.add(fn); },
  removeEventListener(_ev: string, fn: () => void) { this.listeners.delete(fn); },
  fireVoicesChanged() { for (const fn of [...this.listeners]) fn(); },
};
Object.assign(globalThis, { window: globalThis, speechSynthesis: synth, SpeechSynthesisUtterance: FakeUtterance });

const { WebSpeechEngine, START_TIMEOUT_MS, START_TIMEOUT_NEW_VOICE_MS, END_TIMEOUT_EXTRA_MS, RESUME_TICK_MS, VOICE_DID_NOT_START } = await import('@core/tts/webspeech');
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const voiceId = DANIEL.voiceURI;

function resetSynth() {
  synth.spoken.length = 0; synth.speaking = false; synth.paused = false; synth.resumes = 0; synth.throwOnSpeak = false;
  synth.voices = [DANIEL, SAMANTHA, TINGTING]; synth.listeners.clear();
}

describe('WebSpeechEngine', () => {
  beforeEach(resetSynth);

  it('speaks and resolves when the utterance ends', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const h = e.speak('Hello there', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await sleep(5);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual(['Hello there']);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].voice).toBe(DANIEL);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].lang).toBe('en-GB');
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await h.done).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('after cancelling one utterance (stop at a hard word) the next speak waits for the engine to settle', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const a = e.speak('The sanguine man laughed.', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await sleep(5);
    a.cancel();
    expect(await a.done).toBe('cancelled');
    const b = e.speak('sanguine', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await sleep(10);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual([]); // Chromium drops a speak() issued right after cancel()
    await sleep(80);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual(['sanguine']);
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await b.done).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('cancelAll() also cancels utterances still waiting to be spoken', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    e.cancelAll(); // opens the settle window
    const b = e.speak('ghost sentence', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    e.cancelAll();
    expect(await Promise.race([b.done, sleep(20).then(() => 'pending')])).toBe('cancelled');
    await sleep(100);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a chosen voice that no longer exists falls back to the default British voice, not an unvoiced utterance', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    e.speak('Hello', { voiceId: 'com.apple.voice.enhanced.en-GB.Serena', rate: 1 });
    await sleep(5);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].voice).toBe(DANIEL);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].lang).toBe('en-GB');
    // a Chinese voice that does exist is used as asked
    e.speak('你好', { voiceId: TINGTING.voiceURI, rate: 1 });
    await sleep(5);
    expect(synth.spoken[1].voice).toBe(TINGTING);
  });

  it('waits for voices to load before speaking when getVoices() is still empty', async () => {
    synth.voices = [];
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const h = e.speak('Hello', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await sleep(10);
    expect(synth.spoken).toEqual([]);
    synth.voices = [DANIEL, SAMANTHA];
    synth.fireVoicesChanged();
    await sleep(5);
    expect(synth.spoken[0]?.voice).toBe(DANIEL);
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await h.done).toBe('ended');
  });
});

describe('WebSpeechEngine stuck-synthesizer recovery', () => {
  beforeEach(() => { resetSynth(); vi.useFakeTimers(); });
  afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); });
  const tick = (ms: number) => vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms);

  it('a speak() that throws fails only that utterance; later utterances still play', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    synth.throwOnSpeak = true;
    const a = e.speak('First', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    expect(await a.done).toBe('error');
    expect(a.error?.message).toContain('synthesizer exploded');
    synth.throwOnSpeak = false;
    const b = e.speak('Second', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual(['Second']);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.(); synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await b.done).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('resumes a synthesizer left paused (after a cancel) before speaking', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    synth.paused = true;
    e.speak('Hello', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    expect(synth.paused).toBe(false);
    expect(synth.resumes).toBe(1);
    expect(synth.spoken.map((u) => u.text)).toEqual(['Hello']);
  });

  it('start watchdog: cancels and retries once when onstart never fires, then fails with a clear message', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const h = e.speak('Hello there', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    const first = synth.spoken[0];
    // the first utterance after a (new) voice gets the long warm-up allowance
    await tick(START_TIMEOUT_NEW_VOICE_MS - 100);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    await tick(100 + 300);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1); // the stuck utterance was cancelled and a fresh one spoken
    expect(synth.spoken[0]).not.toBe(first);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].text).toBe('Hello there');
    // the retry gets the normal allowance (same voice now), then gives up
    let settled: string | null = null; void h.done.then((o) => { settled = o; });
    await tick(START_TIMEOUT_MS - 100);
    expect(settled).toBeNull();
    await tick(200);
    expect(settled).toBe('error');
    expect(h.error?.message).toBe(VOICE_DID_NOT_START);
    expect(synth.speaking).toBe(false); // the engine was cleared so the next sentence can start
  });

  it('start watchdog: the retry succeeds when the synthesizer wakes up', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const started: string[] = [];
    const h = e.speak('Hello there', { voiceId, rate: 1, onStart: () => started.push('start') });
    await tick(START_TIMEOUT_NEW_VOICE_MS + 400);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    expect(started).toEqual(['start']);
    await tick(START_TIMEOUT_MS); // no further retry or failure once it started (the end watchdog is at 6.6 s)
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await h.done).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('start watchdog waits while another utterance is still legitimately speaking', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const a = e.speak('A long first sentence that is still being read aloud.', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    const b = e.speak('Second', { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(START_TIMEOUT_MS * 2);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(2); // nothing was cancelled
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await a.done).toBe('ended');
    synth.spoken[1].onstart?.(); synth.spoken[1].onend?.();
    expect(await b.done).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('end watchdog: finishes an utterance whose onend never comes, after twice its expected duration', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const text = 'one two three four five six seven eight nine ten'; // 10 words at 150 wpm = 4 s
    const h = e.speak(text, { voiceId, rate: 1 });
    await tick(5);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    let settled: string | null = null; void h.done.then((o) => { settled = o; });
    await tick(4000 * 2 + END_TIMEOUT_EXTRA_MS - 100);
    expect(settled).toBeNull();
    await tick(200);
    expect(settled).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('ticks resume() every 10 s while speaking (Chromium pauses long utterances)', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const text = Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => `word${i}`).join(' '); // 60 words at rate 0.5: 48 s expected
    const h = e.speak(text, { voiceId, rate: 0.5 });
    await tick(5);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    await tick(RESUME_TICK_MS * 2 + 50);
    expect(synth.resumes).toBe(2);
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    await h.done;
    await tick(RESUME_TICK_MS * 2);
    expect(synth.resumes).toBe(2); // stops with the utterance
  });

  it('probe() reports ok when the voice starts and a reason when it does not', async () => {
    const e = new WebSpeechEngine();
    const p1 = e.probe(voiceId);
    await tick(100);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    expect(synth.spoken[0].volume).toBeCloseTo(0.01);
    synth.spoken[0].onstart?.();
    synth.spoken[0].onend?.();
    expect(await p1).toEqual({ ok: true });
    resetSynth();
    const p2 = e.probe(voiceId);
    await tick(100);
    expect(synth.spoken.length).toBe(1);
    await tick(6000);
    const r2 = await p2;
    expect(r2.ok).toBe(false);
    expect(r2.reason).toContain(VOICE_DID_NOT_START);
    synth.voices = [];
    const p3 = e.probe();
    await tick(2100); // waitForVoices gives up after 2 s
    expect((await p3).reason).toContain('No system voices');
  });
});
```

```ts
import { defineConfig, devices, chromium } from '@playwright/test';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

/**
 * The Chromium this Playwright version expects, or else any Chromium already installed under
 * PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH (machines where the browsers were installed by another Playwright version).
 */
function chromiumExecutable(): string | undefined {
  try { if (fs.existsSync(chromium.executablePath())) return undefined; } catch { /* not installed */ }
  const dir = process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH;
  if (!dir || !fs.existsSync(dir)) return undefined;
  for (const name of fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => /^chromium(-\d+)?$/.test(n)).sort().reverse()) {
    for (const rel of ['', 'chrome-linux/chrome', 'chrome-linux64/chrome', 'chrome-mac/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium']) {
      const p = path.join(dir, name, rel);
      if (fs.existsSync(p) && fs.statSync(p).isFile()) return p;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Smoke test of the web (iPad) build in Chromium with an iPad-sized touch viewport.
 * Run: npx playwright test -c test/web/playwright.config.ts  (builds dist/web first, see smoke.spec.ts)
 */
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: '.',
  testMatch: /.*\.spec\.ts/,
  timeout: 90_000,
  retries: 0,
  workers: 1,
  reporter: [['list']],
  outputDir: '../../test-results/web',
  use: {
    ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
    browserName: 'chromium',
    viewport: { width: 1024, height: 1366 },
    hasTouch: true,
    deviceScaleFactor: 2,
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
    launchOptions: { executablePath: chromiumExecutable() },
  },
});
```

```ts
import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import http from 'node:http';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import type { AddressInfo } from 'node:net';

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '../..');
const dist = path.join(root, 'dist/web');

const TYPES: Record<string, string> = {
  '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', '.js': 'text/javascript', '.mjs': 'text/javascript', '.css': 'text/css',
  '.json': 'application/json', '.webmanifest': 'application/manifest+json', '.png': 'image/png', '.svg': 'image/svg+xml',
  '.gz': 'application/gzip', '.map': 'application/json', '.woff2': 'font/woff2',
};

let server: http.Server;
let base = '';

/** A tiny static server for dist/web (no compression, like a plain static host). */
function serve(dir: string): Promise<http.Server> {
  const srv = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    let rel = decodeURIComponent(new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://x').pathname);
    if (rel.endsWith('/')) rel += 'index.html';
    const file = path.normalize(path.join(dir, rel));
    if (!file.startsWith(dir) || !fs.existsSync(file) || fs.statSync(file).isDirectory()) { res.writeHead(404); res.end('not found'); return; }
    res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': TYPES[path.extname(file)] ?? 'application/octet-stream', 'cache-control': 'no-cache' });
    fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res);
  });
  return new Promise((resolve) => srv.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve(srv)));
}

test.beforeAll(async () => {
  execFileSync(process.execPath, [path.join(root, 'scripts/build-web.mjs')], { cwd: root, stdio: 'pipe' });
  server = await serve(dist);
  base = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;
});

test.afterAll(async () => { await new Promise((r) => server?.close(r)); });

/** First start: skip the level test, finish the settings tour, land in the library. */
async function onboard(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await expect(page.getByTestId('level-intro')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByTestId('level-skip').tap();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('settings')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByTestId('finish-onboarding').tap();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('library')).toBeVisible();
}

const TEXT = `The Lighthouse

Mara climbed the narrow stairs of the old lighthouse every evening. The wind was fierce, and the sea below was restless and grey.

She lit the lamp and watched the beam sweep across the water. Somewhere out there, a small boat was searching for the harbour.

When the boat finally reached the shore, the fisherman waved to her. Mara smiled, because the light had done its quiet work again.`;

test('web build: paste a text, read it, switch Reading <-> Listening, data survives a reload', async ({ page }) => {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(e.message));
  await page.goto(`${base}/index.html?e2e=1`);

  // the browser API is installed, and unknown methods resolve harmlessly
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => typeof window.readalong.importText)).toBe('function');
  expect(await page.evaluate(async () => (await (window.readalong as unknown as Record<string, () => Promise<unknown>>).someFutureMethod()) ?? 'undefined')).toBe('undefined');
  // local speech recognition is feature-detected by the renderer and must look absent (typed questions remain)
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => [typeof window.readalong.sttStatus, typeof window.readalong.onSttEvent])).toEqual(['undefined', 'undefined']);

  await onboard(page);

  // the gzipped dictionary inflates in the browser
  const dictWords = await page.evaluate(async () => Object.keys((await window.readalong.loadDictionary()).w).length);
  expect(dictWords).toBeGreaterThan(10_000);

  // paste a text
  await page.getByTestId('paste-text').tap();
  await page.getByTestId('paste-title').fill('The Lighthouse');
  await page.getByTestId('paste-body').fill(TEXT);
  await page.getByTestId('paste-import').tap();

  // the reader opens in Reading mode with the text
  await expect(page.getByTestId('reading')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 20_000 });
  await expect(page.getByTestId('doc')).toContainText('narrow stairs');

  // Reading -> Listening -> Reading
  const showBars = async () => { if (!(await page.getByTestId('topbar').isVisible())) await page.getByTestId('doc').tap({ position: { x: 500, y: 600 } }); };
  await showBars();
  await page.getByTestId('switch-mode').first().tap();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('listening')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('listening')).toContainText('lighthouse');
  await page.getByTestId('listening').getByTestId('switch-mode').tap();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('reading')).toBeVisible();

  // touch targets in the reader bar are at least 44 px high
  await showBars();
  const box = await page.getByTestId('switch-mode').first().boundingBox();
  expect(box?.height ?? 0).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(44);

  // the book, settings and onboarding live in IndexedDB: after a reload the library still has it
  await page.goto(`${base}/index.html?e2e=1`);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('library')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('book-card')).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(page.getByTestId('book-card')).toContainText('The Lighthouse');

  // the web defaults use the browser's own voices, not the Mac-only Dream voice
  expect(await page.evaluate(async () => (await window.readalong.getSettings()).voice.engine)).toBe('webspeech');

  expect(errors).toEqual([]);
});

test('web build: AI explanation streams from the browser (Anthropic SSE, mocked)', async ({ page }) => {
  let headers: Record<string, string> = {};
  let body: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  await page.route('https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', async (route) => {
    headers = route.request().headers();
    body = route.request().postDataJSON();
    const ev = (type: string, data: object) => `event: ${type}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ type, ...data })}\n\n`;
    await route.fulfill({
      status: 200,
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream', 'access-control-allow-origin': '*' },
      body: ev('message_start', { message: { usage: { input_tokens: 1000, cache_read_input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 1 } } })
        + ev('content_block_start', { index: 0, content_block: { type: 'text', text: '' } })
        + ev('content_block_delta', { index: 0, delta: { type: 'text_delta', text: 'Fierce means ' } })
        + ev('content_block_delta', { index: 0, delta: { type: 'text_delta', text: 'very strong. 猛烈的' } })
        + ev('message_delta', { delta: { stop_reason: 'end_turn' }, usage: { output_tokens: 20 } })
        + ev('message_stop', {}),
    });
  });
  await page.goto(`${base}/index.html?e2e=1`);
  await onboard(page);
  const result = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const api = window.readalong;
    const noKey = await new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
      const off = api.onAiEvent((ev) => { if (ev.type === 'error') { off(); resolve(ev.code ?? ''); } });
      void api.aiExplain({ kind: 'word', target: 'fierce', sentence: 'The wind was fierce.', before: '', after: '', book: { title: 'T', chapter: '1' }, history: [] });
    });
    await api.setSecret('anthropic', 'sk-ant-test-key');
    const deltas: string[] = [];
    const done = await new Promise<{ text: string; usd: number; input: number }>((resolve, reject) => {
      const off = api.onAiEvent((ev) => {
        if (ev.type === 'delta') deltas.push(ev.text);
        else if (ev.type === 'done') { off(); resolve({ text: ev.text, usd: ev.usage.usd, input: ev.usage.inputTokens }); }
        else { off(); reject(new Error(ev.message)); }
      });
      void api.aiExplain({ kind: 'word', target: 'fierce', sentence: 'The wind was fierce.', before: '', after: '', book: { title: 'T', chapter: '1' }, history: [] });
    });
    return { noKey, deltas, done, usage: (await api.getUsage()).length };
  });
  expect(result.noKey).toBe('no_key');
  expect(result.deltas.join('')).toBe('Fierce means very strong. 猛烈的');
  expect(result.done.input).toBe(1000);
  expect(result.done.usd).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(result.usage).toBe(1);
  expect(headers['anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access']).toBe('true');
  expect(headers['x-api-key']).toBe('sk-ant-test-key');
  expect(body.stream).toBe(true);
});

test('web build: the service worker precaches the app shell and the dictionary', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto(`${base}/index.html`);
  const cached = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;
    for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
      const keys = await caches.keys();
      const name = keys.find((k) => k.startsWith('dream-read-'));
      if (name) {
        const urls = (await (await caches.open(name)).keys()).map((r) => new URL(r.url).pathname);
        if (urls.some((u) => u.endsWith('dict.json.gz'))) return urls;
      }
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));
    }
    return [];
  });
  expect(cached).toContain('/main.js');
  expect(cached).toContain('/dict.json.gz');
  expect(cached).toContain('/pdf.worker.mjs');
});
```

# Appendix A: The full iPad research (R1 to R9)

Eight research tracks and a code porting map. Each track ends with a fact-check by an independent checker who tried to disprove the key claims. Where a fact-check corrects a claim, the fact-check wins. R4 (the 7 characters) is Part 5.

## R1. Which way to build the iPad app


### Summary

My recommendation: build Dream Book as a real App Store app with Expo (React Native). Expo keeps the "brain" of Dream Read, which is the plain TypeScript in src/core and src/shared. That is about 10,000 lines and the 650 tests: book import, levels, the teaching flow and the prompts. Only the screens get redrawn for iPad. The most important reason is "sleep and listen". iPadOS often pauses web pages when the screen is locked. That covers the Safari web version and also web pages wrapped inside an app. A real app with background audio can keep reading for hours and show controls on the lock screen. The second reason is your Mac. Since 28 April 2026, Apple only accepts apps built with Xcode 26, which does not run on macOS 13 Ventura. Xcode 27, which came out on 14 September 2026, only runs on Apple-silicon Macs, and from April 2027 Apple will require it. Expo builds the iPad app on its own Macs in the cloud: 15 free iOS builds a month, or $19 a month for faster builds. So you and your AI assistant never need a new Mac. Second choice is Capacitor 8, which wraps the existing web version in an app. It is faster to start, but the night-time listening would still need to be written in Swift (Apple's programming language). A fully native Swift app would sound and feel best. But it means rewriting everything and buying an Apple-silicon Mac, so it is not a good fit now. Before building screens, the first week should test one thing on your real iPad: 2 hours of listening with the screen locked, plus the lock-screen controls and the voices. Then you decide.

### Detailed findings

## 0. Method and limits
- First I read the repo docs: HOW-IT-WORKS, RULES, MY-TEACHING-STYLE, IPAD, KOKORO, VOICE and research/*. Then I measured the code (line counts below) and ran about 37 web searches.
- **WebFetch could not reach any site** (DNS failure in the sandbox), so every fact below comes from search-result extracts. Many sources are third-party; I mark these.
- The search budget ran out near the end. A few points come from my background knowledge and are marked **(unverified)**.
- Nothing in the repo was changed.

## 1. What Dream Book needs from the iPad (from the repo docs)
| Need | Why it decides the platform |
|---|---|
| **Hours of listening with the screen off, no speaking** ("I just want to sleep and listen") | iPadOS suspends web content in the background. Only a native audio session with the `audio` background mode is reliable. |
| Karaoke word highlight | Needs per-word timings from the voice (Kokoro duration output, Apple voice word markers, or cloud timestamps). |
| Two voices in one script (English, plus Chinese for the 2 meanings) | RULES.md §2: Chinese must never be spoken by an English voice. |
| 5-second commands-only window (active mode) | Mic plus on-device speech recognition. Today this is Moonshine v2 + Silero VAD through sherpa-onnx on the Mac. |
| Local free voice (Kokoro "Dream voice") | Today it uses onnxruntime-node, which is Mac-only (KOKORO.md). |
| EPUB/PDF import, keys, account + cloud restore | File picker, Keychain, and a sync backend. |

**Code inventory (counted in this repo):**

| Folder | Lines | Files | Status on iPad |
|---|---|---|---|
| src/core | 9,132 | 41 | Plain TypeScript. Browser-only spots: `tts/audio.ts` (HTMLAudioElement), `tts/webspeech.ts` (speechSynthesis), `ai/client.ts` + `tts/registry.ts` (`window.readalong` bridge), `segment.ts` (Intl.Segmenter), `import/pdf.ts` (pdf.js). Everything else, including the hand-written EPUB parser using JSZip, is pure logic. |
| src/shared | 869 | 3 | Types, settings, `styles.ts` (teaching prompts). Fully reusable. |
| src/renderer | 4,674 | 30 | React DOM screens. |
| src/main | 4,044 | 31 | Node/Electron. Replaced on **every** iPad route. |
| src/web | 1,570 | 14 | The browser version of the main-process API (IndexedDB, `fetch` to Anthropic/OpenAI/ElevenLabs). A good template for any non-Electron port. |

The `TtsEngine` interface (`src/core/tts/engine.ts`: `speak`, `onWord`, `readAhead`, `cancelAll`) is clean. A native voice can plug in behind it without touching `listen/controller.ts` or `listen/playback.ts`.

## 2. The constraint that decides a lot: building iPad apps from an Intel Mac on macOS 13
| Date | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| since 28 Apr 2026 | App Store Connect uploads must be built with **Xcode 26+ and the iOS/iPadOS 26 SDK** | https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ , https://expo.dev/blog/app-store-connect-minimum-sdk-26 |
| Xcode 26.0–26.3 | needs **macOS Sequoia 15.6+**; Xcode 26.4.1+ needs **macOS Tahoe 26.2+** (third-party table, not checked against Apple) | https://mungomash.com/software/xcode/versions/ |
| 14 Sep 2026 | **Xcode 27 runs only on Apple-silicon Macs** (arm64-only binary, macOS Tahoe 26.6+) | https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/829619 , https://blakecrosley.com/blog/xcode-27-drops-intel |
| from Apr 2027 | uploads must use the **iOS 27 SDK**, so Xcode 27, so an Apple-silicon Mac | https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=k1mtkt1k |
| Intel Macs | Sequoia supports MacBook Pro 2018 and later. Tahoe supports only the 16-inch 2019 and the 13-inch 2020 (four ports), and Tahoe is the last Intel macOS. | https://www.macworld.com/article/2416662/macos-sequoia-compatibility-can-your-mac-run-the-new-version-of-macos.html , https://www.macworld.com/article/2808358/if-you-own-an-intel-mac-you-have-12-months-to-upgrade-to-a-new-model.html |

**What this means:** the learner's Mac can no longer produce an uploadable iPad build, and from 2027 no Intel Mac can. Every route except the PWA therefore needs a **cloud Mac** or a new Apple-silicon Mac.

**Cloud build options:**
- **EAS Build** (Expo). Builds iOS in the cloud from any computer, Linux included. Free plan: 15 iOS builds a month in a low-priority queue that can wait 90+ minutes at peak. Starter: $19 a month with $45 of build credit (about $2 per iOS build). Sources: https://expo.dev/pricing , https://docs.expo.dev/billing/plans/ , https://vibecoding.app/blog/expo-eas-review
- **GitHub Actions**. An Xcode 27 runner image has been in public preview since 16 Jul 2026, on arm64 runners only: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-16-xcode-27-runner-image-now-in-public-preview
- **Xcode Cloud**. 25 free compute hours a month with the Developer Program, but setup normally starts inside Xcode: https://developer.apple.com/xcode-cloud/get-started
- **For Capacitor:** Ionic Appflow is being shut down (end date 31 Dec 2027, no new customers). Capawesome Cloud offers builds from $9 a month (vendor's own claim): https://capawesome.io/compare/ionic-appflow/ , https://capgo.app/blog/appflow-shutdown-alternative
- **Apple Developer Program:** $99 a year, needed for TestFlight or installing on the iPad on every route except the PWA **(unverified, standard fee)**.

## 3. The five options

### A. The existing PWA in Safari (iPadOS 18/26)
- **Code reuse:** 100%. It already exists (docs/IPAD.md). Effort: days.
- **Background listening is unreliable.**
  - A WebKit bug documents audio stopping when a standalone web app is left: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=198277
  - Background audio for Home Screen web apps only arrived in iOS 15.4, with "known regressions … on iOS 26". The `navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback'` hint "can't override the OS when iOS suspends a Home Screen web app": https://github.com/elammaryo/gameover/pull/17 , https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioSession
  - Users report PWA audio breaking on iOS 26: "much better" in 26.1, some issues in 26.2: https://forums.macrumors.com/threads/ios-26-audio-issues-in-pwa-web-apps-not-fixed-in-26-1-or-26-2-but-much-better.2466839/
  - `speechSynthesis` stops when Safari goes to the background. That report is from the Safari 15.4 era, so it may be dated: https://weboutloud.io/bulletin/speech_synthesis_in_safari/
  - Dream Read's playback loop runs in JavaScript, sentence by sentence, so any suspension stops the book.
- **iOS 26 change:** every site added to the Home Screen now opens as a web app by default: https://webkit.org/blog/17333/webkit-features-in-safari-26-0/
- **Voices:**
  - Only Safari's system voices.
  - The `boundary` (word) event is "not Baseline", and I could not confirm iOS support: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechSynthesisUtterance/onboundary
  - Safari 26 turns on WebGPU for iOS/iPadOS 26, so kokoro-js could run in theory: https://appdevelopermagazine.com/webgpu-in-ios-26/ . But kokoro-js gives no word timings (KOKORO.md), and background suspension still applies.
- **Speech recognition:**
  - `webkitSpeechRecognition` needs Siri and is listed as **not available in web apps added to the Home Screen** (possibly outdated): https://docs.w3cub.com/browser_support_tables/speech-recognition
  - getUserMedia works, but a local recogniser would have to be WASM. No proof that this is practical on iPad.
- **Storage:**
  - Home Screen apps have their own "days of use" counter, and WebKit says it does not intend to delete their data. Developers still report wipes (bug 232302 closed WONTFIX): https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/710157 , https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=232302
  - Since iOS 17 a browser origin may use about 60% of disk: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria
  - Keys are stored unencrypted (IPAD.md).
- **No App Store** (no review risk, but no app).
- **Verdict:** keep it as a free fallback and test bed. It cannot meet "sleep and listen".

### B. Capacitor 8 (wrap the web build)
- **Status:** Capacitor 8 was announced 8 Dec 2025 with Swift Package Manager as the iOS default: https://ionic.io/blog/announcing-capacitor-8 . The CocoaPods trunk goes read-only on 2 Dec 2026 (third-party): https://capgo.app/blog/ios-spm-vs-cocoapods-capacitor-migration-guide/
- **Code reuse:** highest of the app routes. Roughly src/core + src/shared + src/renderer + most of src/web, about 16,000 of 20,400 TS lines.
- **The catch is the WKWebView.**
  - Page JavaScript is paused when the app is in the background. The Cordova issue was closed "Won't Fix": "no javascript callback will be executed unless the app is either in the foreground…": https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CB-10657
  - AudioContexts inside WKWebView froze after about 27 s in the background: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/121822
  - Web Audio fails after screen lock: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/658375
  - Capacitor guides say background audio needs the native `audio` mode plus a native audio plugin: https://capgo.app/blog/how-to-play-audio-in-the-background-in-capacitor/ , https://capawesome.io/blog/how-to-play-audio-in-the-background-in-capacitor/ (Capawesome's Audio Player handles the lock screen natively since 8.4.0)
  - So `ListenController` (pause at a hard word, explain, re-read) cannot run in JS with the screen off. The night queue must be native and **pre-rendered**.
- **Plugins:**
  - Voice: Capawesome Speech Synthesis (paid "Insiders"; background audio and boundary events): https://capawesome.io/plugins/speech-synthesis
  - Speech recognition: `@capgo/capacitor-speech-recognition` 8.1.10. It uses SFSpeechRecognizer by default with `contextualStrings`, and an opt-in SpeechAnalyzer path on iOS 26: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@capgo/capacitor-speech-recognition@8.1.10/README.md . Capawesome also has an on-device-only SpeechTranscriber mode: https://capawesome.io/plugins/speech-recognition/
  - Kokoro needs a custom Swift plugin.
  - getUserMedia in WKWebView can prompt for permission on every call: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=220416
- **App Store Guideline 4.2:** the app must "elevate it beyond a repackaged website". Push notifications or sharing alone are not enough: https://www.mobiloud.com/blog/app-store-review-guidelines-webview-wrapper/ , https://capgo.app/blog/how-to-pass-app-store-review-2026/ . With native voice, speech recognition, background audio and Files import, the risk is moderate.
- **Builds:** needs a cloud Mac (GitHub Actions or Capawesome Cloud). The AI can develop the UI in a browser on Linux, which is a fast loop.
- **Effort (my estimate):** 4–7 weeks, about half of it native Swift plugin work.

### C. React Native with Expo (reuse src/core, rewrite the UI)
- **Status:**
  - SDK 55 (25 Feb 2026): React Native 0.83, React 19.2, Legacy Architecture removed: https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-55
  - SDK 56 (21 May 2026) and SDK 57 (30 Jun 2026) per https://expo.dev/sdk
  - npm `latest` showed expo 58.0.14; I found no SDK 58 changelog: https://www.npmjs.com/package/expo?activeTab=versions
- **Code reuse:**
  - src/core + src/shared, about 10,000 lines and the 650 tests, as a shared package used by both the Mac app and the iPad app.
  - Adapters needed:
    - Hermes has **no `Intl.Segmenter`**. It is still listed as missing on RN 0.86–0.87: https://npm.io/package/hermes-intl , https://www.npmjs.com/package/unicode-segmenter . Fix with `@formatjs/intl-segmenter` (https://formatjs.io/docs/polyfills/intl-segmenter) or Apple's NLTokenizer. Re-run the segment tests either way.
    - pdf.js → PDFKit module, or pdf.js inside a DOM component.
    - `AudioTtsEngine` (HTMLAudio) → native player.
    - `window.readalong` → an injected API. The `fetch`-based src/web/ai.ts is the model; streaming needs `expo/fetch` **(unverified)**.
    - Hermes WebAssembly support is contested (https://www.callstack.com/events/react-native-0-84-and-other-news), so the espeak-ng WASM phonemizer cannot be counted on.
  - src/renderer (4,674 lines) is rewritten as RN views. zustand and the React patterns carry over.
  - **Expo DOM components** (`'use dom'`) can temporarily reuse DOM screens such as Settings, Vocabulary or Reading mode. They are still WebViews: weaker touch, throttled in Low Power Mode, separate JS context: https://expo.dev/blog/the-magic-of-expo-dom-components
- **Background audio:**
  - `expo-audio` has `enableBackgroundPlayback` and lock-screen controls (`setActiveForLockScreen`, SDK 55 API): https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/audio/ . Fix for a missing Now Playing card: https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/40919
  - Limits: lock screen offers only ±10 s seek with no next/previous, and `AudioPlaylist` has no lock-screen controls: https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/43538
  - react-native-track-player v5 (`@rntp/player` 5.7.0) supports the New Architecture but **needs a paid licence for production/revenue apps** (v4 stays Apache-2.0): https://rntp.dev/docs/ , https://www.rntp.dev/llms.txt
  - A small custom Expo module in Swift (AVQueuePlayer + MPNowPlayingInfoCenter) is the cleanest night player.
  - RN's JavaScript runs inside the app's own process. iOS keeps an app with the audio background mode running while it plays, so the controller and network calls can continue with the screen off. This is standard iOS behaviour **(unverified here; check it in the first test week)**. WKWebView pages run in a separate WebKit process that gets suspended.
- **Voices and speech:**
  - `expo-speech` has `onBoundary` (fires at each word). It is silent when the iPad is in silent mode: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/speech/
  - `react-native-sherpa-onnx`: Kokoro TTS, offline STT, VAD; iOS 13+; bundles sherpa-onnx iOS 1.12.35. That is the same toolkit as the Mac app: https://github.com/XDcobra/react-native-sherpa-onnx
  - `@react-native-ai/apple` wraps SpeechAnalyzer: https://www.callstack.com/blog/on-device-speech-transcription-with-apple-speechanalyzer
  - Custom native modules mean a development build. Expo Go cannot load them.
- **Builds:** EAS Build/Submit from any OS. An AI assistant on Linux can run TS tests, `eas build -p ios` and `eas submit` to TestFlight.
- **AI tooling:**
  - Expo MCP server (`claude mcp add --transport http expo https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp`).
  - Expo Skills plugin for Claude Code.
  - `create-expo-app` scaffolds a CLAUDE.md: https://docs.expo.dev/agents , https://docs.expo.dev/agents/claude
- **App Store:** no Guideline 4.2 web-wrapper risk.
- **Effort (my estimate):** 7–11 weeks.

### D. Native SwiftUI (full rewrite)
- **Best platform access:**
  - `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write(_:toBufferCallback:toMarkerCallback:)` renders Apple voices to audio buffers **with word markers**, ideal for pre-rendered night audio: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avspeechsynthesizer . One iOS 18 report says markers lost sync on a provider audio-unit path: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/769342
  - SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber on iPadOS 26 is on-device after a model download, but has no custom vocabulary: https://blog.addpipe.com/apple-speechanalyzer-api/ , https://blakecrosley.com/blog/speech-framework-vs-sfspeechrecognizer
  - Foundation Models framework (about 3B parameters, on-device; M1+ iPads per third parties): https://developer.apple.com/ipados/whats-new/ , https://www.atelier-socle.com/en/articles/foundation-models-api-guide
  - Kokoro in Swift:
    - FluidAudio (CoreML/ANE, about 224 MB first download): https://huggingface.co/FluidInference/kokoro-82m-coreml
    - speech-swift (RTF 0.08 on an iPhone 16 Pro): https://github.com/soniqo/speech-swift
    - kokoro-ios (MLX, per-token timestamps since 1.0.8): https://swiftpackageregistry.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios
  - PDFKit and NaturalLanguage come built in.
- **Risks:**
  - 0% code reuse. About 20,000 lines of logic, prompts and tests would have to be ported to Swift.
  - Two codebases (Mac Electron and iPad Swift).
  - Swift for iOS cannot be compiled or tested on Linux, so an AI needs a Mac with Xcode. Xcode 26.3 adds Claude Agent and Codex (shipped Feb 2026): https://www.mactech.com/2026/02/27/apple-releases-xcode-26-3-with-support-for-agentic-coding . But Ventura cannot run Xcode 26, and from 2027 the Mac must be Apple silicon.
  - Background TTS has its own reported failures, e.g. TTS stopping in background on iOS 16.5: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/732576 . Pre-rendering avoids them.
- **Effort (my estimate):** 14–24 weeks, plus a Mac.

### E. Tauri 2 mobile
- **Status:** v2 stable since 2 Oct 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tauri_(software_framework)). Mobile is "less proven than desktop" with "rough edges around plugin support, signing, and webview quirks": https://blog.codercops.com/blog/tauri-2-desktop-mobile-apps-rust-web-2026 , https://github.com/orgs/tauri-apps/discussions/10197
- **Same WKWebView background problem as Capacitor**, plus Rust, plus Swift plugins, with no TTS/STT plugins found and no hosted iOS build service.
- **Effort (my estimate):** 6–10 weeks with the highest uncertainty.

## 4. Scorecard (5 = best; my judgment from the evidence above)
| Criterion | A PWA | B Capacitor | C Expo | D SwiftUI | E Tauri |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Code reuse | 5 | 5 | 3 | 1 | 4 |
| Effort for this app | 5 | 4 | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| Long books + karaoke speed | 3 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
| **Hours of screen-off listening** | 1 | 2 (only with native pre-rendered queue) | 4 | 5 | 2 |
| On-device voice / speech | 1 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 2 |
| App Store acceptance | – (no store) | 3 | 5 | 5 | 3 |
| **Build from Intel Mac / Ventura** | 5 | 2 | 5 | 1 | 2 |
| Maintainability with the Mac app | 4 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 2 |
| AI assistant can build *and verify* | 4 | 3 | 5 | 2 | 2 |

## 5. A "sleep mode" design that works on any native route
1. **When a book is added:** the AI reads the whole book, chapter by chapter (the `hints.ts` chapter job already exists). It finds the words, phrases and sentences above the learner's level and plans the stops (no repeat within 500 words).
2. **Ahead of playback:** it writes the explanations for the next chapters in the active teaching character, following RULE ONE/TWO/THREE from MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md.
3. **Pre-render 30–60 minutes of audio:** book sentences + explanation scripts (English voice) + the 2 Chinese meanings (Chinese voice). Saved as files plus word-timing JSON (Kokoro duration output, Apple voice markers, or ElevenLabs timestamps).
4. **A native queue player** with the `audio` background mode, Now Playing, AirPods/phone-call handling and a sleep timer. When the screen is on, the highlight follows the player's time.
5. **Hands-free mode follows RULES.md §1:** silence means "explain", and after the explanation, silence means the word "stays learning". So no mic is needed at all.
6. **Keep audio queued ahead.** iOS may suspend an app whose audio stops. Using background audio for anything but real playback breaks App Review 2.5.4 **(unverified wording)**.

## 6. Other notes
- **China:** new apps in the China storefront need an ICP filing (since 2023), and Apple removed 100+ generative-AI apps there in Aug 2023: https://www.mactech.com/2023/10/03/new-apps-must-have-a-government-license-before-being-offered-in-chinas-apple-app-store/amp/ , https://daoinsights.com/news/ai-apps-taken-down-from-chinas-app-store/ . Publish outside the China storefront, or use TestFlight.
- **Expo vs Capacitor speed:** RN "pulls ahead" on gestures, animation and long virtualized lists. No benchmark of karaoke highlighting exists: https://vp0.com/blogs/react-native-vs-capacitor-2026-performance
- **Still unverified** (the search budget ran out):
  - the exact iPadOS 26 device list
  - whether Keychain items survive app deletion
  - `expo/fetch` streaming
  - Kokoro speed on the learner's specific iPad

(The 7 teaching-character prompt texts belong to the teaching-styles topic, not this platform topic.)

### Recommendation

## Recommendation: C, Expo (React Native) + EAS cloud builds, with a native "night player"

**Why:**
1. **It is the only route that meets "sleep and listen" while still reusing most of the code.**
   - React Native runs JavaScript in the app's own process, which iOS keeps running while background audio plays.
   - The PWA, Capacitor and Tauri run the teaching loop inside a WebKit page, and iOS pauses that in the background (CB-10657 "Won't Fix"; WebKit bug 198277; iOS 26 PWA audio regressions).
2. **It works around the learner's Intel Mac on macOS 13.**
   - Uploads need Xcode 26 (since 28 Apr 2026). Xcode 27 is Apple-silicon-only, and from April 2027 it is effectively mandatory.
   - EAS Build compiles in the cloud from any OS: free plan 15 iOS builds a month, Starter $19 a month. An AI assistant on Linux can test, build and send to TestFlight without any Mac.
3. **It reuses the tested parts.**
   - src/core + src/shared (about 10,000 lines, 650 tests) become one shared package for the Mac app and the iPad app.
   - Only the screens (about 4,700 lines) are rewritten, in the same React/zustand style. Expo DOM components can carry some old screens over for a while.
4. **It has full native access when needed.** Through Expo modules: Apple voices with word boundaries, SpeechAnalyzer, the sherpa-onnx Kokoro and Moonshine stack the Mac already uses, Keychain, Files, and Now Playing.
5. **AI assistants know TypeScript/React best.** Expo also ships an official MCP server and Claude Code skills (docs.expo.dev/agents).

**Build plan (each step ends with a TestFlight build the learner tests on the iPad):**
1. **Week 1, a go/no-go test** on the learner's own iPad (a development build):
   - 2 hours of pre-rendered book audio with the screen locked, with Now Playing, AirPods pause and phone-call interruption
   - Apple-voice `onBoundary` word timing
   - Kokoro speed through `react-native-sherpa-onnx`
   - the Intl.Segmenter polyfill passing the existing `segment` tests
2. **Weeks 2–3:**
   - Move src/core into a shared package.
   - Write the iPad adapters: `TtsEngine`s, the storage layer, the AI client (from src/web/ai.ts), and PDF via a PDFKit module.
3. **Weeks 3–5:** Listening screen (karaoke), library, word card, settings for the 7 characters.
4. **Weeks 5–7:** hands-free Sleep mode. Whole-book analysis, pre-made explanations and a pre-rendered audio queue (design in §5 of the findings), plus a sleep timer.
5. **Weeks 7–9:** active mode. The 5-second commands window with SpeechAnalyzer or Moonshine.
6. **After that:** account + cloud restore. Reading mode can stay a DOM component at first.

All time estimates are my own judgment, not from a source.

**Main risks:**
- Hermes has no `Intl.Segmenter` (use the polyfill or Apple's NLTokenizer).
- Hermes WebAssembly support is unclear (use sherpa-onnx's native G2P, not the espeak WASM).
- `expo-audio` lock-screen limits (a small Swift Expo module for the queue fixes this).
- react-native-track-player v5 needs a paid licence for commercial apps.

## Runner-up: B, Capacitor 8
**When to choose it:** if getting an App Store app fast matters more than a clean design. It reuses about 80% of the TypeScript (the renderer as it is), and the AI can develop the UI in a desktop browser.

**Conditions:**
- The night player and Kokoro must be native Swift plugins playing a **pre-rendered** queue, because WKWebView JavaScript stops in the background.
- Plan for the Guideline 4.2 web-wrapper review.
- Use cloud builds: Capawesome Cloud (from $9 a month, vendor claim) or GitHub Actions. Do not use Ionic Appflow, which ends 31 Dec 2027.

## Not now
- **D, native SwiftUI:** the best audio and voice quality, but a full rewrite (0% reuse) and two codebases. It also needs an Apple-silicon Mac (Xcode 27 only runs there). Reconsider only if the learner buys an Apple-silicon Mac and wants a pure iPad app later.
- **A, PWA:** keep it as a free fallback and quick test page. It cannot promise screen-off listening, has no local speech recognition in Home Screen apps, and has no App Store.
- **E, Tauri 2 mobile:** the same WebView limits as Capacitor, with fewer plugins and Rust on top. No benefit for this app.

## Text to paste into the AI assistant
"Build Dream Book for iPad with Expo (latest stable SDK) and EAS Build, with no local Xcode. Move src/core and src/shared into a shared package and keep all their tests passing. Polyfill Intl.Segmenter for Hermes. Implement TtsEngine with native voices: Apple voices with word boundaries, Kokoro via sherpa-onnx, and the cloud voices. Play all book and explanation audio through a native background-audio queue with Now Playing. Build Sleep mode as pre-rendered audio: the whole-book analysis and the explanations are prepared ahead, and no mic is needed. First deliver a week-1 test build that plays 2 hours with the screen locked on my iPad. Follow docs/RULES.md and docs/MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md exactly."


### Fact-check of the key claims (an independent checker tried to disprove them)

- **confirmed**: Since 28 April 2026, apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later against an iOS/iPadOS 26 SDK; Xcode 26.0–26.3 needs macOS Sequoia 15.6+, so macOS 13 Ventura cannot produce uploadable builds.
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ (April 28, 2026: 'Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26...'). https://developer.apple.com/support/xcode/ (Xcode 26 / 26.1 / 26.2 / 26.3: 'macOS Sequoia 15.6 - macOS Tahoe 26.x'; Xcode 26.4.1: 'macOS Tahoe 26.2 - macOS Tahoe 26.x'). The general web search budget was used up, so I checked these Apple pages directly.
- **confirmed**: Xcode 27 (released 14 Sep 2026) installs and runs only on Apple-silicon Macs (macOS Tahoe 26.6+), and from April 2027 uploads must be built with the iOS 27 SDK.
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/news/releases/ (lists 'Xcode 27 (27A266a) September 14, 2026'). Xcode 27 release notes JSON at developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-27-release-notes.json (Deprecations section: 'Xcode 27 will only install and run on Apple silicon Macs'; overview: 'requires a Mac running macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later'). https://developer.apple.com/support/xcode/ (Xcode 27: macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later). https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=k1mtkt1k (Sept 9, 2026: 'Starting April 2027... iOS and iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS 27 & iPadOS 27 SDK or later').
- **confirmed**: EAS Build compiles iOS apps in the cloud without a Mac; the free plan includes 15 iOS builds per month (low-priority queue), and the Starter plan costs $19/month with $45 build credit.
  - Evidence: https://expo.dev/pricing (fetched with curl: 'Free ... $0/MONTH ... 15 Android and 15 iOS builds Low-priority queue'; 'Starter ... $19/month +additional usage cost ... $45 of build credit High-priority queue'). https://docs.expo.dev/billing/plans/ ('For $19 per month, you get $45 of build credit to use for priority builds'; 'free access to a limited quantity of low-priority builds').
- **corrected**: Audio in Home Screen web apps stops or misbehaves when the app is backgrounded (WebKit bug 198277; iOS 26 regressions only partly fixed in 26.1/26.2), and navigator.audioSession 'playback' cannot override iOS suspending a Home Screen web app.
  - Correct / uncertain: The WebKit bug 198277 citation is out of date. That bug ('Audio stops playing when standalone web app is no longer in foreground') was fixed in iOS 15.4. It is RESOLVED DUPLICATE of bug 232909, which is FIXED. Since iOS 15.4, an HTML <audio> element can keep playing in the background in a Home Screen web app. The general warning still holds, for three reasons. (a) An Apple WebKit engineer said in the same thread that Web Audio (AudioContext) counts as 'Ambient' audio and the system blocks it once the app leaves the foreground. That matters if the TTS plays through Web Audio. (b) There are open regressions: WebKit 295518 'REGRESSION (iOS 26): Audio Element Fails to Play on Reopen in PWA (Add to Home Screen)', WebKit 291892 'WebAudio AudioContext silent after PWA returns from background', and, now that iOS 27 is out, WebKit 325274 'REGRESSION (iOS 27): Web Speech (speechSynthesis) silences Web Audio (AudioContext)'. (c) navigator.audioSession.type has existed since Safari 16.4. I could not verify that 'playback' cannot override suspension: the only source is an unreviewed GitHub PR that says it was 'Not verified on a real iPhone.' I also could not open the MacRumors thread on 26.1/26.2 (Cloudflare blocked it).

## R2. Building and publishing from my Mac (Intel, macOS 13)


### Summary

The learner's Intel MacBook Pro on macOS 13 Ventura cannot put an app on the App Store as it is now. The newest Xcode that runs on Ventura is Xcode 15.2, and since 28 April 2026 Apple only accepts uploads built with Xcode 26 or newer. Upgrading macOS helps only for a short time. A 2018–2020 MacBook Pro can move to macOS 15 Sequoia or macOS 26 Tahoe and run Xcode 26. But Xcode 27 (out since September 2026) runs only on Apple-silicon Macs, and Apple normally raises the upload rule every April. So an Intel Mac will probably stop being able to submit around April 2027. A 2017 model is stuck on Ventura already. The cheapest path that keeps working does not need a new Mac. Pay Apple $99 a year for the Developer Program, build the app on rented cloud Macs (free tiers exist: GitHub Actions is free for this public repo, Codemagic gives 500 free minutes a month, Expo EAS gives 15 free iOS builds a month), and install it on your own iPad through TestFlight. For the App Store, Dream Book needs several things. It needs a privacy policy and privacy labels. It needs a clear consent screen before book text goes to Claude or OpenAI, and in-app account deletion if it has accounts. If it offers Google login, it must also offer Sign in with Apple or an equivalent private login. Microphone permission should be asked only in Active mode, and Apple must be able to test the AI during review (for example, a test API key). Do not release in mainland China at first. Anthropic does not serve mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau. China's App Store also needs a government ICP filing and, for book-content apps, a publishing permit, which an individual developer cannot easily get.

### Detailed findings

## 1. Xcode, macOS and this Intel MacBook Pro

### 1a. Which Xcode runs on which macOS ([Apple: Xcode system requirements](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/))
| Xcode | Minimum macOS | iOS/iPadOS SDK | Can it upload to the App Store today? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15.0 – **15.2** | Ventura 13.5 | 17.0–17.2 | **No** |
| 15.3 – 15.4 | Sonoma 14.x | 17.4–17.5 | No |
| 16.0 – 16.2 | Sonoma 14.5 | 18.0–18.2 | No |
| 16.3 – 16.4 | Sequoia 15.2 / 15.3 | 18.4–18.5 | No |
| 26.0 – **26.3** | **Sequoia 15.6** | 26.0–26.2 | **Yes** |
| 26.4.1 – **26.6** | **Tahoe 26.2** | 26.4–26.5 | **Yes** |
| 27.0 / 27.1 / 27.2 RC | Tahoe 26.6 | 27.x | Yes, but **Apple silicon only** |

- **Highest Xcode on macOS 13 Ventura = Xcode 15.2** (needs 13.5 or later).
- **Xcode 27 release notes:** "Xcode 27 will only install and run on Apple silicon Macs." It needs macOS Tahoe 26.6. ([Xcode 27 release notes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-27-release-notes))
- So the **last Xcode an Intel Mac can ever run is Xcode 26.6** (on Tahoe 26.2+), or **26.3** on Sequoia 15.6+.

### 1b. Can this Intel MacBook Pro upgrade? (Apple Support pages, fetched 2026-10-20)
| MacBook Pro model | Highest macOS | Highest Xcode | Can it upload now? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 (13" or 15") | **Ventura 13** (not on the Sonoma or Sequoia lists) | 15.2 | **No.** Cloud builds only |
| 13" 2018 (four TB3 ports), 15" 2018, 13" 2019 (two or four ports), 15" 2019, 13" 2020 (two TB3 ports) | **Sequoia 15** ([support.apple.com/en-us/120282](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120282); Sonoma has the same list: [105113](https://support.apple.com/en-us/105113)) | 26.3 | Yes, after upgrading to 15.6+ |
| **16" 2019**, **13" 2020 (four TB3 ports)** | **Tahoe 26** ([support.apple.com/en-us/122867](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122867), published 2026-09-14) | 26.6 | Yes, after upgrading to 26.2+ |

- Apple said at WWDC 2025 that **Tahoe is the last macOS for Intel Macs**. macOS 27 "Golden Gate" came out on 14 September 2026 and needs Apple silicon. The latest Tahoe is 26.7.1 (28 September 2026). ([Wikipedia: macOS Tahoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS_Tahoe))
- How to find the model: Apple menu → About This Mac → the model name and year.
- Dream Read (Electron) needs macOS 13 or later (INSTALL.md), so upgrading macOS does not break it. Make a Time Machine backup first.

## 2. Apple's minimum Xcode/SDK for uploads ([Upcoming requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/))
- **Since 28 April 2026:** apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with **Xcode 26 or later** using the **iOS/iPadOS 26 SDK**. This applies to **TestFlight uploads too**, because TestFlight goes through App Store Connect.
- Earlier steps: Xcode 14.1 (25 April 2023), Xcode 15 (29 April 2024). The April 2025 step to Xcode 16 / iOS 18 SDK is no longer on the page because it was replaced (unverified, from memory).
- **Since 9 September 2026:** iOS/iPadOS apps must target iOS 13 or later (easy to meet).
- **Age-rating questionnaire:** the new rating questions had to be answered by 31 January 2026. New apps answer them when they are created.
- **Privacy manifest:** required since 1 May 2024 for "required reason" APIs, including those inside SDKs.
- **No 2027 requirement is listed yet.** Every year so far the rule moved up in late April. **If Apple asks for Xcode 27 in about April 2027, no Intel Mac will be able to build an App Store upload** (a likely forecast, not announced).
- **Verdict:** as it is now (Ventura), **this Mac cannot submit at all**. A 2018–2020 model upgraded to Sequoia 15.6+ or Tahoe 26.2+ **can submit until roughly April 2027**.

## 4. Apple Developer Program, TestFlight, free Apple ID
- **Apple Developer Program: US$99 a year**, or the same in local currency ([what's included](https://developer.apple.com/programs/whats-included/); the Chinese page says the same: [cn](https://developer.apple.com/cn/programs/whats-included/)). Includes 25 h of Xcode Cloud a month, **CloudKit with "up to 1PB of free storage for each app"**, Sign in with Apple, In-App Purchase and push notifications. Fee waivers exist only for non-profits, schools and governments. An individual enrolment shows the learner's legal name as the seller (unverified detail). In the EU, "trader" status shows contact details publicly ([requirements page](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/)).
- **Free Apple ID (Personal Team)**, per [compare memberships](https://developer.apple.com/support/compare-memberships/):
  - up to 10 App IDs and 3 devices, which **expire after 7 days**;
  - up to 3 apps per device;
  - needs Xcode on a Mac and Developer Mode on the iPad;
  - **does not support** CloudKit/iCloud, push notifications, **In-App Purchase**, **Sign in with Apple** or associated domains. Background modes and keychain sharing do work ([supported capabilities](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/reference/supported-capabilities-ios)).
  - Whether Xcode 15.2 on Ventura can install onto an iPad running iPadOS 26 is **uncertain** and probably will not work. So the free route really needs the Mac upgraded to Sequoia/Tahoe with Xcode 26.
- **TestFlight** ([TestFlight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/), [overview](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/test-a-beta-version/testflight-overview)):
  - up to 100 internal testers (no review) and 10,000 external testers (the first build needs Beta App Review);
  - up to 30 devices per tester;
  - **each build works for 90 days**.
  - This is the easiest way to get Dream Book onto the learner's own iPad without any Mac.
- **What needs the paid account:** TestFlight, the App Store, ad hoc installs (a list of device UDIDs, no 7-day expiry), Sign in with Apple, CloudKit sync ("comes back after reinstall"), In-App Purchase, push notifications and App Store Connect API keys for cloud builds.

## 5. Sign in with Apple, Guideline 4.8 ([App Review Guidelines, updated 16 Oct 2026](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/))
- If the app uses a **third-party or social login** (Google, Facebook, WeChat, X…) for the main account, it **must also offer an equivalent login** that:
  - collects only name and email;
  - lets users hide their email;
  - does not collect data for advertising without consent.
- Sign in with Apple meets these rules. **Not required** if the app uses only its own email/password sign-in.
- For Dream Book: **Sign in with Apple first, plus email, and no Google button**. That is the simplest way to comply.
- When an account that used Sign in with Apple is deleted, its tokens should be revoked through Apple's REST API (unverified detail).

## 6. App Store rules that matter for Dream Book (all from the 16 Oct 2026 guidelines unless noted)
| Rule | What it says | What Dream Book must do |
|---|---|---|
| **5.1.2(i) third-party AI** | "You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, **including with third-party AI**, and obtain explicit permission before doing so." | Before the first AI call, show a consent screen naming Anthropic/OpenAI and saying that book text, questions and voice text are sent to them. Repeat this in the privacy policy |
| **5.1.1(i) privacy policy** | Link required in App Store Connect **and** inside the app | Write and host a policy (GitHub Pages is fine) |
| **App Privacy "nutrition labels"** | Filled in App Store Connect ([app privacy](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-app-information/manage-app-privacy)), plus the privacy manifest | Declare account email, user content (books, vocabulary) and audio if voice is sent anywhere |
| **5.1.1(v) accounts** | "If your app supports account creation, you must also offer **account deletion within the app**." Also: "If your app doesn't include significant account-based features, let people use it without a login." | Add a Delete account button that removes cloud data. Let the app be used **without an account** (local only), with the account as an option for backup and sync |
| **5.1.1(iv) access** | Don't force unnecessary permissions | Ask for the **microphone only when Active mode is first turned on**. Hands-free mode must never ask |
| **Microphone strings** | `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` "is required if your app uses APIs that access the device's microphone" ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsmicrophoneusagedescription)). `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` is needed if Apple's Speech framework is used, or "your app crashes" ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsspeechrecognitionusagedescription)) | Write plain purpose strings, for example "Dream Book listens only for 'I know', 'I don't know' and 'go on' during the 5-second window." |
| **2.5.4 background audio** | Background modes only "for their intended purposes: VoIP, **audio playback**…" | `UIBackgroundModes: audio` is legitimate for "sleep and listen". Add lock-screen Now Playing controls. Explain in the review notes that playback continues with the screen locked. Using the mic in the background (Active mode with the screen off) needs a clear explanation; review risk is **uncertain** |
| **4.2 minimum functionality** | "elevate it beyond a repackaged website" | Do **not** ship the current PWA in a bare WebView. Add native features: background audio, lock-screen controls, Keychain for keys, on-device voice, Files import, Sign in with Apple, offline use |
| **2.1 review access** | Provide "an active demo account or fully-featured demo mode… Enable backend services" | With bring-your-own-key, put a **test API key with a small spend limit** (and a demo login) in the Review Notes, or include a short built-in trial |
| **1.2 user-generated content** | Now names "**AI content creation apps**": filtering, reporting, blocking, contact info | Explanations are private, so 1.2 probably does not apply fully. Still, add a cheap "Report this explanation" button and a support email |
| **2.5.2 code** | No downloading code that changes features | Downloading the Kokoro or speech **models (data)** is fine. Over-the-air JavaScript updates should only be bug fixes |
| **3.1.1 In-App Purchase** | Unlocking features or subscriptions **must use IAP**; no licence keys | If Dream Book sells AI access, it needs an IAP subscription and its **own server** holding the AI key (never ship your key in the app). Commission: 30% standard, **15% in the Small Business Program** (under $1M proceeds a year) ([SBP](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/small-business-program/)) |
| **Bring your own key** | No guideline mentions API keys. A user's own Anthropic/OpenAI key is not an Apple "licence key" that unlocks paid features, and many App Store apps work this way (unverified precedent) | Keep BYO key at launch (matches Dream Read today). Store it in the **iOS Keychain**, which is safer than the PWA's IndexedDB |
| **US anti-steering** | 3.1.1(a) and 3.1.3: the ban on buttons or links to other purchase methods "does not apply" to the **United States storefront**; other storefronts need entitlements | US users may be linked to a web checkout. This followed the 30 April 2025 Epic v. Apple court order (date unverified). Whether Apple may later charge a commission on those link-outs is still uncertain |
| **Export compliance** | — | If only HTTPS and Apple's own crypto are used, set `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = NO` (usual case; confirm in App Store Connect) |
| **Screenshots** | iPad apps need at least one **13-inch iPad** screenshot (2064×2752 or 2048×2732) ([specs](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/screenshot-specifications)) | An iPad-only app does not need iPhone screenshots |

## 7. China
- **Anthropic:** the [supported countries list](https://www.anthropic.com/supported-countries) does **not** include mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau (Taiwan is listed): "Any country or region not listed is unsupported." On **4 September 2025** Anthropic also banned companies **more than 50% owned** by companies headquartered in unsupported regions such as China ([announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/updating-restrictions-of-sales-to-unsupported-regions)). INSTALL.md already says Anthropic refuses mainland, HK and Macau phone numbers and billing addresses.
  - If the learner lives in mainland China, the Claude API is **not available to them**.
  - Dream Book must not offer Claude to users located there. OpenAI also blocked API access from China in July 2024 (unverified).
  - I do not recommend ways around these restrictions.
- **China App Store** ([App Store Connect reference](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/app-information)):
  - MIIT requires an **ICP Filing Number** for some apps.
  - "**apps with books and magazine content must secure an internet publishing permit from China's National Press and Publication Administration (NPPA)**".
  - News apps need a CAC permit.
  - Generative-AI services offered to the public in China also need **CAC algorithm/large-model filing** under the Interim Measures for Generative AI Services, effective 15 August 2023. Apple has been withholding generative-AI apps without such approval (unverified today).
  - An individual or foreign developer realistically cannot get these.
- **What it means:** in App Store Connect → Pricing and Availability, **deselect "China mainland"**. If the learner's own Apple Account region is China mainland, they cannot download an app that is not offered there. Installing a TestFlight build in that case is **uncertain**. Any provider used for China-based users (for example a Chinese model) would bring the CAC filing duty with it.
