## 8. Step-by-step path for this learner (with costs)
| Step | What to do | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | About This Mac → model year (2017 / 2018–19 / 16" 2019 or 13" 2020 four-port) | $0 |
| 1 | Enrol in the **Apple Developer Program as an individual** at developer.apple.com (Apple Account with 2-factor login) | **$99/year** |
| 2 | In App Store Connect (web browser, works from Ventura): create the bundle ID (e.g. `com.<name>.dreambook`), the app record (**iPad only** at first), and an **App Store Connect API key** for the cloud builder | $0 |
| 3 | Pick the cloud builder to match the code: **Capacitor** (reuses the existing React renderer) → GitHub Actions (free, public repo) or Codemagic (500 free min a month). **Expo/React Native** → EAS (15 free iOS builds a month, then $2 each) | $0 normally; up to $19/month if more is needed |
| 4 | Cloud build → upload → **TestFlight** → install the TestFlight app on the iPad as an **internal tester** (no review). Rebuild before the 90 days end | $0 |
| 5 | Optional, only if the Mac is 2018 or newer: upgrade to Sequoia 15.6+ (Xcode 26.3) or Tahoe 26.2+ (Xcode 26.6) for local debugging on the iPad. Back up first; Xcode needs 40 GB or more of free disk (unverified figure) | $0 |
| 6 | Before review: privacy policy URL, support URL, App Privacy labels, age-rating questions, AI consent screen, in-app account deletion, mic string, background audio, iPad 13" screenshots, Review Notes with a test API key, export-compliance answer, **China mainland unticked** | $0 (a test key with about a $5 limit) |
| 7 | Submit for review in App Store Connect | $0 |
| 8 | **Spring 2027:** Intel Macs cannot run Xcode 27. Cloud builds carry on. Buy an Apple-silicon Mac only if daily Xcode use becomes necessary (MacBook Neo from $699) | $0 to $699+ |

**Year-one total:** about **$99** (membership), plus $0–$60 in builds, plus your own AI usage. A new Mac is optional, not required.

### Recommendation

**Do not buy a Mac now. Pay $99 for the Apple Developer Program and build Dream Book in the cloud. Test it on your own iPad through TestFlight. Publish outside mainland China first.**

Why:
1. **Your Mac cannot submit as it is.** Ventura tops out at Xcode 15.2, but uploads need Xcode 26+ and the iPadOS 26 SDK since 28 April 2026. Upgrading a 2018–2020 MacBook Pro to Sequoia 15.6+ or Tahoe 26.2+ gives Xcode 26.3 or 26.6. But Xcode 27 runs **only on Apple silicon**, so an Intel Mac will probably lose the ability to submit at the next yearly step (about April 2027). Cloud Macs do not have this problem.
2. **The cloud is cheap.**
   - GitHub Actions macOS runners are **free** for your public repo.
   - Codemagic gives 500 free M2 minutes a month.
   - Expo EAS gives 15 free iOS builds a month, then $2 per build.

   Pick by code type. If Dream Book wraps the existing React renderer with **Capacitor**, use GitHub Actions or Codemagic. If it is rebuilt in **Expo/React Native**, use EAS with EAS Submit (simplest for a non-developer).
3. **TestFlight replaces the 7-day free sideloading.** Internal testing needs no review and each build lasts 90 days. The free Apple ID route also cannot use Sign in with Apple, CloudKit or In-App Purchase, which the account and cloud features need.
4. **Optional:** if your MacBook Pro is 2018 or newer, upgrade macOS (free, Dream Read still runs) and install Xcode 26 for local debugging. A 2017 model should use the cloud only.
5. **App Store rules for the first release:**
   - Keep **bring-your-own API key**, stored in the Keychain, and put a low-limit test key in the Review Notes.
   - Show a **consent screen before sending book text to Anthropic/OpenAI** (5.1.2(i)).
   - Make the app usable **without an account**.
   - Use **Sign in with Apple + email** (no Google, so 4.8 is simple), and add **in-app account deletion** (5.1.1(v)).
   - Ask for the **microphone only in Active mode**; hands-free mode never asks.
   - Declare **background audio**.
   - Add enough native features to pass 4.2.
   - Add In-App Purchase subscriptions (15% small-business rate, plus your own AI proxy server) only later, if the app starts paying for AI.
6. **China:** untick China mainland. Anthropic does not serve mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau. China's App Store needs an ICP filing, an NPPA publishing permit for book-content apps, and CAC generative-AI filing, none of which an individual can easily get. If you live in mainland China, the Claude API is not available to you, and I do not recommend workarounds.

**Expected year-one cost:** about $99 plus $0–60 for builds, plus your own AI usage. Buy an Apple-silicon Mac (MacBook Neo from $699) only if everyday Xcode work becomes necessary after spring 2027.

## R3. The automatic whole-book engine and sleep mode


### Summary

I could not run any web searches for this report. The search tool said its limit was already used up by other agents in this run. Instead I read the official pages directly: Anthropic pricing and batch docs, OpenAI and DeepSeek pricing, Apple's developer docs and support pages, the FSRS project, and two sleep-learning papers plus one review. Treat any figure marked "uncertain" as unchecked.

When you add a book, Dream Book first reads the whole book once with a cheap AI model. It writes a short guide to the story, splits it into chapters and sentences, and lists every word, phrase and sentence above your level. Then it decides where explanations go. With Claude Haiku 5.5 and Anthropic's 50%-cheaper batch service, this reading costs about 5–10 US cents for a 100,000-word novel. Writing the explanations themselves costs about $0.10–0.50 per book with Haiku 5.5, or about $2–9 with the better Claude Sonnet 5.5. Most of the cost is the explanation text the AI writes, not the book text it reads.

Explanations and all their audio are made ahead, a few chapters at a time, by a free voice that runs on the iPad. They are saved on the iPad, about 15–30 MB per hour of audio, so a whole night plays offline with no waiting.

The app learns which words you know without you speaking. It uses the first quick test, optional button taps (for example on AirPods), words you rewind, and your review answers, and old evidence slowly counts less.

Sleep mode never asks questions and never waits. It gives no explanations or only tiny ones, uses a slower and quieter voice, and has a timer with a soft fade. It also guesses when you fell asleep. In the morning it offers to start again from that sentence and shows the words you heard while you were still awake.

Science says you cannot really learn new words while asleep. But quietly replaying words you learned that day during deep sleep helped in lab studies, so a "night replay" could be added later as an experiment you can switch off.

Active mode keeps your exact 5-second command rules.

Apple's free on-device AI on iPad works offline. Its memory is small (4,096 tokens), so it is good for short jobs, not whole books. It does not work on iPads bought in mainland China, and the Claude and OpenAI APIs do not serve mainland China or Hong Kong.

## 2. Whole-book analysis (runs when a book is added)

### 2.1 Pipeline

```
Import (local, free) -> Stage 0 Book read (1 AI call) -> Stage A Chapter analysis (1 call per ~18k chars)
  -> Stage B Plan (local, free) -> Stage C Explanation text (batch) -> Stage D Audio (on-device Kokoro)
```

- **Stage 0, Book Map.** One call reads the whole book and writes a story guide: characters (name, role, relationships, first chapter), places, a timeline of 3–5 easy sentences per chapter, genre and domain (this feeds the existing domain-aware context rules), narrator voice, and the 10 plot-key words of the book.
  - The whole book is about 175k tokens. On **Claude Haiku 5.5**, any prompt over 100,000 tokens costs 5 times as much ($0.50/$2.50 per million tokens). Stage 0 still costs only about $0.11 standard or $0.06 with batch.
  - On Sonnet 5.5 (1M context, flat price) it costs about $0.45, or $0.23 with batch.
  - The guide (8–10k tokens) then becomes the **cached prefix** of every later call.
- **Stage A, Chapter analysis.** One call per chunk of the existing 18,000-character size, built on `buildPhrasesPrompt`. Every chunk prompt stays well under 100k tokens, so Haiku keeps its low price. It returns:
  - the phrases, as today;
  - the hard sentences (section 2.2);
  - a chapter summary and newly introduced characters.
  Use **structured outputs** (`output_config.format` with a JSON schema) instead of the current tolerant JSON parsing.
- **Stage B, Plan.** Local and deterministic (section 2.3).
- **Stage C, Explanation text** (section 3).
- **Stage D, Audio** (section 3).

### 2.2 Finding items above the learner's level

- **Words:** `annotateSentence` hard tokens, minus names, minus words already marked known or ignored. That is the current behaviour.
- **Phrases:** the AI phrase finder plus the dictionary phrases (existing).
- **Sentences (new):** a sentence becomes an item when its difficulty score passes a threshold.
  - Formula: `sentDiff = 0.35*min(1, words/40) + 0.35*min(1, hardTokensInSentence/3) + 0.30*(aiDifficulty/5)`, where `aiDifficulty` is 0–5 from Stage A (0 if Stage A did not flag the sentence).
  - Starting threshold: **0.55**, to be tuned on real books.
  - Stage A flags sentences a listener at the learner's level would misunderstand **even knowing every word**: inverted or long structure, irony, ellipsis, unclear "he/it", cultural reference, figurative language.
- **Rough size for one B2 learner and a 100k-word adult novel (uncertain, varies 2–3x by book):** about 2,000 unique hard words, about 800 phrases, about 300 hard sentences, so **about 3,100 items**.
  - Under RULES.md section 1 ("pause at every …") that is roughly **one pause every 30–50 words**.
  - The app should compute the exact count at import (free, local) and show it, for example: "This book has 2,140 items above your level, one pause every 47 words at your settings."

### 2.3 Planning where explanations go

```ts
// proposed src/core/plan/planBook.ts (pure TS, like the rest of src/core)
for each candidate c:
  c.pKnown = learner.pKnown(c)                      // section 4
  c.value  = (1 - c.pKnown) * usefulness(c)
usefulness(c) = freqW(rank) * (1 + 0.25*ln(1+countInBook)) * (plotKey ? 1.3 : 1)
              * levelW(c.level - learnerLevel) * kindW(c.kind)
  freqW: COCA rank 2k–10k -> 1.0, 10k–20k -> 0.6, >20k -> 0.3, <2k -> 0.8
  levelW: +1 level -> 1.0, +2 -> 0.8, C2/off-list -> 0.6;  kindW: word 1.0, phrase 1.1, sentence 1.2
Pass 1 (in-book spacing): first meeting = 'full'; later meetings only if pKnown < tau and the gap
        >= 2,000 / 8,000 / 30,000 words -> 'micro' reminder; at most 3 reminders; never within 500 words (RULES).
Pass 2 (overlap): a sentence item (RULE TWO) suppresses word/phrase items inside it except the single highest-value one.
Pass 3 (mode decisions, greedy by value inside a sliding window):
  active:     every item with pKnown < 0.5 (RULES.md: no cap unless the learner agrees to one)
  hands-free: pKnown < 0.4, at most 1 pause per ~300 words (~2 min of audio)
  sleep:      pKnown < 0.15 and top value, 'micro' only, at most 1 per ~5 min, none in the last 15 min of the timer
```

Changing the Active-mode density is a rule change. RULES.md wins, so the learner must agree first.

### 2.4 Prompt for the chapter analysis call (system text; the user text sends numbered sentences like `[12] …`)

> You analyse one chapter of an English book for a native Chinese speaker at CEFR {{level}} who will LISTEN to it, not read it. The book guide above tells you who is who. Return only the JSON object the schema asks for. "phrases": expressions of 2 to 5 words that literally appear in the text — idioms, phrasal verbs, fixed expressions, slang — that a {{level}} listener would not understand from the single words; copy "text" exactly; give "lemma", a CEFR "level" and a 2–6 character Chinese meaning as used here. "hardSentences": the numbers of sentences a {{level}} listener would probably misunderstand even if they knew every word, each with "reason" (structure, irony, reference, figurative, idiom-dense, dialect) and "difficulty" 1–5; at most 15. "summary": 3 to 5 very easy English sentences saying what happens and who is there. "newCharacters": people who appear for the first time, with one easy sentence each. Never invent text that is not in the chapter.

**Claude Batch API** (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing):
- 50% off input and output; the discount stacks with caching.
- At most 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch.

### 2.6 Cost for one 100,000-word novel (estimate; script in the scratchpad)

**Token assumptions**
- About 1.35 tokens per word on older tokenizers. Haiku 5.5's newer tokenizer counts about 30% more, so the book is about **175k tokens**. Check the real figure with `count_tokens`.
- 33 chunks for Stage A; 2,000 hint words.
- Each explanation has a cached prefix of 2.5k tokens (rules, style, book guide), 1.3k fresh context tokens (the existing 500 words before and 200 after), and an average of 300 output tokens.

| Stage | Tokens | Haiku 5.5 std / batch | Sonnet 5.5 std / batch | Opus 5.5 std / batch | gpt-6-luna std / batch | gpt-5.4-mini std / batch | DeepSeek flash (peak) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Book read (one 175k call + 10k out) | 0.18M in / 0.01M out | $0.11 / $0.06 | $0.45 / $0.23 | $0.90 / $0.45 | $0.02 / $0.01 | $0.18 / $0.09 | $0.06 |
| A Chapter analysis + Chinese hints | 0.27M in / 0.10M out | $0.08 / $0.04 | $1.54 / $0.77 | $3.07 / $1.54 | $0.08 / $0.04 | $0.65 / $0.33 | $0.20 |
| C Full explanations, every item (3,100) | 4.0M fresh, 7.75M cached, 0.93M out | $0.96 / $0.48 | $18.46 / $9.23 | $36.93 / $18.46 | $0.96 / $0.48 | $7.85 / $3.93 | $2.40 |
| C Planned items (700) | 0.91M fresh, 1.75M cached, 0.21M out | $0.23 / $0.12 | $4.42 / $2.21 | $8.85 / $4.42 | $0.22 / $0.11 | $1.82 / $0.91 | $0.56 |
| C Short explanations (700 × 120 tokens) | 0.08M out | $0.17 / $0.08 | $3.17 / $1.58 | $6.33 / $3.17 | $0.16 / $0.08 | $1.25 / $0.63 | $0.41 |

**What drives the cost**
- **Output tokens are 50–75% of the cost.** The two real levers are how many items get a full explanation, and how long each explanation is.
- Caching each chapter's text as the prefix lowers Sonnet's full-book cost only from about $18.5 to about $14.4 standard, because output dominates.
- An extra "I don't know" (deeper) explanation done live costs about $0.008 on Sonnet 5.5 and about $0.0004 on Haiku 5.5.
- Thinking tokens are billed as output:
  - Haiku 5.5: thinking is on by default. Send `thinking:{type:"disabled"}`, which is allowed at effort high or lower.
  - Sonnet 5.5: send `thinking:{type:"between_tools"}`.
  - Opus 5.5 cannot switch thinking off; use `effort:"low"`.
- The current `server-side-fallback` beta in `src/main/ai.ts` is **rejected by the Batches API**. In batches, retry refusals one by one.

### 2.7 On-device: the Apple Foundation Models framework

**What Apple's documentation says**
- **Platforms:** iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 26.0+. On-device model versions so far: 26.0–26.3, 26.4 and 27.0. Each OS update changes the model, so prompts must be retested. (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel)
- **Model:** about **3B parameters**, compressed with 2-bit quantization-aware training (2 bits per weight), embeddings at 4 bits, key-value cache at 8 bits. Apple: "not designed to be a chatbot for general world knowledge". It is good at summarising, extraction, rewriting, short dialogue and tool calling. (https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/apple-foundation-models-2025-updates)
- **Context window:** **4,096 tokens per session**, counting the instructions, prompts, tool schemas and all outputs. English is about 3–4 characters per token; Chinese is about 1 character per token. On overflow it throws `contextSizeExceeded`. (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/managing-the-context-window)
- **Developer features:** guided generation with `@Generable`, tool calling, `tokenCount(for:)` and `contextSize`.
- **New in iPadOS 27 (June 2026):**
  - an improved on-device model;
  - a `LanguageModel` protocol, so any server or on-device model can be plugged in;
  - `MLXLanguageModel` and `CoreAILanguageModel` for open models running on the device.
  (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/updates/foundationmodels)
- **Private Cloud Compute (PCC) model, iOS/iPadOS 27+:**
  - **32K-token context** and reasoning levels light / moderate / deep;
  - needs a network connection;
  - a **daily request limit per person** (more with iCloud+);
  - developers must request a managed entitlement and meet eligibility requirements;
  - the exact quota is not published **(uncertain)**.
  (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/adding-server-side-intelligence-with-private-cloud-compute)
- **Which devices and languages:** iPad with M1 or later, or iPad mini (A17 Pro). Needs up to 8 GB of storage (up to 14 GB on M4 iPads with 12 GB of memory). The device language and Siri language must be the same supported language; supported languages include English and Chinese (Simplified).
- **Mainland China:** "Apple Intelligence features will not currently work for supported devices purchased in China mainland", nor in mainland China with a China-mainland Apple Account. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115)

**What it can do for Dream Book** (free, offline, unlimited)
- Sleep-mode micro-glosses.
- RULE THREE easy-English retelling of one sentence.
- Chinese meaning in context for a single word.
- Morning recap built from stored summaries.
- A short offline fallback explanation.
- Classifying a passage of about 1,500 words for hard sentences.

**What it cannot do:** read a whole chapter or book (4K context), or write long, rich explanations in the learner's own style. Keep those in the cloud. With PCC (32K context), a whole chapter fits.

### 2.8 Regions

- The Claude API's supported-regions list has **no mainland China and no Hong Kong**: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/supported-regions
- OpenAI's list has Taiwan only: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/supported-countries.md
- Apple Intelligence is blocked as described above.
- So keep the AI provider replaceable. DeepSeek serves China and offers an Anthropic-format URL, `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`. China nights (22:00–06:00 Beijing time, which is 14:00–22:00 UTC) fall in DeepSeek's half-price off-peak hours.
- On iPadOS 27, `MLXLanguageModel` could run an open model on the device for the same jobs **(uncertain quality)**.

---

## 3. Pre-generation, storage and budget

**Rolling plan**
- At import: Stage 0 and Stage A. Chapter 1 is done synchronously so playback can start within minutes; the rest goes into one batch.
- Explanation text: always the current chapter plus 2 ahead (in a batch). A button "Prepare whole book for offline" first shows the cost from section 2.6.
- Audio: always keep **≥ 2 h** rendered ahead.
- Before Sleep mode starts, check that `timer + 30 min` of audio is ready. If not, render it now with a progress bar, or fall back to the system voice.

**iPad mechanics**
- Background audio mode (`audio`) keeps playback and rendering going all night.
- `BGProcessingTaskRequest` (iPadOS 13+) can render at night while charging.
- `BGContinuedProcessingTask` (iPadOS 26+) runs a user-started "Prepare book" job with a progress Live Activity. The system can end it under resource pressure, and tasks that report no progress are ended first. (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/backgroundtasks/bgcontinuedprocessingtask)

**Voices on the iPad**
- **Kokoro, native:**
  - KokoroSwift (MLX Swift, iOS 18+): "~3.3 times faster than real-time … on iPhone 13 Pro"; per-token timestamps since version 1.0.8. (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios/main/README.md)
  - FluidAudio (Core ML, Kokoro 82M, used by the "Local Narrator" iOS audiobook app). (https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio)
  - At 3.3x real time, 1 h of audio takes about 18 min to render. iPad M-series speed was not measured **(uncertain)**.
- **System voices:** `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write(_:toBufferCallback:)` (iPadOS 13+) renders system voices, including the Chinese voice, into buffers you can save. That fits the rule that Chinese must be spoken by a Chinese voice. (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avspeechsynthesizer/write(_:tobuffercallback:))
- **Cloud voice, for comparison:** OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` costs $0.60 per 1M text tokens plus $12 per 1M audio tokens. At the repo's earlier estimate of about $0.015 per minute, that is about $0.90 per hour, or about $14 per book.

**Storage** (Kokoro outputs 24 kHz mono; a book is about 10.8 h of narration at about 155 words per minute)

| Format | MB per hour | 8-hour night | Book + 700 short explanations (~15 h) |
|---|---|---|---|
| WAV, 16-bit PCM | 172.8 | 1.38 GB | 2.6 GB |
| AAC-LC 64 kbps (recommended) | 28.8 | 230 MB | 430 MB |
| AAC 48 kbps | 21.6 | 173 MB | 324 MB |
| HE-AAC 32 kbps | 14.4 | 115 MB | 216 MB |
| Opus 24 kbps (Opus encoding on iOS is uncertain) | 10.8 | 86 MB | 162 MB |

**Listening time**
- 3,100 full explanations would add about **57 h** of audio, more than five times the book.
- 700 full ones add about 12.8 h; 700 short ones (60 words) add about 4.5 h.
- This is another reason for planning and length tiers: **micro** (≤12 words plus 1 Chinese meaning), **short** (40–60 words), **full** (the learner's RULE ONE / RULE TWO).

**Caching and data**
- Audio files are a regenerable cache (least-recently-used eviction; "keep audio for the current book / the last 3 books").
- Explanation text is user data (about 1 KB per item) and syncs to the cloud.
- An explanation's key is `(itemId, styleId, styleVersion, levelBand, lengthTier)`. Changing the style creates new keys; nothing is overwritten.

**Budget controls**
- A cost estimate per book before Stage C.
- A per-book cap (default $0.50 on Haiku).
- The existing daily warning and monthly cap.
- At 80% of the monthly budget, switch automatically to Haiku or the on-device model.
- Sliders for "pauses per 10 minutes" and "explanation length".
- A model choice per stage.
- A **free mode**: dictionary + local plan + Apple on-device model + Kokoro, $0.

## 4. Automatic level: knowing which words are known without speaking

**Model:** per-word log-odds on top of the existing Beta band model.

- Prior: `p0(w) = α_b/(α_b+β_b)` for the frequency band `b` of word `w`, taken from `LevelModel.bands()`.
- `L(w) = logit(p0(w)) − 0.5·max(0, levelIdx(w) − learnerLevelIdx) + Σ_i s_i·wt_i·0.98^(weeks since event i)`
- `pKnown(w) = σ(L(w))`
- Evidence counts for 98% as much after one week, which is the same decay already in `adapt.ts`.

| Evidence (none of it needs speaking) | Sign × weight (log-odds) | Also feeds the band model (`observe`, weight) |
|---|---|---|
| Level test "yes" / "no" (pseudoword-corrected) | +2.0 / −2.0 | via `fromTest` |
| "I know" (voice, button, double tap, AirPods next-track press) | +3.0, and marks known | 0.5 |
| "I don't know", single tap, AirPods previous-track press | −3.0 | 0.5 |
| Active mode: silence, then the AI explained | −0.7 | 0.15 |
| "Go on" (saved as learning, per RULES) | −0.3 | 0 |
| "Explain last 20/30/40 s", or rewinding over the item | −0.5 for each hard item in that span | 0.15 |
| Review or morning card: correct / wrong | +1.5 / −1.5 (FSRS grade) | 0.5 |
| Met while awake in hands-free mode (incidental) | +0.15 per meeting, at most +1.5 | 0 |
| Met while probably asleep | 0 | 0 |

**Decisions**
- Explain if `pKnown < τ`: 0.5 in Active, 0.4 in Hands-free, 0.15 in Sleep.
- Mark known automatically only when `p ≥ 0.95` **and** there are ≥2 positive strong events (or a review passed at an interval of ≥21 days). Silence alone never makes a word known.
- **Optional taps:** the morning card asks about 5 words whose `|p − 0.5| < 0.15` and whose value is highest, which gives the most information per tap. Skipping is always fine.

**Change to existing code:** let `LevelModel.observe(word, knows, dict, at, weight)` take a weight, and allow repeated observations with a per-word cap. Today it counts each word only once.

The research doc's Elo alternative (`θ += K(y − σ(θ − d))`, K = 0.1) remains a fallback.

**Note on incidental learning (uncertain, from memory, not re-checked):** studies suggest roughly 8–12 meaningful meetings are needed for incidental vocabulary gains. That is why exposure counts only a little.

---

## 5. Sleep mode

| | Active | Hands-free | Sleep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Microphone | 5-second windows only (plus the talk button) | off | off |
| Pauses | every item above level (RULES) | planned, capped | none, or a micro-gloss after the sentence ends |
| Explanation | full style; deeper on "I don't know" | pre-generated short or full, plays automatically | micro (word, short meaning, 1 Chinese meaning in a Chinese voice) or easy-English retelling (RULE THREE), or nothing |
| Waiting windows | 5 s + 5 s | none | none |
| Word said 3 times | yes | yes (option: once) | no |
| Questions or quiz | allowed | no | never |
| Voice | chosen voice, 1.0× | same | calmer voice, 0.85–0.9×, −6 dB, 600 ms between sentences (now 250 ms) |
| Word status | from commands | "learning (auto)" | exposure only |
| Screen | full | dim | black; locking allowed |

**Timer:** 15, 30, 45, 60 or 90 minutes, or end of chapter.
- Explanations stop in the last third of the timer.
- Then a 60 s fade: about −1 dB every 2 s down to −40 dB, then pause. A volume ramp in 50 ms steps on the player or mixer node.
- Audiobook apps commonly offer an adjustable sleep timer (for example BookPlayer: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TortugaPower/BookPlayer/main/README.md).

**Sleep-onset estimator** (every 30 s; a night log stores `{t, sentenceKey}` at the start of every sentence)

```
idle = now - max(lastInteraction, sleepModeStart)
pAsleep = sigmoid((idle - L)/4 min), where L = this learner's median onset time (default 15 min)
if headphone motion is available (CMHeadphoneMotionManager, iPadOS 14+, needs NSMotionUsageDescription):
    head still > 5 min -> +0.25; big movement -> pAsleep = 0 and treat as an interaction
if a system/remote pause arrives with no touch (AirPods sleep auto-pause, if present) -> 0.95
touch or screen-on -> 0
pAsleep > 0.8 three times in a row -> asleepAt = the first time it crossed 0.5
    -> finish the paragraph, fade, pause
    -> resume point = the paragraph start about 60 s before asleepAt
morning (optional): HealthKit sleep samples (Apple Watch) refine asleepAt
```

Uncertain parts of the estimator:
- Whether head-motion updates arrive while the app is in the background.
- The iPadOS 26 AirPods "pause when falling asleep" feature, and whether apps can see it.
- Whether Health data from the iPhone or Watch syncs to the iPad.

**Default:** stop the story when the learner falls asleep, so no story is lost. Option: keep playing to the end of the timer, but still resume from the sleep point.

**Morning recap** (≤2 minutes, easy English, no questions):
- "Last night you listened 38 minutes, chapters 7 to 8. You fell asleep near: '…'."
- The story so far, from chapter summaries up to the sleep point.
- The words explained **while awake**. Only these count as exposures.
- An optional 5-word card.
- Buttons: Resume from sleep point / Resume where it stopped.

The recap prompt: system "Write ≤120 words of calm, very easy spoken English. No questions. No labels." plus the summaries, the awake items and the resume sentence. It can run on the device.

**Science of sleep listening (checked via Europe PMC):**
- Schreiner & Rasch 2015 (Cerebral Cortex, PMID 24962994): replaying already-learned Dutch words during NREM sleep improved later recall of their German translations; cueing while awake did not.
- Hu et al. 2020 meta-analysis (Psychological Bulletin, PMID 32027149): 91 experiments, N = 2,004. Targeted memory reactivation overall g = 0.29; NREM2 g = 0.32; slow-wave sleep g = 0.27; **not effective in REM or wake**.
- Züst et al. 2019 (Current Biology, PMID 30713104): new word pairs heard at slow-wave peaks formed only *implicit* associations.

So: no real new learning while asleep. A **"night replay" experiment, off by default** could work like this:
- Starts 30 min after the sleep point, during the first 2–3 h of the night.
- Plays today's learned words (the English word only) quietly, about 20 dB under the story volume, one every 6–10 s.
- Blocks of 10 min on and 10 min off, at most 60 min.
- Stops on any movement.
- Caveat: home use without EEG cannot target NREM and may disturb sleep.
- A **bedtime review** (3–5 min of today's words before the story) is the safer, evidence-friendly default.

## 6. Active mode (binding rules, RULES.md section 1)

1. Pause at every word, phrase (2–5 words), slang or short sentence above the level, and at every "learning" word; never twice for the same word within 500 words.
2. The card appears under the word, and the word is said 3 times.
3. A 5-second commands-only window; nothing said is sent to the AI.
   - "I know", K or the button: known for good, no explanation.
   - "Go on", "bye bye", "continue", "next", Esc or the button: no explanation, saved as learning.
   - "I don't know", D or the button: explanation now.
   - Silence or anything else: explanation when the 5 s end.
4. After the explanation, a second 5 s window: "I don't know" gives a deeper explanation (then this window again); "I know" marks known; "go on" or silence keeps the word as learning.
5. Resume from the **start** of the interrupted sentence.

How pre-generation fits in:
- The word audio (said 3 times) and the full explanation are already rendered, so the explanation starts at once.
- "Deeper" is generated live (streamed), or pre-generated only for high-value items where `pKnown < 0.2`.
- Chinese parts are always rendered with a Chinese voice.
- Every command is logged as evidence (section 4).

---

## 7. Review: spaced repetition and the spoken review class

**Algorithm:** replace the fixed 1/3/7/14/30-day schedule with **FSRS**.
- `ts-fsrs` latest stable is **5.4.2** (published 2026-09-01). `6.0.0-beta.15` defaults to FSRS-7. (https://registry.npmjs.org/ts-fsrs; README: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-spaced-repetition/ts-fsrs/main/README.md)
- FSRS-6 uses 21 parameters and a trainable forgetting curve `R(t,S) = (1 + factor·t/S)^(−w20)`, with `factor = 0.9^(−1/w20) − 1`. (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/open-spaced-repetition/awesome-fsrs/The-Algorithm.md)
- Which FSRS version ts-fsrs 5.x runs by default: **check before use**.
- Desired retention 0.90 by default (0.85 for a "lighter" setting).
- An older alternative is Duolingo's half-life regression, Settles & Meeder, ACL 2016 (https://github.com/duolingo/halflife-regression).

**Grades**

| Event | FSRS grade |
|---|---|
| "I know" in review or the morning card, or at a pause on a learning word | Good |
| "I don't know" or a tap | Again |
| "Go on" | Hard |
| Explained hands-free or met asleep | no grade (exposure only; the due date stays) |
| Same-day repeat meetings | do not re-grade |

**Spoken class (works hands-free):**
- Each item takes about 25 s: the book sentence played from the narration audio (as in RULE ONE "play the complete sentence") → the word twice → 3 s of optional answer → micro explanation + Chinese (Chinese voice).
- Then the existing context review (`groupByChapter`).
- Size: due items + session items, at most 20 (about 8–10 min).
- A Bedtime review (3–5 items) runs before Sleep mode.

## 8. Data structures (TS, platform-neutral; syncable)

```ts
interface BookPlan { bookId: string; planVersion: number; levelAtPlan: CefrLevel; createdAt: string;
  map: { summary: string; characters: { name: string; who: string; firstChapter: number }[];
         chapterSummaries: string[]; domain: string; plotKeyLemmas: string[] };
  chapters: { index: number; stage: 'pending'|'analysed'|'text'|'audio'; usd: number; tokens: { in: number; out: number } }[];
  items: PlannedItem[] }
interface PlannedItem { id: string /* `${sentenceKey}:${start}-${end}` */; kind: 'word'|'phrase'|'sentence';
  lemma: string; text: string; sentenceKey: string; span: [number, number]; level: CefrLevel; rank?: number;
  countInBook: number; meeting: number; pKnown: number; value: number;
  decision: { active: 'full'|'micro'|'none'; handsfree: 'full'|'short'|'micro'|'none'; sleep: 'micro'|'easy'|'none' };
  text?: { key: string; body: string; zh: [string, string]; model: string; usd: number };
  audio?: { file: string; ms: number; voice: string; words: { c: number; s: number; e: number }[] } }
interface WordKnowledge { lemma: string; logOdds: number; lastEvidenceAt: string; awakeMeetings: number;
  status: 'unknown'|'learning'|'known'|'ignored'; fsrs?: { s: number; d: number; due: string; reps: number; lapses: number; last: string } }
type LearnEvent = { t: string; type: 'test'|'know'|'dont_know'|'go_on'|'silence_explained'|'tap'|'rewind'|'review'|'heard';
  lemma?: string; sentenceKey?: string; mode: 'active'|'handsfree'|'sleep'; pAsleep?: number; grade?: 1|2|3|4 }
interface NightLog { bookId: string; start: string; timerMin: number; marks: { t: string; key: string; pAsleep: number }[];
  asleepAt?: string; resumeKey?: string; source: 'heuristic'|'health'|'timer' }
```

The append-only `LearnEvent` log is the record that syncs to the cloud. It merges cleanly across devices, and a reinstall rebuilds `WordKnowledge` by replaying it. Audio is never synced.

### Recommendation

## Recommended design: a hybrid "plan once, render ahead, play offline" engine

### 1. Use different models for different steps (today the app defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` for everything)

- **Stages 0 and A** (book guide, chapter analysis, Chinese hints): **Claude Haiku 5.5** through the Batch API with structured outputs. Turn thinking off (`thinking:{type:"disabled"}`). About **$0.05–0.10 per 100k-word novel**.
  - Keep each chunk prompt under 100k tokens, because Haiku costs 5 times as much above that.
  - Do chapter 1 synchronously so the book can start within minutes.
- **Explanations in "My Teacher" style:** offer the learner one choice:
  - Haiku 5.5 batch for every item: **≈ $0.50 per book**.
  - **Sonnet 5.5 batch** for about 700 planned items: **≈ $2.2 per book**. **This is the default I recommend** for quality.
  - "Deeper" explanations are generated live, at about $0.008 each.
- **Opus 5.5 only when the learner asks for it.** The batch API does not accept the current fallback beta, so retry refusals one by one.
- **Audio:** render everything on the iPad with native Kokoro (KokoroSwift or FluidAudio). Use the system Chinese voice for Chinese, through `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write`. Store AAC 64 kbps (about **29 MB per hour**). Keep ≥2 h rendered ahead, and check before Sleep mode that timer + 30 min is ready.
- **Apple Foundation Models** (on iPads with M1 or later; iPadOS 26/27): use it for free, offline small jobs: micro-glosses, easy-English retelling, morning recap, and an offline fallback. Its context is 4,096 tokens, so not for whole books.
- **Mainland China:** Claude and OpenAI do not serve mainland China or Hong Kong, and Apple Intelligence is blocked there. Keep the provider replaceable (DeepSeek has an Anthropic-format endpoint and half-price off-peak hours), and keep a fully free local mode.

### 2. Three modes on one planner

- **Active:** RULES.md exactly as written (5 s + 5 s windows; resume from the start of the sentence).
- **Hands-free:** no microphone; pre-generated explanations play automatically with a pause cap; optional AirPods presses work as "I know" / "I don't know".
- **Sleep:** no microphone, no waiting, micro-glosses only (or none); calmer voice at 0.85–0.9×; timer with a 60 s fade; the sleep-onset estimator; **the story stops when the learner falls asleep** so no story is lost; morning recap and resume point.
- Make "Night replay" an **off-by-default experiment**, because the evidence comes from lab studies of NREM cueing and only covers words already learned. Offer a bedtime review by default.

### 3. Learner model

- Per-word log-odds on top of the existing Beta band model, built from weighted, decaying evidence that never requires speaking (section 4 of the findings).
- Never mark a word known from silence alone.
- A 5-word morning card asks about the words the model is least sure of.
- Replace the fixed review schedule with **FSRS**: ts-fsrs 5.4.2 stable, desired retention 0.9.
- Store everything as an append-only event log that syncs to the account. Reinstalling rebuilds all state from it; audio is a cache that can be rendered again.

### 4. Build order (small steps, per the working agreement)

1. Book guide and chapter analysis, plus a screen that shows the item count and cost estimate.
2. Planner with per-mode decisions.
3. Weighted evidence log and per-word model.
4. Batch explanation generation with a budget cap.
5. Native Kokoro rendering ahead and AAC storage.
6. Sleep mode (timer, fade, estimator, morning recap).
7. FSRS review class.
8. Optional Apple Foundation Models / PCC and night replay.

### 5. Questions for the learner before building

- RULES.md says to pause at *every* item above the level. For a B2 learner that could be one pause every 30–50 words. May Active mode use a density cap?
- In Sleep mode, should the micro-gloss give one Chinese meaning or the two that RULES.md asks for?


### Fact-check of the key claims (an independent checker tried to disprove them)

- **confirmed**: Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens and $0.50 / $2.50 above that; cache reads are $0.01 and 1-hour cache writes $0.20. Claude Sonnet 5.5 costs $2 / $10 with $0.10 cache reads; Claude Opus 5.5 costs $4 / $20 with $0.20 cache reads.
  - Evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing has these rows. Haiku 5.5 up to 100K: $0.10 input, $0.125 for 5-minute cache writes, $0.20 for 1-hour cache writes, $0.01 cache reads, $0.50 output. Haiku 5.5 over 100K: $0.50, $0.625, $1, $0.05, $2.50. Sonnet 5.5: $2, $2.50, $4, $0.10, $10. Opus 5.5: $4, $5, $8, $0.20, $20. A footnote says cache hits on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 cost 0.05x the base input price.
- **confirmed**: The Claude Message Batches API gives 50% off input and output and stacks with prompt caching. A batch holds at most 100,000 requests or 256 MB; most finish within 1 hour, they expire after 24 hours, and results are kept for 29 days. Cache hits inside batches are best-effort, typically 30% to 98%.
  - Evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing says: "limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever is reached first"; "most batches completing within 1 hour"; "Batches expire if processing does not complete within 24 hours"; "Batch results are available for 29 days after creation"; "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices"; "The pricing discounts from prompt caching and Message Batches can stack ... cache hits are provided on a best-effort basis. Users typically experience cache hit rates ranging from 30% to 98%".
- **confirmed**: OpenAI gpt-6-luna costs $0.10 input / $0.01 cached input / $0.50 output per million tokens ($0.05 / $0.005 / $0.25 in batch). gpt-5.4-mini costs $0.75 / $0.075 / $4.50. gpt-4o-mini-tts costs $0.60 per 1M text tokens plus $12 per 1M audio tokens.
  - Evidence: WebFetch could not resolve platform.openai.com, so I read the official markdown copy at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.md. Standard table: "gpt-6-luna | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.125 | $0.50 | $0.20 | $0.02 | $0.25 | $0.75" and "gpt-5.4-mini | $0.75 | $0.075 | - | $4.50". Batch table: "gpt-6-luna | $0.05 | $0.005 | $0.0625 | $0.25 ...". Audio table: "gpt-4o-mini-tts | Audio | - | - | $12.00" and "gpt-4o-mini-tts | Text | $0.60".
- **corrected**: Apple's on-device Foundation Models model has about 3 billion parameters, is compressed to 2 bits per weight, and has a 4,096-token context window per session (counting instructions, prompts and outputs). On iOS/iPadOS 27 the Private Cloud Compute model offers a 32K-token context and reasoning levels, with a daily per-person request limit and a managed developer entitlement.
  - Correct / uncertain: Mostly right, but the parameter count and 2-bit figure come from Apple's 2025 report, and Apple released a new generation of models on June 8, 2026. On iOS/iPadOS 27 the on-device model is AFM 3 Core, which Apple calls "the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model", so about 3B still holds. The 2-bits-per-weight figure was published for the 2025 model, and Apple's AFM 3 page does not restate it, so it is unconfirmed for the current model. Apple also has a second on-device model, AFM 3 Core Advanced (20B sparse, 1 to 4B active), for its most capable chips. The docs do not say whether the Foundation Models framework uses it. Everything else checks out: 4,096 tokens per session, counting prompts, instructions, tool definitions and their input and output, schemas and responses. Private Cloud Compute gives a 32K context, three reasoning levels, a daily per-person request limit (more with iCloud+), and a managed entitlement developers must request. It is available on iOS 27 and later.
  - Evidence: I read the Apple developer docs as JSON (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/foundationmodels/...). managing-the-context-window says: "Apple's on-device foundation model has a context window of 4096 tokens per session ... This includes all prompts, instructions, tool definitions and their input and output, generable type schemas, and all of the model's responses." adding-server-side-intelligence-with-private-cloud-compute says: "larger 32K-token context size", "People just need a device that supports Apple Intelligence and gets a daily request limit", "request access to the managed entitlement", "three reasoning levels", and "available on iOS 27, macOS 27...". https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/apple-foundation-models-2025-updates says "compressed the on-device model to 2 bits per weight" and "~3B parameter". https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/introducing-third-generation-of-apple-foundation-models (June 8, 2026) says "AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model" and describes AFM 3 Core Advanced as "20-billion-parameter ... activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters". It does not mention 2-bit quantization.
- **confirmed**: Apple Intelligence (and therefore the Foundation Models framework) needs an iPad with M1 or later or an iPad mini (A17 Pro), supports Chinese (Simplified), and does not currently work on devices purchased in mainland China.
  - Evidence: WebFetch could not resolve the host, so I fetched https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115 with curl. It says: "Apple Intelligence in iOS 27, iPadOS 27 ... available on ... iPad mini (A17 Pro) ... iPad models with M1 or later". Languages include "Chinese (simplified), Chinese (traditional)". It also says: "Apple Intelligence features will not currently work for supported devices purchased in China mainland."
- **confirmed**: Mainland China and Hong Kong are not on the Claude API's supported-regions list; OpenAI's supported-countries list includes Taiwan but not mainland China or Hong Kong.
  - Evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/supported-regions.md has 181 lines. Searching for china, hong kong, macau and macao finds nothing; only "Taiwan" appears. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/supported-countries.md also has "Taiwan" and nothing for China, Hong Kong or Macau.
- **confirmed**: Replaying already-learned foreign words during NREM sleep improved later recall (Schreiner & Rasch 2015). A meta-analysis of 91 experiments found targeted memory reactivation effective in NREM sleep (overall g = 0.29) but not in REM sleep or while awake (Hu et al. 2020). New word pairs heard during deep sleep formed only implicit associations (Züst et al. 2019).
  - Evidence: From the Europe PMC REST API abstracts. PMID 24962994 (Cereb Cortex 2015, doi:10.1093/cercor/bhu139): "Re-exposure to Dutch words during sleep improved later memory ... verbal cueing failed to improve memory during active and passive waking." PMID 32027149 (Psychol Bull 2020, doi:10.1037/bul0000223): "91 experiments with 212 effect sizes (N = 2,004) ... overall sleep TMR was highly effective (Hedges' g = 0.29) ... NREM 2: g = 0.32; slow-wave sleep: g = 0.27 ... not effective during REM sleep nor during wakefulness." PMID 30713104 (Curr Biol 2019, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2018.12.038): pairs played during slow-wave sleep in a nap; associations formed when "coincided with an ongoing slow-wave peak" and "guided forced choices on an implicit memory test."
- **confirmed**: ts-fsrs latest stable is 5.4.2 (published 2026-09-01); version 6 (in beta) defaults to FSRS-7. FSRS-6 uses 21 parameters with a trainable forgetting-curve decay. KokoroSwift (iOS 18+) generates speech about 3.3 times faster than real time on an iPhone 13 Pro and gives per-token timestamps.
  - Evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/ts-fsrs lists dist-tags latest '5.4.2' (time 2026-09-01T02:23:24Z) and beta '6.0.0-beta.15'. The README in the 6.0.0-beta.15 tarball says: "DefaultScheduler() uses FSRS-7 when version is omitted." The awesome-fsrs wiki page The-Algorithm (raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/open-spaced-repetition/awesome-fsrs/The-Algorithm.md), FSRS-6 section, says: "This version uses 21 parameters" and "The forgetting curve's decay is trainable" (w20). The README at https://github.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios says: "~3.3 times faster than real-time on the release build on iPhone 13 Pro after warm up", "Added timestamps for each token" (new in 1.0.8), and "iOS 18.0+".


## R4. Seven teaching characters

See Part 5, which is this research track in full.

## R5. Voices on iPad: natural, word timing, all-night playback


### Summary

Dream Book can have a natural, free, offline voice on iPad. The best way is to make the audio before the learner goes to sleep, not while they sleep. The recommended voice is Kokoro-82M, the same "Dream voice" the Mac app already uses. It runs on iPads and iPhones at about 3 to 5 times real time, and paid App Store apps (KO Reader, Ghost Reader) already use it this way. The important iPad rule: when the screen is locked, apps may not use the graphics chip. So the fast Kokoro versions cannot make new audio at night. Apple's own voice can also stop when the screen locks (one developer report). Because of this, Dream Book should prepare the next few hours as small audio files with word timings: the book, the word repeats, and the explanations the AI already wrote. Then it plays these files all night, which is reliable and uses little battery. One hour of audio takes about 15–30 MB and about 3–18 minutes to make on a recent iPad, so do it while the iPad is charging. Apple's built-in voices (Premium or Enhanced, free) are the backup: they start instantly, can work with the screen off if the app turns them into audio itself, and give the Chinese voice for the short Chinese meanings. Paid cloud voices are optional extras that use the learner's own key: Azure ≈ $0.81 per hour, Google Chirp 3 HD ≈ $1.62, ElevenLabs ≈ $2.70–5.40, OpenAI ≈ $0.90. OpenAI and probably Anthropic cannot be used from mainland China; Azure has a China region. A lock-screen player, sleep timer with fade-out, and correct handling of phone calls and headphones are all standard iPad features, and the findings list exactly what to build.

### Detailed findings

## 0. Scope, method, limits

- I read the repo docs first: HOW-IT-WORKS, RULES, MY-TEACHING-STYLE, IPAD, KOKORO, VOICE and research/*. The advice reuses what already works on the Mac: Kokoro with word timings from the model's duration output, about 8 sentences prepared ahead, clause splitting at ≤150 characters, Chinese only ever spoken by a Chinese voice (`zhVoiceId` in `src/core/listen/controller.ts`), the `TtsEngine` interface with its `wordBoundaries` flag, `estimateWordTimes()` for engines without timings, and `CHARS_PER_HOUR = 54,000` for prices.
- I ran about 34 web searches, then hit the search budget. WebFetch could not reach any site (DNS blocked), so every fact comes from search-result extracts. Points marked **(not re-checked)** come from general platform knowledge and were not confirmed by a search in this session.
- Date context: 2026-10-20, iPadOS 26.x current.

---

## 1. The one rule that shapes everything: the iPad with the screen off

| Fact | Evidence | What it means for Dream Book |
|---|---|---|
| A backgrounded or locked app may not send work to the GPU. Metal fails with "Insufficient Permission (to submit GPU work from background)". Core ML can hit the same error. | [Apple forum 76818](https://forums.developer.apple.com/forums/thread/76818), [coreml-survival-guide #3](https://github.com/hollance/coreml-survival-guide/issues/3), [iOS 18 SoundAnalysis report](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/757715?page=2) | MLX (GPU) Kokoro cannot make new audio while the screen is locked. Core ML **CPU-only** worked in the background in one report ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/Mco7777/items/f07bd644c00f3eed38d8)). Whether the Neural Engine is allowed in the background is unverified. |
| iPadOS 26 adds `BGContinuedProcessingTask`. The user starts a long task, it keeps running in the background, and a Live Activity shows its progress. It can ask for background GPU (`.gpu` + the `com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu` entitlement), but only if `BGTaskScheduler.supportedResources` contains `.gpu`. One beta report had that always false on an iPhone 16 Pro. | [dev.to WWDC25 summary](https://dev.to/arshtechpro/wwdc-2025-ios-26-background-apis-explained-bgcontinuedprocessingtask-changes-everything-9b5), [Apple forum 807370](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/807370), [skill ref](https://playbooks.com/skills/charleswiltgen/axiom/axiom-background-processing-ref) | Good for a "Prepare this book / tonight" button that keeps rendering after the learner leaves the app. Treat GPU in the background as a bonus, not something to count on. |
| AVSpeechSynthesizer `speak()` reportedly **pauses when the screen locks** and resumes on unlock, even with the background audio mode on. No fix was posted. | [Apple forum 849627](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/849627) | Do not rely on live `speak()` all night. Render Apple voices to buffers with `write()` and play them through Dream Book's own audio engine. |
| App Review 2.5.4: the background "audio" mode is only for audible content. Apps that play silence to stay alive get rejected. One TTS reader app was rejected three times. | [Apple forum 826849](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/826849), [Zoom forum](https://devforum.zoom.us/t/ios-app-was-rejected-from-apple-appstore/37734) | Dream Book is a real audio app, so the mode is legitimate. But do not fill long AI waits with silent audio. Waits at night are avoided by preparing the audio ahead. |

**Conclusion:** the reliable all-night design is pre-rendered audio files plus a simple file player. Live synthesis is a daytime, screen-on feature.

---

## 2. Apple built-in voices (AVSpeechSynthesizer)

**Quality tiers.** Compact (robotic), Enhanced, and Premium (neural, best). The learner must download Enhanced and Premium voices in Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content (or "Read & Speak" in newer iOS) → Voices ([Logos support](https://support.logos.com/hc/en-us/articles/6024414864269-How-do-I-set-up-enhanced-voices-in-iOS)). `speechVoices()` lists only voices already downloaded, and there is no API to list or trigger downloads ([forum 748464](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/748464), [758460](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/758460)). The app must show a short "how to download a better voice" guide. Users mention British Premium Jamie and Serena and American Premium Zoe ([AppleVis](https://applevis.com/comment/139749)). **Siri voices are not available to apps.** If the user picks one, a fallback voice is used ([WWDC20 10022](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2020/10022/)).

**Word timing.**
- Live: `speechSynthesizer(_:willSpeakRangeOfSpeechString:utterance:)` fires before each word ([NSHipster](https://nshipster.com/avspeechsynthesizer)). iOS 17 added `speechSynthesizer(_:willSpeak marker:)` ([Apple docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avspeechsynthesizerdelegate/speechsynthesizer(_:willspeak:utterance:))). There are historic bugs with wrong ranges ([forum 133104](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/133104)).
- Rendering ahead: `write(_:toBufferCallback:)` (iOS 13+) gives `AVAudioPCMBuffer`s that you write to an `AVAudioFile` ([forum 122690](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/122690)). The iOS 17 variant `write(_:toBufferCallback:toMarkerCallback:)` returns `AVSpeechSynthesisMarker`s (word, sentence, paragraph, phoneme, bookmark), each with a `byteSampleOffset` into the audio ([AVSpeechSynthesisMarker](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avspeechsynthesismarker)). That would give exact word times in a rendered file. **But** one developer said the marker callback was never called ([forum 738048](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/738048)). **Test this on iPadOS 26.** If it fails, use `estimateWordTimes()` as the app already does.

**Known problems to design around.**
- iOS 17: buffer audio was choppy in betas, and long utterances stopped after about 300 words (FB13188396). The workaround is short utterances per sentence ([forum 737685](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/737685), [738048](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/738048)).
- iOS 26: `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language:)` ignores the user's chosen voice (FB20271264). **Always pick voices by `identifier`** ([forum 804648](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/804648)).
- "Mac (Designed for iPad)" goes silent with some voices ([forum 841198](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/841198)).
- Personal Voice needs `requestPersonalVoiceAuthorization`, and Apple says it is mainly for assistive (AAC) apps ([WWDC23 10033](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10033/)). It **cannot be used with the buffer callback** ([forum 736148](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/736148)), and iOS 26 betas garbled it ([forum 792409](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/792409)). Do not use it in Dream Book.

**Verdict.** Free, instant, offline, small. It is the right fallback and the right Chinese voice. Premium English is good, but less natural than Kokoro for hours of book listening.

Faster on Apple chips, but **not measured on iPad** | ~1–2 GB (estimate) | **Yes**, port `align.ts` to Swift | the Mac uses espeak-ng WASM (GPL-3.0) | **Yes (CPU)** |

Other facts:
- Real apps already ship this. **KO Reader** is fully local Kokoro: EPUB/PDF, export to m4a/m4b, $3.99, iPadOS 18.6+ ([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6761862109)). **Ghost Reader AI** offers 8 Kokoro voices, US/UK ([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/ghost-reader-ai/id6759826819)). So the approach is proven on iPad.
- Voices: British bf_emma (B-, the Mac default), bm_george, bf_isabella, bm_fable, bm_lewis. American af_heart (A, the best), af_bella (A-), am_michael (KOKORO.md). These are a natural voice for each of the 7 teaching characters.
- **Chinese in Kokoro:** the v1.0 voices zf_xiaobei and the others are graded **D** ([Replicate grade table](https://replicate.com/alphanumericuser/kokoro-82m/readme)). The separate **Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh** has 100 professional Chinese speakers and 100+ hours of data, with 55 zf_/45 zm_ voices in an MLX port ([PromptLayer](https://www.promptlayer.com/models/kokoro-82m-v11-zh), [1038lab MLX](https://huggingface.co/1038lab/Kokoro-82M-zh-MLX)). It is an option for later, but it is a second large model.
- **Licence risk (not re-checked):** espeak-ng is GPL-3.0, and GPL code in App Store apps is widely seen as a licensing conflict. FluidAudio's own docs flag eSpeak-NG as GPL-3.0. KokoroSwift's default MisakiSwift path avoids eSpeak. Get the exact licence checked before release.
- **Download:** about 190–330 MB of model. Hugging Face and GitHub can be slow or blocked from mainland China. Bundle the model in the app, or host it on a CDN that works in China. Apple-hosted Background Assets (WWDC25) is another option **(not re-checked)**.
- iPad RAM (for the 1.5–2 GB peak): base iPad A16 6 GB, iPad mini A17 Pro 8 GB, iPad Air M4 12 GB ([tbreak](https://tbreak.com/best-ipad-for-everyone-in-the-uae-2025-ipad-pro-air-mini/); 2026 base-iPad chip reports conflict, see [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/best-ipad-to-buy)). Keep segments ≤150 characters, as on the Mac, so 6 GB devices do not run out of memory.

## 6. Pre-rendering a chapter, a night or a whole book

**What to render.** In hands-free mode the AI has already read the book and written the explanations. So the whole listening programme is known ahead: book sentences, word ×3, explanation (RULE ONE/TWO in the learner's style), the two Chinese meanings in the Chinese voice, re-reading the interrupted sentence, the word ×10 and so on. Render each piece as a clip. In active mode, also pre-render the first explanation. Render the deeper "I don't know" explanation on demand.

**Storage per clip:** `.m4a` (AAC, mono, 24 kHz, made with `AVAudioFile` and AAC settings) plus a small JSON with `[charIndex, charLength, startSec, endSec]` per word (~0.3 MB per hour). Key the cache like the Mac does: hash(model version, voice, speed, text).

**Disk per hour** (size = kbps × 0.45 MB; [hydrogenaudio](https://hydrogenaud.io/index.php/topic,32153.0.html), [speedtesthq](https://speedtesthq.com/guides/streaming/audiobook-streaming-bandwidth)):

| Format | MB / hour | 8-hour night | 10-hour book |
|---|---|---|---|
| raw 16-bit PCM 24 kHz (what Kokoro outputs) | 173 | 1.4 GB | 1.7 GB |
| AAC 64 kbps mono | 28.8 | 230 MB | 288 MB |
| **AAC 48 kbps mono (suggested)** | 21.6 | 173 MB | 216 MB |
| AAC 32 kbps mono (iTunes audiobook level per forum) | 14.4 | 115 MB | 144 MB |

**Render time per hour of audio:** A15 KokoroSwift 3.3× ≈ **18 min**. iPhone 15 Pro Max Core ML 4.7× ≈ **13 min**. FluidAudio's 23× claim ≈ **2.6 min**. M-series iPad: no measurement found; expect somewhere in this range (**test it**). A 10-hour book takes about 0.5–3 hours, so render **while charging**.

**When rendering runs:**
1. In the foreground: a calm "Getting tonight ready… 63%" screen with `isIdleTimerDisabled` and a dark screen.
2. On iPadOS 26: `BGContinuedProcessingTask` from a "Prepare book" tap, which keeps going after the learner leaves.
3. With the screen locked: CPU-only work (Apple `write()`, an ONNX CPU Kokoro). GPU/MLX will not work.

Keep a rolling window: always the current chapter plus at least the sleep-timer length plus 30 minutes. Default "Prepare tonight" = the next 3 hours.

**Speed changes:** play pre-rendered 1.0× audio through `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` (changes speed without changing pitch; divide word times by the rate). If the learner changes their default speed, re-render in the background with Kokoro's own `speed` input, which sounds better than stretching at 0.5–0.7×.

---

## 7. Playback that lasts all night

**Audio session** (Info.plist `UIBackgroundModes = audio`):
- Hands-free / sleep mode: `.playback`, mode `.spokenAudio`, not mixable. Route-sharing policy `.longFormAudio` is Apple's policy for audiobooks and podcasts **(not re-checked)**.
- Active mode (5-second command windows): `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker` and `.allowBluetoothA2DP`. Note **(not re-checked):** while the microphone is open on AirPods, iOS uses the low-quality Bluetooth call profile. This is one more reason why the sleep mode should never open the mic.
- A non-mixable category plus at least one remote-command handler is what makes the lock-screen player appear ([Axiom now-playing guide](https://agentskills.so/skills/charleswiltgen-axiom-axiom-now-playing), [forum 690354](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/690354)).
- **Start playback in the foreground.** A background app can usually only start mixable audio ([forum 668820](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/668820), [forum 791865](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/791865)).

**Player:** one `AVAudioEngine`: `AVAudioPlayerNode` → `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` → mixer. Schedule clip segments back to back (`scheduleFile` / `scheduleSegment`) with no gaps, and keep about 2 clips queued.
- Use the node's `playerTime(forNodeTime:)` as the clock for word highlighting. The `scheduleBuffer` completion handler fires when the buffer is *scheduled*, or on stop, not when it has played ([Apple docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioplayernode/schedulebuffer(_:at:options:completioncallbacktype:completionhandler:))).
- Check `engine.isRunning` when the app returns to the foreground ([forum 132684](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/132684)).
- Handle `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` and `mediaServicesWereReset` by rebuilding the engine.

**Lock screen / Control Center:**
- `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter`: book title, chapter, cover, chapter duration, elapsed time, playback rate.
- `MPRemoteCommandCenter`: play, pause, togglePlayPause, skipBackward (= previous sentence or 15 s), skipForward, next/previousTrack (= chapter), changePlaybackPosition, changePlaybackRate. These map well to the Mac's Up/Down = previous/next sentence.

**Interruptions:**
- `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification`. On begin: pause and save the position. On end with `.shouldResume`: resume **from the start of the interrupted sentence** (RULES §1.5). Interruptions come from calls, FaceTime, Siri and alarms.
- `routeChangeNotification` with `.oldDeviceUnavailable` (headphones pulled out): pause.
- One forum thread says Now Playing setup changes interruption behaviour, so test it ([forum 668820](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/668820)).

**Sleep timer with fade-out:**
- Options: 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90 min, end of chapter, end of the current explanation.
- Fade the mixer volume over the last 30–60 s with a 20 Hz stepper, *then* stop. Calling `stop()` right after `setVolume(_:fadeDuration:)` cuts the sound off and skips the fade ([HWS forum](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/forums/macos/observing-avaudioplayer-volume-ramp-during-fade/3934), [MacRumors](https://forums.macrumors.com/threads/fading-in-and-out-volume.587750/)).
- Then deactivate the session with `.notifyOthersOnDeactivation`. Save a "you probably fell asleep here" bookmark at the start of the fade (or 5 minutes earlier) so the next session starts there.
- AirPods sleep detection in iOS 26 **(not re-checked)** sends a normal pause, which the remote-command handler already covers.

**Battery:** I found no measured figure. Playing compressed files with the screen off is the cheapest possible path. Neural rendering is the expensive part, which is why it happens while charging.

---

## 8. The Chinese voice for short Chinese meanings

- **Default:** Apple zh-CN voice chosen by identifier (Tingting or Lilian; Enhanced if downloaded), rendered with `write()` into a clip like the English. It is free, offline, and works in the background. Compact zh-CN voices are usually present **(check on the device)**. For simplified Chinese the mainland voice is correct, not Taiwan's Mei-Jia ([Pleco forum](https://www.plecoforums.com/threads/text-to-speech-chinese-language-ios-vs-english-ios.6365)).
- **Cloud upgrade:** Azure zh-CN neural voices, with the Azure China region for a mainland account.
- **Later:** Kokoro v1.1-zh voices. **Avoid** the Kokoro v1.0 zf_ voices (grade D).
- Keep the existing rule unchanged: if no Chinese voice exists, skip the Chinese rather than letting an English voice read it (`controller.ts` already does this).

---

## 9. How this maps onto the existing code

- Keep the `TtsEngine` contract (`speak`, `readAhead`, `wordBoundaries`, `probe`) and add one native method: `render(text, voice, speed) → {fileURL, words[]}`.
- Kokoro (KokoroSwift timestamps or ported `align.ts`), Azure and ElevenLabs set `wordBoundaries = true`. OpenAI, Chirp 3 HD and Apple without markers use `estimateWordTimes()`.
- `CHARS_PER_HOUR = 54,000` and `pricePerHour()` already give the per-hour prices in the table above.
- The playback loop (`playback.ts`, `stopAt`/`onStop`) becomes "play the next prepared clip". The controller's flow stays the same.

---

## 10. Must-test list on the learner's iPad (one or two days)

1. KokoroSwift: real-time factor, first-audio latency and peak memory for 20 sentences. Do word timestamps line up with the audio?
2. Lock the screen during file playback for 8 hours: any gaps? Battery % used?
3. Apple `write()` with `toMarkerCallback` on iPadOS 26: do markers arrive, and are the offsets right?
4. With the screen locked: does KokoroSwift fail as expected? Do Apple `write()` and ONNX-CPU Kokoro work, and how fast?
5. Interruptions: phone call, Siri, alarm, unplugging headphones, removing AirPods, end of the sleep-timer fade.
6. `BGContinuedProcessingTask`: does `.gpu` appear in `supportedResources` on this iPad?

**Build-tool note (not re-checked; belongs to the app-building topic):** current Xcode needs a much newer macOS than Ventura 13, and MLX cannot run in the iOS Simulator. Plan for building on a newer Mac or a cloud Mac, and testing on the real iPad.

### Recommendation

## Recommended: "prepare ahead, play files" with Kokoro as the default voice

**Default voice: Kokoro-82M on the iPad, rendered ahead into small audio files with word timings.**
- Voices: bf_emma (British), the same Dream voice as the Mac. Offer af_heart (American, the best Kokoro grade) and give each of the 7 teaching characters its own Kokoro voice.
- Why: it is free, offline and natural, with real word timings. It is proven on iPad by KO Reader and Ghost Reader, and it matches the Mac app, so the learner hears the same teacher everywhere.
- **Engine:** start with **KokoroSwift (MLX, Swift Package, iOS 18+)**. It already gives per-token (≈ per-word) timestamps and uses MisakiSwift instead of GPL eSpeak, and it is the easiest for an AI-assisted beginner.
- Put the engine behind one `render(text) → audio file + word times` interface, so it can be swapped later for:
  - FluidAudio Core ML Kokoro: faster on the Neural Engine, but uses GPL eSpeak and gives no word timings.
  - ONNX-Runtime CPU Kokoro, reusing the Mac's `duration` + `align.ts` pipeline: slower, but it can render with the screen locked.
- **How it plays all night:**
  - A "Prepare tonight" step (while charging; iPadOS 26 `BGContinuedProcessingTask` keeps it going) renders the next ≥3 hours. That covers the book plus the AI's pre-written explanations, word repeats and Chinese meanings.
  - Files are AAC 48 kbps mono: ≈22 MB per hour, ≈216 MB for a 10-hour book.
  - Sleep mode then only plays files: `.playback` session, background audio mode, AVAudioEngine with TimePitch for speed, lock-screen controls, interruption handling, and a sleep timer that fades over 30–60 s and bookmarks where the learner fell asleep.
  - Never open the microphone in sleep mode.

**Fallback 1: Apple built-in voices (free, always there).**
- Use Premium or Enhanced English voices chosen **by identifier** (iOS 26 bug). Render them with `write()` into the same player instead of using `speak()`, which reportedly pauses when the screen locks.
- Use them for:
  - the first minute before Kokoro catches up;
  - live answers while the screen is locked (GPU not allowed);
  - iPads with too little memory;
  - **all Chinese meanings** (zh-CN Tingting or Lilian).
- Show a one-screen guide for downloading Premium voices.

**Fallback 2: cloud voices with the learner's own key, also pre-rendered and cached.**
- **Azure Neural** is the best value: ≈$0.81 per hour, real word boundaries, very good Chinese, and a legal mainland-China region.
- **ElevenLabs** is the luxury option: $2.70–5.40 per hour, character timestamps.
- **Google Chirp 3 HD**: $1.62 per hour, ~18 free hours per month, timings estimated.
- **OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts**: ≈$0.90 per hour, steerable character styles, no timings, not usable from mainland China.
- Do not ship the free Edge voice (unofficial, being blocked).

**Do first:** a 1–2 day on-device test on the learner's iPad (the must-test list in §10 of the findings) before building the full app. It decides whether KokoroSwift alone is enough or whether the CPU ONNX path is needed for screen-locked synthesis.


### Fact-check of the key claims (an independent checker tried to disprove them)

- **confirmed**: KokoroSwift (MLX Swift port of Kokoro-82M, iOS 18+/macOS 15+) generates audio about 3.3x faster than real time on an iPhone 13 Pro after warm-up, and version 1.0.8 added per-token timestamps.
  - Evidence: https://github.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios README: 'iOS 18.0+', 'macOS 15.0+', '~3.3 times faster than real-time on the release build on iPhone 13 Pro' 'after warm up / first run', 'New in 1.0.8: Added timestamps for each token.' Tag dates come from https://github.com/mlalma/kokoro-ios/tags. swiftpackageregistry.com did not resolve from this environment.
- **corrected**: iOS apps cannot submit GPU (Metal) work while backgrounded or locked; Core ML can hit the same error, while a CPU-only Core ML configuration reportedly works in the background.
  - Correct / uncertain: This is the default behavior but no longer an absolute rule. Apple documents that iOS and tvOS block command buffers committed after an app moves to the background, failing them with MTLCommandBufferError.notPermitted, with a short grace period at deactivation. Since iOS/iPadOS 26, a user-started BGContinuedProcessingTask can use the GPU in the background on supported devices. It needs the Background GPU Access entitlement (com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu) and requiredResources = .gpu after checking supportedResources. That covers finite jobs, not continuous playback. The Core ML evidence is weak: in hollance/coreml-survival-guide issue #3 the owner says the background-GPU error 'was probably just a misleading error message' caused by a shape mismatch, and fixing the shapes 'also solved the GPU on the background error'. I could not verify the claim that CPU-only Core ML works in the background, because qiita.com did not resolve.
  - Evidence: Apple, Preparing your Metal app to run in the background (developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/preparing-your-metal-app-to-run-in-the-background): 'iOS and tvOS restrict a background app's access to the GPU... the system prevents those commands from executing.' https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/76818 has the error text 'Insufficient Permission (to submit GPU work from background) (IOAF code 6)'; the only reply is a 2017 community answer, with no Apple engineer. https://github.com/hollance/coreml-survival-guide/issues/3 says the error was caused by shapes. Apple's 'Performing long-running tasks on iOS and iPadOS' and the GPU entitlement page document the iOS 26 exception.
- **confirmed**: AVSpeechSynthesizer speech reportedly pauses mid-utterance when the device locks, even with background audio modes declared, and resumes on unlock (no confirmed fix posted).
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/849627: 'speech that has already started reliably pauses mid-utterance the moment the screen locks, and resumes and completes the moment the screen is unlocked'; 'The app has UIBackgroundModes: ['audio', 'location'] declared'; Replies 0.
- **uncertain**: Fully local Kokoro TTS reader apps already ship on the App Store for iPad (KO Reader: EPUB/PDF, export to m4a/m4b, $3.99, iPadOS 18.6+).
  - Correct / uncertain: Could not verify. apps.apple.com and itunes.apple.com (lookup API) did not resolve from this environment, and the web search budget was used up. I could not check the app name, price, minimum OS, the 'fully local Kokoro' description, or the m4a/m4b export.
