## R6. Speech recognition on iPad (active mode)


### Summary

Dream Book's active mode needs two kinds of listening. The first is a tiny 5-second window that only has to catch "I know", "I don't know" and "go on / bye bye". The second is a free talk with the tutor, where the learner can interrupt while the iPad is speaking.

The best starting point is Apple's own on-device speech recognition in iPadOS 26 and later. It is free, works offline, sends no voice to the internet, and needs no model inside the app. Use Apple's "dictation" recogniser for the commands. It is the only Apple recogniser that accepts a list of expected phrases, and it has a setting for speakers with a heavy accent. Then keep the Dream Read fuzzy matcher, which already knows Chinese-accent variants like "I no" and "bai bai".

For conversation, use Apple's newer "speech transcriber" where the iPad supports it. Turn on Apple's echo cancellation and play the tutor's voice through the same audio engine, so the learner can talk over the tutor. If Apple's accuracy is not good enough for the learner's accent, two free add-ons can be plugged in: sherpa-onnx, the same engine as the Mac app with Moonshine and keyword spotting, or FluidAudio's Parakeet models on the iPad's neural chip.

In sleep mode the microphone should stay completely off. Silence already means "explain it" under the rules, so the book plays and explains by itself. Words heard while sleeping stay "learning" and never become "known". A sleep timer fades out and remembers where the learner fell asleep. Cloud recognition is optional and cheap (about $1–3 a month), but on-device is better: it costs nothing, keeps the voice private, and works in mainland China.

One limit: the shared web-search budget was used up, so I read Apple's documentation and GitHub pages directly. Vendor price pages could not be reached, so the cloud prices come from the repo's own October 2026 research and should be checked again.

### Detailed findings

## 0. How this was researched (read first)

- **Repo docs I read:** HOW-IT-WORKS.md, RULES.md, MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md, IPAD.md, VOICE.md, KOKORO.md, research/research-voice.md, plus `src/core/voice/commands.ts`.
- **Web search was blocked.** The session's shared WebSearch budget (200 calls, shared by all agents) was already used up when this step started. Every one of my WebSearch calls was refused.
- **What I fetched directly instead:**
  - Apple developer documentation (the JSON behind each page).
  - Apple Developer Forums threads.
  - GitHub pages for sherpa-onnx, WhisperKit, FluidAudio, Moonshine and Silero.
- **Sites that failed with "DNS not found" from the sandbox:** openai.com, deepgram.com, assemblyai.com, ai.google.dev, argmaxinc.com, macstories.net, k2-fsa.github.io and readthedocs.
- **Effect on prices:** cloud prices below come from the repo's own `docs/research/research-voice.md` (October 2026, secondary sources). Re-check them before paying.
- **Dates:** GitHub release pages show dates without a year. I read them as 2026 from the release order and asset timestamps.

## 1. What the app needs from speech recognition

These needs follow from RULES.md §1 and §6 and VOICE.md:

| Need | Details | Hard part |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Commands window** (5 s, after the word is said 3 times) | Only "I know" / "I don't know" / "go on, bye bye, continue, next". Any other speech is ignored and **never sent to the AI**. | A Mandarin-accented speaker; short phrases; "I know" is inside "I don't know"; the speech can be cut off when the window closes. |
| **B. Conversation** (mic button, M key, Always on) | Free questions with the book context. The book pauses when the learner speaks. Speaking interrupts the tutor (barge-in). "Bye bye" ends the call. | Echo of the iPad's own voice; delay before the answer; questions may be in Chinese or in mixed Chinese and English. |
| **C. Sleep mode** (new in Dream Book) | The learner never speaks. | Must not need the mic at all. |

The Mac pipeline that already exists:
- **Mic:** 16 kHz mono with echo cancellation.
- **VAD (voice activity detection):** Silero, with these segment rules: speech of 200 ms or more starts a segment, 600 ms of silence ends it, 15 s maximum, 300 ms padding.
- **Recogniser:** sherpa-onnx Moonshine v2 base int8, 111 MB.
- **Matcher (`commands.ts`):**
  - Normalises the text (lowercase, contractions, filler words removed).
  - Treats more than 6 words as conversation.
  - Has a per-intent phrase list with Mandarin-accent variants, for example `i no`, `i now`, `i don no`, `bai bai`, `by by`.
  - Checks in the order DONT_KNOW → KNOW → BYE.
  - Uses Levenshtein ≥ 0.80 or a phonetic key; ≥ 0.85 when confidence is below 0.6.
  - Fires on two agreeing partials or one final.

All of this logic is plain TypeScript and should be **ported 1:1 to Swift**, or run in JavaScriptCore if Dream Book is a hybrid app.

## 2. Apple on-device options

### 2.1 SpeechAnalyzer family (iOS/iPadOS 26+). This is the main recommendation.

- **Availability:** `SpeechAnalyzer`, `SpeechTranscriber`, `DictationTranscriber`, `SpeechDetector`, `AnalysisContext` and `AssetInventory` are all **iOS/iPadOS 26.0+** ([SpeechTranscriber](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber), [DictationTranscriber](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/dictationtranscriber)).
- **Where the model lives** ([WWDC25 session 277](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/277/)):
  - "Transcription is entirely on device but the models need to be fetched."
  - The model "does not increase the download or storage size of your application, nor does it increase the run-time memory size. It operates outside of your application's memory space."
  - The system updates the model automatically.
- **Downloading the model:**
  - `AssetInventory.assetInstallationRequest(supporting:)` then `downloadAndInstall()`. You can show a progress bar.
  - Each app gets a limited number of locale "reservations" (`maximumReservedLocales`).
  - Assets are shared between apps and stay between launches.
  - The system may unsubscribe unused assets ([AssetInventory](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/assetinventory)).
- **SpeechTranscriber** is "appropriate for normal conversation and general purposes", long-form and distant audio.
  - **Hardware:** it has "certain hardware requirements" that Apple does not publish. Check `SpeechTranscriber.isAvailable`. `supportedLocales` "is empty if the device does not support the transcriber".
  - **Presets** ([Preset](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber/preset)):

    | Preset | volatileResults | fastResults | alternativeTranscriptions | audioTimeRange |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | `transcription` | – | – | – | – |
    | `transcriptionWithAlternatives` | – | – | ✓ | – |
    | `timeIndexedTranscriptionWithAlternatives` | – | – | ✓ | ✓ |
    | `progressiveTranscription` | ✓ | ✓ | – | – |
    | `timeIndexedProgressiveTranscription` | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ |

  - **Reporting options:** `volatileResults`, `fastResults` ("faster but also less accurate"), `alternativeTranscriptions` ([ReportingOption](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber/reportingoption)).
  - **Result attributes:** `audioTimeRange` and **`transcriptionConfidence`** ([ResultAttributeOption](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber/resultattributeoption)). The confidence can feed the existing "confidence below 0.6 → stricter matching" rule.
- **DictationTranscriber** is "similar to system dictation features and compatible with older devices". It uses the same model as on-device `SFSpeechRecognizer`. Unlike `SFSpeechRecognizer`, it does not need Siri or keyboard dictation switched on in Settings (WWDC25 277).
  - **Content hints** ([ContentHint](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/dictationtranscriber/contenthint)):
    - `shortForm`: "audio is only expected to be a minute or so long".
    - `farField`: the speaker is far from the microphone.
    - **`atypicalSpeech`:** "a speaker with a heavy accent, lisp, or other confounding factor".
    - `customizedLanguage(modelConfiguration:)`: a custom language model built with `SFSpeechLanguageModel` (iOS 17+) ([SFSpeechLanguageModel](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/sfspeechlanguagemodel)).
- **Expected phrases (contextual strings):**
  - Set with `AnalysisContext.contextualStrings: [ContextualStringsTag: [String]]` and `analyzer.setContext(_:)` ([AnalysisContext](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/analysiscontext)).
  - **Important:** an Apple engineer answered: "currently, contextual strings only help transcriptions from the DictationTranscriber module. The SpeechTranscriber module does not currently take contextual strings into account" ([forum thread 811083](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/811083)).
  - Another developer in that thread kept SpeechTranscriber and added Levenshtein fuzzy matching, which is exactly Dream Read's approach.
  - I could not confirm whether iOS 27 changed this.
- **Latency** ([forum thread 794720](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/794720)):
  - A developer measured the final transcript arriving **≈2.1–2.2 s after speech ended**, while using `[.volatileResults, .fastResults]`.
  - With `prepareToAnalyze(in:)` the average was **1.45 s** (11 tries; range 0.05–3 s).
  - Another reply (March 2026) says:
    - the volatile result matched the final one "~95% of the time for short utterances";
    - a 16 kHz mono tap "shaves ~200ms";
    - a cold Neural Engine adds variance.
  - Apple's own advice: call `prepareToAnalyze(in:)` and use `ModelRetention` options ([SpeechAnalyzer, "Improve responsiveness"](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechanalyzer)).
- **SpeechDetector (built-in VAD module, iOS 26)** ([SpeechDetector](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechdetector)):
  - It only works alongside a transcriber.
  - In 2025 it did not compile inside `SpeechAnalyzer(modules:)` because of a protocol-conformance bug. Apple said it "will be fixed in the next point update" ([thread 797544](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/797544)).
  - Treat it as optional and keep your own VAD.
- **iOS 27 addition:** `CaptureInputSequenceProvider` (iOS/iPadOS 27.0) feeds a microphone straight into the analyzer ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/captureinputsequenceprovider)). Its page says nothing about echo cancellation, so for barge-in keep your own `AVAudioEngine` tap.
- **Accuracy numbers:** Apple publishes no WER (word error rate). Third-party benchmarks (Argmax, MacStories) could not be opened from the sandbox. From memory, MacStories' June 2025 test found SpeechAnalyzer about 2× faster than Whisper large-v3-turbo on a Mac. Treat that as unverified.
- **Mainland China:** recognition runs on the device. The one-time model download comes from Apple's servers, which are normally reachable in China. I believe this works but could not test it.

### 2.2 SFSpeechRecognizer (older API, iOS 10+, on-device since iOS 13)

- **On-device flag:** `requiresOnDeviceRecognition` ("must keep its audio data on the device"). Check `supportsOnDeviceRecognition` first.
- **Other request settings:** `contextualStrings: [String]` (no documented size limit), `customizedLanguageModel` (iOS 17), `addsPunctuation`, `taskHint` (`.confirmation` suits short yes/no-style commands), `shouldReportPartialResults` ([SFSpeechRecognitionRequest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/sfspeechrecognitionrequest)).
- **Limits** ([SFSpeechRecognizer](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/sfspeechrecognizer)):
  - "the framework stops speech recognition tasks that last longer than one minute".
  - Per-device and per-app daily limits apply to the network service.
  - Restart a task for each utterance. This is harmless for 5-second windows.
- **Use:** only as the fallback for iPads that cannot run iPadOS 26. On 26+, `DictationTranscriber` gives the same model with a modern API.

**sherpa-onnx Swift API** (from [`SherpaOnnx.swift`](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/blob/master/swift-api-examples/SherpaOnnx.swift)):
- `sherpaOnnxOfflineMoonshineModelConfig`: Moonshine v2 needs only `encoder` + `mergedDecoder`.
- Offline transducer (Parakeet TDT).
- `hotwordsFile` / `hotwordsScore` (default 1.5).
- `SherpaOnnxVoiceActivityDetectorWrapper` (Silero / TEN VAD).
- `SherpaOnnxKeywordSpotterWrapper` with `keywordsScore` (default 1.0) and `keywordsThreshold` (default 0.25).
- Keyword spotting is open-vocabulary: you can change the keywords "without re-training". Each line of the keywords file can carry `:boost` and `#threshold`, and `@` marks the original phrase ([KWS docs](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa/blob/master/docs/source/onnx/kws/index.rst)).

**Mandarin-accent accuracy:** I found no published WER for Mandarin-L1 English on any of these engines. The only accent-specific tool is Apple's `atypicalSpeech` hint. VOICE.md already lists "real accented-speech evaluation" as missing. Build the in-app voice test from §7 and decide with the learner's own recordings.

## 4. Echo cancellation and barge-in on iPad

**Main API:** `AVAudioIONode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(_:)` (iOS 13+, [doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioionode/setvoiceprocessingenabled(_:))) turns on Apple's voice-processing audio unit: echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain. Apple's sample is "[Using voice processing](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/using-voice-processing)" (iOS 17, Xcode 15.4).

**Rules of thumb:**
- Enable it on `engine.inputNode` **before** `engine.start()`.
- Play every tutor or book sentence through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` in the **same engine**, so the echo canceller has the reference signal:
  - For Kokoro, play the PCM buffers.
  - For Apple voices, use `AVSpeechSynthesizer.write(_:toBufferCallback:)`.
- Turning it on or off needs an engine stop and start. Switch only at sentence boundaries.
- Voice processing tends to lower playback loudness and quality ("phone sound"), and the input format can change. These are common developer reports that I did not verify today. So **use it only while Active mode is on**.

**Other audio APIs:**

| API | iOS | Use in Dream Book |
|---|---|---|
| `voiceProcessingOtherAudioDuckingConfiguration` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioinputnode/voiceprocessingotheraudioduckingconfiguration)) | 17+ | Advanced ducking is off by default. Set a minimal ducking level so the book voice stays loud. |
| `setMutedSpeechActivityEventListener` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioinputnode/setmutedspeechactivityeventlistener(_:))) | 17+ | Tells you about speech while the input is muted. |
| `AVAudioSession.setPrefersEchoCancelledInput` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/setprefersechocancelledinput(_:))) | 18.2+ | **Only "certain 2024 or later iPhone models"**, `.playAndRecord` with `.default` mode. Not for iPad: use voice processing. |
| Category option `.bluetoothHighQualityRecording` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/categoryoptions-swift.struct/bluetoothhighqualityrecording)) | 26+ | Full-quality AirPods mic. **Not in the EU.** "May increase input latency … isn't recommended for real-time communication." Fallback is `.allowBluetoothHFP`. |

**Headphones:** with AirPods it is better to use `.allowBluetoothA2DP`, so output stays high quality and the iPad's own mic is used. Test this on the device.

**Barge-in recipe** (on top of the existing segmenter):
1. Silero VAD runs on the echo-cancelled stream. While the tutor is speaking, use a stricter threshold (for example 0.7 instead of 0.5) and require 250–300 ms of speech.
2. On a speech start, fade the tutor to about 20% within 100 ms. Do not stop it yet.
3. If the speech lasts 400 ms or more, **and** the first recognised words are *not* the words the tutor said in the last ~3 s, stop playback and cancel the AI and TTS streams. The app knows exactly what it said, from Kokoro's per-word timings, so this "echo text check" removes most false interruptions.
4. Otherwise fade the tutor back up.

**The 5-second command window needs no echo cancellation:** open the mic about 150 ms *after* the third repetition ends, and nothing is playing.

## 5. Permissions (Info.plist)

- **`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`**: "required if your app uses APIs that access the device's microphone" ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsmicrophoneusagedescription)).
- **`NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`**: required for the Speech framework "regardless of whether you set requiresOnDeviceRecognition". "If this key is not present, your app will crash when it calls requestAuthorization." Apple also advises: "delay requests until the user interacts with the portion of your app that uses such features" ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/asking-permission-to-use-speech-recognition)).
- **`UIBackgroundModes` → `audio`**: needed to keep reading with the screen locked ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/uibackgroundmodes)).
- **Simplified Chinese:** put the zh-Hans text in `InfoPlist.strings` rather than mixing two languages in one string.
- **Example text:** "Dream Book listens only in Active mode, for 'I know', 'I don't know', 'go on' and your questions. Your voice is recognised on this iPad." Change it if you turn on cloud recognition, and declare "Audio Data" in the App Store privacy label in that case.
- **Sleep mode never asks** for the mic or speech permission.

## 6. Cloud options

Prices are from the repo's `docs/research/research-voice.md` (October 2026, secondary sources; vendor pages were unreachable today, so re-check).

| Service | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | ≈$0.003/min | Billed on audio sent, so gate it with VAD. Realtime transcription socket with `semantic_vad`. |
| OpenAI `gpt-4o-transcribe` | ≈$0.006/min | Handles Chinese–English mixing well (unverified). |
| Deepgram Nova-3 streaming | $0.0077/min ($200 free credit) | `keyterm` biasing. Flux ≈$0.008/min with end-of-turn detection. |
| AssemblyAI Universal-Streaming | $0.15/h | **Billed on socket-open time.** Bad for Always on. |
| Google STT v2 chirp_3 | $0.016/min, 60 free min/month | Not competitive. |
| Full speech-to-speech (OpenAI Realtime 2.1-mini; Gemini Live) | ≈$0.02–0.05/min; Gemini has a free tier | Replaces Claude as the tutor. Not recommended. |

- **Real usage:** the learner speaks perhaps 5–15 min a day, about 300 min a month. That is about **$0.90/month** with gpt-4o-mini-transcribe or **$2.30/month** with Deepgram.
- **Mainland China:** OpenAI's API is not offered there, and Anthropic does not serve mainland China. Cloud speech recognition may not work for a China-based learner. On-device does.

## 7. Recommended design

**Commands window (Need A):**
1. **Engine:** `SpeechAnalyzer` + `DictationTranscriber(locale: en-US)`, configured with:
   - `contentHints: [.shortForm, .atypicalSpeech]`;
   - volatile results and confidence;
   - `AnalysisContext.contextualStrings` set to the command phrases and accent variants, **plus the current target word**, so a repeated word is recognised correctly and then ignored.
2. **Pre-warm:** call `prepareToAnalyze` when the word card appears, so the window starts "hot".
3. **Window timing:** the window lasts 5 s. If speech started before 5 s, extend by up to 2 s so "I don't kn—" is not cut. End-of-speech silence is 500–600 ms.
4. **Matcher:** port `commands.ts` as it is (DONT_KNOW before KNOW, 6 words or fewer, fuzzy and phonetic matching). Fire on two agreeing volatile results or one final. Anything else is ignored and never sent to the AI.
5. **"Teach Dream Book my voice"** (about 1 minute, optional, synced to the account):
   - The learner says each command three times.
   - Store what the recogniser actually heard as personal aliases.
   - Show a hit-rate score. This doubles as the accented-speech test VOICE.md is missing.
6. **Second ear, only if the test shows misses:** sherpa-onnx keyword spotter (gigaspeech 3.3M mobile, 14.9 MB) on the same audio. Tune boost and threshold from the calibration. Optionally use the zh-en model to accept 知道 / 不知道 / 继续.
7. **Fallback** for iPads below iPadOS 26, or if Apple's asset is missing: sherpa-onnx Moonshine v2 base + Silero VAD, the identical Mac pipeline.

**Conversation (Need B):**
- **Audio:** an `AVAudioEngine` with voice processing on while Active mode is on, and all speech output through the same engine.
- **VAD:** Silero via FluidAudio or sherpa.
- **Recogniser:** `SpeechTranscriber` with volatile results and confidence where `isAvailable`, otherwise `DictationTranscriber`. Act on the stable volatile text when the VAD sees the end of speech; do not wait the 1.5–2 s for the final result. Claude repairs misheard words from the book context; RULES already says "work out the meaning from the book".
- **Better-accuracy add-on:** a 480 MB download of FluidAudio Parakeet (v2 English or EOU streaming).
- **Chinese questions:** a setting "I ask in: English / 中文 / both". 中文 uses the zh-CN transcriber; "both" uses WhisperKit large-v3-turbo or cloud.
- **Expected delay:** about 1.5–3 s to the first audio. Use a soft chime, never filler words, to fit the no-filler rule.

**Sleep mode (Need C):** see the recommendation.

## 8. Constraints worth knowing

- Since **April 28, 2026**, App Store uploads must be built with **Xcode 26 or later and an iOS/iPadOS 26 SDK** ([Apple](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/)). The SpeechAnalyzer APIs need that SDK.
- Apple lists **Xcode 26.6 as needing macOS Tahoe 26.2+**; Xcode 27.2 RC needs Tahoe 26.6+ ([system requirements](https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/)).
- The learner's Intel MacBook Pro on Ventura 13 **cannot build this app**. They need a cloud Mac (Xcode Cloud, GitHub macOS runners, Codemagic) or a newer Mac. This belongs to the build/tooling research topic.

### Recommendation

## Recommendation

### 1. Commands window (5 s)
- **Default engine:** Apple on-device **`SpeechAnalyzer` + `DictationTranscriber`** (iPadOS 26+). It costs nothing, adds 0 MB to the app, works offline, keeps the voice private and works in China. It is the only Apple recogniser that uses **contextual strings** and has an **`atypicalSpeech`** ("heavy accent") hint.
- **Keep the matcher:** feed its text into the existing Dream Read command matcher, ported from `commands.ts`, including the Mandarin-accent variants.
- **Add a 1-minute "teach my voice" calibration.** It stores what the recogniser actually hears as personal aliases, which also answers the open accuracy question.
- **Only if the learner's own test shows misses:** add the sherpa-onnx keyword spotter (14.9 MB) as a second ear.
- **iPads below 26:** use sherpa-onnx Moonshine v2 + Silero VAD, the same pipeline as the Mac app.
- **Always keep:** big buttons, keyboard keys and headphone-button shortcuts.

### 2. Conversation with barge-in
- **Audio:** an `AVAudioEngine` with **`setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)`**, only while Active mode is on. Play all speech through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` in that same engine, so echo cancellation has the reference.
- **Barge-in:** Silero VAD with a stricter threshold while the tutor talks: duck first, stop only after 400 ms or more of speech that does not match the tutor's own recent words.
- **Recogniser:** **`SpeechTranscriber`** where `isAvailable` (better for conversation; contextual strings are ignored), otherwise `DictationTranscriber`. Act on the volatile text at end of speech instead of waiting about 1.5–2 s for the final, and call `prepareToAnalyze` early.
- **Optional accuracy upgrade:** FluidAudio Parakeet (Neural Engine, about 480 MB).
- **Chinese or mixed questions:** WhisperKit, or cloud gpt-4o-transcribe outside China (about $1 a month).

### 3. Sleep mode (the learner never speaks)
- The **mic is never opened** and no permission is asked. The audio session is `.playback` / `.spokenAudio` with `UIBackgroundModes: audio`, at full audio quality, with no voice processing.
- The 5-second window becomes a short quiet pause (default 1.5 s, adjustable 0–5 s), then the explanation plays automatically. RULES already says silence means "explain".
- Words explained during sleep stay **learning**, never known, and the level estimate is not changed by sleep-mode silence.
- **Sleep timer:** end of chapter, or 15/30/45/60 min, with a 60-second fade-out. It saves a "fell asleep here" bookmark and next time offers "start 2 minutes before you fell asleep".
- **Automatic switch:** if Active mode hears nothing for about 6 windows in a row, close the mic and show a small "Listening only, tap to talk" note.
- Lock-screen and AirPods controls (play/pause, next = I know or skip, previous = explain again) are customisable and need no speaking.

### Paste-ready instruction for the AI coding assistant
"Speech in Dream Book:
1. Create a `SpeechEngine` protocol with these implementations:
   - `AppleDictationEngine` (iPadOS 26 `DictationTranscriber`, `contentHints [.shortForm, .atypicalSpeech]`, `contextualStrings` = command phrases + target word, volatile results + confidence, `prepareToAnalyze` when the word card appears);
   - `AppleConversationEngine` (`SpeechTranscriber` if `isAvailable`, else dictation);
   - `SherpaEngine` (Moonshine v2 base + Silero VAD + optional keyword spotter, SPM `github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx` ≥ 1.13.8).
2. Port `src/core/voice/commands.ts` and the segmenter (200 ms start / 600 ms end / 15 s max / 300 ms pad) to Swift with the same unit tests.
3. The commands window opens the mic 150 ms after the 3rd repeat, lasts 5 s, and extends up to 2 s if speech is in progress. Non-command speech is discarded and never sent to the AI.
4. In Active mode, the `AVAudioEngine` has voice processing on and all TTS goes through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` in that engine. Barge-in = duck at VAD start, stop after 400 ms unless the transcript matches the last 3 s of TTS words.
5. Sleep mode: no mic, `.playback` session, auto-explain after 1.5 s, words stay learning, sleep timer with fade and bookmark.
6. Info.plist: `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`, `UIBackgroundModes` audio. Ask for permission only when Active mode is first turned on.
7. Add the 'Teach my voice' calibration screen that saves per-user aliases to the account."


### Fact-check of the key claims (an independent checker tried to disprove them)

- **confirmed**: SpeechAnalyzer, SpeechTranscriber, DictationTranscriber, SpeechDetector, AnalysisContext and AssetInventory are available from iOS/iPadOS 26.0; the models run on device, out of the app's process, are downloaded via AssetInventory and do not add to the app's size or memory.
  - Evidence: Apple doc JSON (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/speech/{speechanalyzer,speechtranscriber,dictationtranscriber,speechdetector,analysiscontext,assetinventory}.json) lists iOS 26.0 and iPadOS 26.0 for all six. The AssetInventory page says assets are 'machine-learning models downloaded from Apple's servers and managed by the system... shares it with other apps'. The WWDC25 session 277 transcript (https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/277/) says: 'transcription is entirely on device but the models need to be fetched' and 'The model is retained in system storage and does not increase the download or storage size of your application, nor does it increase the run-time memory size. It operates outside of your application's memory space.' https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber covers the isAvailable caveat.
- **confirmed**: Contextual strings (AnalysisContext.contextualStrings via analyzer.setContext) currently only help DictationTranscriber; SpeechTranscriber ignores them (Apple engineer answer).
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/811083 quotes Apple_Agent: 'currently, contextual strings only help transcriptions from the DictationTranscriber module. The SpeechTranscriber module does not currently take contextual strings into account.' https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/analysiscontext/contextualstrings says 'With the DictationTranscriber module, you can use this property...' and 'Limit the total number of phrases across all tags to no more than 100.' The SpeechAnalyzer docs list setContext(_:) as 'Sets contextual information to improve or inform the analysis.'
- **confirmed**: DictationTranscriber offers ContentHint.shortForm and ContentHint.atypicalSpeech ('a speaker with a heavy accent, lisp, or other confounding factor'), plus customizedLanguage with an SFSpeechLanguageModel (iOS 17+).
  - Evidence: The DictationTranscriber.ContentHint doc JSON (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/dictationtranscriber/contenthint) lists these cases: atypicalSpeech, 'A processing hint indicating that the audio is from a speaker with a heavy accent, lisp, or other confounding factor.'; shortForm, '...audio is only expected to be a minute or so long.'; farField; and customizedLanguage(modelConfiguration:), 'A hint specifying a custom language model...'. The SFSpeechLanguageModel doc JSON gives iOS 17.0 and iPadOS 17.0. The DictationTranscriber 'Improve accuracy' text describes supplying custom vocabulary with SFSpeechLanguageModel plus the customizedLanguage hint.
- **confirmed**: A developer measured SpeechTranscriber's final transcript arriving about 2.1-2.2 s after speech ended even with volatile and fast results; with prepareToAnalyze the average fell to 1.45 s (n=11, range 0.05-3 s); the volatile result matched the final about 95% of the time for short utterances.
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/794720 contains these quotes. Bersaelor: 'it took the SpeechAnalyzer 2.1s to get the transcript finalized' and 'I'm already using reportingOptions: [.volatileResults, .fastResults]'. Bersaelor in Aug 2025: 'n: 11, avg: 2.2s, Var: 0.75' and 'with calling prepareToAnalyze: n: 11, avg: 1.45s, Var: 1.305 (the delay varied greatly between 0.05s and 3s)'. eddiewangyw in Mar 2026: 'the volatile transcript matches the final one ~95% of the time for short utterances.'
- **confirmed**: AVAudioIONode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled is available from iOS 13; voiceProcessingOtherAudioDuckingConfiguration from iOS 17; AVAudioSession.setPrefersEchoCancelledInput (iOS 18.2) works only on certain 2024-or-later iPhone models with playAndRecord + default mode, so iPads must use voice processing.
  - Evidence: Apple doc JSON for https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioionode/setvoiceprocessingenabled(_:) gives iOS 13.0 and iPadOS 13.0. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioinputnode/voiceprocessingotheraudioduckingconfiguration gives iOS 17.0 and iPadOS 17.0. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/setprefersechocancelledinput(_:) gives iOS 18.2 and iPadOS 18.2 and says: 'This option is valid only when used with playAndRecord category and default mode, and is only available on certain 2024 or later iPhone models. Query the isEchoCancelledInputAvailable property...' and 'Audio sessions using Apple's voice processing APIs don't need this option because the system automatically applies echo cancellation.'
- **confirmed**: sherpa-onnx v1.13.8 (10 Sep 2026) supports Swift Package Manager (since v1.13.5); its Swift API includes Moonshine v2, Silero VAD and a keyword spotter (defaults keywordsScore 1.0, threshold 0.25) whose keywords can change without retraining; the English KWS model is 14.9 MB and a zh-en KWS model is 31.4 MB.
  - Evidence: https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases shows v1.13.8 on 10 Sep marked Latest, and v1.13.5 lists 'Support swift package manager (SPM)'. In https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/blob/master/swift-api-examples/SherpaOnnx.swift: the Moonshine config notes 'For v2, you need two models: encoder, mergedDecoder'; sherpaOnnxSileroVadModelConfig is present; sherpaOnnxKeywordSpotterConfig has 'keywordsScore: Float = 1.0, keywordsThreshold: Float = 0.25' plus keywordsFile and keywordsBuf, so keywords are supplied at runtime. The C API also has SherpaOnnxCreateKeywordStreamWithKeywords for inline keywords per stream. Asset sizes are from https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/expanded_assets/kws-models.
- **confirmed**: NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription is required even with requiresOnDeviceRecognition, and the app crashes on requestAuthorization without it; Apple advises asking only when the user first uses the feature.
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/asking-permission-to-use-speech-recognition says: 'You must include the NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription key... This applies regardless of whether you set requiresOnDeviceRecognition to true or false. If this key is not present, your app will crash when it calls requestAuthorization(_:)' and 'Do not request access to speech recognition if you do not intend to use the feature right away. Instead, delay requests until the user interacts with the portion of your app that uses such features.' The NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription key page says the same.
- **confirmed**: Since April 28, 2026 App Store uploads must be built with Xcode 26+ and an iOS/iPadOS 26 SDK; Xcode 26.6 requires macOS Tahoe 26.2 or later, so the learner's Intel Mac on Ventura cannot build the app.
  - Evidence: https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ says: 'Since April 28, 2026 — Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26...'. https://developer.apple.com/xcode/system-requirements/ lists: Xcode 26.6 'macOS Tahoe 26.2 - macOS Tahoe 26.x'; Xcode 27/27.1 'macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later'; Xcode 26 'macOS Sequoia 15.6 - macOS Tahoe 26.x'. The Intel Tahoe compatibility list is recalled, not fetched. Note: the WebSearch budget for this turn was used up after one search, so every check was done by fetching the official pages directly (Apple doc JSON, Apple forums, GitHub).


## R7. iPad listening and reading design, sleep-friendly and simple


### Summary

Dream Book on iPad should feel like a calm audiobook player first and a teacher second. The Home screen has one big Play button that continues exactly where you stopped, and three modes: Learn (you can tap or say "I know / I don't know / Go on"), Relax (completely hands-free; the teacher explains by itself) and Sleep (dark screen, sleep timer, slow fade-out, no sudden sounds). The Listen screen shows the book like song lyrics: the current sentence is large, the current word is lit, and big thumb-sized buttons sit at the bottom where you can reach them. When the teacher stops at a hard word, a small explanation card appears next to the word on a full iPad screen, and as a bottom panel when the app window is narrow (this follows Apple's own rules). In Sleep mode the app lets the iPad screen turn off. The audio keeps playing, the controls stay on the Lock Screen, and the next morning the app asks where to restart (by default, a little before you fell asleep). Customisation stays easy: a few ready-made presets, about five simple sliders, an "Advanced" area for everything else, and an "Edit buttons" mode where you can move, resize or change any button. Your seven teaching characters sit on one screen, with your own style first and as the default. Each character has a "hear a sample" button and an editor. One limit: the shared web-search budget for this run was already used up, so I worked from about 60 official sources fetched directly (Apple's design rules and iPad guide for iPadOS 27, current App Store pages, and the open-source code of two iPhone and iPad audio players). A few competitor details are marked as not checked.

### Detailed findings

## 0. How this was researched, and what it does not cover

- **Search limit:** the run's shared WebSearch budget was already used up (all 4 of my WebSearch calls were refused). I did not work around the limit with a search engine. Instead I **fetched about 60 primary sources directly**:
  - Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG) pages, through the JSON data behind developer.apple.com/design. The change logs run to **9 Sep 2026**.
  - Apple developer documentation.
  - Apple's **iPad User Guide for iPadOS 27**.
  - Current App Store listings (versions dated Oct 2026).
  - MDN browser-compat-data.
  - The source code of two open-source iOS audio players: **Pocket Casts iOS** (commit of 19 Oct 2026) and **BookPlayer** (commit of 18 Oct 2026).
- **Not verified** (marked "unverified" below):
  - Audible's exact sleep-timer menu: help.audible.com could not be reached.
  - Apple Books' list of sleep-timer durations: the guide only says "choose a duration".
  - Calm and Headspace in-player controls.
  - LingQ's current iPad app: its App Store ID returned 404, so I rely on docs/research/research-ux.md.
  - iPad point sizes: the HIG device table moved in the 9 Sep 2026 update, so the sizes are from memory.
- **Repo context used:** RULES.md (the 5-second commands window, word said 3 times, read again from the start of the sentence, Chinese only at the end with a Chinese voice), MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md (RULE ONE, TWO, THREE), HOW-IT-WORKS.md, IPAD.md, and the existing settings in `src/shared/settings.ts`. Relevant existing settings: `commandWindowMs`, `repeatWindowWords`, `maxStopsPer10Min`, `wordRepeats`, themes `night|sepia|light|grey`, and the 10 styles in `src/shared/styles.ts`. The current `ListeningScreen.tsx` bottom bar has about 12 controls. That is too many for a sleepy, thumb-first iPad screen, and this spec cuts it down.

## 1. Platform facts that shape the design (October 2026)

| Topic | Fact (with source) | What it means for Dream Book |
|---|---|---|
| Current OS | **iPadOS 27** is current. It runs on iPad (9th gen) and later, iPad mini 6 and later, iPad Air 4 and later, and iPad Pro 11" 2nd gen to **M5** and 12.9"/13" 4th gen to **M5** ([models](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/ipad-models-compatible-with-ipados-27-ipad213a25b2/ipados)). iPadOS 27 adds a slider for how Liquid Glass looks, from ultraclear to tinted ([what's new](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/whats-new-in-ipados-27-ipad8d9d296d/ipados)). | Target iPadOS 18 or later (Audible needs 18.1: [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/audible/id379693831)). Use system bars so Liquid Glass and its slider work automatically. |
| Screen sizes | From memory of the older HIG table (unverified): 11" iPad and iPad Air **820×1180 pt**, iPad Pro 11" (M4/M5) **834×1210 pt**, iPad Air 13" **1024×1366 pt**, iPad Pro 13" (M4/M5) **1032×1376 pt**. | Two main layouts (regular and compact width), not one per device. |
| Size classes | HIG: "Determine layout based on size classes, not device type or orientation". "Don't change your app's functionality based on the space it occupies", but you may show less ([layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout)). | A narrow window beside Notes keeps every feature; some move into a "⋯" menu. |
| Windows | iPad windows can be **Full screen** or **Windowed** (freely resizable). Stage Manager is still an option. Window controls sit at the leading (left) edge of the toolbar, so "move buttons inward when the window controls appear" ([HIG windows](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/windows), [iPad guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/work-with-multiple-windows-at-the-same-time-ipad08c9970c/ipados)). | Do not put "Back" hard against the top-left corner. |
| Menu bar | The iPad menu bar is hidden until revealed. Dynamic menu items exist only with a hardware keyboard, so "ensure that people can access all of your app's functions through its UI" ([menu bar](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/the-menu-bar)). | Every shortcut also has a button. |
| Tab bar | On iPad the tab bar sits at the top and can turn into a sidebar. Aim for **5 or fewer** default tabs ([tab bars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-bars)). | 4 tabs: Home, Library, My Words, Progress. |
| Popover vs sheet | A popover suits a small amount of content. It should point at what opened it. **"Avoid displaying popovers in compact views… use a sheet"**. **"Always save work when automatically closing"** a popover. Show only one at a time, and never use one for warnings ([popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers)). Sheets have **medium (about half) and large detents**, a grabber and swipe-to-dismiss. On iPad, prefer page or form sheets. A nonmodal sheet lets people keep using the main view ([sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets), updated 24 Mar 2026). | Explanation card: a popover anchored to the word in regular width, a medium-detent sheet in compact width. |
| Touch targets | Default control **44×44 pt**, minimum 28×28 ([accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility)). Use **one or two prominent buttons per view**, and "use style, not size" to mark the preferred choice ([buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons)). | Main actions are 72 to 96 pt (sleepy thumbs). Only Play and "I don't know" are prominent. |
| Text | Default text **17 pt**, minimum **11 pt**. Contrast **4.5:1** up to 17 pt and 3:1 from 18 pt or bold. Dynamic Type "Large" (default) is Body 17/22, Title 1 28/34, Large Title 34/41. At AX5, Body is 53 pt ([typography](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography)). Allow at least 200% enlargement. | The book text follows Dynamic Type and also has its own A–/A+ control. |
| Timers in the UI | **"Minimize use of time-boxed interface elements… Prefer dismissing views with an explicit action"** ([accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility)). | This conflicts with the learner's 5-second window and self-closing card. RULES.md wins, so add the safety valves in §4.4 (hold to pause, adjustable length, history). |
| Motion | Respect **Reduce Motion**: use fades instead of slides and no zooming ([accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility)). | The karaoke scroll becomes a cross-fade when Reduce Motion is on. |
| Keyboard | Prefer ⌘ as the modifier and avoid Control. Do not take over standard shortcuts ([keyboards](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards)). Holding ⌘ shows the app's shortcuts ([iPad guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/use-keyboard-shortcuts-ipad271212e1/ipados)). ⌘, opens settings ([settings](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings)). | See §5. |
| Pointer | iPad pointer effects: highlight, lift and hover. Let the pointer reveal auto-hidden controls ([pointing devices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pointing-devices)). | Auto-hidden Listen bars come back when the pointer moves near them. |
| Apple Pencil | Pencil should work on every control. Do not start actions on hover. **Double tap and squeeze must be non-destructive and easy to undo**. Design for left and right hands, and "consider letting people reposition" controls ([Pencil](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pencil-and-scribble)). | Pencil Pro squeeze = "Explain this sentence" (optional). "I know" always gets an Undo. |
| Audio | An audiobook or language-learning app uses the **Playback** category (plays when the silent switch is on, can play in the background) ([playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio)). With the **Audio background mode**, audio "continues when people… lock their iOS device" ([media playback](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfoundation/configuring-your-app-for-media-playback)). Pause when headphones are unplugged. Pause indefinitely for primary interruptions ([multitasking](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/multitasking)). | Sleep mode = let the iPad lock. Audio continues. |
| Screen on | "Most apps should let the system turn off the screen… **This includes audio apps**" (`isIdleTimerDisabled`, [docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/isidletimerdisabled)). | Keep the screen awake only on the Read screen and the optional "dim clock". |
| Lock Screen | Now Playing info appears on the Lock Screen and in Control Center ([MPNowPlayingInfoCenter](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpnowplayinginfocenter)). Remote commands: play, pause, toggle, next/previous track, skip forward/back, change playback position, change rate, bookmark ([MPRemoteCommandCenter](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpremotecommandcenter)). HIG: **"Avoid repurposing audio controls"**. | Next/previous track = next/previous part. Skip = 15 s, snapped to a sentence start. |
| Live Activity | On the iPad Lock Screen. Best for tasks of **8 hours or less**. One simple interactive element ([live activities](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities)). | A sleep-timer countdown with a "+15 min" button. |
| Focus | An app can react to Focus changes through `SetFocusFilterIntent` (iPadOS 16+) ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents/setfocusfilterintent)). The Sleep Focus can be switched from Control Center ([iPad guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/use-a-sleep-focus-ipad6a82f607/ipados)). | Optional: Sleep Focus on → Dream Book offers Sleep mode. |
| Control Center | Apps can add their own controls to Control Center and the Lock Screen ([controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/controls)). | A "Dream Book: Sleep" control. |
| Fade | `AVAudioPlayer.setVolume(_:fadeDuration:)` ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudioplayer/setvolume(_:fadeduration:))). | A built-in way to fade. |
| Haptics | iPad itself has no general haptics. Apple Pencil Pro and some trackpads do ([haptics](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-haptics)). | Never depend on vibration. |
| Web version (PWA) | Media Session API since Safari 15. **Screen Wake Lock works in home-screen web apps only from iOS/iPadOS 18.4**; before that, it did not work in standalone apps ([MDN BCD](https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/WakeLock.json), [WebKit bug 254545](https://webkit.org/b/254545)). Unverified: Web Speech (Safari voices) is unreliable once the screen locks. | Sleep mode needs real audio (generated audio files) and Media Session at the very least. Native is safer. |

## 3. Design principles for Dream Book

1. **Listening first.** Every screen has one obvious next step. On Home it is Play. In Listen it is Play/Pause. In a pause it is "I don't know" (the default answer, because silence = explain).
2. **Three modes, one switch:** **Learn** (active: buttons and voice commands, the RULES.md flow), **Relax** (hands-free: the same flow with no commands window) and **Sleep** (dark, a timer, gentle teaching). The mode is a large three-part control on Home and a small chip on Listen.
3. **Nothing is lost.** Every self-closing card stays in the "Explanations" history and in My Vocabulary. Every "I know" has an Undo. This is how the self-closing card meets the HIG's timed-UI rule.
4. **Calm visuals:** Night theme by default. One accent colour. No badges, red dots, streak pressure or sounds from the interface. Fades instead of slides.
5. **Easy customisation in three levels:** (a) presets, (b) about five sliders on the screen they affect, (c) "Advanced", plus (d) "Edit buttons" mode for any button.
6. **Same features in every window size.** Fewer things are visible in narrow windows.

---

## 4. Screen-by-screen spec

### 4.0 Navigation (global)
- **Top tab bar (iPadOS 18+ style):** Home · Library · My Words · Progress. Settings is a gear on Home (and ⌘,). It also turns into a sidebar on 13" landscape if the learner wants.
- **Listen and Read** are full-screen views with the tab bar hidden. Leaving them (swipe down or Back) leaves a **mini-player** at the bottom of every tab, like Apple Books. It shows the cover, the current sentence (one line), Play/Pause and the mode chip.
- **Account and sync status** is a small cloud icon in Settings ("Saved online ✓ 2 min ago"). Sign-in options: **Sign in with Apple** and email. Google sign-in is blocked in mainland China, so offer it only as an extra.

### 4.1 Home: "one big Play button"
- **Top:** a greeting by time of day ("Good evening"), the gear, and the teacher avatar chip ("My Teacher ▾": tap to switch character).
- **Hero card** (full width, 60% of the visible height): the blurred book cover behind it, then the book title, "Part 4 of 23 · The Garden · 18 min left in this part" and a **Play/Continue button 120 pt round** (largest object on screen). Under it, one line: "Continue from 23:10 (you fell asleep here last night) · Start of part".
- **Mode control** under the hero: three equal segments 72 pt tall with icon and word: **Learn** (hand), **Relax** (headphones), **Sleep** (moon). The choice is remembered. Sleep opens the timer sheet (4.7).
- **Below** (small, quiet): "Today: 12 new words · 35 min listened" and "Your new book is being prepared… 64%" when the AI is still reading a book.
- **Empty state:** one button, "Add your first book" (Files picker, paste text or share sheet), plus a 2-line explanation in easy English.
- Size behaviour: on 13" landscape, the hero sits on the left (60%) and "Continue listening" (the next 3 books) on the right. In compact width, everything stacks.

### 4.2 Library
- Grid of covers (180 pt wide on 11", 200 pt on 13"). Each cover shows a thin progress line and a **status chip**: "Preparing (AI reading 64%)" → "Finding hard words" → "Making parts" → "Ready". Long-press menu: Play · Read · Parts · Book info · Remove from this iPad (keeps the online copy) · Delete everywhere (confirm).
- **Book page:** cover, "Your level vs this book" ("About 3% of words are new to you: good for learning"), a list of **parts** (the AI splits the book into parts of about 10–20 min at scene or chapter boundaries, each with a title and the number of hard items), a "Start" button and a choice of character for this book.
- Sort: Recent · Title · Progress. Filter: Listening · Finished. Search (⌘F).

### 4.3 Listen (main screen)
**Layout, regular width (11" or 13", portrait or landscape, or a wide window):**
- **Top bar** (auto-hides 4 s after playback starts; tap anywhere or move the pointer near the top to show it again). It is moved inward when window controls show. It holds: Back (to Home), "Book · Part 4: The Garden", a **Listen | Read** switch (L), the character chip and ⋯ (Go to, Skip panel, Text size, Help).
- **Karaoke area:** the current sentence is placed at about 40% of the height, so it is never under the thumbs. **Current sentence at 2× Body**: about **32 pt on 11", 36 pt on 13"** at Dynamic Type "Large", growing with Dynamic Type and the A–/A+ slider. The 2 sentences before and after are at Body+3 (about 20 pt) with 45% opacity. **Current word** gets a soft rounded background (no weight change, so the line does not reflow). Hard words are underlined in learning yellow or unknown blue, with the small Chinese hint underneath (existing rule). Maximum width 34–40 characters per line for the current sentence (existing `listenMaxLineChars`).
- **Timeline** above the controls: the current **part**, with chapter ticks and hard-word dots. Tap to switch to whole-book scope (existing `Timeline.tsx`). With a pointer, a click sets a precise position.
- **Bottom bar** (a Liquid Glass bar, 96 pt tall plus safe area):
  - Left: **mode chip** (Learn / Relax). Learn shows the mic state when voice commands are on.
  - Centre: ⏮ sentence (56 pt), **Play/Pause 72 pt**, ⏭ sentence (56 pt).
  - Right: **speed** ("1.0×", which opens a popover with 0.75 · 0.9 · 1.0 · 1.1 · 1.25 and a slider from 0.5 to 2.0), **moon** (sleep timer), **中文** toggle, and **≡ Explanations**.
- **Answer bar** (Learn mode only) sits just above the bottom bar. See 4.4.
- **13" landscape, optional:** a right **Explanations inspector** 340 pt wide. It is a nonmodal panel listing each explanation as text: word, Chinese, explanation, "Play again". It is hidden by default and opened with ≡.
- **Compact width** (narrow window in Windowed Apps or Stage Manager): one column. Current sentence about 24 pt. The bottom bar keeps only Play, "I don't know" and ⋯. The explanation card becomes a sheet.
- **Reduce Motion:** the line change is a 200 ms cross-fade, not a scroll.
- **Relax mode differences:** no answer bar and no mic. At a hard item: card, word said 3 times, a **1.5 s quiet pause**, then the explanation, then reading again from the start of the sentence. The word is saved as **learning**. This follows the RULES.md silence path, minus the window. A "How often to stop" setting (Advanced) offers Every hard item (rule default) · Only much harder (level +2) · Max N per 10 min (existing `maxStopsPer10Min`) · Never (collect for review).

### 4.4 Active-mode buttons (I know / I don't know / Go on)
- **Default position:** a row centred above the transport in portrait. In landscape the **"Two thumbs" layout**: "I don't know" at the bottom-left corner, "Go on" and "I know" at the bottom-right corner, each 24 pt in from the safe area.
- **Size:** each button **88 pt tall**, at least **180 pt wide on 11"** (3×180 + 2×16 gap = 572 pt, fits in 820 pt portrait) and **220 pt on 13"**, with a 16 pt gap. Label text 22 pt semibold with an icon. These are well above the HIG 44 pt minimum because the user may be lying down.
- **Style:** "I don't know" = the one prominent filled accent button (it is also what silence does). "Go on" = neutral fill. "I know" = outlined green. Following the HIG, all three are the **same size**; only style differs.
- **Order** (default): I know · I don't know · Go on. The learner can reorder them.
- **Countdown:** a thin ring fills around the card, plus 5 small dots. **No ticking sound.** Default length from RULES.md: **5 s** (adjustable 3–15 s, existing `commandWindowMs`). **Touch and hold the card = countdown pauses** ("Take your time"). This is the safety valve for the HIG timed-UI rule. With VoiceOver on, the window grows to 15 s automatically.
- **Mistake protection:** "I know" is permanent, so a quiet toast appears for 6 s: "Saved as known · **Undo**". It can also be changed later in My Words.
- **Keyboard:** K = I know, D = I don't know, Esc (or ⌘. on keyboards without Esc) = Go on, matching the Mac app. Voice: the existing commands-only mic with sound-alike matching. This needs a speech recogniser on iPad: Apple's on-device recogniser or a port of Moonshine, which is a different research topic.
- **Headphone buttons:** the HIG says do not repurpose audio controls. Offer it in Advanced only, off by default: "During the 5-second window, headphone Next = Go on".

### 4.5 Explanation card (word, phrase or sentence)
- **Presentation rule:** regular width → **popover anchored to the word**, with the arrow on the word and placed so it does not cover the current sentence (prefer below it). Compact width or Read mode on 11" portrait with a long phrase → **sheet at the medium detent** (with grabber and swipe-down to close). There is only ever one card. A new card first closes the old one (HIG: one popover at a time, no cascades).
- **Size:** popover 380–420 pt wide and as tall as its content (maximum about 60% of the height). Never cover the answer bar.
- **Content (top to bottom):**
  1. The word or phrase (28–34 pt), IPA, level chip (B2/C1) and a speaker button.
  2. **Chinese meaning in context** (28 pt PingFang SC, shown only when 中文 is on).
  3. Short English meaning (17–20 pt).
  4. The book sentence with the word highlighted.
  5. While the teacher speaks, a live caption of the explanation, scrolling slowly.
  6. Buttons: I know · I don't know (deeper) · Go on · ★ Save · 中文.
- **Behaviour:** appears at the pause (word said 3×), stays during the explanation, **closes by itself** after it (RULES.md), and is then copied to the Explanations history. HIG: "save work when automatically closing". Tap outside = close (the explanation keeps playing; the text is in history).
- **Phrases and sentences** (RULE TWO): the card shows the whole phrase or sentence, with no IPA, and the "Easy English" version (RULE THREE) under it.
- **VoiceOver:** announce "Explanation: [word]". The card is a modal-like group, and focus returns to the sentence afterwards.

### 4.6 Read (pages)
- Kindle and Apple Books patterns from the existing Reading mode: tap the left 20% = back, the right 20% = forward, the middle = bars. Option "Both margins go forward" (as in Apple Books).
- **Tap a word = explain** (popover card). **Double tap = I know**, with the Undo toast, because the HIG warns against double-tap actions that change content without undo. **Select text = explain the phrase or sentence.**
- **While audio plays in Read mode:** a "Line Guide" style focus. The current sentence is normal and the rest of the page dims to 60% (as in Apple Books' Line Guide). Pages turn by themselves.
- **Aa panel** (a popover from the top bar): presets (Night, Sepia, Light, Grey, plus "My look"), A–/A+, font (Serif · Sans · OpenDyslexic), line spacing slider, margin slider, **Reset**.
- **Apple Pencil (optional):** Pencil taps behave like a finger. Pencil Pro **squeeze = "Explain this sentence"** (non-destructive). Pencil **double tap** follows the system setting and never marks words as known.
- Keep the screen awake only while the Read screen is visible and the learner is reading (not listening).

### 4.7 Sleep mode
- **How to start:**
  - "Sleep" on Home.
  - The moon in Listen.
  - A Control Center control "Dream Book Sleep".
  - Siri or Shortcuts ("Start Dream Book sleep").
  - Optionally, a gentle offer when the **Sleep Focus** turns on (Focus filter): "Start Sleep listening?"
- **Timer sheet** (medium detent, very large buttons on a dark background):
  - 10 · 15 · 20 · 30 · 45 · 60 · 90 min · **End of this part** · **End of chapter** · Custom (5–180 min). The last choice is pre-selected.
  - "Teaching while asleep": **Quiet: no stops, save hard words for the morning** (proposed default; the learner must confirm, see §7) · Gentle: short explanations only, no repeats · Normal: the same as Relax.
  - Big "Start" button.
- **Screen:**
  - A 3-second message, "Sleep well · stops at 23:40", then a fade to **pure black** over 5 s.
  - The app does **not** keep the screen on, so the iPad locks normally and audio continues (Playback category plus the Audio background mode).
  - Option "Show a dim clock" (keeps the screen on: black background, a 10%-grey clock that moves slightly every minute to protect OLED iPad Pros from burn-in, and a battery note).
  - One tap on the black screen shows three huge, very dim controls (dark amber text on black) for 8 s: **Pause** · **+15 min** · **Wake up** (leave Sleep mode).
- **Sound rules:**
  - One loudness target for all voices (reading voice, teacher voice, Chinese voice), so nothing jumps. A target near −16 LUFS is a common speech standard (from memory, unverified).
  - Sleep mode lowers the level by a further 6 dB.
  - No chimes, interface sounds, notifications, or "are you still listening?" prompts.
  - **Fade-out over the last 60 s** (adjustable 5–120 s). Pocket Casts uses 5 s, and BookPlayer starts fading with 5 s left; a longer fade is gentler for sleep.
  - Unplugging headphones = pause (HIG). A phone call = pause and do not resume by itself.
- **Lock Screen and Control Center (Now Playing):**
  - Title = part name, artist = book title, artwork = cover. Elapsed time and duration are per part.
  - Play/Pause. Skip back/forward 15 s, snapped to the start of a sentence. Next/previous track = next/previous part.
  - **Live Activity** (at most 8 h): timer countdown plus one button, "+15 min" (Pocket Casts precedent).
- **Auto-restart:** if Play is pressed within 5 min after the timer ended, the same timer starts again (Pocket Casts).
- **Where you fell asleep:** save the point where the fade started. Next time, Home offers **"Continue from 23:10, a little before you fell asleep"**. The default rewind is 3 min, snapped to a sentence start (adjustable: 0, 1, 3 or 5 min, or the start of the part). The alternative "From the start of this part" is one tap away. This answers the Headspace complaint about missing parts while settling in.
- **Morning card** (on Home the next day): "While you slept: Part 4–5 · 14 hard words heard · Review them now (5 min)". It opens the spoken review class.
- **Background sound:** do not build a sound machine. A link says "Add rain or ocean sounds under the voice" and opens Settings → Accessibility → Background Sounds. That feature has "Use When Media is Playing" and its own timer.

### 4.8 Teaching character picker
- **Screen:** a grid of 7 cards (2 rows on 11" portrait, 1 row of 4 plus 3 on 13" landscape), each **240×200 pt**, plus one "+ New character" card.
- **Card 1 = "My Teacher"** with the badge "Your style · default". It uses MY-TEACHING-STYLE.md (RULE ONE single words, RULE TWO sentences and phrases, RULE THREE very easy English). It can be edited but never deleted, and it has "Reset to my original words".
- **Each card shows:** name, a one-line description in easy English, a **"Hear a sample"** button (10 s, made from a sentence of the current book so the learner hears the real thing), and **Use**. The selected card has a thick accent border.
- **Proposed 7** (mapped from the existing 10 styles in `src/shared/styles.ts`; the teaching-style research topic decides the final list):
  1. My Teacher (custom)
  2. Friendly Teacher (teacher)
  3. Storyteller (story + imagination)
  4. Word Builder (chunks + word parts)
  5. Quiz Coach (quiz)
  6. Philosopher
  7. Poet & Songs (poetry + lyrics)
- **Smart default:** My Teacher is always the default. Dream Book may *suggest* a character for the book type ("This book is poetry. Try Poet?"), but it never switches by itself.
- **Editor** (a sheet at the large detent):
  - **Presets:** Short · Normal · Deep.
  - **Sliders:**
    - Length (short to long).
    - Word repeats before (1–5, default 3) and after (0–10, default 10 per RULE ONE).
    - Scene painting (off, short, rich).
    - Chinese at the end (off, or 2 meanings).
    - Teacher speaking speed (0.7–1.2×).
  - **Voice** (per character).
  - **Advanced:** the full prompt texts for Word / Sentence-phrase / Easy English, the AI model, and "Copy character".
  - Changes play a new sample at once.

### 4.9 Settings: simple and advanced
- **Simple page** (one screen, no scrolling on 11"):
  - **Top row of presets:** **Study** · **Relax** · **Sleep** · "+ Save my own". Each preset sets mode, stop frequency, speed, theme and timer together.
  - **8 rows:**
    1. Teacher.
    2. Default mode (Learn / Relax).
    3. Voice.
    4. Speed.
    5. Text size (A–/A+ with a live sample line).
    6. Look (Night default, Sepia, Light, Grey; or follow the system).
    7. Chinese meanings (on/off).
    8. Default sleep timer.
- **"Advanced settings"** (one button at the bottom; its own page with a search field):
  - **Listening rules:** commands window 3–15 s (default 5), "don't explain the same word again within" 500 words, stops per 10 min, word and sentence repeats, pause after an explanation.
  - **Buttons:** Edit buttons; layout presets Bottom row / Two thumbs / Left hand / Right hand.
  - **Keyboard shortcuts:** view and rebind.
  - **Highlights and hints:** colours, underline only, Chinese hints under words.
  - **Skip panel:** headers, footers, footnotes, citations, brackets, URLs and similar.
  - **Voices per role:** reading, teacher, Chinese.
  - **AI:** provider, model, monthly budget, keys. Note: Anthropic does not serve mainland China, so the provider list must allow alternatives.
  - **Account and sync:** status, "Back up now", "Restore".
  - **Data:** export vocabulary CSV through the share sheet, delete data.
  - **Diagnostics.**
- **"Edit buttons" mode** (from Advanced, or by long-pressing any button in Listen):
  - Buttons wiggle as on the Home Screen. Drag to move them between allowed zones (top bar, bottom bar, answer bar, corners).
  - Tap a button to open a small sheet: **Action** (from a list: Play/Pause, previous/next sentence, I know, I don't know, Go on, Explain last 30 s, Explain this sentence, Easy English, 中文, Sleep timer, Speed, Bookmark, Ask a question), **Label** (icon / word / both), **Size** (M 56 / L 72 / XL 88 pt), **Hide**.
  - "+ Add a button". **Reset to default.**
  - Layouts are saved in the account, so a reinstall brings them back.

### 4.10 Level test
- **First launch:** "Let's find your level (3 minutes) · or **Start listening now** and I will learn your level while you listen". This follows the HIG: optional onboarding, postpone setup.
- **Test screen:** one large word in the centre (48 pt), two huge buttons 96 pt tall, **"I know it"** and **"Not sure"**, and a progress line ("12 of 40"). This is the existing 2-stage yes/no test with made-up words to catch guessing (`src/core/level`). In Relax style, the word can be spoken as well.
- **Result:** "Your level: **B2** · about **7,800** words you know". One sentence in easy English, then the same in Chinese. Buttons: "Good, start listening" and "Take the test again".
- **Later:** the level keeps adjusting from I know / I don't know / Go on (existing Beta model). Progress shows "Level updated: B2 → B2+".

### 4.11 My Words (My Vocabulary)
- **Top:** a segmented control **Learning · Known · All**, search, and a "This book / All books" filter.
- **Each row** (64 pt tall): word or phrase, Chinese, level chip, book, date. Tap it to open the same explanation card with "Play explanation again" and the book sentence.
- **Swipe actions:** Known · Learning · Delete (with confirmation).
- **Buttons:** **"Review now (spoken, 5 min)"** (the existing review class with spaced-repetition dates) and **Export** (share sheet: CSV to Files or AirDrop).
- **Sync line:** "Saved on this iPad and online ✓".

### 4.12 Progress
- **One calm page:**
  - A big number, "**3,214** words known in Dream Book", and the level badge.
  - Bars per CEFR level for known / learning / unknown. Tapping a level shows its unknown words (existing rule).
  - "This week: 4 h 20 min listened · 2 parts finished". A gentle 7-dot week strip, with no streak-loss messages.
  - Books finished.
- **VoiceOver** reads a one-sentence summary of each chart (HIG VoiceOver: describe charts).

## 5. Keyboard, trackpad, Pencil

| Key | Action | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Space | Play / Pause | as on the Mac |
| ← / → | Previous / next sentence | |
| ↑ / ↓ | Explain previous / next sentence | RULES.md §5 |
| K / D / Esc (⌘.) | I know / I don't know / Go on | From memory (unverified): the older Magic Keyboard for iPad has no Esc key, the 2024 iPad Pro Magic Keyboard has a function row, and ⌘. works as Esc |
| L | Listen ⇄ Read | |
| M | Voice line (if available) | |
| Q | Stops at hard words on/off | |
| ⇧E | Explain the last 30 s | |
| S | Sleep timer | |
| [ / ] | Slower / faster | |
| ⌘+ / ⌘− | Text size | |
| ⌘1–⌘4 | Home / Library / My Words / Progress | HIG: tabs as View-menu items with shortcuts |
| ⌘, | Settings | system convention |
| ⌘O, ⌘F, ⌘/ | Add book, search, help | |

Register shortcuts as commands so holding ⌘ lists them. Never use Control as the modifier (HIG). Trackpad: the pointer reveals auto-hidden bars, and timeline clicks are precise. Pencil: see 4.6.

## 6. Accessibility checklist
- Dynamic Type everywhere. Book and karaoke text scale from the Dynamic Type base and the in-app A–/A+. Test at AX5 (Body 53 pt): the answer bar stacks vertically, and the bottom bar moves extras into ⋯.
- Contrast at least 4.5:1 for text up to 17 pt, in Night, Sepia, Light and Grey, also with Increase Contrast. Dim context lines at 45% must still pass at 3:1 at 20 pt or larger.
- VoiceOver: the karaoke area is one element that is **not** re-announced on every word. A rotor for "Sentences" and "Hard words". Every icon button has a label. The card is announced. The commands window extends to 15 s.
- Full Keyboard Access works. Reduce Motion means fades. No information is given only by colour (underline style plus colour for word status).
- Timed elements: an adjustable window, hold to pause, and history for self-closing cards.

## 7. Open questions to confirm with the learner (working agreement: repeat back first)
1. Sleep-mode default: no stops and words saved for the morning, versus the full RULES.md stops while falling asleep (RULE ONE says the word 10 times, which is long at night).
2. Relax mode: is a 1.5 s pause before the automatic explanation right, or none?
3. Should "I know" be at the edge (harder to hit by mistake) or in the middle?
4. Is "Two thumbs" the right default in landscape?
