## 6. Copy, avoid, do better
**Copy**
1. ElevenReader: you pay for making audio, and replays are free (cache every sentence on the device).
2. Speechify: skip panel and wide speed range (Dream Read already has these); talking with the book.
3. Kindle: spoiler-free AI (only what has been read) and the morning "Story so far" recap.
4. Whispersync: one position across reading, listening, Mac and iPad.
5. Voice Dream: pronunciation dictionary, playback with the screen locked, word plus line highlight.
6. LingQ: word statuses, known-word milestones, spaced-repetition reviews.
7. Readlang: free plan with 10 AI explanations a day; context-aware explanation as the paid feature.
8. Duolingo: streak freeze and streak revival.
9. Calm: slow pace, fade-out, no sudden sounds.
10. BookPlayer: open-source Swift player code to study.

**Avoid**
1. Surprise yearly charges and hard cancelling (Speechify complaints). Send a reminder before a trial ends, and make cancelling one tap.
2. Taking away features people paid for (Voice Dream 2024).
3. Confusing tier names and many plan lengths (LingQ).
4. A free plan that runs out in one lesson (LingQ: 20 saved words).
5. Robotic free voices (Speechify and ElevenReader free plans). Kokoro is good enough to be the free voice.
6. Cloud-only playback that fails at 3 a.m. when the Wi-Fi drops.
7. Guilt notifications.

**Do better (Dream Book's unique value)**
1. **It explains words by itself while you listen**, at the learner's CEFR level, with phrases found by the AI. No competitor does this. They only answer when you ask or tap.
2. **A tutor that knows you are asleep.**
   - Right now, silence in the 5-second window means "explain". Asleep, that would mean about 20 explanations an hour that nobody hears, for 8 hours.
   - Detect sleep: no reply in 2–3 windows in a row, the AirPods sleep pause, or the timer ending.
   - Then switch to "story only, slower, no pauses", mark where you fell asleep, and stop AI calls.
3. **Chinese support for a Chinese speaker:** two Chinese meanings spoken by a Chinese voice, and voice commands that understand a Chinese accent.
4. **A morning review:** "Last night you heard 23 new words. Here are the 6 you asked about", plus a recap from where you fell asleep.
5. **Clear prices:** one free plan forever, two paid plans, a cheap monthly price, and no tricks.

## 8. The 10 features that matter most for a learner listening while falling asleep
1. **Playback that never stops all night** with the screen locked. It needs a native audio session, lock-screen controls, and handling for interruptions such as calls and alarms.
2. **A calm, natural voice that works offline:** Kokoro on the iPad, slower speed in sleep mode, longer pauses between sentences.
3. **A smart sleep timer:** set minutes, end of chapter, or after this explanation; gentle fade-out; extend.
4. **Sleep detection** (no answers to the 5-second windows, the AirPods sleep pause, or the timer). Then stop explanations and AI calls and continue the story only, or stop.
5. **A "fell asleep here" bookmark and a morning recap:** what happened in the story, plus jump back.
6. **Hands-free voice commands with the screen off:** I know, I don't know, go on, again, slower, stop. They must understand a Chinese accent.
7. **Short spoken explanations in context, then two Chinese meanings in a Chinese voice.** They should be quieter and shorter as the learner gets sleepy.
8. **Karaoke lyrics view with word highlight and a true-black night theme,** for the minutes before sleep.
9. **Morning review with spaced repetition and a gentle streak with freezes:** words from last night, no guilt.
10. **Easy import and preparation:** EPUB, PDF and text from Files or the Share sheet; a skip panel; next chapters made in advance on Wi-Fi; Mac and iPad position sync.

## 9. Check before you build (uncertain)
- The Xcode and macOS needed for App Store uploads in 2026, and whether your Intel MacBook can run them.
- Whether the iOS Kokoro ports (CoreML and MLX) give per-word timing.
- Whether microphone listening with the screen locked works reliably on iPadOS 26.
- Whether Live Activities work on iPad.
- The exact current prices of Audible, Duolingo, Speechify monthly, Gemini TTS and Speechify's Simba API.
- Word Wise on iOS.

#### Recommendation
1. Build Dream Book as a native iPad app, not a Safari web app. The sleep features need native code: playback all night with the screen off, the microphone listening while the iPad is locked, the free Kokoro voice running on the iPad, and lock-screen controls. Two ways to do this:
   - fastest: keep the current React screens inside a Capacitor shell, and add native Swift parts for audio, the microphone and Kokoro
   - next: move to SwiftUI screens that run the existing TypeScript core inside JavaScriptCore

2. First check whether your Intel Mac on macOS 13 can build App Store apps today. I could not verify this before the search limit. If it cannot, update macOS or use a cloud build service.

3. Voices:
   - free default: Kokoro on the iPad, with Apple Premium voices as backup
   - cheap: one HD cloud voice for Premium (Inworld TTS-1.5 Mini at about $0.28 an hour, or Azure Neural)
   - best: ElevenLabs v3 or Flash (about $2.75–5.50 an hour) only with the learner's own key
   - save every generated sentence on the iPad, so listening again costs nothing

4. Add sleep detection before anything else. Today silence means "explain", so a sleeping learner would get about 20 AI explanations an hour that nobody hears. When there is no reply 2–3 times in a row, or the AirPods sleep pause happens, or the timer ends: stop explaining, mark "fell asleep here", and offer a recap in the morning.

5. Copy:
   - ElevenReader: users pay for making audio; replays are free
   - Kindle: spoiler-free AI, and a "Story so far" recap
   - Audible: an "End of chapter" sleep-timer option
   - Voice Dream: playback with the screen locked, a pronunciation dictionary
   - LingQ and Readlang: word statuses and clear prices
   - Duolingo: streak freezes, but no guilt messages

   Avoid Speechify-style surprise yearly charges and Voice Dream-style removal of paid features.

6. Prices:
   - Free: offline voices and 10 AI explanations a day
   - Plus: $6.99 a month or $49.99 a year, with an unlimited Haiku 5.5 tutor (about $0.015 per hour)
   - Premium: $14.99 a month or $119.99 a year, with a Sonnet 5.5 tutor (about $0.25 per hour) and 20 hours a month of HD cloud voice
   - a 14-day trial with a reminder before it ends


### Raw research: voices

#### Summary
I ran 44 web searches. Direct page fetches were blocked by DNS, so every figure comes from search extracts. Most prices come from third-party pages, and each is marked where sources disagree. As of 20 October 2026, the top of the Artificial Analysis (AA) Speech Arena is a tight group: ElevenLabs Eleven v4 / v4 Turbo at about 1,320–1,333 Elo (launched 28 Sep 2026), Alibaba Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus at about 1,292–1,300, Cartesia Sonic 3.6 at about 1,273–1,287 (it was #1 on 23 Sep), Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS at about 1,260–1,281, Inworld Realtime TTS-2 at about 1,252, and Speechify Simba 3.2 at about 1,237. Kokoro-82M is at about 1,064, so the leaders win roughly 4 out of 5 blind comparisons against it. Recommended tiers for Dream Book. (1) BEST: ElevenLabs Eleven v4 at about $4.32 per listening hour (about $389 a month at 3 h/day), with Cartesia Sonic 3.6 as backup (about $2.0–2.7/h). (2) CHEAP: Speechify Simba 3.2 at about $0.32–0.54/h (about $40 a month), with Inworld Realtime TTS-2 as backup (Flash at $0.81/h, TTS-2 at $0.68–1.35/h). Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS in batch mode (about $0.41/h until 31 Dec 2026, then double) is the cheapest top-5 voice if the app also builds a word-timing aligner. (3) FREE: Kokoro-82M running on the iPad through CoreML/Neural Engine ($0, offline, word timings from the model's duration output). Backup is Apple's built-in Premium/Enhanced en-GB voices ($0, native word callbacks, lower quality). The main design point: synthesise each book once at 1.0x, cache audio plus word timings on disk, and change speed by time-stretching. Use one forced-alignment fallback so any voice can drive the karaoke highlight.

#### Findings
## Voices for Dream Book: the best, the cheap and the free (state on 2026-10-20)

**Method and caveats.** 44 web searches. WebFetch to artificialanalysis.ai, huggingface.co and pandanpc.com failed (DNS), so the live leaderboards could not be read; their numbers come from search extracts and secondary posts. Most prices are from third-party pages; official pages are cited where the extract showed them (AWS, MiniMax, Speechify, Fish Audio docs, Microsoft blog). **Elo scores come from short-clip blind votes, not hours of narration.** No independent long-form audiobook listening study was found ([search summary of audiobook guides](https://notevibes.com/best-ai-voice-generator-for-audiobooks)).

**How the costs are worked out.** 1 listening hour ≈ 54,000 characters. 3 h/day × 30 days = 90 h ≈ **4.86 M characters/month** of *new* book text. Listening again from the cache costs $0. Spoken explanations add extra characters; estimate +10–20% (my estimate). An average novel (~90k words ≈ 540k characters ≈ 10 h) is shown as "per book".

## 3. Open and free models

**These can run on the iPad itself:**
- **Kokoro-82M v1.0** (Apache-2.0; no official v1.1/v2 English release found; a v1.1-zh Chinese variant exists, [model card](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M)). CoreML ports for the Neural Engine report **16.9× real time on iPhone 16 Pro** and 25× on an M4 Mac mini ([kokoro-coreml-ane](https://github.com/Jon-Schneider/kokoro-coreml-ane)). Another port reports **4–4.5× real time on A17 Pro** ([mattmireles](https://huggingface.co/mattmireles/kokoro-coreml)). Other Swift packages: [Jud/kokoro-coreml](https://github.com/jud/kokoro-coreml) (iOS 18+, ~99 MB, streaming), [speech-swift](https://github.com/soniqo/speech-swift) (claims RTF 0.08 on iPhone 16 Pro), [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio) (says physical iOS is not yet validated). **Warning:** int8 and sherpa-onnx builds ran *slower than real time on iPad* in one evaluation ([VoicePing](https://voiceping.net/en/blog/research-offline-tts-eval/)), so use CoreML/ANE in fp16. The same lesson is already in docs/KOKORO.md.
- **sherpa-onnx** has Swift packages with prebuilt XCFrameworks (v1.13.14, 10 June 2026, [SPM](https://swiftpackageregistry.com/willwade/sherpa-onnx-spm)). It runs Kokoro, KittenTTS v0.8, Matcha (zh+en) and Piper.
- **Tiny CPU models** (no iOS benchmarks found; desktop CPU numbers from [heyneo](https://heyneo.com/blog/kokoro-supertonic-inflect-nano-pocket-tts-cpu-benchmark) and [Picovoice](https://picovoice.ai/blog/on-device-tts/)):
  - Kyutai **Pocket TTS**: 100M parameters, 1.4× real time on CPU; licence given as MIT or CC-BY-4.0 (sources conflict).
  - **Supertonic 3**: 99M parameters, 4.2–8.3× real time; OpenRAIL-M licence.
  - **Kitten TTS Nano**: 42 MB int8, Apache-2.0, slow.
  - **NeuTTS Nano**: 2.1 GB peak memory, too heavy.
  - **Piper / MeloTTS**: real time but older, more robotic sound.

**Server or GPU only** (quality closer to the paid leaders, but impractical on an iPad):
- **Qwen3-TTS** 0.6B / 1.7B: Apache-2.0, 10 languages including Chinese, 97 ms streaming, needs a CUDA GPU.
- **Chatterbox / Turbo / Multilingual**: MIT, adds a watermark.
- **CosyVoice 2/3**: Apache-2.0, strong Chinese.
- **Fish S2 Pro**: open weights; licence not confirmed and probably requires a paid licence for commercial use; needs ≥16 GB VRAM.
- **Voxtral TTS**: CC BY-NC.
- **Higgs Audio v3**: non-commercial.
- **VibeVoice**: MIT on paper but research-only; Microsoft withdrew the 7B model.
- Sources: [yaps.ai](https://www.yaps.ai/blog/best-local-tts-models), [Cartesia guide](https://www.cartesia.ai/learn/open-source-tts), [tryspeakeasy](https://www.tryspeakeasy.io/blog/open-source-text-to-speech-2026).

**Not re-verified today** (from model cards as I know them; check before use): Orpheus 3B (Apache-2.0 plus Llama licence), Sesame CSM-1B (Apache-2.0), Dia 1.6B (Apache-2.0), Zonos v0.1 (Apache-2.0), F5-TTS (weights CC-BY-NC), Spark-TTS (CC-BY-NC-SA), StyleTTS2 (MIT), IndexTTS2 (custom Bilibili licence). None of these is a better fit for Dream Book than Kokoro on the iPad or a paid API in the cloud.

**Apple's built-in voices.**
- `AVSpeechSynthesizer`: free, offline, en-GB and zh-CN **Premium/Enhanced** voices (the user downloads them).
- Word callbacks come from `willSpeakRangeOfSpeechString` ([NSHipster](https://nshipster.com/avspeechsynthesizer)). `write(_:toBufferCallback:)` can render audio to files for caching.
- The Siri neural voices are not available to apps. iOS 26 has a reported regression where the voice chosen in Settings is ignored; selecting the voice by identifier works around it ([Apple forum](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/804648)).
- Quality is clearly below the 2026 neural voices; no arena score was found.
- **Personal Voice** needs user authorisation and Apple intends it for AAC (communication-aid) apps ([WWDC23 notes](https://wwdcnotes.com/notes/wwdc23/10033)). Do not use it for book narration.

## 5. The three tiers for Dream Book

### Tier 1: BEST quality, whatever the price
- **Main: ElevenLabs Eleven v4.** It is #1–2 on AA (~1,320) and ElevenLabs aims it at audiobooks ([DataNorth](https://datanorth.ai/news/elevenlabs-releases-eleven-v4-and-eleven-v4-turbo)).
  - **Price:** $0.08 per 1k chars = **$4.32/h**. At 3 h/day: **~$389/month**, plus ~$20 for live explanations through v4 Turbo at $0.04/1k. About $43 per novel.
  - **Word timings:** `/with-timestamps` gives character alignment, which you group into words. If v4 is not accepted there (unconfirmed), run the shared forced aligner (section 6) or ElevenLabs' Forced Alignment API.
  - **Build:** cloud. Render each chapter in 10k-character requests at 1.0×, store the audio and timings JSON, and never synthesise the same text twice.
- **Backup: Cartesia Sonic 3.6.** It was #1 on 23 Sep (1,273) and leads 8 of 9 language boards.
  - **Price:** **$2.0–2.7/h**, ~$182–243/month.
  - **Word timings:** native word and phoneme timestamps.
  - **Fit:** the WebSocket also makes it a good live explanation voice.

### Tier 2: CHEAP and still excellent (target under $1/h)
- **Main: Speechify Simba 3.2.** It is top-5 on AA (1,237) at **$0.32–0.54/h**: **~$40/month** on Starter ($10 including 1.9M chars, then $10/M), about $3–5 per novel.
  - **Word timings:** native word speech marks (batch JSON or SSE).
  - **Fit:** Speechify's own reading app runs on the same model, and its pattern (free on-device voices, paid cloud HD voices) matches the three-tier plan here (see docs/research/research-ux.md §2).
  - **Risks to test first:** whether its 8 voices include a British accent; that 3.2 is English-only (use another voice for Chinese); and the 2k-character request limit (chunk by paragraph).
- **Backup: Inworld Realtime TTS-2.**
  - **Price:** Flash at $15/M = **$0.81/h** (~$73/month, or $0.38/h on the Growth plan); full TTS-2 at $0.68–1.35/h.
  - **Word timings:** native WORD timestamps.
  - **Fit:** it is #1 for Mandarin, so one vendor covers both English and the Chinese meanings.
- **Honourable mention: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS in Batch mode.** Top-5 quality at **~$0.41/h now, ~$0.81/h from 1 Jan 2027**; prompt-steered British accent; good Chinese.
  - **Catch:** no word timings, so it only makes sense once the shared aligner exists.
  - **Fit:** Batch is a natural fit for "render the whole book once on import".

### Tier 3: FREE and good
- **Main: Kokoro-82M on the iPad (CoreML, Neural Engine, fp16).**
  - **Price:** $0, fully offline, so all-night sleep mode needs no network.
  - **Speed:** 4–17× real time on A17 Pro to A18 Pro class chips (community numbers; M-series iPads should be similar or faster).
  - **Word timings:** take them from the duration-predictor output, exactly as the Mac app does (docs/KOKORO.md). **Check that the chosen CoreML port exposes `duration`.** If not, add it to the conversion (the [mattmireles pipeline](https://github.com/mattmireles/kokoro-coreml) is open source).
  - **Licence risk:** the Mac app's G2P is espeak-ng, which is **GPL-3.0**. That is a problem for App Store distribution; use the port's own G2P or a permissive one.
  - **Voices:** British bf_emma and bm_george. For Chinese, use Kokoro v1.1-zh or Apple's zh-CN voice.
- **Backup: Apple AVSpeechSynthesizer** with the en-GB Premium/Enhanced and zh-CN voices. $0, built in, native word callbacks, can write to file for caching. Clearly lower quality.
- **Free cloud allowances** (the learner's own keys, as in Dream Read):
  - Google Chirp 3 HD: 1M chars/month ≈ **18 h** (no timings).
  - Azure F0: 500k ≈ **9 h**, with word boundaries.
  - Speechify: 500k ≈ 9 h (official figure; third parties say 50k).
  - Gemini 3.8 TTS free tier: small, unpublished limits; Google may use the data.
  - ElevenLabs free: 10k chars ≈ 11 min, non-commercial.

### The Chinese voice (two short meanings per word)
The volume is tiny (tens of characters per word) and each item can be cached per word and meaning, so even premium voices cost cents per month. Choices by tier:
- **Best:** Inworld TTS-2 (#1 Mandarin), MiniMax Speech 2.8 or Qwen-Audio TTS.
- **Cheap:** Azure zh-CN Neural (free 500k, word boundaries).
- **Free:** Apple zh-CN Premium voice or Kokoro v1.1-zh on the iPad.

## 6. How to build it into the iPad app (applies to all tiers)
1. **One `VoiceProvider` interface:** `synthesize(text, voice) -> (audioFile, [WordTiming])`. The cloud providers and the on-device Kokoro and Apple engines all plug in behind it.
2. **One shared forced aligner** for voices without timings (Gemini, OpenAI, Chirp 3 HD, Qwen, MiniMax). Because the text is known exactly, alignment is easy:
   - On the iPad: Apple SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26), refined by Desert-Ant-Labs **Align** (claims 113.5 → 44.9 ms mean error, [HF](https://huggingface.co/desert-ant-labs/align)).
   - On a server: aeneas ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/aeneas-ng/)) or the ElevenLabs aligner.
   - Last resort: estimate times in proportion to character count.
3. **Render once, cache for ever.**
   - Key each item by hash(engine, model version, voice, text).
   - Store AAC/Opus at about 32–48 kbps, roughly 15–22 MB per hour, so a novel is about 150–220 MB. Put it in Application Support (not Caches, which iOS can purge) and exclude it from backup.
   - Synthesise at 1.0× only. Play 0.5–2.0× with `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` and scale the timings, so a speed change never costs another render.
4. **Render ahead, not live.**
   - Cloud tiers: on import, or chapter by chapter ahead of playback (Gemini Batch at −50%).
   - Kokoro: render the next 1–3 hours in the foreground or while charging (BGProcessingTask).
   - iOS refuses GPU work in background apps, and Neural Engine use in the background is not guaranteed (**test this**). Sleep mode should therefore play from files already rendered, using the `.playback` audio session and the `audio` background mode.
5. **Live explanations** need low latency and are unique text, so use the streaming endpoint of the same family (v4 Turbo, Sonic, Inworld, Simba streaming) or Kokoro on the device. Cache them per word and context too.
6. **Rate limits to design around:** ElevenLabs 10k chars per request (v4); Speechify 2k (20k streaming); MiniMax 10k sync / 1M async; Gemini free tier is small and unpublished.

## 7. Changes since docs/research/research-voice.md
- New models: Eleven v4 / v4 Turbo (28 Sep 2026), Sonic 3.6 (Aug), Inworld TTS-2 GA (2 Sep), Simba 3.2 (Jul), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (launch prices end 31 Dec 2026).
- Price changes: Azure HD dropped to $22/M (Mar 2026); ElevenLabs list prices are now $80 / $40 per M (were $100 / $50 in September).
- Services gone or blocked: PlayHT is closed; Edge TTS is blocked in browsers.

#### Recommendation
For Dream Book, build three voice tiers behind one `VoiceProvider` interface. Every tier renders a book once at 1.0x, caches the audio plus word timings, and handles speed by time-stretching.

1. **BEST:** ElevenLabs Eleven v4, about $4.32 per listening hour, roughly $389 a month at 3 h/day. Use v4 Turbo for live explanations. Backup: Cartesia Sonic 3.6, about $2.0–2.7/h, with native word timestamps.
2. **CHEAP:** Speechify Simba 3.2, about $0.32–0.54/h, roughly $40 a month on the $10 Starter plan, with native word speech marks. Before committing, check that it has a British voice. Backup: Inworld Realtime TTS-2 (Flash at $0.81/h, or $0.38/h on the Growth plan), which has word timestamps and the best Mandarin. If an aligner is built, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS in Batch mode is about $0.41/h until 31 Dec 2026, then about $0.81/h.
3. **FREE:** Kokoro-82M on the iPad through CoreML/Neural Engine in fp16. It costs $0 and works offline; the next chapters are rendered ahead so sleep mode plays from files. Word timings come from the model's duration output, as in the Mac app. Backup: Apple's Premium/Enhanced en-GB and zh-CN voices, which have word callbacks.

Two things to build alongside the voices:
- **A shared forced aligner** (Apple SpeechAnalyzer plus the Align refinement on the iPad, or aeneas on a server). With it, voices that give no timings (Gemini, OpenAI, Chirp, Qwen) can still drive the karaoke highlight.
- **A separate small Chinese voice:** Inworld, Azure zh-CN, or Apple zh-CN for free. Its cost is negligible.

Run these checks before committing:
- whether v4 is accepted by ElevenLabs' `/with-timestamps` endpoint;
- the British accents of Simba 3.2's voices;
- whether the chosen Kokoro CoreML port exposes the duration output;
- an App-Store-safe G2P to replace the GPL-3.0 espeak-ng;
- whether the Neural Engine keeps running while the iPad is locked.

Re-check all prices on the official pages; most of the figures here come from third-party snapshots in September and October 2026.


### Fact-check: apps

- [confirmed] Speechify's iOS app is native Swift (RxSwift, SwiftUI, UIKit in job requirements); its stated stack also includes Kotlin, React and TypeScript (frontend), NodeJS and Go (backend), and Python (AI). (job-boards.greenhouse.io/speechify (fetched 2026-10-20) says: 'Some of our tech stack includes: Swift, Kotlin, React, Typescript (frontend), NodeJS, Go (backend), and Python (AI).' The public Greenhouse API (boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/speechify/jobs) lists 492 postings, all Android Team Lead or Tech Lead roles; job 5726733004 is gone.)
- [corrected] Speechify Premium is about $139/year ($29/month where offered); sources conflict on whether monthly billing exists. Users complain about surprise annual charges after trials. => The prices are right, but the 'conflict' is settled: speechify.com/pricing has a Monthly/Yearly toggle, and Premium is $29/month billed monthly or $139/year (yearly marked 'SAVE 60%'). The complaints are real: CostBench (October 2026) collects reports of the 3-day trial turning into an annual charge of about $125–140, and of charges continuing after cancellation. - [corrected] Chirp 3 HD voices reject SSML/markup, so SSML mark timepoints are probably unavailable (user report, not official). => Chirp 3 HD does not reject SSML or markup. Google's official docs list a supported SSML subset for synchronous requests: speak, say-as, p, s, phoneme, sub, break, audio, prosody and voice. Other tags are ignored, and SSML is not supported for streaming. The markup field with [pause] tags is supported. <mark> is not on the supported list, so mark timepoints are in fact unavailable, but for that reason. (cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs/chirp3-hd, 'Chirp 3: HD SSML support': 'The following SSML tags are supported for synchronous requests ... Any tags that are not on this list will be ignored ... SSML tags are not currently supported for streaming requests'. The list has no <mark>. In the forum thread (discuss.google.dev/t/185977) the Apr 2025 report was later followed by an Oct 2025 user saying markup with pause tags 'works like a charm now'.)
- [corrected] Desert-Ant-Labs Align refines Apple SpeechAnalyzer word timings on-device, claiming mean error falls from 113.5 ms to 44.9 ms. => What it does is correct: it refines the word timings from Apple SpeechTranscriber/SpeechAnalyzer on-device, using about 560 KB of Core ML. The 113.5 → 44.9 ms figures no longer appear on the model card. It now reports: all nine languages, clean audio, 124.2 → 43.9 ms (−65%) and noisy 88.3 → 33.4 ms; on LibriSpeech with Apple SpeechAnalyzer, test-clean 106.4 → 20.2 ms and test-other 111.6 → 24.8 ms. The license is source-available, with a commercial license required at scale. (huggingface.co/desert-ant-labs/align (v1.1.0): 'Corrects the word-level timings that Apple's SpeechTranscriber and SpeechAnalyzer return'; Accuracy table 'Clean 124.2ms → 43.9ms 65%'; 'Apple SpeechAnalyzer test-clean 106.4ms 20.2ms 81%'. The page does not contain the strings 113.5 or 44.9.)

The edge-tts Python library kept shipping fixes (a cluster on 11–12 Dec and v7.3.0 on 13 Oct with 'Sec-MS-GEC v2 token support'), which suggests the unofficial endpoint still works for non-browser clients. No date of 17 Dec. On github.com/rany2/edge-tts/releases: 7.2.4–7.2.7 dated 11–12 Dec (year not shown), 7.3.0 on 13 Oct adds Sec-MS-GEC v2.)
